Air conditioning in bedrooms was welcome as the street outside the hotel was too noisy to keep windows open at night but that's just Istanbul. Will certainly stay here next time we visit.

author: Washboardmary
title: Excellent location and nice hotel
text: This hotel is in the perfect location in the heart of Sultanahmet. It is easily within walking distance of many attractions and about 3 blocks from the streetcar. The staff is not friendly really, but certainly not unfriendly. Our room was very small and faced the street, so if you are a light sleeper, be sure to ask for a back room.There is a unbelievable view from the breakfast terrace. The breakfast itself needs some work. We were there during the heat of summer when it is in the 90s before 9am. All of the food is open to the air and much of it sits in the direct sun. They would be better off to serve many fewer choices and make sure they stay at proper temperature. Also, keep in mind that the whole hotel seems to be open for smokers--the terrace, the rooms and of course, the staff smokes right at the door (standing on the ledge or the sidewalk).

author: ViajerodelUniverso
title: Charming small rooms and great terrace in Sultanahmet
text: Upon returning from a tour around Turkey I wanted to spend my last two nights at Sultanahmet area. There was a great offer for this hotel at Booking.com. The reviews I read were accurate. The rooms are small but I got a quiet one as requested on the top floor. The manager at the front desk was kind enough to keep one of my luggage in their storage room while I was away during the tour. I had to do an early check-in, since the room was not ready he offered the opportunity to have breakfast at their terrace with spectacular views of Hagia Sofia, Blue Mosque, the Sea of Marmara and as far as the Bosforus. Yes the showers and the sinks in the bathrooms are as shown in pictures. Just a beautiful and charming hotel.

author: mezza_muzza
title: Good location but needs improvement
text: We stayed at the Burckin for 2 nights, and was impressed with the location and the hotel itself. The hotel is walking distance to all the sights in the old city and the decor is is beautiful, the rooms we had were a good size with a nice bathroom. The hotel has a great roof terrace with views to Aya Sofya and the Blue Mosque which is great for evening drinks. When we checked in we were given the last room for the night which was their family room and told we had to move to another room the next day. The family room was great great except for the broken shower heads. Breakfast is served on the terrace which has amazing views unfortunately there are only 3 umbrellas for shade, 2 of which are over the food and bar area. The area is not big enough for the number of guests so we had to leave and come back. We were back about 9.30 and the food had not been replenished. On our last morning the staff had not even bothered to open the one and only umbrella available. Also unlike other hotels we have stayed at throughout Turkey the water is not free.

author: Rozli
title: Great clean hotel to stay at if you will be staying in Sultahnamet
text: Stayed at the above hotel for 3 nights (26-29 june) and was excellent! Grand bazaar, the blue mosque, hagia Sophia each within less than 5mins walk! The buffet breakfast was varied and had Turkish food on the rooftop where you could see the mosques and the sea. The room we stayed in was cleaned everyday and the hallways were nicely decorated and I would say security was good- there was always somebody at the front desk, even at odd hours of the night. The staff were always smiley and courteous. With the windows being double glazed didn't hear much of street noise and had good sleeps. Also the shower had a powerful jet of water! I definitely recommend this hotel should anyone want to stay in the heart of Sultahnamet and doesn't want to do too much of walking and the road was safe n just a minute off the main road.

author: Hughsnews
title: Lovely hotel
text: We stayed in the hotel over five days towards the end of May. Overall, the hotel is clean and in a great location. The staff are friendly although the loud dance music in the morning seemed more for their enjoyment than ours. Our room was small but everything in it worked and was well kept. Unfortunately, our room was a bit expensive. It was because we were there for a weekend. The online rate for the weekdays was dramatically cheaper. All in all, it is a lovely hotel and well worth staying in, especially if you can get a cheaper rate.

author: moscowgirl55
title: Walking distance to everything
text: We just spent four nights at the Burckin in Istanbul. We were picked up from airport and checked in effortlessly. The location is great, minutes away from the Blue Mosque, Aya Sophia and the Grand Bazaar and plenty of shops and restaurants close by, including a wonderful book shop on Divan Yolo with every book thats ever been written on Turkey in English! We had nothing but positive experiences and conversations with everyone we met. The staff at the hotel were friendly and helpful, the breakfasts were varied and tasty. Try the white cheese on bread with honey mmmm! The room was small but very comfortable and clean. Fabulous roof terrace overlooking Blue Mosque etc, but a bit chilly in February! We would use the hotel again for its comfort and location.

author: JaneNearBath
title: Wonderful views from the breakfast terrace, ideal location, clean, great service
text: We stayed at the Burckin Hotel last year for 3 nights and have nothing but very happy memories. The standard was brilliant with all the luxuries you might expect from a more expensive place. Fabulous views from the terrace on the top of the hotel and charming service. A great deal of integrity and good will was evident in the business. Breakfast was a treat - different every morning!!(I was shocked at my fellow guests being so greedy though and taking advantage of the generous buffet) with fresh fruit which is always lovely. We have been away a couple of times since then and had nothing but wretched experiences. I can't recommend this hotel highly enough. Keep it up!!!

author: 247sarahd
title: A real jewel
text: Six of us stayed in this delightful hotel for our last night in Istanbul, a last-minute deal, and we were totally charmed. It was wonderfully central--an easy walk to the Blue Mosque and a bit further to Topkapi. We had 3 adjoining rooms which were small but beautifully appointed, and especially enjoyed the excellent shower! The staff brought wine and fruit while we waited, and most of them spoke excellent English. They were most helpful making a lovely dinner recommendation as well as the reservation. The price was a real steal at 100 euros per room, and it included a copious breakfast. We were allowed to leave our bags in a secure place after checking out until we needed to cllect them for our return flights.. The staff was always friendly and most helpful. I would stay there again in a heartbeat!

author: JanM219
title: Good location hotel
text: Perfect location if you want to explore Istanbul (Blue Mosque, Haga Sofia etc). Friendly staaf which helps you with arrangements, though…it is probably cheaper to make arrangements through Tourist information. Breakfirst is ok - everything you need but not first-rate. Nice rooms in modern style. Located near Tramway Station "Sultanahmet", which makes it easy to go and from Airport. From the Airport Havalimani Ataturk - just take the Metro to end station "Aksaray". Then walk between Metro and Tramway. Take Tramway in direction "Kabatas" and jump off at "Sultanahmet". Walk back in the same direction you came with Tramway, second street to the left (just after two ATM) turn left and furher down this street on the right hand you will find the hotel (iron and glas door leading down to reception).

author: ranissima
title: The One!
text: Great Hotel, I am so glad i stayed here. This is my second trip to Istanbul, the first one i stayed with my husband at Antik Hotel which was far off in Beyazit and this time I travelled with my mom and i needed to stay at a Hotel closer to the main attractions, and boy am I glad i chose Burckin, it was spot on. The hotel is on a quiet side street, yet few minutes walk to everything, really few minutes. The staff is very friendly. The room which included a full set of shampoos, gel wash, bathroom, slippers, etc... was a bit small but not a big deal. The breakfast wasnt extravagant but also not a big deal. We had a smooth transportation from/to Sabiha Gocken Airport. After 2 trips to Istanbul I have to admit that I love staying in Sultanahmet and will definitely be back at the Burckin Suites.

author: Dougdog
title: Excellence staff and central location
text: We booked the Burckin Hotel because it seemed to offer excellent value and judging by the reviews was very close to some of the main sights of Istanbul. The hotel rooms are modern, comfortable and clean. The bathrooms, as has been mentioned before, are on the small side (particularly the shower space) but were perfectly adequate for our needs. The hotel is indeed very close to the main sights and the view from the roof terrace was quite amazing. We had one minor problem with our room (it was clear that something was up with the drains) but when we spoke to the staff they were extremely obliging and found us a new room very quickly. The only thing I would recommend the hotel provide is some information in the room about e.g. when (or if) the roof terrace is open, that there is a small smoking area for guests (if required) and some details about the TV channels (there were a 1000+ channels, but no guide, so to find one in your language could take a while unless you were lucky). Overall, this is a great hotel which offered value for money, good customer service and a wonderful view. I would happily stay here again.

author: Pavel-akshan
title: excellent
text: the hotel is absolutely marvelous! it is located right in the center of Sultanahmet area of Istanbul, so you get full access to Sultan Ahmet Mosque (aka the Blue Mosque) and Aya Sofia! Tram station is just few meters away, so you need´t travel by taxi all the time. The Grand Bazaar, Yerebatan Cistern, Topkapi - all those interesting places of Istanbul are located not far from the hotel. Needless to mention lots of cafés and shops on Divan Yoglu street... The staff is very friendly and ready to help you 24/7! Room size can seem a bit small to some people, but we only spent nights at the hotel so it did not matter at all. I´d like also to mention that the hotel has a great roof terrace with breathtaking view! I would highly recommend this hotel to those visiting Istanbul first time!

author: GlennA712
title: Great location
text: Very pleased with our stay. Can not beat the central location. Very good included breakfast. Wonderful view from the roof top terrace. We had three rooms. Two were very small (401 & 407) with bed up against the wall. Room 403 was larger with open space on both sides of the bed. Quiet side street just a block off main tram line.

author: NettyKo
title: Excellent!
text: It was my first time in Istanbul,so didn't really know what to expect in terms of the hotels. I chosed Burckin cause the room rates were decent and location seemed ok. The reality was much better than I expected! The location is just excellent - in the heart of the Old Town, just a few meters away from main attractions such as Blue Mosque, Haga Sophia or Grand Bazaar, but it is located in one of the quiet back-streets so you have the feeling of being in the center, same time not too busy/noisy! The staff is great, very helpful and can really give great advice on resturants. My room was very small indeed but very clean and really nicely decorated. Huge and comfortable bed, shower with jacuzzi options :) The absolute highlight is the roof tarace... amazing view on the Bosphorous and Blue Mosque. Great breakfasts and relatively cheap drinks. I can highly recommend this hotel!

author: fsnomad
title: Wonderful location, great stay!
text: The rooms are cozy, but quite comfortable. The staff is most accommodating. Being American, I like a top sheet on the bed... they brought 2 extras. The rooftop terrace breakfasts were consistently good. The views from our room and the rooftop were stunning! Located 5 minutes from the tram running through Sultanahmet, 3 minutes from very good restaurants and tourist shopping, less than a 10 minute walk to the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia. A wonderful 5 night stay!

author: ilovefoodme9999
title: Tourist Trap
text: Booked 10 days in advance on Hotels.com. Got to hotel at midnight after delayed flight and was told room was not available? Guy was unhelpful and rude. Did not take other hotel as seems a trick, also would not say how far it was or how to get there. After seeing booking on computer we booked another and left. Hotels.com are refusing the refund and have not given a reason. Glad i booked on a credit card, chargeback will sort them out. Not a safe place to be at midnight, plenty of people around trying to be your tour guide for a price. Riad will not answer phone to hotels.com and hotels.com are not helping me now. Just do not book this hotel, it seems it is not the first time they have done this.

author: agugc
title: Simple Riad
text: We stayed at the riad in April. The place was simple but nice and the staff was overall helpful. However, rooms needed a little work (the photos were definitely taken by a very skillful photographer.) Apart from this the rooms were humid and everything including towels felt cold. This was partially solved on our second night when we turned on the heating. Hot water does not last enough for two people so maybe waiting between showers is a good idea. The place is very hard to find (especially is you arrive at night) and the phone number that appears in the website does not correspond to the riad anymore. You should ask for very precise instructions before arrival. I guess that the relation price / service provided was ok.

author: amandasJ6996UK
title: Midnight trek to another riad
text: We book 3 rooms on this riad for our group trip to marrakech. After a delayed flight, we reached this riad at about 11 pm to be told that there is a double booking in the rooms and they have given 2 of 3 rooms away to other guests. Obviously we are not pleased. We were told that they have emailed us this change earlier in the evening but we were on the plane at that time! We were send away to Riad Oulaya (15 minutes trek at midnight though the closed souks) which is another riad owned by the same man. Riad oulaya was not the riad we expected it to be with tired decor, broken floor tiles, blocked shower and broken shower head. No financial compensation offered, no gestures of apologies at all. We think that we are a one off case but upon reading previous review this had happened to other guests on other occasion as well. I am not sure of the other quality of this riad as we did not actually end up staying here but the management of this riad is appaling! Be careful if you book a room in this riad because you might not get what you book for.

author: Tai_Travels
title: A Marvel in the Medina
text: To start and end with the Staff the Staff the Staff!!!!!!! They were so great!!!! Badr and Lorena were extremely hospitable. Badr gave us a short tour of the Medina's labyrinth streets shortly upon arrival and invited all of the Riad's tenants to diner and a local restaurant where we all got to know each other pretty well, a night full of jokes, stories and experiences of different folks from around the world. Bad and Lorena enjoyed and stayed with us the whole night ensuring that after a night of drinks that we still all made it back to our rooms (LOL). The room was a gem, beautiful authentic accents all around. Spacious bedrooms and a really nice and spacious bathroom. Breakfast was nice and in line with the local trends. This is definitely a great stay when visiting the heart of Marrakech and plan to stay in the Medina. Thanks to the staff for a great experience!!!!!

author: NeilM646
title: Beautiful Riad but Language Barrier
text: I stayed in two different Riads during my 3-day stay in Marrakech (one night in Dar Zaman and two nights in Dar Eliane). I would say that Dar Eliane is one of the most beautiful interiors I've ever seen in a building. Very traditional and Moroccan and there is a lot of attention to detail - everything from the doors to the lights are artistic in nature. The location is good (if you can find it by yourself in the Medina, but that's true for most places in the Medina!) and the manager was friendly. The reason I've given this 4 instead of 5 stars was that I thought the customer service at Dar Eliane wasn't as strong as it was in the other Riad I stayed in. The manager did not go out of her way to help us and advise us on sights in the city, etc. We had to ask and push for help. Secondly, she did not speak great English so if you're an English speaker, this poses some obstacles.

author: Chicagoan_For_Now
title: Beautiful Riad Oasis
text: I was admittedly not prepared for the Marrakech medina environment, so the trek into the heart of the old city with its narrow streets and pedestrian/motor bike/donkey cart traffic was a big surprise. The taxi brought us as close as they could, and a local man showed us the way in for a few dirham. (In hindsight we probably should have made inbound arrangements with the Riad...) Nonetheless, after arriving the Riad manager Slimane made us feel welcome, and got us settled into a beautiful room with a private bath. If you are not comfortable with the bed & breakfast model, don't stay in a Riad. If you are, this one is spectacular. We had a lovely breakfast served to us every morning, and ordered dinner one evening which was served in a main room with a very local feel. This is well located for exploring ("getting lost") in the old city, clean and beautiful. I would recommend this riad highly.

author: Chettle
title: Great Riad to escape the Hectic
text: 2 of us stayed at the Riad Dar Elaine in October 2013. We had organised our own transfer from the airport who dropped us as far as his car would allow, he then arranged a man with a handcart to take our luggage and show us the way. I would highly recommend this as we would never have found the Riad otherwise! We were greeted with Mint Tea on arrival which was a welcome sight. It would have been good if we were given a bit more information on the surroundings such as places to eat/visit, perhaps supply a welcome pack to include this, wifi details and options of food/beer etc. However when we did eventually find out that food was available we organised a meal in, which was lovely (although rather expensive for our budget). There is a great little restaurant just outside and turn right (found on the left), its very basic with little choice, but the food was fantastic at a very good price. The Riad itself has great character, clean and spacious rooms, in a location right in the middle of things (although you wouldn't know once in the Riad as it was very peaceful). Very good breakfast and friendly staff. I would highly recommend staying here to get a real taste of Marrakesh.

author: ReviewerFortyTwo
title: A charming, atmospheric riad with warm, helpful staff
text: Having read the reviews on Tripadvisor, we decided to stay at Riad Dar Eliane for our first trip to Marrakech. We were not disappointed. The riad is beautifully decorated, immaculately clean and tidy and has some lovely places to sit. The staff are superb, and Slimane, after insisting on our arrival that we "make ourselves at home" spent the following three days of our stay ensuring that we did. The breakfasts are a feast, and the components vary from day to day, which is a nice touch. My only recommendation to potential visitors would be to make sure you know the exact way there before you arrive. The souqs are a labyrinth, and we spent quite some time dragging our suitcase in circles and stubbornly refusing to be assisted. Failing that, pay a guide to take you there (but no more than 10 dirham!)

author: 872SimonS
title: Fantastic stay at Riad Dar Eliane
text: We have just returned from a long weekend in Marrakesh and we could not have booked a better place to stay than Dar Eliane. The Riad is beautiful and clean and only a 5 minute walk to Jemaa el-Fnaa. The staff at the Riad were very friendly and nothing was too much trouble. The breakfast was amazing and really set us up for the day walking around the myriad of souks and bizarres. They arranged our transfers to and from the airport which went without incident and even popped down to the shops if we requested something which was not on hand at the house. Marrakesh was a delight and made even more so by staying at the Dar Eliane. Thanks to all the staff and John for a memorable stay. Simon & Nicky

author: sarahcA5074RU
title: First time in a riad - did not disappoint!
text: Our first visit to Marrakesh and our first time staying in a riad. It was so refreshing to return here after the craziness of Jamaa El Fna square! Set right in the middle of the medina, and less than ten minute walk to the square so location is perfect. Staff were so friendly and helpful and welcoming. The breakfast was great, such a big spread of food - crepes, bread, eggs, fruit salad, yoghurt, coffee, cake, etc. I would agree however with previous reviewers who mentioned ear plugs - the birds do make a lot of noise in the courtyard in the mornings. This didn't bother us too much because we were up early most mornings anyways but its something to bear in mind. Will definitely be returning to Riad Dar Eliane WHEN (not if) we return to Marrakesh again! :)

author: Bethany746
title: A Beautiful Riad
text: We had a fabulous stay at Riad Dar Eliane we loved the Riad the location was perfect for us for exploring the souks. It's a great little oasis in the middle of hectic and vibrant city of Marrakech It was peaceful and beautiful. All the staff were super polite and friendly. I absolutely adored the fact that you can hear birds in the morning while eating your morning breakfast. Our room was super romantic. The walk to the main square was only 10min.We walked from the Riad to Majorelle Gardens also. Be aware the mosque call will wake you up super early but this will happen in any Riad as there are so many mosques in the medina. I would totally recommend anyone to stay here.

author: EvaB346
title: 1001 nights
text: Our stay at Riad dar Eliane was like a fairy tale. The house is beautiful, the decoration amazing and the service is very good. We had some difficulty finding the riad in the labyrinth of Marrakesh and the manager send someone to help us find a parking and the riad. The instructions to find the riad could be a lot better. The room was very nice and clean, and the breakfast was delicious. The rooftop terrace overlooking Marrakesh was a nice surprise. The only negative remark is that the dinner the offer was very expensive and they served us a starter and dessert without asking, but of course we did have to pay for it. The food was good, but you can find the same dishes for half of the price somewhere else. Especially the young boy (I forgot his name) helped us a lot and was very friendly.

author: dannoAuckland
title: Appearances can be deceptive
text: We were picked up at the airport by a taxi arranged by the riad, and dropped off near the riad & met by the local barrowman who set off at a fast clip with our bags in his cart. We were slightly concerned when he headed down an alley & hauled the cart over a massive mound of gravel blocking the alley - then a couple of turns & we were in the riad - & what a haven of peace & quiet after the razzamatazz of the medina. Bouchra welcomed us & showed us our room on the first level - a day bed, a double bed with a small passage to bathroom & toilet - all beautiful lamps & screens. The late lunch (which we thought would be a sandwich) turned into a gorgeous tagine of meatballs & eggs. The riad was a great place to stay - though in spite of maps & careful directions we kept getting lost somewhere not too far away, though once we found the vegetable market all was well. Our room was quiet, the bed was comfortable, & everything about the riad was great. Staff very friendly & helpful - & contacted our tour guide to arrange our departure pickup. Oh yes, by the time we went for our first walk an hour or so after we arrived, the mound of gravel had totally vanished - and the alley was far smoother!

author: olly_1000
title: Home from home in the heart of Marrakech
text: Fantastic riad that made our holiday all the more enjoyable. The hustle & bustle of the main square and the various souks are just a few mins walk away, yet when you enter the Riad it's wonderfully tranquil, a welcome retreat from all the noise of the city. We stayed 4 nights in total over the week, the staff happy to accomodate us as we went off on various trips away from Marrakech. There was no problem with us leaving a bag when we were away for a couple of nights, and Symon the night porter was always there to make breakfast and bring fresh mint tea whatever hour we were having to rise. We stayed in two different rooms, both decorated to a high standard to create a real feel of the local culture. It was a real bonus to have a very effective wall mounted heater for the chilly nights, and a lovely large shower to return to after a days haggling in the markets. Special thanks to the owner John who we met on our second day, and walked with us to the main square to find the local excursion operators to help us book a trip to the Sahara. I cannot recommend this riad highly enough. Top service, excellent rooms and courtyard, a great roof terrace to take in the view, and probably the best mint tea we were served throughout our entire week.

author: SoulTraveller_10
title: Just beautiful....
text: I stayed here for 4 nights, didnt want to leave.! All the staff were fabulous, very friendly, always smiling and helpful. A special thanks to Sleeman ( sorry if the spelling is wrong!) he was more than happy to help wth anything at any time of the night.. a bulb blew in a lamp he had it fixed within seconds.We got lost getting back to the Riad on our first night, we rang him and within minutes he found us and escorted us back to the Riad all with a bright smiling face. Afterbuying more rugs than I had intended, Bouchra the owner personally took my rugs to the Post Office and rang me with a price to send then back to Australia.....all done in her own time.!! Only thing I would suggest would be a little more light in the rooms.I found it difficult to find things in my suitcase, when I mentioned this to Sleeman he put and extra lamp in my room ...still it could have been lighter. Overall I would definitely stay here again and highly recommend this Riad to others. The warm greeting as well as mint tea upon arrival was a most welcomed surprise....Robyn Australia

author: AndyEye
title: Excellent Riad, very helpful staff, just minutes from Main Square
text: The Riad was very helpful in arranging a taxi for our arrival. Most riads are in tiny alleyways making them difficult to find if your taxi driver does not know where he has to go so it helps if the Riad can arrange a taxi for you. We paid 10 Euros from the airport for a 20 minute journey. They also helped us book restaurants, a local guide and a daytrip to the Ourika Valley. The riad itself is very pleasant and situated within a 10 minute walk of the Jamaa El Fna (Main Square) and it is a great starting place to explore the Medina from. The staff were very helpful and always around when you needed them. The rooms were clean and tidy and if you needed anything you simply had to ask and you would get it immediately. I would definitely recommend this Riad.

author: Ronnie79UK
title: Very friendly Riad
text: We stayed at Riad Dar Eliane for four nights and our stay could not have been better. It was the first time that we have stayed in a riad so did not know quite what to expect. It is very different to a hotel but we enjoyed every minute of it. All the staff were very friendly and helpful throughout our stay. We had breakfast every morning on the roof terrace and it was absolutely delicious. It was such a nice clean place to come back to at the end of our day. The riad is conveniently situated just 10 minutes’ walk from the main square. We would definitely stay there again if we were to go back to Marrakech.

author: Mags121
title: Wonderful - it made the holiday.
text: Myself and two other female friends booked the entire Riad for five nights. We felt comfortable, welcomed and help was on hand if need be. On the first night Suleman took us to the main square and gave us his phone number in case we got lost on the way back (we didn't). The staff were on hand to help with anything - even when we all got stomach bugs!. All of the rooms were nice and comfortable - and air conditioned. We felt at home as soon as we arrived and having a lovely base really topped off our stay in Marrakech. NB Would love to hear if Bouchra had a boy or a girl as she was 8 months pregant while we were there (and working in the 100+ degree heat - puts us to shame!) I'd definately recommend the airport transfer - it includes a man to take you (and more importantly your cases) from the taxi through the alleys to the Riad. We would never have found it otherwise. Make sure you have some change as tips!

author: RF84UK
title: Delightful Riad with very friendly and helpful staff
text: We loved the Riad Dar Eliane. The staff were exceptionally polite, very helpful, friendly and always good humoured. The Riad itself is beautiful with a lovely roof top terrace that has a good view across the surrounding souks. The food at the Riad is amazing, comprising of all the authentic tastes of Morocco. The Riad feels like a home and not at all like a hotel. You feel at home from the moment you step in, and you don't want to leave. The Riad is in the north of the medina and souks, but offers a unique opportunity to live among the locals and experience the culture and lifestyle of Marrakech more intimately. The experience at the Riad made our trip very memorable.

author: Maddy82
title: This is a lovely place to stay
text: We stayed for four nights at Riad Dar Eliane and we would very much recommend this riad to others. Our room was very nice, the courtyard is lovely and the terrace is fantastic, also the breakfast is excellent too. It really is a haven of tranquillity amidst the madness that is Marrakech. On our arrival at the riad we were greeted with mint tea and very helpfully shown our bearings on a map and given directions on how to get around which was very useful. Finding our way to the Jamma el Fna square the next day seemed a bit daunting at first but after we'd done it once it was fine. It takes about 10 minutes to walk there from the riad. Getting back to the riad after a day of exploring Marrakech is great, because it is so relaxing and quiet. I'd recommend allowing the riad to arrange a taxi to meet you at the airport as it is a bit tricky to find on your own. This cost is 10 euros but it is well worth it.We were very happy staying here and we would highly recommend it to others.

author: TonyonTour
title: Impressive Riad with Excellent Staff
text: If you are planning to spend a few days in the medina where all the action is in Marrakech, then this is the riad for you. After weaving around the dusty and busy streets of Marrakech we were led down an alleyway and into the palatial surroundings of Riad Dar Eliane which became a retreat for relaxation after the madness of Marrakech. The riad’s whole look and feel was really authentic and impressive. Our room was superb, decorated in the traditional style with a large en-suite. The location is fantastic, it feels like it's off the tourist trail but close to the souks and the main square which were easy to find with the help of a very well-drawn map given to us on arrival. We had breakfast on the roof terrace every morning with its 360 degree view of medina. We also had dinner at the riad on our first night which was exceptional. Bottles of wine and beers are available to buy in the riad which is great as not many other places serve alcohol. All in all the staff at this riad are very welcoming, friendly and helpful; they provide a first-rate service and good advice. We were very impressed with this riad and would highly recommend.

author: Wilki1982
title: The perfect place to stay in Marrakech
text: The other reviews here of Riad Dar Eliane say it all guests can expect a friendly and attentive service from John and all his staff. The riad is immaculate with an exceptional level of cleanliness and very tasteful and stylish decor and furnishings. In traditional local style the riad is arranged so that rooms on the ground and first floors all open onto a central courtyard area which is open to the sky. This makes the riad feel very light, airy and spacious yet extremely peaceful. The main square in Marrakech where it all happens is only a ten minute walk away through bustling alleyways which twist and turn through the souks guests can experience authentic Medina life yet easily retreat to the tranquillity of Riad Dar Eliane when they need to recharge their batteries. Above all, because of the intimate size of Riad Dar Eliane John and his staff are able to provide great and friendly service. I really could not fault anything during my week-long stay. Highly recommended.

author: V_V_Derby
title: Perfect
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at this Riad for a week at the beginning of March and we couldn't recommend it enough. Situated in the souks the Riad is only a short walk away from the Marrakech Museum and the Medrasa Ben Youseff and only a 10 minute to the main square. Despite the riad being located in the middle of the hustle and bustle of the souks once inside the riad ensured you have entered a haven of peace and tranquillity especially after a hard days walking, sightseeing and negotiating in the frenzied souks! All of the staff are extremely pleasant and helpful and they were great at giving much needed advice about Marrakech, plus booking restaurants and recommending places to visit etc. The traditional Moroccan dinners at Riad Dar Eliane were fantastic which we ended up having twice as it was so good! The roof terrace was lovely and a great place to relax with a book or sunbathe after a long days sightseeing. Our room was superb; everything was very clean and comfortable with a lovely en-suite and furnishings. I would definitely recommend to anybody wanting a friendly, welcoming and relaxing riad in Marrakech.

author: BellaUK38
title: Charming Riad
text: We recently stayed at this riad for three nights, the riad arranged our transfer from the airport which worked to perfection and the driver was happy wait for us so we were able to change some money at the bureau de change in the airport. When we arrived near the riad Dar Eliane a porter was there to meet us and taking our luggage on a hand cart walked with us to the riad. Bouchra the manageress was very welcoming and gave us time to relax with a drink before she gave us a tour of the riad and provided us with a map of the area and highlighted some points of interest. We were then shown to our room which was large and beautifully furnished. Breakfast was very good, crepes, bread, jams and eggs in various options, tea and coffee which can be taken on the roof terrace or in the courtyard. The riad is located in a quite corner away from the noise and the hustle and bustle of the souks but is still amazingly only a few steps away from the souks and within a 10 minute walk to the main square. All in all this is a charming riad with stylish touches, very well located and most importantly for us helpful and friendly staff. We would recommend strongly.

author: Linz24
title: Lovely riad, shame it was so cold
text: Just returned from a 4 night stay at Riad Dar Eliane. We enjoyed our stay overall but the cold weather meant that the public areas of the Riad were very cold (a plastic cover on the roof was pulled over to protect the main courtyard from the rain). The Riad is very beautiful, with lovely (heated) bedrooms and bathrooms, really well decorated and characterful. I am sure it is ideal in warm weather. I would not recommend it for families with small children, unfortunately all sounds reverberate around the Riad, not ideal with a 3 year old (difficult trying to keep him quiet!). The service was excellent - lovely, friendly staff, nothing was too much trouble for them. 3-course dinner was lovely. The riad is an 8 min walk through the souks from the main square, with a short walk at the end down a narrow, quiet lane.

author: 5arah80
title: Ideal place in the real medina
text: This riad is the absolute ideal place to stay when visiting Marrakech The raid is gorgeous and quaint. It is small and intimate and beautifully decorated to reflect the Moroccan atmosphere. The rooms are absolutely gorgeous and the beds are extremely comfortable. The staff are extremely friendly and they are always available for all your possible needs. The food at the riad is delicious and plentiful and there are options for those who are vegetarian. This Riad will instantly feel like home with its warm atmosphere and friendly staff. The location is ideal, giving the guest a true feel for the old part of Marrakech, while still providing easy access to all the tourist locations. I can truly not say enough good things about this riad and we had an incredible experience while visiting.

author: Alex23UK
title: Charming
text: From the moment we arrived we were made to feel welcome. The staff immediately proved attentive (but never intrusive), warm, charming and incredibly good humoured. The atmosphere, the staff, the fantastic Moroccan decor was perfect. After the chaos and hectic pace of Marrakesh, Riad Dar Eliane was an oasis of calm. Dinner was cooked to order, a true taste of Morocco, superbly presented and excellent quality. The ladies in the kitchen took great pride in producing wonderful food. Breakfasts were equally good. Nothing was too much trouble for the staff, you are in the middle of Marrakesh, so it’s easy to find the jamaa el fna on your own, but if you need any help ask the staff and they'll help you anytime. So there is really nothing bad to say about Riad Dar Eliane and it will certainly not be our last stay there.

author: DianaDavey
title: Beautiful Riad
text: Beautiful place very calm and cool after the hot streets. This was our first time in Marrakech. Wow what an assault on our senses. The sights sounds and smells were terrific. We managed to eat up high overlooking the main square just as the sun was going down and the lights of the stalls were coming on – what a sight! Really please with our room, the staff were all really lovely. We will certainly recommend the riad to our friends. Loads of luck for the future, thank you for an amazing few days, lots of memories to take with us.

author: J0s85
title: Intimate and tastefully decorated Riad
text: If you are looking for a small riad in an accessible part of the medina, then look no further. The riad has just four rooms; two on the upper level and two at ground floor level. The rooms are well maintained, very clean, with good beds. Breakfast is included in the cost of the rooms, fresh orange, coffee, home made bread with a variety of jams, natural yogurt, pancakes and homemade cake. Having stayed in several riads, I can definitely recommend this one. The staff are very pleasant and friendly, multi-lingual, and ready to help with whatever questions you may have. The centre of the riad has the obligatory courtyard, highly decorated in traditional plaster carving and the main doors are beautifully hand painted in traditional style. There is also a great roof terrace to catch the breezes and relax. On my last night I asked if I could eat at the riad and a magnificent three course meal was prepared for me, probably the best meal I had had whilst in Marrakech and not expensive by any means. Well worth a visit.

author: jordana123xx
title: Fantastic experience, Fantastic city and a hotel to match!
text: When we arrived at the airport our flight was slightly delayed and the taxi was there to meet us then he waited whilst we qued up to exchanged our money. Dropped us near the Riad, we were slightly apprehensive when he dropped us off as it was dark and we thought we were going to get lost down all the Marrakesh alleys/souks. Then a porter came and took our bags, we were met by Slimen who was more then welcoming, he made us feel right at home. He directed us to a gorgeous restaurant for some classic Moroccan food, which we highly recommend, it is around a 2min walk from the Riad. Our room was beautiful, we felt safe and comfortable immediately. All very clean and room was tidied and cleaned every day! As the Riad is open air, you get woken up around 6ish when they call pray then again at 7 with the birds - but all adds to the experience and we got use to it and wouldn’t have it any other way. The walk to the square was fairly daunting on the first day but again we got use to it fairly quickly, we didn’t get lost once! Stay here you will not be disappointed. Jordana and Doug - London and Loughborough

author: MeaganWales
title: Lovely little Riad in Marrakech
text: I have very high standards and Riad Dar Eliane satisfied them and more it is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in. It is beautifully decorated and spotlessly clean. The roof terrace and the courtyard are really nice peaceful places (and beautifully lit in the evenings) to sit and chill when you want to escape the madness that is Marrakech, The service was excellent - I was welcomed with mint tea, and more importantly, a decent map! The breakfasts were delicious. I was pleasantly surprised by the quality and service of the dinner that is available and have to say that it was much better than a lot of restaurants that I experienced during my stay in Marrakech. The Riad is located on a quiet side street 10 minutes walk from the main square and is easily accessible to many of the major points of interest. In addition, the staff were very attentive to my needs and helped me with things such as adapters and wi-fi. Riad Dar Eliane is the best Riad in Marrakech and won’t disappoint you!!!

author: NantwichCheshire_Cat
title: Relaxed Retreat
text: I have been promising myself I would write a review about our stay at Riad Dar Eliane for sometime and now with the weather so bad at home I have found myself with some time on my hands so here it is. We stayed at Riad Dar Eliane for three days at the end of September 2010. Having never been to Marrakech before, it was an amazing experience and I am so glad we stayed within the Medina therefore truly experiencing Marrakech's sights & sounds but with the ability to retreat within the Riad walls. The Riad itself is beautifully decorated with very efficient, helpful and friendly staff. The Bedrooms were all unique with amazing colour schemes. The food & wine was delicious and plentiful. The breakfasts which included crepes, homemade breads, delicious jams, yoghurts, mint tea and coffee were sufficient to start off the day. I think the positive comments are well deserved because of the overall experience and value for money of our stay. Riad Dar Eliane sells itself on its relaxed informal service and that’s what it delivers.

author: StephieHill
title: A Stylish, Peaceful Riad
text: We loved our stay at Riad Dar Eliane, perfectly located in the Marrakech Medina, just minutes from the souk and the main square; it was quiet, peaceful and beautiful. The owner John was incredibly helpful, giving us a good intro to the city and even a quick tour of the souk. He was always on hand to answer questions or advise us on places to explore. We ate one night on the terrace, a delicious home cooked tagine, sitting under the stars gazing over the rooftops towards the Koutoubia Mosque, a fabulous view and a delicious meal. We ordered wine and beers every night which we drank in the Riad, because alcohol is not available in the Medina. The breakfasts were fantastic, the other guests were very friendly, and overall it was a great experience. We had a truly wonderful time and I would recommend the riad to anyone of any age. It is great value, with a wonderful owner, and wonderful staff.

author: BillandLizUK
title: Great place to stay in Marrakech
text: We stayed at this Riad for 4 nights in September. We were met by Rachid the taxi driver when we arrived at the airport and instantly made to feel welcome. The Riad only has four bedrooms but every room is different, each room has amazing attention to detail down to the hand painted doors.The Riad also has a roof top terrace to relax and enjoy the sunshine. The staff led by Bouchra were very friendly and accommodating and anxious to ensure we made the most of our stay. The Riad is very close to the main square so an evening walk to the cafes and restaurants to watch all the activities is very easy. If you decide to get away from the hustle and bustle and have an evening meal made by the in house chef at the Riad you will not be disappointed. We really enjoyed our stay and when we come back to Marrakech will look to stay at Dar Eliane again. Bill & Liz

author: MARCUSNottingHill
title: A calm oasis, in a busy city
text: My girlfriend and I stayed at Riad Dar Eliane for 4 nights and were made to feel very welcome from the minute we entered the hotel. It is decorated in a Moroccan chic style with a good sized roof terrace that's great for sun bathing and relaxing. It is located about 10 minutes from the main square, Jemma el fna, 10 minutes from La Foundouk a spectacular restaurant and about 10 minutes from Cafe Arabe a more relaxed restaurant. Each morning we had a traditional Moroccan breakfast (served between 8am 11am) in the open riad courtyard. We opted for an evening meal on our final night and were given a traditional and tasty three course meal for around 25 Euros each, it is also possible to purchase wine and beer at the hotel for a very reasonable cost. Riad Dar Eliane also organized for my girlfriend to have a traditional hammam treatment and massage at the Didi spa near the square. Marrakesh is quite a hectic place, which made us realize how fortunate we were to have such a relaxing riad to come back to. Bouchra and her team really did their best to make our stay comfortable and enjoyable and we had a great time at the Riad Dar Eliane.

author: CharlieChelmsford
title: Excellent Riad - full of character
text: This is a lovely place; it’s down a side passage off a bustling thoroughfare in the northern medina, lined with shops and full of shoppers, tradesmen and people on motorized scooters. Our room was excellent and we found all staff at the riad to be very friendly and helpful. Bouchra the manageress met us when we arrived and gave us information about how to get to the Jemma El Fna square. We arranged to have a meal the night we arrived. It was really good, and very plentiful we would recommend eating here one night on your stay; the wine and beer are good too! The riad offers to get a taxi to pick you up at the airport for a 10 euro fee. This is a reasonable deal and the driver takes you to the nearest point that cars can reach, from there the riad is about a five minute walk. We walked through the more modern part of Marrakech, Gueliz where many of the western style hotels and you really could be anywhere in Europe in this quarter. If you want an authentic experience in a place central to the heart of Marrakech, then this fits the bill.

author: FiestasonaShoestring
title: Excellent Riad - Perfect stay
text: Service was excellent at this Riad. It's a short walk away from the rush and teeming life that is the Medina but it feels another world away as soon as you step through the door. It's tranquil, relaxed and very well run, with 24 hour reception facilities. From the welcome cup of mint tea to them seeing you out the door, the service is seamless. It's a beautiful property, well furnished and beautifully restored. Our room was clean, well furnished and had a comfortable bed. We ate in the riad for our second night and had a 3 course dinner with wine. The quality of the food was extremely high, and it is worth staying in for. Breakfasts were also very good and the roof terrace is a lovely place to eat highly recommended.

author: JFWembley
title: Excellent Hospitality - Well Located
text: In terms of value for money, Riad Dar Eliane is really hands down! The Riad is centrally placed in the old Medina (Souks) down a warren of alleys in an atmospheric family neighbourhood. All of the local residents are very friendly and welcoming. The Riad’s internal courtyard has been attentively restored and all the rooms are very colourful and spacious. The staff are both kind and considerate and if you book a dinner there, it is of the highest quality and has a real home-made feel. All of the key sites are within walking distance of the Riad which makes life much easier by way of not having to get a taxi everytime you venture out. Hanging out and relaxing on the roof terrace is a must do after a day in the hustle-and-bustle of Marrakech. So if you're interested in staying at a great Riad with caring and attentive staff, good food, try Dar Eliane!

author: BradSeall
title: Fantastic Riad Amazing Food
text: The Dar Eliane is a fantastic little Riad in the middle of the Medina. It is impossible to comprehend that the manic streets of Marrakech are just a few steps away from you whilst drinking a bottle of wine on the roof terrace of this beautiful hideaway. The service is one of the best I have encountered, very personal and very attentive and you get exactly what you see/read on their website. I booked this Riad after reading the reviews on TripAdvisor and was not disappointed. In terms of location, I have no complaints. It is true that the riad is only about 10 minutes walk from the main square, and I looked forward to this walk everyday as it gave me a different taste of Marrakech, away from areas often frequented by tourists. The Riad is quiet, clean with lovely interior; amazing food (you must try their dinner!!) Bouchra and her staff are fantastic team who go out of their way to make your stay a memorable one. I would highly recommend this Riad.

author: MarkyCornwall
title: Great place to stay in Marrakech – really friendly & helpful
text: My girlfriend and I stayed here for 3 nights after staying in Essaouira for 3 nights - came home this morning. It’s a great little place to stay. A 10 min walk to the Jemma El Fna square - though didn’t seem like it as it was a very entertaining walk. Bouchra was a great help and nothing was too much trouble for her. She gave us lots of info on what to do and see ,my girlfriend enjoyed the Bains de Marrakech and is well worth a visit - as was Chez Ali a fantasia evening with masses of food. The service in riad is fantastic, good room, clean and tidy, great breakfasts and the staff were really friendly. We didn’t eat in the riad in the evening but another couple did and they commented on how good the food was there, also Bouchra let me use the laptop in the riad to post some emails on internet just to keep in touch with friends. We would definitely recommend this riad without exception or hesitation.

author: LizzySanders
title: Authentic Riad
text: We had previously arranged with the Riad to be picked up at the airport (10 Euros) where we were met by an English speaking driver who welcomed us ,we drove through the maze of streets before stopping after about 20 minutes then we walked down a small street into an old alley which led to the entrance to the Riad. We entered into a beautiful courtyard with large plants, various lanterns and carpets, the manageress Bouchra greeted us warmly and we were invited to sit in the small lounge and given mint tea, emphasizing that the Riad was our home during our stay and nothing was too much trouble for us. The next day we took breakfast on the terrace enjoying the views, a wonderful blue sky and sun with a view of the Koutoubia Mosque. Breakfast was simple but ample and Sleimen the waiter was very friendly. Marrakech is not for everyone although those with a spirit of adventure will find plenty to do. Be prepared to get lost in the maze of Souks but we felt safe, even out late there are plenty of people around to help you if you get lost. The main square in the evenings, strolling around sampling traditional music, food and the snake charmers is a must. If you want a hotel with hard edges, a reception that has little or no real time for you, boring rooms and indifferent food then I am sure that the Dar Eliane is not for you. But if you want a chance to appreciate what life might have been like 300 years ago yet still enjoy modern conveniences, the ability to be in the middle of the old town within minutes, friendly and caring staff then this is the place to do it.

author: JRonherjollys
title: The most perfect place to stay.
text: Dar Eliane is tucked away down a winding terracotta street and could easily be missed. Once the front door is opened, you are greeted with smiles and a very warm welcome. The riad is simply a gem. The detail has been carefully thought out and everywhere you look there is something to delight the eye. Glass, carved plaster, arches and vibrant colour. After a busy day shopping or sight seeing, it is a calm quiet place to retreat to. Our hosts where attentive and helpful but not at all intrusive. Thank you all so much.

author: 5BarberTarr
title: A real little gem of a place!
text: Some might think it's location tucked away, down a very small alley, 10 mins walk from the main square is a disadvantage but don't let this deter you from this super little place. We never felt threatened either at night or in the day (but then so much of this is down to how you act and dress). It has 4 double rooms which you can book individually (or apparently you can book the whole riad) - they're all done out beautifully. As it is a traditional riad the room all look into the central courtyard - we noted that some people felt they lacked privacy but we certainly never felt that as we were either out exploring, sleeping or chatting to the other lovely guests staying at the riad which was all part of the adventure. We were well looked after by Bouchra and Slimane - if you needed anything organised like taxis, dinner, etc, they were always most helpful (they also made sure that if you got lost they were always available at the end of the phone to come and rescue - thankfully, we didn't have to call upon them but we were in no doubt that they would have been there). Breakfast was hearty, best described as a Morrocan continental breakfast of pancakes, a orange (flower?) cake, a sort of a muffin/crumpet with jam, fresh OJ and the best coffee ever all served up in the central courtyard. You could have dinner at the rias, cooked by Bouchra - whilst we decided to try out the food stalls on the square and enjoy the hustle and bustle, some of our fellow guests had supper in and said it was very good. All in all, a great place and well worth a stay for 2-3 nights if you want a taste of real Marrakesh! If you're not vaguely adventurous, then this probably isn't for you (more traditional Western style hotels can be found outside the Medina).

author: PlanetZoey
title: Excellent Service from a Relaxed and Friendly Team
text: We would like to thank John and his staff for their hospitality at the Dar Eliane we stayed there for the first two nights of our week holiday to Morocco and again on the last night. We were spending four nights in the desert. A trip we had planned in are minds but took five years to achieve! John and his staff knew how nervous we were of actually doing it but their kindness, attentiveness and their can do attitudes made our nerves disappear. We now have fantastic memories and photos of our dream trip, and the staff could not wait for us to return for the last night of our stay to tell them what we thought. We had a celebration meal that evening at the Dar Eliane that evening washed down with several glasses of wine in sublime surroundings then we slept like logs. All we can say is that without a doubt it was one of the best holidays we have ever had, and thank you again to the lovely staff at the Dar who made us feel so special while we were there. Will come again, without hesitation! Zoe Wood Brighton UK

author: beccafulcher
title: Beautiful perfection!
text: What an incredible Riad! We have just spent the most amazing 2 days of our lives in Marrakech and cannot rave about the Riad enough. We arranged the taxi with the riad which was definitely recommended as we would never have found it on our own (this cost 100dh). The riad is a beautiful peace of heaven in the middle of the souks – it is decorated in true Moroccan style and the pictures on the website just do not do it justice. We stayed in the beautiful Jawhara twin room which was lovely upstairs. Bouchra and Slemen were amazing hosts and attended to our every needs and were such lovely people. The riad is very easy to get to from the square – its literally 7 mins or so up one street and then a couple of turns so no worries about getting lost. The breakfast we were served again was incredible – far too much for us to possibly eat but beautiful. We will be returning to Marrakech asap and will be staying again at Dar Eliane – pure perfection!

author: The_Gibb0n5
title: Hidden Gem
text: After four nights in the desert we were looking forward to coming back to civilisation, the Dar Eliane was warm and welcoming. After Tom and I had showered we sat by the fire and had the most delicious home cooked tagine a few glasses of wine and an early night. The next day after breakfast we ventured out in to the souks, the noise and chaos was a world away from the Dar Eliane we were amazed, we did get carried away with the idea of buying so much stuff but thank goodness we came to our senses! What a nightmare it would have been trying to get it all home. We had coffee and some freshly cooked crepes whilst we were out and they were delicious, and then wandered back to the house with our souvenirs. That evening we went to the square I have never seen so many people it was incredible it’s like a free circus full of jugglers and acrobats and my goodness there were some real characters to be seen. You can eat in the square but we would not be brave enough, we were not sure what was being cooked on the open fires in big caldrons! Bouchra had asked if we would like evening meals that evening I am so glad we had said yes. Our last night in Marrakech was perfect the staff were really helpful as we decided to eat out that evening and we did not have a clue where to go John gave us a good idea of different types of cuisines we could expect as well as a rough idea of how much it would cost, and we were absolutely delighted with our choice and the icing on the cake was Sleiman came and met us at the end of our evening and walked us back to the house where we had a few drinks (remember the Medina is dry) then we retired to bed as we had an early flight the next day. Sophie_London

author: tonks28
title: Wonderful
text: I haven't really got a great deal to add to the other reviews, as this is a great place to stay. The rooms are really unique - the Riad experience is so much more enjoyable than the standard chain hotel. We stayed in Jawhara room which is on the 1st floor and has a balcony to the bathroom - not recommended for those who are conscious of privacy as popping to the loo in your nightie was in full view of anyone in the riad!! I definitely was glad to be upstairs though as the two downstairs rooms open out into the courtyard and in my view were less private. The location has to be mentioned - I was under the impression that taxis could get to the riad - how wrong I was! The entrance is down a tiny little alley (derb) which then leads to one of the narrow streets of the souk - plenty of bikes and donkeys but not wide enough for cars. It is actually quite easy to find with the helpful map provided by Sleman, about 10 minutes walk from the main square through the souks. All in all, this riad is great value, in a great location and hghly recommended.

author: Mancun1an
title: Excellent
text: We stayed for 4 nights at Dar Eliane and had an absolutely wonderful visit. The Ryad is in a perfect location only a short walk from the centre of the medina in Marrakech. The first thing I noticed was the contrast from the bustle and noise of the medina. The staff are wonderful and really make you feel at home while taking care of your every need. The location is great, and the house is very comfortable and relaxing. The rooms are very colourful and big with a good ambiance. I would completely recommend it as it's great to have such a nice calm place to return to after touring the often hectic streets of Marrakech. We did a tour of the city and a trip to the mountains that we arranged with the Ryad and both were very enjoyable. JPR Manchester

author: HappyTravell3r
title: Peaceful Oasis
text: Dar Elaine is just 10 minutes walk to Djeema Fina through an open market and colourful souks. The riad is charming, calm and peaceful which is welcoming after a day of walking through the busy medina. Great place to relax in between Marrakesh adventures. Bacha and John who run the place are really nice and approachable. The house and rooms are decorated beautifully, the only thing I didn't like was the polyester/satin sheets which was hot and uncomfortable for sleeping. The air conditioning does ease the discomfort although it was hard for me to get a good nights sleep. Breakfast is simple, a french stick cut up with butter and jam & a piece of pastry, Coffee and Orange juice. Overall the place is nice although I think I don't think it's the best value for money comparing with some other places I stayed in Morocco.

author: Sp00kyT00th
title: Pure Oasis
text: This riad is perfect for anybody who would prefer to avoid the big hotel chains in the new city of Marrakech. The whole riad is very highly decorated and well furnished; each room has their own bathroom and air-conditioning. The staff are excellent, the food was of high quality and nothing was too much trouble. The riad is centrally located in the Medina very close to the Jemma El Fna.well placed for sightseeing, restaurants and the souks, to begin I would recommend the horse and carriage ride around the city this helps you to get an understanding of your bearings. You will find that most people will not speak English; fluent French is a big advantage in Marrakech. The Jemma El Fna in the evening is a must with its array of acrobats, snake chamers, storytellers, singers and dancers and the seemly endless stalls with their delicacies. The riad is a pure oasis and at the end of each day it was relaxing to be back inside its four walls away from the madness of the medina. We would recommend this riad and we certainly plan to return. J Foster Nottinghamshire

author: susie-nyc
title: Worth every Dirham
text: The location was awesome the service was fantastic and the staff were great, eager to help in any way without being overbearing. I found there English to be Ok although there second language after Arabic is French. The rooms were clean, colourful and exceptional well furnished, each corner with its own charm. The roof terrace offered a fabulous view the Koutoubia Mosque and the Atlas Mountains. The breakfast was really cool with coffee, breads, jams, yogurt, cheeses, and eggs. We were informed by some other guests there that the evening meal was a must and Boushra the chef did not let us down. I have already recommended this place to friends going out in the fall and will continue to do so. Sue NYC

author: thomas654
title: A delightful little jewel
text: The entrance to the riad is off Rue de Azbezt, a very busy and dusty street, but pretty much everything is close to hand, the riad is friendly, clean and quiet. Bouchra cooked a very nice dinner for our first evening which we enjoyed with a bottle of Moroccan red wine. Bouchra also arranged and escorted us to a wonderful Hammam the following day which was just off the main square. We visited the Majorelle gardens which were once owned by Yves St Laurent the French fashion designer an experience not to be missed for its beauty and tranquillity. The many different sounds and aromas in the Jemma El Fna square at night are over whelming and it’s a great place to go for a cheap evening meal and to watch the many street performers. I must admit I did not feel comfortable haggling in the souks but the manager Badr was on hand too help me out with a few items. This is a delightful little riad, with a decent service in comparison to the usual Moroccan standards, Overall I would recommend it to anyone. Thomas, South Wales

author: flyboyarl
title: Beautiful retreat from the madness
text: The riad is very beautifully and intricately appointed, in the public spaces and in the rooms. We stayed in both the Jawhara and the room on the first floor. Even though Jawhara is the bigger room upstairs, we actually liked the downstairs better because of the connected bathroom, though the downstairs is a bit louder because it's right next to the courtyard where the breakfasts are held. The decorations in both rooms are amazing, giving you a feeling of being in a Moroccan palace. It was a great retreat from the craziness that is the souks and Jemaa El Fna Square, though it was about a 10 minute walk away. Bader and the staff were very attentive and always willing to help, whether it's to get a cart guy to come get your luggage, recommend restaurants, arrange drivers, and a friendly face when you run into them while wandering the souks. The only downside would be the dark alley you have to go through to get to the riad. Unfortunately, I think this seems to be common for riads so just be prepared.

author: JimfromIreland
title: Don't think of going anywhere else
text: We stayed in 4 Riads/Hotels while traveling in Morocco. They were all good but this one was truly exceptional. The staff are friendly and very helpful - they went out of their way to be assist with bookings/travel etc. and were very hospitable and acommodating. The Riad is gorgeous. A beautiful house has ben restored with real style and the result is perfect - very stylish but very comfortable. There is a lovely courtyard, beautiful rooms and to top it all a fantastic roof terrace. At first effort it seems hard to find but you soon get used to it and it is well worth the effort.

author: dorothypincheng
title: A peice of heaven with out the heavy cost.
text: I must say that I have been to a lot of Hotels in Marrakech and there are a selected few that I have fully enjoyed staying in, this being one of them. Once you walk in to this delightful building, first thing that hits you is the freshness of the place as though it had just been opened. The service is second to none, the décor are just beautiful with every corner you turn just reminds you that you are on a lovely vacation far far away. The place just jumps out with class and it feels that the owner has really spent over the odds to make this place a holiday not to be forgotten. The rooms are clean crisp and airy with much natural day light coming through. The toilets are again like new as though you are the first visitor ever. My favourite place must be the terrace, it’s a wonderful place especially at night with stars glowing above you, and you really do feel like you are in heaven. I come from Hong Kong and you will never enjoy a moment of pureness and its delight that Dar Eliane offers, it's so nice to get away from the busy hassle and bustle, it’s a real retreat which I will tell all my friends and family about. This place is a must, yes you may find better hotels and larger ones but you’ll be paying the odds for it, besides, smaller places you get the attention and quietness you want and exploring the towns and that’s what a exotic hotel place is all about, getting away to your own comforable space and this place does it for me.

author: sirrajk
title: Cool Riad
text: We have just returned from Morocco,and had a great time. This is a great riad if you book 3 or 4 rooms for your family or group. The decor is fantastic making use of all the traditional Moroccan furnishings. The Riad is located down a couple narrow alleyways with locals living either side which gives the fealing you are living like a Marrakechi person. It is near some of the major cultural attractions in Marrakech. The staff are wonderfull and seem to disappear when you don't need them making you feel like the place is your own. Breakfasts were nice with speacial treats for the little one's and something different everyday. We had to put up with the heat in July but the rooms were naturally cool and the aircon made them perfect after working up a sweat in the heat of the Madina. The Kara family Leicester U K

author: lexlimbu
title: An Oasis amidst the Madness
text: You can get a taxi from the Supratours bus station however it is better if you tell them to come pick you up as cars arent able to get right to the hotel. Dont take a lot of baggage as the taxi will be parked in a small square then you will have to walk for another 10 minutes down the alleys which is very Marrakech and you'll see people smiling on the way and selling stuff. Once you get deep into the different passages you'll see a single door and you'll regret booking into Dar Eliane however once the door opens and you are greeted you'll feel as if your in a different world as the Dar Eliane is beautiful in achitecture and has got many nice light colours. The team there are wonderful and they will also assist you to the main square and the souks. If you think you'll be ripped off badly then take them with you. Our room was amazing with nice windows, cieliengs and designs, there were two sinks and a nice authentic moroccan style shower. The riad has a lounge where you can order drinks, smoke seesha, watch movies and they have few DVD's however you can also bring your own dvd's. The breakfast in the morning is lovely and go on the terrace to soak up some sun oh and even though they dont have a swimming pool they have a nice air cooler in the room and theyll also provide maps for the square.

author: Miles-Perryman
title: Wow Factor
text: Amazing place to stay. We found this on Trip Advisor, thought it looked right for us, and it was. Booked direct with the owner at , we felt, a reasonable rate and couldn't wait to get there. As mentioned by others, the approach could be a little foreboding to some, but we had no problems navigating to and from, day and night. Set around a bright courtyard, the two storey accommodation is well presented and traditionally furnished; our first floor room was colourful and exactly as we had hoped for; certainly had the wow factor. We opted for a traditional meal in on our first night, served by the extremely friendly and helpful staff, Bouchra and Badre, and were very impressed with the tagine of honeyed lamb with prunes and apricots with walnuts amongst other local fare. We found the main square an easy ten minute walk and the property is well placed for other nearby sights such as the Medersa Ben Youssef which is well worth a visit. Dar Eliane was a great place to escape from the "madness" ,and to be able retreat to the Riad for instant peace and quiet, the only noise coming from birds nesting in the courtyard area, was wonderful. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

author: Seemore_G
title: Wonderful Dar Eliane
text: We (four couples) exclusively rented the Dar Eliane for a short break. Even before we arrived we had plenty of helpful advice from the owners - a good omen! The riad is a beautiful oasis of calm in the hustle and bustle of the medina. It does take a little walk to reach as it is right in the heart of the souks, but our helpful taxi driver (booked through the riad) walked us the whole way, managing to get a local to transport our luggage in his cart to the riad. We all had a tour of the four rooms before choosing our own. Each had its own character and all were decorated to a high standard. Nothing was too much trouble for Badr and Bouchra throughout our stay. Badr, the manager, even walked us across the old city to an excellent restaurant, so we didn't get lost. If you would like to be in the heart of the souks and markets, we would all highly recommend the riad as a great base to explore old Marrakesh.

author: ukpat02
title: There couldn't be a better riad
text: I sincerely wish I could convey how wonderful my stay at the Dar Eliane was with words. I've traveled all over the world and am fairly positive that I haven't encountered such a friendly staff that would go out of their way to make my stay in their city so pleasant. Bader and Boushra are truly wonderful people who everyone must meet. From Boushra continuously calling the airport to check on our lost bags to Bader taking me on his scooter to the hammam and finding me safety pins when I really needed them, they both truly bent over backwards to make our trip to the Dar Eliane memorable. The Djemma al-Fnaa isn't exactly easy to find on your first trip out, but once you figure that out (and it really doesn't take long) it's about an 8 minute walk, which isn't bad at all. Bader is also there to help you arrange hammam visits, taxi rides and day trips to the High Atlas. All in all, location is wonderful, the staff is world-class, and Marrakech is a gem of a city. If you're planning a trip to Marrakech, include the Dar Elaine in your plans.

author: Jasby
title: beautiful riad but freezing cold
text: We stayed at Dar Eliane in december. The riad has been beautifully renovated with attention to detail. The food is delicious and is good value. We were in a downstairs room - rather dark and no privacy. There was a very bad smell early in the morning, I think it came up the drain in the shower. The heating, though advertised, was out of order so we were freezing cold. The riad is in a dangerous area. Taxi drivers don't want to take you there. One driver left us with some youths who then threatened and abused us. I would not recommend this riad to women travellers.

author: LoinerLoiner
title: Oasis of Calm in the mania of the Medina
text: Our stay at this Riad was really good. In all honesty, Marrakesh was a tad too hectic for us, but Dar Eliane was an oasis of calm. The standard of the accommodation is good, probably equivalent to an top-end B&B in the UK, rather than hotel. The staff could not have been more helpful - they collected us from the little square where the taxi from the airport stopped. Be aware that this Riad is really in the heart of the Medina - you will be dragging your stuff through the tiny, narrow lanes. The Riad is down a dark little alleyway, but if you can get past the initial assault on your senses, the homely welcome of Dar Eliane will be worth it. We thoroughly recommend eating here during your stay. The salads and tagines were better than a very expensive restaurant that is recommended in all the guides. Brilliant value for money.

author: Steve5392
title: A good stopover hotel
text: We have stayed here three times now. The first time it took some finding for the sat nav but once you know where it is it's straightforward. On our first stay the hotel was only a year or so old and now three years later it looks just the same - clean, tidy, well maintained and pleasant staff. This is a typical budget hotel format offering simple en suite rooms and a good buffet breakfast. It is on the side of the river and next to the International freight centre but don't be put off by that. There is a simple restaurant next door but it is not always open. We have eaten at Au Peita just down the road towards Bayonne and it has been good. On our trips we stay at all range of hotels from those in unique locations and with good restaurants and high prices to this one which meets our needs perfectly before a days drive to Salamanca. We will definitely return on our next trip through the area.

author: YorkshirePair
title: Great hotel but tricky to find
text: My only criticism of this lovely new hotel is that it is difficult to find. On an industrial estate it certainly gave our sat nav a run for it's money! That aside the hotel is new, well presented and welcoming. The rooms are clean, comfortable and well appointed. The staff friendly and helpful. As we were there in December we were pleased to find the room warm. Breakfast was very good with a wide choice of dishes. Parking outside was no problem. Highly recommended!

author: karlheinzs421
title: Very Basic, but worth the money
text: Booked on short notice on a tour with my convertible through the French Alpes and along the Côte D´Azur, my aim was to find good midrange room in the center of the village/city with a locked garage or parking area for my (valuable) car. The last was the hardest to evaluate on my daily search, therefore I highlight this point. Adonis has no Garage, but a own parking area. As well the public parking space in front of the hotel is ok - at least it was at my time, which was in low season. The hotel itself is very basic as well as the breakfast. Normally I am looking for more, but for one night it was ok. From a value for money perspective it was good. Remark:In low season it is hard to find a open restaurant in the evening.

author: CauzIsaid
title: Quaint cabins
text: These cabins are quaint & away from Sedonas busy area. It was surprising the noise level at cabin 10. You could hear the cars on the highway until about 1am. The water in Oak Creek was rushing & would have been so soothing vs cars all night. Other cabins may be different. There is a transition strip from the carpet to flooring towards the bathroom in bare feet in need of repair. Since it's a cabin wasnt expecting much, mattress was too firm, chair arm was ripped. Small upgrades would be suggested at $200 per night would make this a really great stay.

author: FancyFree1
title: The Butterfly Inn came to our rescue
text: My son and I have just returned from Sedona. There was an incident with our car at 5am one morning and we well and truly stuck. The Butterfly Inn, namely Frank, the owner, and Tamara came to our rescue. They didn't know us as we were UK travellers just passing through. However, I will go back and stay in one of their cabins. Their kindness, friendliness and sincerity turned our misfortune into an adventure. We are truly grateful for their generosity and warmth. By the way, their cabins look great! Sue and Robert

author: kerri2019
title: A Cozy Getaway
text: This was our second time staying at the Butterfly Garden Inn. It was just a relaxing as we remembered it. Both times we visited in December. We stayed in Cabin #11 - one of the smaller cabins, but it had everything we needed for a romantic weekend away. We love that it is a separate cabin and you can't hear others through the walls. The gas burning stove adds to the coziness of the cabin. The cabin was cutely decorated and clean, the staff was great and the food was delicious. The Cuban Burger is the best burger we have ever tasted. When we return to Sedona, we will definitely be staying at the Butterfly Garden Inn!

author: kenjacobsen
