title: Best Back-to-Nature Lodging in the Area
text: These are really great historic cabins built maybe in the 1940s, which gives them the real cabin-in-the-woods feel that's hard to find in this area and impossible to fake. They've been perfectly maintained, furnished and updated in keeping with their character and without getting frou-frou or "modernized" with, say, hot tubs or giant TVs. In fact, there's no TV or phone at all, which is perfect. (Although I admit I was happy to have cellphone reception and wifi there. I'm not THAT 'back to nature' when staying near Sedona.) What one ridiculously disgruntled reviewer called a "smelly river" is actually beautiful Oak Creek, which runs on the Inn's property right across the road and worth a wander in itself, not to mention the West Fork of Oak Creek just down the road. And the little shop the Inn runs is really handy as well. And the price wasn't too high either. Five stars!

author: 190sherylr
title: Family reunion destination
text: The cabins are cute, and the staff is very friendly. I rented 5 cabins for a family reunion. One cabin had no fridge, no microwave, or coffee pot and it was the same price as ones that had those items and were newly remodeled. So the couple that chose that cabin for the name Morning Glory and were disappointed to say the least after seeing everyone else's cabins. So if you are planning a group rental, please verify that beforehand. All cabins should be equal if the price is in my opinion. There are no trails or places to explore on foot except their garden area, and the smelly river across the street. We had to travel into Sedona to hike and bike. The cabins were clean, and the surroundings really beautiful, the perfect place if you just want to relax and not explore too much.

author: X2008XJnicolel
title: Disappointed this time and won't be back
text: This was our 3rd trip to butterfly garden inn. We looked so forward to going in the winter since our previous visit were closer to the summer and with no ac we were to warm (we like to sleep on the cool side). Unfortunately they discontinued the baskets breakfast which was one of the main reasons we returned. When we prepaid for our stay it wasn't explained that they would not have it anymore. Unfortunately we got an email approx.a week before our trip that it would be included we could have a $10 credit for breakfast at the restaurant. The other major issue was the heater didn't work in one of the bedroom's the first night and no where in the cabin was there any extra blankets. The cabins need some tlc because they are older but with the little extras you recieved prior to the changes you could over look them somewhat. Unfortunately now we will just find another hide away.

author: macotak
title: Great Refuge and Great Little Cabin!
text: We spent a couple of nights in cabin 11 for my wife's birthday. Bad news is that we forgot that the week after Easter was still spring break and Sedona was a nightmare for traffic and throngs of people. Couldn't even get to any of the trail heads it was so crowded! Great news is that we holed up in our cabin for the whole time and enjoyed some very welcome down time and peace. Had nice walks along their 10 acres of riverfront as well, saw lots of trout. We also ate all of our meals there so we were very happy. Very accommodating hosts and staff. Cute, comfortable little cabin, and we did connect to the internet from the cabin.

author: jannettebohlman
title: Weekend trip with grandkids
text: We loved our stay at the Butterfly Garden Inn. The owner Frank is amazing, so gracious and accommodating! He helped us with special surprises for the kids. They welcome children unlike some of the other places we stayed in the area. We loved the special picnic baskets in the morning, more than enough to start your day. The swimming hole is private and beautiful. Can not wait to plan our next trip! Thank you for such a special weekend with our grands!

author: lisapM9043LD
title: You Won't Want to Go Home
text: I chose The Butterfly Garden Inn because they serve breakfast at each cabin, but I enjoyed my stay for many reasons. The bed was comfortable and the room was very clean. I brought 2 small dogs with me and stayed in a pet friendly cabin. The grounds were a great place for us to stroll. Of course, Oak Creek Canyon is absolutely gorgeous. I hiked West Fork Trail which is 1/2 mile north. Bathroom counter space was limited in my cabin and I chose a cabin without a kitchen. I found the setting very relaxing. Cabin tips: Some cabins will get better WiFi signal due to proximity to lobby.

author: kalibaker
title: Perfect getaway in Oak Creek Canyon
text: After 3 wonderful nights at the Butterfly Garden Inn, I didn't want to leave. The cabins are immaculate and stocked with everything you could possibly need. The bed and linens were luxurious. I have a hard time with the smell of strong cleaning and laundry solutions used in many places - but not here. The location was quiet and secluded - the perfect setting for a relaxing getaway. A gas fire waiting for me after a long, chilly hike was so cozy. And breakfast delivered right outside your door with freshly baked goods was refreshing. I'll definitely be back.

author: elkenwood
title: A Utopia Away from the crowds......
text: I happened upon this Inn while driving south on 89A from Flagstaff. What a find and pet friendly too. I was lucky, I call it providence, that Cabin #16, Dreamy Duskywing, was available. I loved my stay so much that I never made it to the convention I was supposed to attend in Phoenix. Breakfast was delivered in a picnic basket every morning. Nefertiny was over joyed that the basket included treats for her as well. We sat alfresco at our own picnic table and not only nourished our bodies with food, but also our souls with the fresh air and forest sounds. Hands down, one our favorite places to escape. We plan to return October 2017.

author: Y699YKkathyh
title: Exceptional experience
text: We celebrated our anniversary here. The cabins were clean, quaint, and quiet. The service was excellent-our baskets had slate covers with personal messages to us each day. The baskets contained yummy baked goods baked on the premises. The cookies in the market were to die for. This place is a labor of love for the owners and it shows at every turn. No detail was left out. Anything we needed they found it. We will definitely be back, hopefully sooner than later. Thank you for a wonderful weekend, Kathy & Mike.

author: AimeeLally
title: My new favorite place!
text: I can't say enough good things about this place! We plan on making this trip an annual family tradition. AMAZING breakfasts baked goods in a cute picnic basket presentation with other breakfast goodies await you on your porch when you wake up. Clean and comfortable cabins. The property is beautiful and set up in a way where my kids just ran wild and explored and made friends with the other guest kids and had a blast. The creek access is private property so it's not crowded. I LOVE this place! Know before you go though, no AC. We slept with the windows open at night with a fan that they provided and it wasn't too bad.

author: BernieM159
title: Comfy cabins just north of Sedona!
text: Sedona can be hot, crowded, noisy and expensive - not what we look for. Butterfly Garden Inn (cabins, actually) is cool, calm, quiet and very, very reasonable. Rosita Patch, our two- bedroom cabin (small house, really) was very comfortable, very clean and had all the necessary kitchen equipment. The general store has everything you need (except produce, which is to be expected). There isn't a restaurant, but there is a take-out menu which has excellent breakfast, lunch and salads available 7 am to 5 pm - delivered to your cabin! Very easy to get to the picnic areas and creekside pullouts along Oak Creek Canyon and just a few miles north of Slide Rock State Park. The staff is friendly and very helpful. Love the place and will definitely return!

author: 504lynne
title: First Class Cabin
text: Thanks to all the great Trip Advisor reviews on the Butterfly Garden Inn, we stayed four nights with our family of four and loved it! Wish we would have spent the whole week there instead of going to Phoenix. We enjoyed having the rustic charm of a cabin with the amenities of a first class hotel. The beds were comfortable, the sheets and towels, crisp and white. We loved looking forward to what would be in our morning picnic basket. The kids enjoyed just hanging out on the property and the creek across the street. The quality of items at the Inn's little market was amazing. Frank the Innkeeper was super friendly and accommodating. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this gem to anyone.

author: marsmomaz
title: Weekend getaway
text: Love, love, love! Sweet cozy cabins north of Sedona. Super clean, well maintained, friendly staff. Early morning breakfast baskets hung by the door, filled with variety of fruit, yogurt parfait, homemade rolls, scones, hard boiled eggs. General store on property with cafe, we didn't get to try, but heard great things about the sandwiches. We already made plans to stay again. Try to get a cabin towards the back to be further from the road noise. If not its cozy enough that it really didn't matter. Thanks for a great weekend!

author: dakotam668
title: Great location, beautiful area, lots of accomodations
text: I think this was a wonderful location to stay. The check in process with the owner was very nice, he was very nice and was very comforting. Having a cafe and a small grocery store provided all of the resources needed, including being able to pick up a bottle of wine and some delicious food. The free breakfast provided for each cabin was wonderful, almost too much food being provided which was wonderful. I did say this does not have wifi in the room, because though it exists in the lounge it does not necessarily reach all cabins. My cabin was able to use it to very slowly run netflix, but I would guess another cabin out might not work at all! But overall the cabin was beautiful, provided everything I needed, very close to both Sedona and Flagstaff, had a beautiful creek. I truly think this was amazing, and I would definitely return here if I ever come back to Sedona.

author: DdelliottazE
title: So good, we came back within 4 months!
text: We visited Butterfly Garden Inn in June and October of 2015 with our little Jack Russell terrier Lucy. The cabins for dogs were cleaner than most "human" places we've visited! We stayed in cabins #6 and #17, and both were spotless and comfortable. This is the perfect location to hike West Fork (which can be difficult to get into due to its popularity) . It's wonderful to wake up in the morning to a fabulous basket of breakfast and baked goods. And on our second visit, instead of driving into town for dinner, we had dinner from the tasty restaurant right on the grounds! You need to order by 6:00pm, but I believe the food is better than most of the restaurants in town. So for a truly relaxing, quiet experience, bring your best friend (dog) and enjoy the hospitality, food and great cabins. I'm sure we'll be back!

author: akinakanish
title: BED BUGS - don't take a chance!
text: If you're thinking of staying at the Butterfly Garden Inn, think twice. My boyfriend and I were lured in by the awesome guest reviews regarding tasty picnic basket pastries and cozy cabins, none of which was worth being ravaged by BED BUGS for $200 / night, and our unbearably itchy, red-welted faces being simply dismissed by the inn's owner. We were eaten alive by bed bugs in the master bedroom of cabin 5. Aside from the countless bites that appeared all over our bodies overnight, and the telltale signs of small blood streaks (tip: looks like dark ink stains) on the sheets, we actually found a dead bed bug among the sheets as well. When we reported the bed bug incident to the owner of Butterfly Garden Inn, he was very dismissive, insisting that the cabin had been inspected for bed bugs just recently. In the same breath, he accused us of bringing in the bed bugs in our luggage. Untrue, unprofessional, and totally unacceptable behavior! He moved us to different cabins (cabin 11 & 12), but refused to acknowledge the pest infestation or compensate us in any way for our utterly miserable guest experience.

author: 773kevinh
title: Fantastic burger! Possibly the best!
text: We stayed once at these quaint little cabins and were impressed with the cute well stocked little store on-site. They had a menu of sandwiches and burgers, but did not seem to have a kitchen so no way we were gonna try anything. Then I saw other reviews and we made a special trip. So glad! The cashier radioed our order (which took a while, but we didn't mind) and a chef brought us the thickest burger I've eaten. We ordered it to share and ordered it well done. It was perfect, although I don't know how he pulled it off since it was so thick. The actual meat was so great that my wife cautiously said that it was the best burger she's ever had. I believe Harrys Hideaway in Cornville is still the best, but this was a close runner up. The table next to us got pizzas which they said were great!

author: JaclynnDodge
title: This place was amazing!
text: My husband and I planned an anniversary trip to Arizona and had stayed a few different places the nights before arriving here and this was definitely the best out of all of them. The owners were both so sweet, friendly, and professional. You can really tell how much effort they put into the place. The cabin was super clean and comfortable. The property was well maintained and beautiful. I was so excited for the breakfast basket in the morning and when I opened it I was so surprised at how much work they put into it and how great everything tasted. We were sad to leave and are really looking forward to returning. I recommend this place to everyone!

author: jmh88
title: Butterfly garden inn
text: Amazing place to stay. Cabins impeccable. Food amazing. Views don't get better. Staff amazing. The grounds are beautiful and neat and clean. Best place I've ever stayed in Sedona. 15 min north of town. Away from hustle and bustle. The owners are super cool.

author: DawnM160
title: Charming Cabins in Gorgeous Oak Creek Canyon
text: This is a lovely property with charming cabins tucked in among the trees. We stayed in the 3 bedroom Blue Eyed Sailor, which was comfortable, clean and nicely decorated. The kitchen was well-equipped and the free breakfast that was delivered each morning was terrific. We also loved the small on-site market, the lounge with board games and the stunning location on Oak Creek Canyon. It would have been handy to have wireless coverage in the cabins but it was really only available in the lounge. Since there is zero cell service in the canyon, it was tough making plans with some friends at another resort nearby without wireless. On the other hand, the Inn does provide a free phone booth for use, which is a nice touch. A wonderful place to stay!

author: Rrrrrrrrr2014
title: Great Place, Great Innkeepers!
text: I love this little place, seems like each visit hooks me a little more. This is such a charming set of cabins, they have all the nice rustic feel on the outside and all the nice soft touches inside. Inn Keepers are so nice and treat you as friends, they make you feel as you are very welcome and not just another person checking in. I love the market they have, a little bit of everything at a decent price! We enjoyed one of the yummy sandwiches the Market Café makes and enjoyed it outside on our picnic table by the cabin. Frank and Nicole have a great wealth of knowledge about Sedona and can guide you with whatever you may want to do. They offer a great hiking map and give you creek towels to use for the day! They also have a great little lounge with tons of games to enjoy! Love the Butterfly Garden Inn, counting the days till I go again!

author: Namaskaramleela
title: If You're Looking For A Five Star Stay You've Set Your Sights Too Low!
text: The Butterfly Garden Inn is definitely 10 star. The Butterfly Garden Inn created an experience beginning with what seemed like the holiday homecoming in a Maxwell House Coffee commercial to really sleeping in John Denver's "Grandma's Feather Bed." The cabin, ours vintage log, was warm, welcoming and cozy while being nestled in Mother Nature's Oak Creek Canyon. Our nights were filled with starry skies ....days with quiet sunrises and clean, crisp air.....and a bountiful breakfast at our door! We could not have asked for more. A last minute cancellation notice from another booking made this stay possible. We were the lucky ones. Why not you? We will be back very soon.

author: X1791QKrobertg
title: DON'T Book with this place
text: Staff is rude and they lie. There is a serious mosquito problem. I was over charged. When you go on vacation you don’t need someone lying to so they can make a little extra money. We all work hard for our money. We all would like to have more time for vacation. Don’t make a wreck out of the vacation little time you do get. Stay away from this lady BAD news.

author: downy2015
title: Lovely rustic and romantic cabins
text: Spent 2 nights here on a trip to Sedona. Seriously, avoid downtown Sedona and its boring hotels and go straight here. It's out of the traffic, quiet and peaceful. There is excellent hiking nearby at the west fork at Oak Creek and the grounds are located right in the mountains. We woke to the sounds of birds chirping after a night of sleeping by a warm fire (that automatically turns on when it's cold) and some wine. Then breakfast was delivered in the morning in an adorable picnic basket. It was like something out of a Disney movie! This is the ultimate romantic spot and the rooms are cozy, clean and rustic. I wish I could have stayed longer. There is everything you need on site with a restaurant, general store and picnic tables.

author: spurgec
title: too bad you dont offer more than 5 stars
text: don't let rustic surroundings or cabin living scare you. This is a first class operation. great detail spent on ALL aspects of the business. Breakfast was awesome, plenty of food. The cabins were exceptionally clean. So glad we were away from the "uptown Sedona" as we found that part of town to be unnecessarily tourist trap. Only comment would be for better wifi in cabins. I don't mind no TV but I would have spent more time in cabin with the wifi. It was nice to use the lounge but not always as comfortable as your own living area.

author: AQgreytgrl
title: Owners couldn't be more friendly and helpful!
text: I was looking for a secluded place that would be within close proximity of Sedona that also accepted dogs on a solo road trip I took from NY. And the Butterfly Garden Inn was exactly that: within 10 miles of Sedona, but in the beautiful and scenic Oak Creek Canyon. I could have stayed here my whole trip, since there are great trails just across the road from the cabin. The owners, the Garrisons, couldn't be more friendly. They were always around to say hello, and to make sure my stay was absolutely wonderful. The best part of staying at the Butterfly Garden Inn: the homemade breakfasts in a picnic basket delivered to your door first thing every morning. I will definitely be staying there again the next time I go to northern Arizona. You will not be sorry if you choose stay here!

author: Cooking_With_Wolfes
title: Amazing Stay
text: I cannot say enough good things about the Butterfly Garden Inn. Not only was the setup and actual rooms extremely nice, but the people who own and work there are some of the nicest ever. Frank gave us great advice for hikes and experiences, and he always went out of his way for us. The rooms were very clean and cozy. The other couple we arrived with stayed in Mimic, and that is quite a cabin. All the cabins are decently spaced for privacy, and the entire place has a nice calm to it. Breakfast was great each morning and always had something new to enjoy. We had to leave early our last day to catch our flight, and Frank packed us up an early breakfast the night before. Again, the thoughtfulness and care of this place makes it one of the best hotels I've ever stayed at.

author: Amanda575
title: Perfect for a family get away
text: We stayed in the very clean, cozy 3 bedroom Cabin #15 with our 3 children. It is right across from the playground with chairs to relax in while you watch your kids play. The Inn has private access to the creek across the street for fishing, swimming, and/or exploring. We loved the basket of fruit, yogurt, muffins, and kid cereal with milk delivered even before the kids woke up. We borrowed 2 board games from the main house to play once it was too dark for the kids to be outside (we were looking for a getaway w/o TV or video games). The market was great to order take out food or to pick up any supplies you might have forgotten. The pizza was delicious (which they delivered to our cabin). I have never taken the time to write a review before, but this place was so great I felt I needed to!

author: spankyangel
title: Cozy Woodsy Corner of Arizona
text: This beautiful little corner of the Oak Creek Canyon has been lovingly restored by the Garrison family. The individual cabins are quaint and cozy, the common area is well-kept and lovely for strolling or playing with your children. No television or telephone suited us perfectly, for those craving a connection to the world Wi-Fi worked pretty well. As others have commented, the lovely breakfast basket with fruit muffins and juice is a delightful way to start the morning, if one has need of specific requests they seem all too happy to accommodate. The little kitchen and store in front of the cabins also produces yummy breakfast lunch and hiking food options. Our only complaint was a Yankee candle scented nightlight that was burning in the room when we arrived, it took us a while to figure out where the sent was coming from both my husband and I are sensitive and felt a headache coming on. if you love Yankee candle scents than this will be great otherwise let them know before you arrive to remove that from the room. We are looking forward to returning and spending more time at the butterfly garden Inn!

author: desertrose52
title: Great Getaway
text: We awoke this morning with a dusting of snow on the ground. But we were warm and cozy in our cabin with the gas fireplace blazing. We are staying in the Cuban Crescent cabin which has a king bed, kitchen, and extra easy chairs. Plenty of room for the two of us! We are awaiting our daily breakfast basket of goodies, which is hung outside the door. We ordered burgers for dinner on the day we arrived and they were very tasty. Also, we noticed the Pink Jeep vans stopping by here in the morning for lunch pick-ups for the tour group. With the cold weather, we were not able to use the gas grill outside our cabin. But this is an easy place to bring your own food to cook or just order from the market in front. After a day in the tourist-filled streets of Sedona, Is was a joy to return to this quiet escape in the trees of Oak Creek Canyon

author: AnnYeoh22
title: cozy restaurant and best services ever
text: Pass by this restaurant/ Inn on my way from flagstaff to oak creek canyon/sedona. We stop by to get some quick lunch and hot drink. The staff is unexpectedly helpful and friendly. She even help us to cut the burger we order ( just one burger since we had late bfast), and gave us extra fries ( as the fries looks a lot to me). She brought us to the hall which is warmer and we even get to watch TV when we had lunch! Highly recommended to take their Inn or even drop by if u pass by! Feel warm in cold winter! :)

author: hillbsand
title: Pristine, peaceful, and perfect!!!
text: For years, while passing through Oak Creek Canyon to get to Sedona, I have wanted to stay in the beautiful area. When my husband and I decided to go on an Arizona trip, and stay in Oak Creek Canyon, my search for a cabin started. After reducing my list based on price, look, and reviews, I finally settled on The Butterfly Garden Inn. When all I could find was one so-so review, that still couldn’t say anything bad about the place, I decided this was the place for us. I was not disappointed! It really, really is the place for us. Not only is it spotlessly clean but it is extremely comfortable and just what we were looking for. The owners, Frank and Nicole, couldn’t be kinder and more helpful. We enjoyed our stay immensely and will definitely return!

author: Anne_from_Ohio
title: Customer Service Oriented and Great Sandwiches
text: We stopped in here to buy a picnic lunch enroute to the West Fork hiking trail in Oak Creek Canyon (coming up from Sedona, it is on the right). We discovered a very friendly convenience store that also offered upscale sandwiches made-to-order. We both got wraps and they were stuffed with lots of meat and other goodies for about $10 each. The sandwiches were served with crispy, perfectly fried home-made potato chips. With a couple sodas and some fruit, we had an ideal picnic. After our hike, we stopped back in here and got a home-made cookies and apple tart. Both of these baked goods were absolutely excellent and freshly made that day. I definitely recommend the Butterfly Garden Inn.

author: RZTR
title: Stopped for lunch
text: We stopped here for lunch while traveling through Sedona and Oak Creek Canyon. I had the Fancy Schmancy Salad that had feta, dried cranberries and olives in it. It was very good. My husband had a big juicy burger with fries. He said the burger and fries were very good also. (I had a few fries and they were delicious!) They also had bottles of wine available if you wish to have a drink with your meal. It is a very casual setting. You place your order in the small market and then they prepare the food and bring it out to you. We sat at the tables that were outside on the lawn. It is a beautiful setting in Oak Creek Canyon.

author: 391kellyg
title: Happy Honeymooners
text: I first found the Butterfly Garden Inn early last spring and we tried to get away then. Instead, we decided to use it for our honeymoon in Sedona. We LOVED it!! The cabins were adorable and incredibly clean. The king bed in our room was so comfy that we slept for 11 hours straight and we hadn't done that in over a year. We enjoyed sitting out under the stars in the evening and looked forward to finding out what breakfast treats were in our picnic baskets each morning. It was delightful to be able to visit and hike in Sedona and come back each afternoon to the cabins. We definitely will be back.

author: tomnmo
title: sedona get away
text: We came two years in a row and savored the atmosphere, the peace and quiet. Took some exhilarating hikes. Enjoyed the delightful couple who own and run the Cabins. This year we are taking our whole family and renting 5 cabins for a long weekend. We can't wait! When you get to the Butterflly Garden Inn, you can stop....... and breath.... and relax........ The best kept secret in Arizona!

author: rd628
title: Enjoyed our lunch
text: We stopped by just for lunch and it did not disappoint. We had burgers and they were AMAZING. They were huge, flavorful, moist, tender burgers with fresh delicious toppings and buns. Made to order, gourmet, perfect burgers. The fries were wonderful, seasoned with coarse ground salt and pepper. We ate in the shade of beautiful overhanging trees on a grassy lawn. A lovely experience. If you have the chance to enjoy a meal here, don't miss it! (The menu offered several other appetizing options... I hope to return!)

author: tuin
title: Amazing setting.
text: I had pretty high expectations after reading the reviews on here and to my surprise not only did The Butterfly Garden Inn meet them but it also exceeded them. We were a little disappointed due to the closure of the parks and hiking trails but the setting of the property made up for it. Set on 10 acres of land we were still able to see the creek and enjoy some of the canyon's picturesque views. We stayed in the Cuban Crescent which we came to find out was the original cabin and built in 1929. We had planned to utilize the kitchen for dinner but opted for the offerings of the onsite market. The menu, while small, still offers a good deal of variety. Finally the thing that truly sets his inn apart is the incredible attention to detail and hospitality of the owners. We felt so welcome and hope to be back again soon.

author: anner873
title: Fire no problem
text: We are presently staying at The Butterfly Garden Inn between Sedona and Flagstaff. It is our first time, and I must say it is a pleasant, beautiful retreat for the summer. The fires although devastating to many first responders and some home owners has not destroyed the beauty and tranquility of this place. There are so many places to hike, especially right now in Flagstaff . Sedona is quite hot, but flagstaff is remarkable. The creek has been shut off because of the rains, but it has not posed any problem for us. There is still so much to do and see! I would not recommend canceling or postponing your trip. This is great! So quiet, so pleasant.

author: missyt608
title: Perfect wedding weekend
text: Butterfly Garden Inn was the perfect place to spend numerous days and nights and have my wedding. The grounds were beautifully taken care of. The cabins were clean, cozy, and had everything we needed to cook dinners on site. The homemade breakfasts were to die for (we brought along our dog, and she even had some breakfast treats!) The staff was amazing!!! From the housekeeping to the maintenance staff, everyone was eager to do whatever possible to make sure we had everything we needed. The owners Nichole and Frank were the icing on the cake. They went above and beyond our wildest expectations, and couldn't have asked for a better place to get married. We can't wait for our next visit!!

author: kflat
title: Glad we stayed here
text: This is a great small resort with very friendly owners and I highly recommend staying here. The breakfast that is brought to the door every morning is amazing, lots of homemade goodies, yogurt and granola, fruit, etc. It has a cute store with all the basics and a area to hang out in and play board games, watch TV, try the piano, etc. We stayed in Rosita Patch and it was perfect for us. Loved the kitchen table with benches. Housekeeping was so-so, we had left a couple of dishes in the sink and they cleaned around them and also just left the towels on the couch instead of putting them in the bathroom. Housekeeping was also loud at times and somewhat unprofessional in my humble opinion. Overall, a wonderful place to stay especially with young children.

author: Janinnh
title: Paradise!
text: My husband had driven thru area last year and had stopped at the little market there. The owners were so hospitable and the property so charming that my husband promised to come back when again in Arizona. We had the opportunity again to visit Sedona and our stay was the best part of our trip! A 1905 log cabin with luxury hotel style bed, Keurig etc. almost felt like I was back home in the Maine woods! In the am, they deliver a complimentary picnic basket to our porch with freshly baked muffins, homemade granola, fruit, juices! Perfect escape from the crowded tourism of Sedona. This is what a vacation should be!

author: jingram2014
title: Just what the doctor ordered
text: I stayed in the Shy Yellow cabin a few days ago. I had the most wonderful experience. I called the morning of my stay to see if I could check in early (I was anxious to get out of town). Nicole offered to call me as soon as the cabin was available. I arrived in Sedona around 11am and received a call at 11:30 from Nicole letting me know that it was ready and I was welcome to come and settle in. It was so generous and I was very appreciative. The cabin was cozy, relaxing and hard to leave;) I loved my breakfast waiting for me in the morning, what a treat!!! Thank you to both of you for the hospitality and for the free newspaper on Monday night. I will be back and tell just enough people to keep you busy, but few enough that I can still book a cabin;) Cheers!!!!

author: js353
title: Great Honeymoon location!
text: We stayed at the Butterfly Garden Inn for three nights in October as part of our honeymoon around Arizona. The location is convienient for Sedona activities being right in the Oak Creek Canyon. We stayed in the Julia cabin and it was amazing! Nice and secluded, great comfy bed and cute dinnette area. The couch had gross stains so we avoided using it. We woke up each morning and couldn't wait to see what goodies were in the breakfast picnic basket. The breakfast was hearty enough to last us a morning hike. The staff was very helpful and did a wonderful job maintaining the cabins. I would go back in a hearbeat. In fact, after waking up in boring hotel after boring hotel fighting tour groups for sub-par continental breakfast, I would think about the Butterfly Garden Inn and wonder what would be in the picnic basket!

author: Vacationqueen1111
title: Little bit of heaven..
text: We spent six wonderful days at the Butterfly Garden Inn. We were in the Cabbage White cabin which was a two bedroom cabin. The location of the resort on Oak Creek Canyon is perfect. The grounds are beautiful and besides a little road noise are so peaceful. You can tell by the cleanliness of the cabin and the upkeep of the grounds that the owners take great pride in providing guests with a topnotch experience. Speaking of the owners, they were so friendly and made us feel very welcome. Each morning they would bring us a breakfast basket filled with fruit, juice and delicious homemade baked goods. Our daughter loved trying to catch the "breakfast ninja" each morning. The resort is located about 10 miles out of Sedona but the drive is scenic and never seemed to take long. We enjoyed our stay and plan to return when back in the area.

author: LauriePW
title: We'll be back!
text: The Butterfly Garden Inn is a lovely retreat. You are far from town without being too far. We stayed for three nights in Cabin 7, the Painted Lady. It was so comfortable and inviting and we couldn't wait to see what goodies awaited us in the breakfast basket each morning. The fully stocked kitchen is just that. We grilled and cooked our dinner the last night we were there and it was my favorite meal of the trip. Frank and Nicole are the most genuine hosts I've ever encountered. If you need anything, all you have to do is ask. And don't forget to ask about the Love Lock gate. We added our lock to the gate right before we checked out, so now it's like there is still a part of us at the Butterfly Garden Inn.

author: KarenBluestone
title: Beautiful and cozy place, superb service, great for kids
text: I've been to Sedona 6 or 7 times before with my family and never experienced it quite like I did at the Butterfly. You feel like you're in a cabin far into the mountains, surrounded by beautiful trees and streams. There's a play structure for the kids and even a little reading and board game room in the lobby cabin. The cabins are super clean and bed and linens are very comfortable. The only limitation was the very small bathroom in our cabin, but the roominess of the kitchen and great breakfast in the morning countered that pretty well. Because the kids could roam around and play, my husband and I had more time than usual to just enjoy nature, read, visit with other family members, etc. Slide Rock Park is really close by, too. Great fun for all!

author: TravelBug10292011
title: Peaceful
text: The best place I have ever stayed. on the way there you will get to see the beautiful mountains and off to you right is the Butterfly Garden Inn. Tucked in the back was our cabin Peaceful is all I can say. Waking up wasn't easy so comfortable in the bed I didn't want to leave. For breakfast was fresh fruit an muffins in a cute basket . Needing a great cup of coffee of latte just go to the store in the Lobby the ladies make a nice strong cup , speaking of yummy You HAVE TO TRY FRANKS cookies!!! He makes them every night at 4am and they are still warm and fresh when the store opens. Across the street from the Inn if you walk the path you come to a Stream that you can swim in or just sun bath,you must see this place it's a place to spend a nice afternoon with some friends. The friendless people work there and make you feel like family We will 100% be back to the Inn !!!

author: MissBuzz
title: Awesome Stay!
text: We were in Sedona last December. Family holidays: 3 teens and 4 adults. Our cabin, The Monarch, was perfectly cozy and warm. The morning surprises were the original breakfast delivered at the door. It was our joy to open it and discover what was hiding in the cute basket. We enjoyed also their little communal living room where teens found games while one was looking at his/her email. The owners are young and passionate lodgers, which is reflected in their services, and little touches here and there. It was a pleasure to be their guests and we, my husband and I, have decided to return again in April! It is our first time going back to the same place, a big sign of our satisfaction!

author: Gym_ratte
title: A Fabulous Place to Stay
text: We spent our spring vacation in the Linda cabin. Our teen age daughters like the privacy of having the separate bedroom. The owners were very accommodating and friendly. There is a store on the property that comes in handy when you need something quick. We loved the morning basket of goodies delivered to our cabin. It was always filled with fresh fruit and delicious baked goods. While we were there, we visited the Grand Canyon and many of the Sedona scenic attractions. The Butterfly Garden Inn is a great place to stay.

author: HeatherG542
title: Fantastic Place to stay
text: I have never written a review before but this place was so great that I really wanted to share how wonderful it is. We just returned from a stay in cabin #1, Julia. There was about 8 inches of snow which added to the already amazing beauty of the surroundings. The cabins are cozy with very comfortable beds like you would find in a top hotel and a cozy gas fireplaces. The couple that owns the property are very nice and thoughtful. Each morning there was a picnic basket of wonderful breakfast treats hanging on the porch (I have never has such a fabulous continental breakfast- homemade and delicious) and they were even thoughtful enough to include dog treats for the dog. The immediate area has lots of options for great activities such as visiting Sedona, wine tasting at the Page Springs Winery or a fabulous hike on the West Fork Trail but you could be just as happy staying in the cabin. We will be back.

author: TylerV54
title: Romantic Gem
text: My girlfriend and I just returned from a romantic stay in Cabin #9 at Butterfly Garden to celebrate her birthday. The experience exceeded our expectations. The small one room log cabin was quaint and had a small gas fireplace in the corner. The bedding was extra cushioned and much nicer than that of many high end hotels I've stayed at in the past. The owner's pretty much run every facet of the business from check-in to gracious concierge to the cute, well-stocked general store (they even have wine and cheese). To our surprise they make gourmet coffees to order in the store everyday which was something we hadn't counted on but appreciated (walk across the street to drink your morning coffee on the banks of Oak Creek). It was all in the details for us including the fresh made pastry's (sour cream coffee cake and apple turnovers were delicious!), fruit and juices left in cute little baskets outside our door at 7:00 am every morning. We had a wonderful weekend and more importantly, one that will be remembered:) by Ty and Andrea

author: kcmcg
title: Great little get away
text: We ended up here by accident after driving from Phoenix and expecting to find a place to stay in Sedona (which was booked up). We arrived not knowing what to expect. It is a beautiful little place. Very rustic (in a good way). The rooms are clean, comfortable and quaint. There are no TVs in the room and very little cell service (although there is wireless) which I consider a huge plus when you are staying in such a gorgeous area. They owners are very sweet and made us wonderful coffees before our hike. I would definitely come back and would think that one of the cabins would make a great location for a romantic weekend.

author: LisaR422
title: We could not have asked for a nicer place to stay.
text: My husband and I just returned from a week at the Butterfly Garden Inn. We had such a wonderful time. The cabin we stayed in was so lovely. It was immaculate, the bed was so comfortable and the breakfast that is delivered in a beautiful basket daily was absolutely wonderful. The Garrisons, who are the owners and operators of the property could not have been more accommodating . They made us feel at home the second we arrived. Their is a General Store on the property that has anything you could ever need or want. We highly recommend staying at the Butterfly Garden Inn. It's the perfect place for families as well as just a quiet romantic get away. We will be going back a lot!!

author: 182ginak
title: Very nice stay in Paris
text: We stayed there for Christmas and NYE. The stay was convenient. The hotel is so close to St Lazare Station which is one of the main big stations in Paris. It is also minutes walking from Printemps and Galleries La Fayette. There are lots of boulangeries and restaurants around the hotel so you can skip breakfast at the hotel if you wish. The place is safe and clean so you dont have to worry if you are arriving late at night. The staff are helpful and speak good English in case you struggle with French. If you are booking through booking.com or perhaps any other online engine, do check with the hotel if you are arriving with a child because they charge extra for children beds. We had ours sharing our bed as he is only 6 but for older children, this can be tricky especially if the room is small which is always the case in all Paris hotels.

author: Traveler25860340977
title: Very Bad experience and rude desk manager.
text: Very bad customer service. When i booked a room using hotels.com, it was advertised that a child can fit so i asked for extra bed and they did not send me any message that there will be extra charge and during check out i was charged 30 Euros on top. I don't mind extra charge but lack of desk manager to acknowledge their mistake and calling me dishonest is very rude and do not deserve 3 star rating. Extra bed provided had wooden slabs missing and when i complained this to Expedia, hotel answer was that was me. Which is utter nonsense and pathetic. Avoid this hotel at any cost, AVOD!!! AVOD!!! AVOID!!!

author: aoifed900
title: Weekend trip to Paris
text: We stayed here for 3 nights one weekend in April. We booked two twin rooms for four people. The rooms were perfect and modern. Really nice bathrooms, excellent wifi, clean and had everything we needed. We arrived early and the hotel were accommodating and had our room made ready for us. The staff were extremely friendly and no request was too much. The lady that works at reception was really generous, helpful and kind giving us advice on how to get around the city and helped us book any taxis or buses we needed and we really appreciated all her help. The hotel was close to so many metro stations meaning you could go anywhere in the city for under €2. Also if you are planning to go to Disneyland you can get the Disneyland shuttle bus five minutes walk from the hotel bringing you straight from door to door. Would definitely recommend this hotel and will book a stay next time I’m in Paris as it is so close to everything and perfect for a city break.

author: George19802013
title: Nice Hotel
text: To be honest I didn't like the area where the hotel is located, however, this is only a personal opinion. The hotel was clean, a bit old and would need a revamp. Breakfast was nice and adequate for starting the day. Room was of medium size but i was just on my own so I didn't care about more space. Bathroom was spacious, complimentary toilettries (Azzaro) provided which was a nice touch. Reception and cleanign staff was very polite and always willing to share their expertise and knowledge, answering any question. Stayed for three nights. Decent all in all and not too expensive, but you are in Paris after all!

author: NW-travellers85
title: Good location
text: We stayed in this hotel for a romantic getaway. The hotel is in a good location within walking distance to the main shopping district. We also walked to Notre Dam and to the Arc De Triomphe (although we did it at a very leisurely pace!). The room we stayed in was modern but there was a lingering musty smell. We left the window open whilst in the room which helped. We did however have a great sleep, the bed was comfortable and the room was quiet. Some parts of the hotel look tired and could do with some updating; the furniture in the bar area is very worn. The receptionist was very friendly and helpful. The rooms are quite a good size and a reasonable price too. This is a good hotel for a base to explore Paris.

author: EssiE52
title: Small rooms but good value
text: We stayed in the ATN hotel in march for 3 nights. The staff was really helpful and friendly. Both the lobby and the rooms are really small but it's still a very clean and stylish hotel. Especially the bathroom was modern and even had some special lighting settings. The wifi was good. The only downside was the breakfast - the selection was quite small and they had run out of some foods. The hotel is in a walking distance from the nearest metro stations. The breakfast was not worth it's price, but otherwise I would definitely recommend this hotel, especially for a short stay.

author: WaelH210
title: Nice place with great location
text: Nice place we booked a triple room . Room was really big enough for 3 of us with the luggage. Staff are really helpful. Special thanks to Raj who made everything easy and explained a lot. We didnt try the breakfast as we wanted to taste the Paris street food. Alot of dining places around very close "very few steps" from Sant lazar metro station and RER big station. Super markets and big stores. Will stay again there if we visited paris. Thank you all

author: 150seank
title: I'd recommend this for holiday and business
text: We were in Room 603, ground floor and entrance from the inner gardan/terrace. Room was clean. And was also cleaned during our 3 day stay. Staff is helpful and can assist you perfectly well in English. Price/quality combination is great and you're also quite close to everything. Take an Uber or go by foot. Louvre is about 5 min ride and 15/20 minutes walk, same goes for the Sacre Coeur. From there everything is within an arms reach. Did not have breakfast, but the breakfast location is also really nice. Hotel just looks good and has a great vibe.

author: carastangstins
title: Superior location
text: Stayed here for four nights over the New Year break. Staff were friendly enough but a little brisk (perhaps due to our non-existent French). Having said that, they happily booked our airport transfer and answered any questions. Rooms are incredibly small but quaint and clean. We stayed on the fifth floor and did not experience any noise. Pricey but I believe this was probably due to it being NYE and not the actual hotel. Wifi worked fine and location was absolutely perfect. Would stay again.

author: nauckers94
title: Good hotel but over priced
text: A good hotel but over priced. The hotel is nice but the area it's in is not. Positives Gay friendly, close to st Lazare station and quick access to travel Paris by metro. A lovely cafe at end of the street offering excellent breakfast. The bathrooms are lovely. Negatives. The biggest complaint is that the 3 min journey from the hotel to the station is through a rough street not to be travelled alone. One night per week homeless people gather outside the hotel for free food. And a lot of dodgy people hang around outside the station Cleaners can be noisy. The hot water often didn't work.

author: rl165
title: Great location
text: Clean, modern fittings, average sized rooms for Paris hotels. The wifi is good, but could be better. The breakfast is standard for hotels in that area. The location is fantastic! Its right next to Gare Saint Lazare. There are bunch of cafes around the hotels that are nice, and stay open fairly late. There are a number of ATM within a few min walk, and a laundry within 10 min walk. Recommended for family and business travelers. My only suggestion would be to upgrade the wifi service.

author: ArtoVuori
title: Clean and quiet hotel with good location
text: Stayed five nights here during christmas. Hotel is only two minutes walk from Gare St.Lazare and ten from RER E Hausmann-St.Lazare station. Place is located in small street and you cannot hear any traffic or street noise inside. Rooms are small and soundproof to outside world but not to neighbour rooms. There is couple restaurants to each direction just around the corners. Nearest medium size grocery store is at Gare St.Lazare bottom floor two or three minutes walk from the hotel. Friendly staff. From CDG take RER A to Gare du Nord, change to RER E (Magenta station) and drop off at St.Lazare-Hausmann.

author: 503Melanie
title: Awesome hotel!
text: I recently stayed here for 4 nights with my boyfriend and it was great. The hotel was really easy to find and in a really good location, it's less than 2 minutes walk from Gare Saint Lazare so having heavy/loads of bags wont be a big problem. Travelling from the airport (CDG) was also quite easy having only one transfer and got there in about 40mins from the airport. Staff were friendly and checked us in quickly, we asked for a smoking room but then found out the hotel was non smoking, they gave us a room which was on the bottom floor which had the smoking area right outside the door which was really kind of them. The room was big enough for the two of us and was very clean and everything worked fine, nice lighting in the bathroom too, the bed was comfortable and we had free wifi in the room. The location of the hotel was really good! Near many shops which some are open 24 hours too which was really handy, there is also a small convenience store close to the hotel where you can buy nearly everything. Me and my boyfriend walked everywhere from the hotel, we didn't use the train at all which saved us a lot of money, it's around 20mins walk from the Champs Elysees and 30mins walk from the Eiffel Tower which was great, also close to major shopping department stores; Printemps and Galleries Lafayette. If I came back to Paris I would definitely stay here again! It was worth paying more for this hotel in a good location saving money on transport, rather than paying less and being further away.

author: 540MariaS
title: Good for a short city-trip
text: The hotel is nicely located close to many bars, cafes, train station and within short walking distance to Moulin Rouge and Montmartre. If you plan to visit mostly Rive Gauche then it will require either a metro/bus ride or more walking. The personnel of the hotel is very friendly. We arrived a few hours before the check-in time and already got an access to the room. The rooms are clean and stylish. Everything in the rooms works fine, nothing was broken or malfunctioning. Could be better: if there were snacks (nuts, crisps, cookies) in the mini-bar and a kettle in a room. Overall, great place for a short trip if you plan to explore many parts of Paris.

author: MichaelDowlingDublin
title: Excellent
text: Great location. Nice modern hotel. Great breakfast. Friendly staff. Not much more to say really. For the price its excellent value. I'd definitely stay here again. Right beside Saint Lazare station, so handy for metro to the more popular parts of town.

author: Wanderlust520
title: Great location and excellent value!
text: We spent 4 nights in this cozy hotel with very friendly personnel and an excellent breakfast for the price (considering this is Paris). You can make your own real espresso, not brewed coffee as in most hotels, and they serve fresh pastries, Camembert cheese and yogurt, which was not expected from many of these basic types of breakfast scenarios at hotels. The room, while small as expected in Paris, was nicely appointed and newly renovated. The location was just perfect and walking distance from our favorite spot in Paris, Montmartre. There is also a Metro station withing 3 minutes walking distance. One recommendation. Walk around the corner to Via Chocolat for the best boutique chocolate we have experienced. Ask the hotel for directions. We would stay here again next time in Paris for sure.

author: parobbo
title: convenient and peaceful
text: Hotel convenient for St Lazare station (trains to Cherbourg, Le Havre very regular) and also for Opera metro station and stop for touring bus 10 minute walk. Rooms immaculately clean and spacious. Very quiet area so able to sleep easily and air conditioning worked perfectly in our room (404). Staff exceptionally helpful and polite - called cab efficiently - 10-15 euros to central Paris (Notre Dame and Eiffel Tower) and excellent with directions if needed. Thanks for all your perseverance and help with our son's "little problem". Thankfully she said "yes"! Excellent value for Paris hotel - breakfast varied and plentiful - 12 euros not bad for Paris. Thanks for giving us a good end to our holiday.

author: angecorti
title: nice surprise
text: I was on a business trip to Paris and had to stay overnight. Hotel was agreat surprise. It looked newly remodelled, evrything was clean and personnel really nice and helpful. Modern look. Nice and spacious room, new bathroom with bath tub and shower ( missing a tray or something to hold make up and tootbrush). It was quite strange to have the airdryer in the closet. even if the room was on the first floor facing the road, it was really silent. More noises were coming from nearby rooms (flushing toilet/ door openings elevator,..) Breakfast was self served european style: coffe pastries corn flakes, some fruit, and also some cheeses and eggs. Ambient was with vaults and a lot of mirrors (area is really tiny) Price was including breakfast and really reasonable for Paris. Ottimo!!!!!

author: briebw
title: DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!
text: I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights for a business trip. They charged a small fortune (250 Euros/night). And it wasnt even good. It was basically clean..but thats it. No place I would stay again. Also someone came into my room during the day and took money out of my wallet. I reported this to the hotel insurance company and they said it was my fault. That they cannot be responsible for my belongings when i should have used the safe. so i say to you all DO NOT STAY HERE!!!! keep looking!!!!

author: suesca
title: well located
text: Double bedroom was fine, with minibar and good wi-fi, and great showe and AC. Breakfast was very decent and generous in options (buffet). Service people were nice as well. YOu may leave your bags in there when having a late departure and wanting to go around. This hotel is very close to Gare St. Lazare (5 minutes walk or less) therefore you get really good metro service as well as buses. Brasseries and Cafes all close by or you could walk up to 10 minutes to Printemps and Lafayette Magazines and get many more options for both shopping and dining. The only mini-market i found close by is Monoprix, either on Rue de Pepiniere or the one behind Printemps that is much larger. Montmartre is also very close by car if you wanted to go to the Moulin Rouge or Sacre Coeur.

author: lkobsey
title: Trendy & Compact
text: Stayed for one night . We had a tripple room as we need a twin room and this is what was available.Managment was very friendly and accomodating. Rooms done in a hip colorful them with accent lighting. A lot of care and expense was taken in the bathrooms. Breakfast was fine and served in a valted basement room of the hotel. It is within walking distance of all the great Fr. department stores. LK

author: sethyr
title: Lovely Hotel, excellent location and very friendly staff
text: I booked this Hotel for a weekend in Paris I arranged for my Partners birthday. Was not dissapointed. Staff were very friendly and couldn't do enough to help. Very nice location, very close to a main metro station where you could get around most of Paris from. Also about a 20 minute walk to the Louvre or a 10-15 minute walk northwards up to the Moulin Rouge. Rooms were very nicely decorated, and the corridors and reception/bar area also decorated to a very high and modern standard. Rooms included air con, which is a bonus if like us you go to Paris in the middle of a heat wave! Rooms also include hair dryer and a nice large flat screen tv! Rooms and hotel also have complimentary wi-fi which was very useful! Would highly recommend this lovely boutique hotel and would have no problem staying there again.

author: Experiencehunter
title: Nice hotel
text: This was a really good experience... I booked the hotel thru internet and was not so sure about what i will find when i really get there. But... I had a nice surprise... Everything was great.. The stuff in the reception was friendly and the location was perfect. The room was small but very nice decorated and very clean. Atn hotel was a great value for money...

author: CaerdyddCymru
title: Swings and roundabouts with paper thin walls
text: Stayed at this hotel for a long romantic weekend and was equally surprised and disappointed by it. The rooms were small, but very well decorated and the bathrooms equally were to a very high standard. The entire hotel is bathed in seductive light, from it's neon blue halls to its multi coloured bathrooms. Breakfast was fantastic, with a large selection of croissants, pain au chocolats, danishes, cereals, and hot food. Upon arrival we were greeted by a very friendly and helpful receptionist who pointed out the best things to do in Paris and highlighted them all on a map for us. Be aware, there is NO iron in the rooms, as we found out to our misfortune. We spoke to the night porter on reception who duly set us one up in dining room (basement) but would not allow us to take it to our room, so we had a 11pm ironing session whilst breakfast was being set up around us - not what I would expect for the money paid for this hotel! Please note that the walls are paper thin, and you can hear everything in the next room!

author: DestinationLAX
title: Great Experience!
text: We were very happy with this hotel. The price was fairly reasonable, and everything was brand new. The room (triple) was comfortable and clean and spacious. The staff was helpful too. The location felt safe, although homeless people slept on the corner at night. It was walking distance (2 blocks) from the subway station. It was maybe 1 mile away from the Opera/shopping district. The bad thing was that there weren't any restaurants open late nearby. It was dead at night.

author: yusufaytas
title: Ambience and Hospitality
text: Divan is at the heart of Ankara. One might think it might not be the safest area but that’s certainly not the case. Divan has an impressive view of Ankara, I have enjoyed it a lot. Divan has an amazing decoration. It has a small library and a bar. The rooms are big and again decorated with Anatolian motives. The breakfast was absolutely wonderful. Each dish was prepared amazingly and you can easily taste the quality ingredients.

author: MIHAIL209
title: What a great surprise
text: It is a gorgeous value location to spend some nights in Ankara. Situated in front of a very old castle, newly refurbished and restored. This hotel makes you feel hundred of years ago. The interior lobby with running water pouring through the sofas. The staff exceptionally kindly and ready to help you in any respect. The rooms very clean and well designed. The breakfast is different from most of other Turkish restaurants. It is not a buffet and the waiter brings you different dishes to choose from. They are good quality food products but anyway do not have too great expectations for breakfast.

author: 862waynes
title: A Modern Day Traveller on The Silk Road
text: This phenomenally beautifully restored hotel was originally a caravanserai, where merchants (and their goods and camels) gathered to buy and sell their goods and to sleep. It was one of the largest on The Silk Road in Turkey. In recent times, it was bought and restored, with a modern restaurant addition added at the back. The now-covered courtyard (clear) was filled with comfortable furniture, a stream running through and plants everywhere. Our room was enormous with a huge, modern bathroom, and there were beautiful paintings and decorative items everywhere. The view from our window was over the city. At night, it was magic. Service was impeccable, Sadly, we were there only one night.

author: fari514
title: Great location
text: Great location. We took a bus to get there since it was `nearby`. Had to walk up hill with our luggages at 10pm. Take a taxi!!!! Other than that, it is near everything that needs to be seen in the capital, old fortress, bazaar and the restaurants. Rooms are good. Restaurant inside the hotel is great. I recommend the lamb :)

author: lduffy1
title: Back again and loving Divan Cukurhan
text: The Divan Cukurhan is a wonderful hotel located in an increasingly interesting neighborhood. We stayed here five years ago, loved it and were happy to return this spring. They now have the Safranhan Brasserie, which features outstanding food—and outdoor dining with a spectacular view—and the new, elegant Erimtan Archaeological Museum next door. This is a nice cultural addition to the Ankara Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, one of the top museums in Turkey, which is located just down the street. The hotel’s rooms are distinctive and charming, and the extensive lobby offers a variety of seating areas. The staff is uniformly pleasant and eager to help in any way they can; they become friends. You can’t beat the location: the historic Ankara Citadel is right outside, along with Copper Alley—a collection of shops with a range of unique items. New historic finds are popping up, including Roman baths and an amphitheater, which can be reached on foot. If Ankara is your base for touring the wider region, Divan Cukurhan is the perfect hotel.

author: w0rldlywise
title: Nice building but not much more
text: Nicely restored building and good setting if you want to be in old town but no atmosphere and above all terrible breakfasts. Feels like a room has been tacked on to the side as a restaurant. Breakfast is not buffet. Food of poor quality is handed to you - stale bread, a few cubes of cheese, badly-cooked eggs - and when we asked for fruit or espresso it was "extra charge". Ate in same restaurant for dinner - food was decent but poor service. Hotel rooms a little small but quite nice and good big bathroom. A bit cut off from rest of city. Wouldn't stay here again

author: robb8888
title: Stunning interior, but a little cold/distant
text: This is a boutique hotel located in a renovated 400-year old caravanserai in Ankara. The renovation is beautiful, and the rooms are very well-appointed -- my room had its own giant soaking tub and waterfall shower. As with all of the hotels I stayed in on my trip, the giant Turkish breakfast was fresh and satisfying. But the location is in the old part of Ankara, which is itself a little run-down and seedy and is not very convenient to public transportation. Also the hotel is difficult to find -- a series of narrow, winding, hilly streets -- and its Google Maps location is not quite exact. And it seemed to me that the service -- while polite -- was not the same level of warm, friendly Turkish hospitality that I experienced just about everywhere else in the country. At one point I was trying to upload trip updates, and download map updates, and the WiFi to the entire hotel cut out. And, for Turkey, the hotel is a little on the expensive side, although not exorbitantly so. If I come back to Ankara, I might forgo the beautiful renovation and rooms to stay somewhere a little more convenient and friendly.

author: SelimA571
title: 40th Anniversary With University Classmates
text: "Divan Çukurhan" is a boutique hotel, belonging to Divan Hotel chains, a 400 years old "kervansaray" situated next to Ankara Fortress in the old city. It is surrounded by many old characteristic Ankara houses and old trade houses. It has been meticulously renovated by a group of well known architects and the authenticity has been kept with utmost care. It has around twenty rooms, each different in size and appearance from each other, a very cleverly designed hi-tech housing system which is totally hidden. A reasonable number of old drawings and decorative pieces carefully selected by "Koç Museum" experts can be seen on old brick walls. The rooms are spacious enough for a historic thick walled building with decorative an a comfortable bathroom including a bath tub and a separate shower. The restaurant which is situated at the level -2, opening to a large terrace with a panoramic view of the city has an excellent menu. The staff who have been trained by the experienced senior staff of Divan Hotel Chain are very friendly and professional. For anybody who come to Ankara who has a taste for "old cities" and who prefers to stay in a luxurious hotel with quality.

author: Xphilosopherking
title: Stunning interior, but service is so-so
text: I stayed here for three nights in June. The place had few people staying at it, but it was not empty. There is rarely anyone at the front desk, so if you need help you need to look for someone. One evening I wanted a glass of wine at the bar and that ended up being a lengthy and complex process. The Internet access was sketchy in my corner room. And one evening the AC kept on making a low, loud droning sound which meant I did not get to sleep until 1:30 AM. Finally, they will get you a shuttle to the airport, but unlike other hotels which provide the service, it's expensive. But there are also some very positive things about this hotel, mainly, it is very beautiful and in an historical building. The lobby has large, comfortable couches which are perfect for reading or chatting with friends (but again, good luck getting something to drink). My bed was comfortable, the water pressure and temperature were great, and my in-room coffee maker was much preferable to the instant coffee provided by so many other hotels in Turkey.

author: NZTraveller20
title: Fantastic
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay in this restored 16th century "inn". On two storeys, the hotel has a central covered courtyard surrounded by all the guest rooms. The furnishing is amazing as exhibits have bene brought from all over the world. The service was great and the rooms spacious and comfortable. Breakfast starts with a trsditional platter of cheeses, tomato, olives etc plus jam, honey and other accompaniments. You then choose a hot dish to follow if you wish. The freshly squeezed orange juice is a must try. On top of this the hotel is well located opposite the Ankara castle and close to the Anatolian Civilization museum

author: GeorgeCh60
title: Historical and oriental
text: I spent 2 nights at the hotel. It is supposed to be very attractive but it depends on whether you like to live in a 16th century setting nowadays. The hotel is situated at the foot of the historical fortress hill of the city but it is rather isolated in daytime and really scary in the night. The hotel is clean and well kept. At the beginning of January it was warm enough. The bathroom is perfect - if a separate shower and a bath-tub. The breakfast is not on a block table which is why it is not varied. To my greatest surprise it was not very easy to communicate with the staff - their command of English was not very good.

author: iremu2016
title: Perfect.
text: I have been here in Jan 2016. So beautiful. Small, Chic and clean. Very polite staff. Calm, good restaurant. Near to the museums and the castle. Ideal for business and touristic travels. Best hotel I stayed in Ankara. I really loved the ambience.

author: travel-hawthorne
title: Luxury in a historical setting
text: This place is fabulous! For a bargain price, a night in luxury, surrounded by historical mementos both inside and outside the hotel. After a late-night check-in, they gave us a late check-out with no problem. The room was huge and the bathroom almost the size of the bedroom. There is a nespresso machine in the room with 3 capsules--one even decaf! This was a transit overnight for me, but I could have stayed right in that room. Right outside the door is the Ankara Castle and lots of touristy shopping. The Koc Museum is nearby.

author: Philippa1967
title: Perfect Hotel
text: This really is the perfect hotel. The renovation is beautiful and it's like staying in a luxury museum. I was bemused by comments about the staff being cold, because from the moment we entered the hotel, every single staff member was friendly and couldn't do enough to ensure we had a perfect stay. Even the chambermaid waved and smiled from the bedroom she was cleaning. We luckily had an upgrade and the jacuzzi bath and enormous shower were a real treat. The room was clean and very comfortable. The wifi was fast too. The food and drinks were also amazing and dinner and breakfast were both delicious and reasonably priced. Free entry to the excellent museum next door and a hill top location really do make this a perfect hotel.

author: 724JimB724
title: Absolutely Outstanding!
text: This hotel is first rate in every respect! You might even call it a living museum. Antiques abound everywhere. Accommodations are spacious, attractively furnished and the beds are very comfortable. The service at the hotel is superb! Situated across the street from Akara's Citadel and less than a block away from Ankara's Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, you couldn't ask for a better location, especially if you are a "museum aholic" The newly opened Erimtan Museum is right next door. This hotel is a wonderful place to experience the culture, as well as the cuisine of Anatolia. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

author: jautBrussels_Belgium
title: Nice atmosphere in old style hotel
text: The hotel has an old world charm to it, built in traditional Turkish style with dark wooden details. The hotel is on one of the hills overlooking Ankara and right next door to the old city. There is a taxi station just outside and it takes approx 15-20 mins to the Otogar, depending on the traffic. Staff are friendly but have limited knowledge of the English language. Breakfast is delicious with both Turkish and western elements. Dinner can be had at the restaurant next door, which also doubles as a museum. There is also a bistro adjacent to the hotel. Our room was beautifully appointed and spacious. Suitable both for the business and holiday traveller.

author: BarnyDw
title: Perfect Perfet Perfect.......
text: What can I say..... A beautiful hotel. Stayed with my wife for 3 nights and I don't think 3 weeks would have been enough. Fantastic staff from the security outside to the cleaners, from the reception to the waiting staff, they were all a credit to the Divan Ankara Çukurhan. Our room over looked the inside of the hotel and the only noise we got with the window open was the faint sound of the music.. The room was lovely. We will be returning to Ankara on business again and cannot wait to book this hotel. Don't stay anywhere else in Ankara.

author: Wijehaba
title: Home away from home
text: Luxurious boutique hotel. Stayed a week in a first floor room facing the adjacent property so had a pleasant view. Great location for those interested in heritage, museums and the like. Used the restaurant most nights and was well satisfied. Very good senior management but desk staff's english a bit lacking and sometimes pretended to understand when they did not which lead to some minor confusion. Made hotel transport available for day excursions which was very convenient .Extraordinary good value for theaccommodation and amenities provided. Pleasant lounge and library retreat. Computer. Decorated throughout with interesting folk art.

author: Paul_Wan_Tong
title: A gem of a hotel
text: We stayed for 3 nights while in Ankara. The hotel is a restored caravensarai and an absolute gem. It is about 1.5kms from the train station, and 200m from the Anatolian Civilisation Museum. Our deluxe room was spacious, beautifully decorated and looked out to the main gate of the citadel. The staff are very helpful, and if they don't understand English, will find someone who does. The breakfast is a standard selection of Turkish breakfast foods, followed by your choice of a hot course. The only slight downside is that once you have seen the local sights, any other sites will need a taxi ride off the hill. It can also be particularly quiet on a Sunday night and there can be stray dogs wandering around in the dark, although they seem to leave humans alone. All in all Divan was a wonderful choice for our visit to Ankara and is highly recommended.

author: Ghezli
title: Beautiful place
text: The hotel is beautiful. Our room and the bathroom was amazing. very quite place, right opposite Ankara Kalesi and next to a museum. 5-10 mins drive from the city centre. its also right inside the old part of the city, which gives you access to alot of cool and cosy cafes and shops. The only issue was their staffing. there were only one person available at a time, and most of the times we had to look around the hotel for them. overall we had a very pleasant experience staying there.

author: NickRocco
title: Imagine yourself a silk road merchant
text: The Divan Cukurhan is an artistically modernized caravanserai located high on Ankara's Castle hill. My wife and I stayed there for two nights in September, 2013. The booking was made directly and efficiently via the hotel's website. Valet parking of our rental car was courteous and convenient. Our "deluxe king room" left nothing to be desired. Breakfasts, served graciously in the hotel's beautiful atrium, were ample and delicious. Concierge service was helpful and humorously delivered. The hotel is close to the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations and the entrance to the ancient Ankara Castle is directly across the street. We had to wander only a few blocks to find interesting shops and eateries. In Ankara, this is a great place to stay.

author: AnneL668
title: Wonderful hotel best I have ever stayed in.
text: The hotel is in the restored building of the caravanserais, the public areas are huge pleasant spaces. Each room has a different theme, all are big, some are giant and the bathrooms are spectacular. The beds, bed linen and pillows are gorgeous, really excellent. There was coffee, Nespresso machine and a kettle. It was a pity to leave the room. It was located just below the citadel and 100m from the Ankara Museum. Down the hill there are several streets of authentic craftsmen and shops selling rather old fashioned things which were interesting. The area round the hotel is in the process of being done up and I have a feeling that it will all become super touristy but for now it was a great place to visit.

author: A380fan
title: Super Hotel!
text: The Cukurhan is a lovely boutique hotel, and really was a great place to stay in Ankara. All the rooms are individually furnished, and are terribly comfortable. The staff were polite and friendly, although at times their English was a little hard to understand. There are quite a few decent restaurants in the vicinity, as well as the excellent Cengelhan Rahmi M. Koc Museum next door, and Ankara Castle with some great views. I had some issues with my shower head (water was coming out of the side, rather than down through the holes) – this wasn’t really sorted out, but I was moved to a different room (which also had the same problem, but I could live with it). I also had issues with the heat in the room – it was too hot, so I had to turn the air con on, something I wasn’t expecting to have to do in January! There is a lovely seating area in the lobby. Sadly I didn’t try out the bar or restaurant, but will definitely stop by my next time in Ankara.

author: ASJ-CPH
title: Lovely hotel
text: This hotel is absolutely lovely. It's likely staying in a museum. The staff is super friendly and nice, room is lovely and the bathroom great, however, as experienced by another guest, the wifi internet did not work in my room. There is no minibar, although I did not find that a problem. The room service food was good, but the selection quite limited. The location of the hotel is in the old city, on top of a hill, so it's a bit remote, on the other hand it is authentic and old, rather than new and crowded. I LOVE this hotel, but people who do not share my preferences may not. I will be staying there next time I go back.

author: ClareM142
title: perfect stay
text: I stayed here for 4 nights, my room was luxurious and big! I had 2 sinks to myself, a bath tub with Jacuzzi, a separate shower with rain and waterfall heads, separate, a loo, and of course a room. the bed was ever so comfortable, i had a chaise longe with foot rest and my own nespresso machine, I was in heaven just in my room! but what makes this hotel is the furnishings, each room is decorated differently. From African styles, to Oriental to French Louis 16, each unique and tasteful. The building is a former caravansarie restored beautifully. the breakfast was eggs of choice, olives, breads, honey, preserves, salad, juices, yoghurt, cheeses and coffee or tea. all tasty. I ate several times in the restaurant, but I didn't enjoy the food as much, one time it was microwaved the other 2 times tasteless and oily, but I am still giving it 5 stars for the hotel itself and I would stay again but eat down the hill.

author: A_Toronto_Traveler
title: Well Appointed, Friendly Hotel
text: Very modern,very comfortable hotel. Staff were very friendly and accomodating and the service was excellent. My room was spacious, very comfortable with modern finishings. The location is close to shops, cafes and a park. Located about 45 + minutes from the airport. Pub/cafe and restuarant provided a varied selection of food. Popular spot on Friday night. I was highly recommend this hotel and look forward to returning.

author: jos864
title: WAY better than we bargained for.
text: We arrived late and negotiated hard to get a good price for the room, what we got was a sublime experience! I have only the most fantastic things to say about our stay. The most incredibly beautiful rooms, bar, lobby and library. The building has such an enchanting history, with the unique antiques to match. The cappuccino for brekkie was the best we've had in Turkey (and the machine in the room a little added joy)! Not to mention best hotel brekkie in turkey too. We even snuck in a bit of gym time... All the usual equipment. Maybe I love a bargain, or maybe this is just my favourite hotel in all of Turkey!

author: EliseA86
title: Great hotel
text: Overall, the hotel itself is a great place to stay.
