Had a little bit of trouble with communicating with staff as they don't really speak english.

author: Heldonearth
title: Nice but nothing special
text: Starting with the positives; Great location, ideally placed for the old part of the city and the esplanade. Very good price. Good sized room. Now balance this with negatives; Room was tired and in need of a refurb. There were marks all over the walls, the tiles were marked, the drain in the shower loose, bulbs above the bathroom mirror and at one side of the bed were blown. The bathroom sink smelt and in the separate toilet area there was mould / damp showing through the paintwork and again it smelt rather unpleasant. The mattress was rather on the firm side even for our liking, and the glazing did little to nothing in cutting down outside noise and this meant when the nearby nightclub emptied between 2am and 4am every night we were woken and had fitful night sleeps all four nights, but even this was surpassed when at 22.50hrs on our third night we were awoken by the sounds of a pneumatic drill taking up the pavement opposite before assumedly connecting utilities to the new shop opening opposite. Admittedly some of this is can’t be helped, but some basic stuff can, such as simple cleanliness. While we got what we paid for it has maybe made us rethink our holidaying strategy for future reference and sometimes quality should not be comprised for what on the face of it appears to be a really good deal.

author: KariwaV
title: Best location
text: Very nice hotel for good price. Location perfect. Close to everything- old town, beach, shops, restaurants and bus stops. In the room you have everything what needs- towels, soap, shampoo and body wash gel. If your breakfast not including there are fridge and kettle in the room. We bought food in local shops and have breakfast in our family room. In the hall you can find extra chair which was very handy to have for breakfast time. We stay with 5 years old child. Staff are super friendly they explain everything what we ask. From hotel to airport we take local bus n70 for just 1,50€ its take 30 min(it was traffic at this time) bus stop is just 2 min from hotel so point to take express bus 98 (6€per person) The only thing that room is small, but for us it was fine because we didn’t spent to much time there.

author: TravellingDaveB
title: Friendly Hotel in Great Location
text: I chose this hotel because of the location and reasonable price. I stayed for 3 nights and was very comfortable here. The room was clean and pleasant with tv, ac/heating and free wi-fi. The bathroom was modern. The staff were all very friendly and helpful. Location was perfect, close to the old town, beach, and shops, bars and restaurants. Peaceful and quiet location, but close to everything. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.Excellent.

author: 65plusonthemove
title: Friendly staff, but small room and facilities
text: This is a difficult review to write. The hotel is really well situated. The staff were very friendly and welcoming, the continental breakfast was fine, but the rooms were disappointing. The bedroom was clean but small and with very tired carpeting. The en-suite was clean but is the smallest I have ever seen in years of travel! I am not a big person but could hardly turn around in the shower. The toilet seat faced the shower wall and to get to sit on the seat required a lot of manoeuvring of my feet and knees.Finally the carpet pattern on the stairs from floor 1 to floor 2 is quite frankly dangerous as the pattern confuses where each stair ends. I had to concentrate on each step and eventually decided to use the lift for my own safety.

author: agsiul2013
title: Very good location
text: The hotel is in a great spot as it can be accessed by car/taxi but is close to the centre of town. The room was small and the bathroom was tiny but it was clean though did smell a little of damp. We left the window open while we were in the room. There is a lift so that you don't have to drag your luggage up the stairs. It is one of the old fashioned type, very quaint. As the reception is on the first floor it might not be as secure as other hotels, however, the main door is locked at night and you need to use an access code to get in. There is a small security box in the room. It is big enough for cameras, e-book readers, etc. However, it is not big enough for a laptop.

author: heikkitapanih
title: Mr. Heikki
text: Very nice and frendly Hotel. Location is nearly midle of the town. Breakfast was quite good but not any vegetables. The Rooms was small but enought for two person. Bathroom was clean and simpy. Easy to walk any comon tarfic places. In the nigt time little noice disturb. The insulation of voice between the rooms should be better.

author: pniag
title: location!
text: What a great little hotel - the location is perfect for touring and wandering. It's about 10 minute saunter to the promenade and the beach and even closer to old town. Tons of restaurants right outside the door of the hotel as well as in old town. We were able to walk everywhere we wanted to go. The train to Ventimiglia was easily reached too as was the bus to Monaco. Rooms were sufficient in size and we were comfortable there for our 7 night stay. Bags could be stored there if your room isn't ready or if you stay later on checkout day. Staff was friendly and helpful. A great stay!

author: NoCreditNeeded
title: Small rooms and little storage - but conveniently placed
text: I was a single traveller at this hotel. The (double) room was extremely small, with very little room for storage,. Instructions for the room safe were placed most inconveniently at an angle inside a cupboard - almost impossible to read! TV has no English channels. Other people's remarks about the quirky elevator and the reception not being visible on arrival are accurate: both are a little peculiar. For anyone with impaired sight, the stair carpet (brown with a geometric pattern) can prove hazardous; it would be easy to miss a step, as the edges of the steps are not easy to see. That said, the hotel is VERY conveniently placed for 'buses, Old Town and the sea - and the room refrigerator works! I noticed that on one day my bed had been made up and towels replaced as usual, but no other cleaning (including the lavatory) had been done. I had a view of the street which i enjoyed.

author: davek559
title: reasonable budget hotel, great central location, clean rooms
text: The hotel has a good central location, with excellent access to both the beach and old town, plus good public transport links just a few minutes away. The room, was not overly spacious, but was clean, tidy and well presented. I would imagine the decor was updated fairly recently to try and be a bit modern and funky, and it partway gets there. importantly the bed was comfortable. On the downside, our room was a little noisy both from outside, and adjacent rooms, but bearable for just a few days. We also had some issues with the wifi, which occasionally dropped the signal, and then would not re-connect, but again not a terrible problem for a short stay. Staff were friendly and helpful, offering to arrange a taxi for our early morning departure, which arrived at the precise time. One of the great things is the old fashioned lift, which has been modernised for safety, but has lost none of it's charm, absolutely loved it. All in all not a bad choice for short stay, and certainly good value for money.

author: BaliLover65
title: Very central location, great staff.
text: This hotel is quite small but very central, everything is just a short walk away, the train station is a cab ride but a short one. The street this hotel is on has loads of great little restaurants to choose from, as well as only a short walk to where there literally 100s to choose from. There is a self service laundromat just 75 yards away, take plenty of change as you need coins to get the powder etc. There is a lady working on the front counter who is originally from South Africa who is very helpful indeed, she gave us lots of tips of where to go etc. The main square with the dancing fountains is just at the bottom of the road, the trams are nearby. The rooms are adequate, clean, and have a mini fridge in them, well ours did, the only bad thing is the walls are thin and we could hear the people next door doing things ! if you get my drift. There is a mini mart just a few doors along which sells most things, wine was cheap. All in all a great little place to stay.

author: gilleanopoku
title: Very Central
text: The location of the hotel is very central. Moments away from the main shopping strip, a short walk to the promenade/beach and under 10mins to old town. A bus from the airport stops at Albert Garden which is just a short walk through the park to the hotel. The staff were very helpful with telling me what was around the area and tours available. One staff member told me about the flower market every morning and the chateau ruins where you can see 360 degree views of Nice. Absolutely break taking. The room was clean, modern and decently sized. It's a good option for a weekend get away.

author: ErikL327
title: Good Basic hotel
text: I choose this hotel for its location and quite cheap price level. When we arrived staff (young girls) in reception were little amateurish and not very friendly but we got everything what we asked. Even hotel is located old building and it is just renovated from inside. Double room were small but clean ,new and modern. Bath were particularly small but very neat. Free Wifi worked well. Hotel elevetor was very old and very hard to use with two separate doors so prepare to use stairs. This is good , clean , basic hotel with good location : anything special but works well. I would choose this again.

author: fanuimhirahaon
title: Still Good, and still improving. Helpful and friendly staff.
text: revisited the hotel in May this year. it's still as good as ever. the rooms have been upgraded and even the shower has a new glass surround. always lots of hot running water. room cleaned each day, and the towel fairy also comes every day and leaves more than enough towels. about 20 french channels on the flat-screen HD TV in the room. the prices have increased in last couple of years by approx 20% +, but the quality of the rooms has similarly improved. new air conditioning units in the rooms. staff are happy to let you leave ur bags in the reception area for a couple of hours on checkout day.

author: MissDavina
title: New rooms are a treat!
text: We were upgraded to a comfort room upon arrival and were very pleased with it. A nice big shower and new furnishings make it feel like a 4 star hotel! The reception staff were very friendly and helpful. The negatives are only minor, picky things: - - some parts of the room (walls, architraves etc) weren't well finished, - the elevator was old (but cute!) and could be temperamental, it got our luggage upstairs but we otherwise used the stairs, - no bed sheet, doona and cover only which made us sweat during the night, - breakfast was expensive considering how basic it was but for one or two nights. That said, everything in Nice is expensive! - Nice is a party town and due to its central location, could hear party-goers on the street at early hours I've only listed these as they may be determining factors for some, however these negatives only equate to -1 for us. We would definitely stay here again if the room rate was similar as it is excellent value for money! If the hotel were to improve some or all of the negatives listed above I would give it 5 stars!

author: denniss44
title: Recommended for other young couples!
text: Stayed with my girlfriend for five nights in the double comfort room, we really enjoyed the stay for the price we paid. Great location to visit attractions, the old town, the beach and shopping by foot. Friendly and helpful staff that guided us e.g. how to travel to Cannes and Monaco. The room was small, but not a problem if you don't spend most of your time there. The mini-fridge didn't work so well, but otherwise I can't complain. The rooms looked the same as the pictures. We ate breakfast in the city instead of the hotel, in my opinion I think that's a better choice if you have time and want to eat your breakfast in a beautiful surrounding.

author: dominictys
title: Vulgarities and horrendous service
text: We arrived at Hotel de Kent one day late, and were not able to contact the hotel staff because we did not have a French handphone number. Because they marked us as a no-show on the first day, they billed us for the room for the full 4 days, and kept a room for us. However when we arrived the next morning to inform the receptionist of our check in, the English lady with short blonde hair started cursing at us and in front of my wife, started saying things like ''[--] it'' while trying to get our room ready, which was already available for us in the first place. She took abut 30 minutes to get this done, cursing all throughout. We kept trying to inform her we were no longer interested in staying at a place that has given such a disgusting experience, and confronted her about all her cursing. She followed by denying all the allegations and even said she was so moral that she would never swear, yet at the same time saying ''I never said [--] or [--] it. It's french.'' When asked to contact upper management, she refused to give a contact and we left. DO NOT go to this hotel unless you are wishing for an unhappy visit to France and burning a hole in your wallet.

author: fanuimhirahaon
title: Good location, good value- budget, nice staff
text: I stayed there for a few days. Considering its central location in Nice, it's good value. Basic rooms etc, but if u want luxury you'll pay easily 2 or 3 times the price per night. Much rather spent that on meals, drink etc. it's very close to main Place Massena, quick walk to Beach, close to main bus stops including 98 to and from airport. Staff were welcoming and friendly. Don't know what the breakfasts were like, as I bring my own travel kettle. Which reminds me, there's a small fridge in the room which was ideal for me to keep rice milk fresh, and handy for leaving a bottle of white wine in. Just off rue Hotel de Postes, Definitely stay there again, perhaps even later this year.

author: aaalanaaa
title: Comfortable hotel, location just ok
text: Clean, proper hotel with free outdoor parking next door. Breakfast is okay, nothing to rave aboit but it's enough to start the day. Our room was spacious but the wallpaper kept peeling off the wall and it looked lime the reason for it was mold. Rooms could use a refresher. Wifi is fast and free, rooms with water kettle, fridge and free tea/coffee. That's a plus. We didn't like the location a lot (a 20-minute walk to the KRT and even longer to get to the river!), there's not much else around, so you're forced to take a taxi for sightseeing. Also didn't like that they bribe people into giving them 5*-reviews on TripAdvisor! The hotel wouldn't be so well reviewed otherwise! Pick something in a better location.

author: 127lital
title: A budget hotel with above average quality and service!
text: I googled and booked this hotel based on the pricing and distance from our bridal shop, however, this happened to be my best research on Taiwan's hotels so far :D Being a budget traveler together with my husband, this hotel offers us not only coziness but also full of satisfaction. A good variety of breakfast selection is one of the factors why my husband wouldn't mind waking up early everyday. They serve the best scrambled eggs by the way. Even though the hotel is located at a distance from Kaohsiung Main Station, it provides free shuttle to and fro until 11 pm which is ample for your day activities. Hotel room is clean and tidy with necessary amenities. One of the nights we opted for a room with a big Jacuzzi bath tub, and we felt like our mini honeymoon has just begun! Special thanks to morning shift front desk staffs Wendi, Agnes, and another guy (sorry we forgot to take note of your name), and afternoon shift's Eddie. We've had a great time in Kaohsiung because of your great service.

author: debrawY3722YA
title: Our Getaway in Jordan
text: What a beautiful place to get away! ALL of the people we interfaced with were pleasant and so accommodating. Inn on the Twenty is just lovely! We ordered pizza from an independent place. We ate at Jordan House, Inn on the Twenty, and the cafe next to the Inn....the food is superb at all of them! The warm, fresh baked bread at the Cafe is delicious! We had to bring a couple of loaves home with us! 😊 We visited, and sampled 5 great wineries..... and brought several bottles home with us.

author: D4915CEmikep
title: Business retreat
text: Beautiful spot. Terrific food. Very friendly and accommodating. Great boardroom that allowed us to Pour out our business ideas. They took care of us so that we could work effectively. Restaurant and hotel were beautiful. Had a great tour of Cave Springs winery. Great add on to a wonderful business retreat

author: Travelconnoisseur5
title: Excellent food
text: We went on a Monday evening. Great view of the valley and pretty sunset. The scallops were outstanding and so was the tenderloin. I would highly recommend both. The wine list is limited as they are owned by cave springs. I love a heavy red but dont want a whole bottle. So there was nothing I liked. But other than that a great meal

author: juliemZ9799AJ
title: 20 Stars For Inn On the Twenty
text: Upscale rooms? Yes! Awesome friendly staff?Yes! If you are thinking this is an old school inn off the QEW think no more this is an upscale boutique hotel that will accommodate your every wish and more. Rooms are great, lots of extra touches (roses for bed turn down) who does that anymore which I thought was awesome!.However reality check not much to do at night so top reason you should come here is for the amazing food that Chef Jason Williams and fellow chefs prepare. Considering the hotel is in the heart of growing fields - wine grapes, plants, fruit ( peaches and cherries!) and flowers it’s no wonder the restaurant has a cornucopia of goodness to choose from. Also associated with Cave Springs Winery right there next to the restaurant so lots of interesting varietals to choose from at wallet friendly price points. Always like to try new wine that’s off the hidden path. Run don’t walk to eat and stay here.

author: 878BillS878
title: A real Disappointment
text: My wife and I both stayed here multiple times in the past before the property was sold, and it was always a unique and enjoyable experience in a quaint town in the Niagara wine region. Not so this trip. We stayed in a private cottage next to the inn. While charming, it was not functional, and badly needed updating. the bed was very uncomfortable and we didn't get much sleep. Not worth the price. Service at reception was very slow. They mistakenly charged us for a breakfast that was included. And the service in the restaurant was incompetent --- the bacon didn't show up with the eggs and the food was cold. We wouldn't go back unless they get their act under control.

author: Robin6155
title: Things are changing
text: We celebrated our fourth anniversary this past weekend at the Inn on the Twenty. As we have done each year now since married, we stayed in the same room (Rittenhouse Suite), enjoyed the incredible dining at the restaurant across the street, and visited our favourite wineries in the region. We were delighted, as always, to see the familiar faces of Bev and John, who remember us and remind us each year why this place is so special. We loved every minute of our stay as it really is one of the most meaningful places in the world to us, but we did recognize that the Inn has changed ownership and that things are beginning to change. The packages we've enjoyed over the past four years are no longer structured the same way, and room prices have increased without additional services or amenities. Breakfast is no longer included in the room rates and the full service they used to provide at the restaurant is no longer the same; this change in hospitality is a bit of a heartbreaker, as the joyful routine of that breakfast service, of being taken in hand so thoroughly and resolutely, is not the same (and you can sense that the staff, too, miss the bounty they used to provide so easily). One can, as we did, request that breakfast be included in our room booking, but this unfortunately led to a double charge on our final bill (which was corrected immediately). We were also able to work in a dinner package with our room and, as always, the Inn on the Twenty restaurant absolutely delivered outstanding food and service in such a beautiful setting as the sun settled behind the treeline of the valley. The wonderful staff and the delicious food and the gorgeous landscape and the utter peace that accompanies a stay at the Inn have not changed, but the atmosphere and the values that underwrite it are, and I hope this new corporate climate drifting in does not freeze out the unique hospitality that has made this region as recognizable as its excellent vintages.

author: Zaba62
title: Daughters wedding
text: We had the pleasure of having our daughter and son-in-laws wedding this past Friday February 16, 2018 at Cave Springs Vineyard, Retreat Building. Followed by their reception at Inn On The Twenty. Beverly, the receptionist was absolutely amazing to all of us. Any concerns we had, she directed them ASAP. We had a fresh rose each day on our bed, fresh fruit with our breakfast, and my grandchildren loved using the jacuzzi in the rooms. It was the most elegant wedding I have attended, and not just because it was my daughters. This was the right location for her wedding. All of our out of town guest were amazed with the location and their rooms. I would highly recommend Inn On The Twenty for a weekend get-away and/or a elegant wedding.

author: M5105JDthomase
title: Wonderful Winter Getaway Location
text: The Inn on the Twenty is a gem located in the quaint village of Jordan. The Inn is a lovingly restored building that offers rooms of all shapes and sizes. Our room was a beautiful suite that had a comfortable seating area with fireplace and an expansive bathroom with Jacuzzi-style bathtub. Upon our arrival this frosty day, we were warmly greeted by Bev at the front desk and after a very brief check in process were escorted personally to our room. This added touch of individual hospitality helped us to feel truly welcomed to the property. Located just across the street (and associated with the Inn) are a fine dining restaurant and pub. There is also plenty of great wine to be enjoyed in this region and you can also taste at winery locales within the village or just stroll the small shops and galleries in town. I can highly recommend the Inn on the Twenty for a special getaway.

author: MacBheathain
title: New Years Eve
text: .A very nice relaxed stay . The restaurant was excellent and the winery and shops are right there .Jordan is a very cute little village. Although it was a busy day and the dining room was full, no feeling of being rushed or crammed in. everything was calm and friendly excellent service. Same with breakfast the next day. The room was large and comfortable, Bathroom was large and nicely done, Just one very surprising mistake in my opinion. All the toiletries were made in China . Really? you cheap out at that point.

author: HappyTraveller9999
title: Family wedding weekend
text: What a pretty location. The inn is charming and beautifully decorated for Christmas. The dining room meals are delicious. The staff are outstanding. Cave Spring Cellars winery is just across the street. Perfect weekend getaway. Make sure you try the gem of a spa next door to the inn. I had a mani and pedi and a massage. Holly is the best esthetician I’ve ever had! Worth the trip to Jordan just for a spa day.

author: 796tannerv
title: Incredible experience
text: Spent the night here with my wife as a small getaway as we are from the Niagara area but had never spent the night at Inn on the Twenty. Or in Jordan Village for that matter! Everything was exceptional, especially the staff. They made sure that all of our needs were taken care of and were genuinely friendly. I also can't rave enough about the food in the restaurant. It was incredible. At night we walked down the street to the Jordan House for a drink and some live entertainment and we had a blast. The rooms were updated and well-furnished and had all of the amenities that we needed. Will definitely be coming back as a bit of a getaway in the near future.

author: winteringinPV
title: A few small disappointments
text: Overall, this is a lovely place to stay, probably the best in the Jordan area. However, it is also very expensive and therefore one expects excellence. Staff are wonderful and the facility and setting are beautiful but it is starting to show some age. The window in our room could not open, even though we saw other rooms with windows open. That would have been nice because the temperature control was always too warm and the room was stuffy. When we asked about it we were told that yes the room had an old window. The bathroom needed an upgrade. For that price we expected better than an unlit plastic shower stall. The included breakfast was good but they did not have soy milk for a non dairy alternative, and some of us are allergic to nuts so almond milk wasn't an option for my coffee. I am not usually this picky but, considering the price, we expected the best and it fell a bit short.

author: josev472
title: "Great stay, cozy and comfortable room"
text: Overall,it was an enjoyable experience. Friendly staff and everything across the street was fun. Wine tasting at Cave Springs was quite a treat!. Lots of little shops and boutiques near by. Dinning at the Tavern is just 5 min walk. Good food. Breakfast at the Inn was fine . I would recommend a night stay as a special anniversary treat!

author: BrantfordEfigenia
title: Excellent lunch!
text: Out for a drive on Thanksgiving weekend and decided to drop in for lunch. We both had the Winemakers lunch, I think it was called. 3 course meal starting with the mixed greens which were so fresh! Next my husband had the house made tagliatelle with ricotta. That was relay good. I tried the mushroom quiche- the pastry on it was excellent , the quiche itself was a little on the bland side. To finish we had the maple cheesecake that was delicious! Patty, our server was excellent!

author: Lawrence2300
title: Over rated
text: Every one says this is the place to stay in the area. It is very clean and modern but by no means luxurious. Air conditioner is wall mount and too noisy to run. Within the room, corners are cut everywhere. You would think that they would have mire than one bar of soap or a small shampoo well, sorry your wrong. Beds comfortable housekeeping good service solid. I blame management who are penny pinchers. Think of the guest instead of their pocket book.

author: DaveLon
title: Great stay!
text: We chose the Inn for our 47th anniversary for supper and to stay overnight. Service was excellent, very friendly and very helpful. The room was very clean and the king bed very comfortable. Only negative was that the A/C wasn't as quite nor as efficient as it might have been. Comfortable chair and sofa great for couples to sit and relax. WiFi fast. Hot and cold breakfast included - great biscuits, wonderful jams, eggs (you choose type) and bacon or sausage. The room and meal package allows you anything on the menu - three courses, wine extra. Highly recommended.

author: Waterdown
title: Good restaurant for lunch or dinner.
text: We had lunch here recently. The meal was light and interesting without over facing one. Even though it was three courses. The choice is good. The price is quite acceptable. The dinner menu is also very good. There are large windows in the restaurant givIng a good view while you have a meal. Parking across the street from the restaurant is plentiful. There are also interesting shops in the street if you plan on making a full afternoon of the visit.

author: PatriciaH853
title: We were staying at 2 nights at INN ON THE TWENTY to celebrate my son's wedding.
text: Our suite the"HAYNES" was cozy but spacious. Lovely, large bathroom, with a super tub and toiletries. Very nice to have Keurig coffee and tea in the room. Had it not been July the fireplace would have been delightful to nestle by in our comfortable seating area. Our only DISAPPOINTMENT was the lacking breakfast. The offerings at the paltry so called buffet were not appealing nor were they replenished. The served breakfast plates had eggs, dry cheap quality toast and 2 under cooked bacon slices - not too eye pleasing at all. Water was not given or offered and we had to beg for coffee refills. On the second morning at least the croissants were yummy. Given how great everything else about the INN is, a better breakfast and service is needed!

author: Daniela8511
title: Over-exceeded our expectations
text: My husband and I had a wonderful one-night stay at Inn On The Twenty and it absolutely exceeded our expectations. The town of Jordan is so picturesque. Our room at Inn On The Twenty was lovely - clean and neat, and the staff was delightful. The food at the restaurant was fantastic and our waiter was so pleasant and attentive and made sure everything was perfect for us. We dined by candlelight right by the window that overlooked the ravine. It was very romantic. We also enjoyed our wine tasting and bought several bottles of their Cave Spring Cabernet Merlot. We already recommended Inn On The Twenty to our family and friends. I look forward to our next stay!

author: Sandcastler
title: Beautiful and relaxing for a "WE" weekend...
text: We have stayed, played and dined at this beautifully appointed, friendly and relaxing Inn and it never disappoints. The Secord suite located on the frst floor was roomy and tastefully decorated. A large whirlpool tub, nice sitting/dining area and queen bed were excellent compliments. We ordered room service this evening that arrived quickly, hot and tasty. The gravlax was so tasty as was our roasted lamb dishes served with very tasty season vegetables and nice bottle of red wine that married nicely with our meals. The wine store at Cave Springs is expansive and conveniently across the street (for emergencies of course!). Breakfast in the dining room was relaxing as we gazed out into the valley through the wall of windows. A la Cart and buffett are both available..but why would we want to serve ourselves when we just want to be pampered?

author: ThomasToronto_Canada
title: Good food
text: The restaurant at the Inn was a very pleasant find. The atmosphere was upscale without being stuffy. The large windows overlook a very impressive treed ravine. We were there for lunch on a Sunday and had booked a table for eight. It was not crowded and we were not rushed. We were accommodated in the platform area which was semi private and it created for us an exclusive dining area which was very pleasant. The food was fine and prices reasonable. Service was first rate and friendly. We might go back for the pleasant impressive venue.

author: danieladJ2745NB
title: Very quaint and Very impressed
text: The experience from start to finish was amazing. It was a quick getaway and it was truly perfect. The rooms were well put together and included an intimate fireplace and jacuzzi tub in out room and when we received the room it was spotless. They thought of everything with luxurious robes to all the daily toiletries necessities, I honestly didn't need to pack anything! The customer service was amazing , they showed us our room and invited us to the local restaurants. I even forgot my purse at dinner and the next day when i explained the situation, they assured me that they would take care of it and they did! I was very impressed with the concern of my situation and the attentiveness. I would defiantly go back whenever we need a relaxing weekend away from all the craziness from the city.

author: alexander_rutherford
title: Amazing Stay
text: My wife and I were married at Cave Spring Vineyard and had our reception at the Inn on the Twenty Restaurant. We stayed two nights across the street at the Inn and have nothing but rave reviews. The rooms are great. Comfortable beds, huge bathrooms with whirlpool tubs, and comfortable sitting areas. We changed rooms during our stay, from a two floor room to a private garden suite, and the staff moved all our bags and boxes from the wedding for us. It was a seamless transition. The included breakfast at that restaurant was also delicious. Location-wise it is very close to a number of great vineyards like Cave Spring, Flat Rock, and Malivoire. It's also not far from Dillon's and 40 Creek distillers. All are worth a visit.

author: AMwoolfi
title: Wonderful staff and peaceful rest
text: My daughter and I came to Inn on the Twenty for a girls weekend away. We were warmly greeted by the Manager John. We didn't have time to book a wine tour and they took care of this quickly. We got great advice about what to see and do in the area. We had a loft room and it was quite comfortable. The bed and linen were sooo comfortable. My only comment was the bathrooms are getting dated - although the Jacuzzi is lovely and they are spotless. Lots of nice wineries in the area. The restaurant across the street served a lovely eggs beni and we had a great dinner of duck. Overall, a positive experience.

author: 618terrim
title: Great getaway!
text: Went there to relax and enjoy each other. They spoiled us. The room was very comfortable. The bed...slept like a baby! Took us to the room and would not take the tip! Later when checking out the building ran I to the gentleman who checked us in, gave us a history of the building. Loved it. Thank so much Terri and Pam

author: KAS2991
title: WAITING TO COME AGAIN
text: This hotel actually inspired me to get an account and actually write a review. This is my first. Absolutely beautiful. We had a giftcard and we used it in summer 2016.. We got a fantastic room on the bottom floor and we even got our own backyard patio (with fences so we got privacy, and even a private entrance!). It was an amazing room, We ate breakfast and dinner across the street. Its a more quiet and private area which we prefer. And perfect location near the wineries. Customer service was excellent.

author: Terramarique
title: Fine for a mini break.
text: A few years ago we had enjoyed a stay in one of the Garden Rooms, so chose one again, even though it was a damp January night! The rooms have been beautifully redecorated quite recently and we felt very relaxed in the elegant space, beside the fireplace. The bed was comfortable, traditionally dressed with top sheets rather than a duvet. The bathroom was very spacious, but we thought a walk-in shower with glass doors would have been more elegant than the moulded unit with curtains. (One caution: anyone with challenges such as arthritis in the hands could have difficulty with the faucets in the shower and washbasin, both very stiff!). The whole suite was clean and fresh. Staff at the front desk, in a very well designed lobby,were professionally welcoming, walking us through to the room.There is a stylish seating area outside the four garden rooms which gives a pleasant sense of a private area rather than an anonymous hotel corridor. In the morning, there was a hawk, sitting on the garden trellis outside our window, a perfect moment of natural peace before our return to the highway!

author: edwardc434
title: Great Time!
text: Our room was very nice, it was very large with a jacuzzi tub, fireplace, a sofa, highback chairs and two queen size beds. We ordered room service, it came from the Inn On The Twenty restaurant. I had never had room service that was this good before. The meals we ordered were wonderful. The next morning we had breakfast at the Inn On The Twenty restaurant as well. It was part of the included breakfast. The Eggs Florentine were fantastic. I have stayed at many nice hotels around the world but I have never awaken as relaxed and comfortable as I did at the Inn On The Twenty. I highly recommend it!

author: JoeBCanada
title: Cute Inn located in Jordan Village
text: We were recently married at the Cave Spring Vineyard which is affiliated with Inn on the Twenty so part of our package included an overnight stay at the Inn. The rooms were very spacious, clean and very comfortable. The staff at the Inn were also extremely accommodating with our wedding party and guests who also booked a block of rooms at the Inn. The cookies at the front desk were way too delicious too! We definitely plan on coming back to the Inn in the future. This place is not only charming but now holds a special place in our hearts. See you soon! :)

author: brianbond2016
title: Cave Springs
text: Pros: Beautiful, quiet, and the room was fantastic. Gas fireplace, big ceiling fan, very spacious bedroom & bathroom. Water pressure in the shower is fantastic & the bed was very comfortable. Breakfast both mornings was fantastic. Staff was very nice & helpful. Cave Springs winery across the street has some great wines for tasting and we ended up buying 7 bottles. Cons: Would be nice to have a microwave and fridge in the room as I thought this would be standard in all rooms today. One parking lot is not paved and does leave quiet a mess on a rainy day. Jordan is a beautiful little town but in isolation. The nearest Tim Horton's was 5km from the town.

author: CIAOMARYEH
title: Could of been a Perfect Romantic Evening
text: This Inn has all the offerings to make it a perfect romantic evening however, I was there on a business trip by myself – too bad…..! Walking into the quaint inn you are welcomed by the front desk with a quick check in and then given your key for your room – yes they still use actual keys. Upon entering my room, I was pleasantly surprised – it was beautiful. The room presented a gas fireplace (make sure you turn up the thermostat to get it to work), king size bed, desk, plenty of electrical outlets and a wonderful large bathroom enhanced with a large bath tub. Robes, slippers and quality amenities provided for comfort. My room being on the first floor also offered an outside patio. Parking is free and the town is a beautiful little place to explore not to mention the award winning wineries nearby. Unfortunately the day I was there the spa was not open but upon talking to others – highly recommended and one of the best spas in the Niagara area. Next time I am bringing my husband and taking full advantage of the lovely atmosphere!

author: 630babet
title: Twenty two retired semi-professional women out for lunch.
text: We were given a menu consisting of three choices. Two of which were heavy bread such as a Hamburg and chibattia bread sandwich. We were not given the regular menu. Prior to this we were given a different choice which was not available when we arrived. The service was fine and we tipped accordingly but were very disappointed. We seriously considered moving to the other room and getting full service. We did not receive any discount if you wonder. We are a local group and have children and grandchildren that heard the conversation being discussed over the Thanksgiving Holidays. Prior to this visit we enjoyed ourselves and were looking forward to our lunch.

author: ShinyBlueEyes76
title: Wonderful getaway
text: We enjoyed the hospitality and relaxing comforts of Inn On The Twenty... and I'm sure the best sleep we've had in a while! Our suite was beautiful and welcoming. The staff was available for whatever we needed. Breakfast was delicious both mornings. This would be a wonderful place to stay during the harvest (late September) or during ice wine season (January) where we would take advantage of the cozy fireplace that was in our suite. The cute little patio outside of our room was a perfect place for a glass of wine. Well done Inn On The Twenty!

author: jh492
title: Beautiful inn
text: Stayed at Inn on the Twenty on a recent trip to the Niagara Region. Our room, a Superior Suite, was huge. There is a separate seating area with a fireplace. The bathroom is immense. Tastefully decorated and very well maintained. The hotel restaurant is across the street. Had dinner and breakfast and both were excellent. Jordan is not too far from Niagara on the Lake, approximately 20 minutes. Charming town with a few specialty shops.

author: mamusia
title: Our favorite place
text: My husband and I took a three week road trip, starting in Detroit and basically circling Lake Ontario. After looking at all the choices for a bed and breakfast (our treat after roughing it camping for a few days), I chose the Inn on the Twenty. I left a message for a reservation, and was called back within the hour. The reception desk was very helpful in helping me choose a room and some upgrades (bottle of wine). We were so pleased with the room, as well as the restaurant right across the street. We had a slight problem with our fireplace (operator error), and the staff arrived in five minutes and took care of the issue! Dinner was amazing, and we experienced a very courteous and helpful staff throughout our stay. We will be back.

author: TerryC9510
title: A visit that never disappoints
text: This is our third visit to Inn on the Twenty. Our third two day package which included dinner and two breakfasts. The rooms have everything you need for a quiet getaway. And even more. The food is incredible as are the staff from the front desk to the restaurant. The Twenty Valley walking trails are just down the street but a part of the trails were closed when we were there. Hopefully they will be open on our next visit. Definitely our number one spot for a few days away.

author: KarenL269
title: Anniversary Retreat
text: This is our second stay at the Inn on the Twenty and I couldn't be happier. We booked a two night package. After attending the Shaw Festival, we drove back to Jordan and checked in. Our package included dinner at the beautiful On the Wendy Restaurant, a self guided bike tour of nearby wineries, lunch at the Jordan tavern and 2 breakfasts. Our room was spacious and comfortable, on the second floor with a king sized bed that was so comfortable, fireplace, TV, huge bath, robes and soft towels. The inn offered a locked room to store our bikes. The Place was quiet and restful, and the nearby countryside was spectacular. I feel like we have been away for a week and it's only been two days. Sad to be going home. My only complaint would be the TV was a bit small for being so far from the bed....but we hardly had time to watch it - so that's a minor minor thing.

author: tamrapags
title: The perfect wedding!
text: Inn on the Twenty hosted our wedding in July of 2016. Since the day we met our wedding coordinator, Sharon-Kay, her professionalism, attention to detail and customer “first” approach was most welcomed. She went above and beyond! The same applies for our day-of coordinator, Maribeth, who made sure the day was executed flawlessly. Our guests were very impressed and we have since received such positive reviews and feedback from family and friends; the venue, the vineyard, the accommodations, the food, the wine, and the service at dinner. This praise is a testament to your entire team and the way you do things at Inn on the Twenty, along with your culture of quality, service and friendliness. A big thank you to the entire team once again , for all your effort and hard work to make our wedding a very memorable one. Simply put, it was perfect!

author: 163pattis
title: A bit disappointing
text: This was our first time, and we started out checking in to a very hot two floor loft. They said there was a fan in the closet, no fan. So we went across the street for an avaerage dinner in their average restaurant and came home to no fan. So I asked again, and our room doesn't get a fan. We were so hot we couldn't sleep, and there was NO TV, pretty expensive and no amenities. No coffee in the room, bathroom is huge but very dated. In the am, we went to our included breakfast, it was a gong show. It took over an hour and no one knew what was going on. Returned to check out and they gave us a 10$ bottle of wine. Nice gesture, but geez.

author: MacFamily35
title: Relaxing & Luxirours Stay in the quaint town of Jordan!!
text: We received a gift card to spend one night at Inn on the Twenty. We had never heard of this town near Niagara. We were pleasantly surprised how beautiful and charming the town of Jordan is. The Inn on Twenty is also a beautiful hotel with well appointed and spacious rooms. A wine tour of Cave Springs was included as well, which is directly across the street. The breakfast, which is included, was very good. We did have some issues with the WiFi when we arrived, but they did acknowledge the issue and resolved the problem. Overall, the service is great and a wonderful location to be spend some time.

author: TimothyandLinda
title: Perfect respite
text: Impeccable hotel with great, unique rooms. Our family made use of two rooms, the Merritt Suite (a large suite with jacuzzi tub and private garden) and room '5,' (with loft bedroom and jacuzzi bath). Both beautifully furnished with good lighting. Good facilities, with iced tea and cookies on arrival, large reading areas outside rooms. Excellent, friendly staff and a great restaurant just across the street that provided complimentary breakfast. Complimentary wine tour was also part of weekend package. Hotel was quiet despite wedding party across the street. Entire area is quiet, with a bit of shopping and close to other wineries. Five out of five stars.

author: LifeTravel2011
title: Pretty, Quaint Inn — Jordan Village
text: Last minute weekday getaway — perfect for couple/family quiet time together. Excellent amenities, very spacious room + bathroom; extra high ceilings, grand windows that open for fresh country air! Walk across for breakfast — excellent buffet! Enjoyed 3-course dinner; varied menu and compliments to chef on presentation!! Cave Springs Winery Tour included (across the street). No car necessary here — it's all across the street:) Trails, small boutique shops and restaurant. Friendly service, easy check-in, polite service! Will return.

author: JoanneP50
title: Mothers Day treat...
text: We have been regular guests of the inn for many years. However due to a move in 2006, we are now reacquainting ourselves to the inn, its amenities and to the village of Jordan and surrounding area. The new and beautifully appointed reception area on the ground floor creates a very welcoming impression. Many of the rooms have been updated and refreshed. We stayed in room 15, on the second floor - the suite was well appointed, quiet, and the fireplace made it very cozy. Morning coffee was close at hand as the rooms have Kuerig coffee makers. The staff are welcoming and attentive. We were delighted to see many of the staff that we had known previously. There are lots of things happening in the village - a renovated 4 store mews was being outfitted with shops carrying products new to Jordan. The winery excels as usual - do try their Cabernet Franc Estate and CSV Chardonnay.

author: globalbouncer
title: Nice boutique Inn
text: Stayed at the Inn on the Twenty for one night and it was very nice, although very expensive and I've stayed at nicer hotels for the price. The room was quite large (Suite 9) and it has very nice windows overlooking the main street. The bathroom was very large with a whirlpool tub and separate shower, the fireplace and sitting area were nice (although we didn't really use it), and the bed was large and comfy. I just found the room and hotel accoutrements to be a bit dated or lacking considering $300+ price tag. This price did include a wine tasting across the street and breakfast- with one hot entree and a selection of baked goods and drinks. I also got a massage at the spa, which was pretty good- but too much talking! I wish that the intake form included an option for a quiet massage, so that you don't have to feel uncomfortable or rude asking for that. Also the town itself is quaint, but very small- only a few shops, a winery, On the Twenty restaurant, and a tavern (that was a further walk away than expected!).

author: MaraFromToronto
title: Wonderful inn.
text: The Inn on the Twenty is beautiful, and the staff extremely welcoming. From the moment we walked through the front door we knew our stay would be terrific, and it was. We had a large two-room suite above the spa, which was great since we brought along one of the kids and our dog. Having the space and privacy was great, although these rooms are not as fancy as the ones right in the Inn, but that was fine for this visit! One room was more of a living room with a pullout sofa. The other room was a bedroom. Both had large bathrooms attached. The food at the restaurant was spectacular, and the included breakfast was wonderful. We will be back.

author: CanadianShane
title: Impressive / historic Inn
text: Had a thoroughly enjoyable stay here recently. Got a very good off-season rate on a gorgeous and well-appointed suite. Unique and beautiful furnishings in a spacious layout. Luxurious bathroom. Wonky switch for the whirlpool gave my wife headaches when she was attempting to soak her bones. Pillows were almost totally useless for supporting your head and neck. Even doubled the pillows up to no avail. Staff were fun and professional. Would stay here again if in the area.

author: Karen19691969
title: Amazing vacation
text: We enjoyed 3 nights here during family week. It was lovely and quiet and the service was excellent. The room had an amazing fireplace and jacuzzi and we enjoyed it all as the snow fell outside. The spa services were excellent and my feet were very happy after my pedicure. Suzanne did my massage and then my boyfriend's and she was incredible. He raved about how much better he felt for days after she worked wonders with her deep tissue massage. !! Thank you Suzanne and all the staff at the Inn for a really wonderful getaway!

author: 499alyssas
title: Amazing room, service and food!!
text: The room we stayed in was so comfy and warm. We had a king sized bed and a sitting area with a fireplace. It was nice to turn on the fireplace and have a drink. The bathroom had heated floors with was a great surprise. The staff was so helpful and kind. This kindness overflows from the inn to the restaurant. The food was amazing... melt in your mouth steak! The breakfast was relaxing and quiet! Can't wait to go back for our wedding and then our first anniversary!

author: KimberleeCxx
title: A wonderful Christmas gift!!!
text: My boss got me and my fiancé a night here as my Christmas gift, and it was incredible!! She got us one of the 'loft' rooms where the bed, and HUGE master bathroom (with a standing shower and separate Jacuzzi tub) was on a 2nd floor. The bathroom itself was SO massive, it was insane!! The room was absolutely beautiful, and so comfortable and cozy... felt like a home away from home for sure!! It was so hard getting out of bed in the morning!! The breakfast in the morning across the street at their restaurant (included) was delicious and amazing as well! We also had dinner there the night before with my boss and her husband, and again, absolutely incredible!! Would definitely recommend this place to ANYONE!! :)

author: 309gloriap
title: Wonderful short getaway!
text: From the moment I called to book the room for a special occasion getaway to the moment we left, the experience was excellent. We were greeted warmly and the room (The Merritt) was excellent. They even had a small bottle of wine and a happy birthday note in the room. While Dec is a very quiet time to visit, it's also nice to have the place to yourself. We went to their restaurant for dinner and we were very pleased. The Manager made sure she got to know us. The meal was great and the next morning, the same Manager came by to greet us. What a nice touch!

author: IntSommelier
title: Showing Some Age
text: Certainly a comfortable we'll run inn. The suites are large with fireplaces and jacuzzis. The bathrooms and furnishing are showing age. The bed is comfortable and service is above average. At this price point you might expect a little more wow. Decidedly short on wow. Breakfast is below average for the area and the type of establishment. Eggs over easy with broken yokes, young inexperienced service, coffee on request, short on smiles, and a very ordinary sampling of serve yourself rolls and croissant. Clean but dated. Somewhat poor value.

author: kdimic
title: Great Niagara Vacation!
text: We had a wonderful time at Inn on the Twenty! We visited Jordan Station for a wedding at Cave Springs vineyards, stayed at the inn and enjoyed wonderful, complimentary, made to order breakfasts at the Inn on the Twenty Restaurant. Located in picturesque Jordan Station, the Inn was a wonderful vacation destination! Wine tasting at the associated tasting room, Cave Springs, was a great treat! We live very near Napa, CA and very much enjoyed the regions unique offerings! The Inn on the Twenty offered beautiful rooms, equipped with sitting areas and spacious bathrooms! The staff went above and beyond to make our stay amazing. At the end of each night, the concierge supplied us with milk for our children's bottles! Great vacation, I highly recommend staying at the Inn on the Twenty!!

author: TorontoLady46
title: A wonderful time in a beautiful Inn
text: The Inn on the Twenty is a wonderful Inn in a very pretty location. It is close to wine country and fabulous, scenic drives in the Niagara area. The staff at the front desk are professional, friendly and very knowledgeable. The alcove room was outstanding it was a large room with everything that you needed. You could immediately tell that there was much attention spent on details. It was a very relaxing time away. The Restaurant was also fabulous .....both food and service. We would certainly come back.

author: 643retiredguy
title: Great stay in the Niagara area
text: We had a garden suite on our most recent stay. The room is quite large with a sitting area with fireplace and the bed and bathroom in a separate alcove. The furniture was quite appropriate and we made good use of the entry table, desk, sofa and chairs. Since it was the middle of october we did not sit out in the garden but did enjoy the village of Jordan at the front door of the inn. There are lots of interesting walking opportunities in the area. One thing that could be improved is the location of the TV. It was really only visible from the bed and not from the sitting area. The restaurant across the street is always a pleasure.

author: travelval12
title: Relaxing stay
text: My husband and I stayed at this inn this week and we absolutely loved it. Our room was beautiful and relaxing. It had a king sized bed, a lovely sitting area and a soaker tub in the bathroom. Everything was immaculately clean and so very quiet. It felt like we were the only ones there. The service was excellent and friendly. We had a excellent breakfast at the restaurant across the road and there was wine tasting included with the package. The inn certainly exceeded our expectations. We will definitely be coming back.

author: Euro1
title: Delightful visit with friends
text: Two friends and I went on a girl's getaway to attend a play in NOTL. Neither of my friends previously had the pleasure of visiting Jordan so I recommended a stay at the Inn on the Twenty. We were all delighted with the Inn! The room was so comfortable and spacious due in part to the generous high ceilings and large window. The room and bathroom were very well appointed, spotlessly clean and stocked with extras. The suite looked like we were the first guests to stay there as it did not show the least sign of wear from previous guests. The included breakfast was a treat in the lovely setting of the restaurant and the hotel and restaurant staffs were all very pleasant and helpful. If I have to plan our next girl's getaway, it will be hard to top our stay at the Inn on the Twenty.

author: taylorg43
title: Unbelievable Visit!
text: My husband and I visited for an aniversary get away. The service was wonderful from the moment we walked through the front door; the front desk attendant guided us to our room personally and later assisted my hundband in finding a late night snack. The room was spacious and well appointed; bathroom facilities were well maintained, the jacuzzi was especially luxurious! The winery across the road was lovely, excellent examples of what Niagara has to offer. We did not dine at the restaurant but did stop in for a light dinner and drink at the Jordan House Tavern down the road. Excellent, friendly service, great pub food and a enjoyable vintage atmosphere. All in all a wonderful visit. My husband is tremendously fussy traveler, this is the first hotel he has stayed in and left without a single complaint (and with full intentions of returning again next summer!) Thanks for a great aniversary Inn on the Twenty!

author: sunnytales
title: One night get away
text: Stayed at Inn On The Twenty, as a get away for our anniversary. We were booked into the charming Coppers Cottage. This Cottage is situated steps away from the main Inn. We enjoyed a wine tour of the Cave Springs Cellars as well as tastings. Had a wonderful dinner at the Inn On The Twenty restaurant. Very nice to sit, relax and look out over the treetops of Jordan Valley. My husband and I also had breakfast in the same restaurant the next morning. Just nice to be away and be pampered.

author: BonnieMT
title: Excellent Rooms, Service and Ambience
text: This was our 2nd time staying at this hotel. Both times it was a gift (a "Life Experiences Package"), and both times it was fabulous! I don't know why, but it just feels soooo relaxing here! The rooms are very large with very high ceilings! The washrooms are also giant, and have a wonderful large hot tub that fit both my spouse and I. We felt so refreshed after our stay here, and it felt very romantic. Breakfast was also included in the package. The restaurant had a beautiful view, with beautiful music playing in the background, and the food was excellent! The package also included a wine tour, which was also excellent! My spouse and I will definitely be returning - on our dime next time - and will also be getting this as a gift for my parents!

author: Chris-Phileas
title: Great Getaway
text: Stayed for a weekend in the Farrell suite. We had a lovely romantic getaway. The room was very clean and the staff were very friendly. The food at breakfast was excellent. We had dinner at the Inn On The Twenty restaurant and we tried the wine tasting at Cave Springs. The town is very small so there isn't a lot to do but relax. We had lunch at the unWined Restaurant which was very tasty. The only negative point was the shower was very small however the tub was huge. Looking forward to going next year.

author: 621tanyab
title: Beautiful visit
text: Overall great trip. We stayed there for our wedding night. Suites are beautiful (we had guests in the hotel so saw a few of them). Staff was friendly. There was some construction happening at the front of the building but I'm sure it's all completed by now. Suite was beautiful for taking pre wedding pics in. It was like a tiny village with some shops and restaurants across the street. Recommend.

author: 643retiredguy
title: great getaway weekend
text: We have stayed several times in the past and this stay kept up our high expectations here. Rooms are in a old warehouse/factory that has been reburbished. Further work was going on now but the workmen were very good about not making noise outside of daylight hours. We had a large bathroom with whirlpool and separate shower, lots of water pressure, not always a given in older facilities. The main room had a raised sitting area with loveseat, chair and wall mounted TV. Breakfast was included, at the restaurant across the street. Buffet plus a hot selection that changed day to day. One possible drawback is that the lift is not easy to find but this may change as they are moving the lobby from the second to the first floor.

author: MDCOH
title: Absolutely Fabulous Experience
text: We just celebrated a special wedding anniversary at Inn on the Twenty this past weekend. What a hidden gem! The Inn itself is beautiful with luxury rooms. The staff were amazing. They ducked in and out leaving romantic treats (part of our pkg) and restocked our coffee and water when needed. The meals were absolutely amazing. We also took a 'How to Massage Your Partner' class at the Spa on the Twenty and it was just a fun and great experience! The Inn is tucked away in quiet little Jordan but you are so close to so many places such as Port Dalhousie, Niagara-on-the-Lake and Niagara Falls. Truly an amazing experience. We will definitely go back!

author: 570helenw
title: Wonderful hideaway with great service and amazing food
text: We spent three nights in March. It was still snowing and very cold but the wonderful rooms with fire and a sofa were the perfect place to sit with a glass of local wine watching the snow through the patio doors into our private courtyard. On arrival, certainly in the winter the town of Jourdan seems desolate and the front of the hotel is nothing special. However don't be put off. The welcome from the staff is warm and the rooms are luxury. The restaurant is actually across the road but breakfast was very nice but dinner was the real treat. The food deserves a Michelin star and combined with local wines it was a great. We will definitely be back, it's worth the drive from Toronto and was the highlight of our trip from the UK.

author: Robin6155
title: Anniversary Bliss
text: My wife and I returned to the Inn on the Twenty to celebrate our first wedding anniversary (we eloped there last March), and everything was, again, perfect. We chose the same room, The Rittenhouse Suite, which remains extremely spacious, quiet and beautiful, and took advantage of the Carpe Diem package (2 nights, dinner at the restaurant, and breakfast both mornings - astonishing value). We stayed Sunday-Tuesday morning, so the prices were very affordable, and because the Inn is so much quieter during the week we did not hear a sound nor see another guest except while we were dining for breakfast and dinner at the restaurant. The breakfasts are simple yet elegant, and the dinner we had to celebrate our anniversary was fantastic (beautifully prepared food and professional service without being pretentious). We enjoyed a short 30-minute drive to see the Falls, and lavished our palates in 4 outstanding wine tastings at several regional vineyards within 15-minutes drive of the Inn, including Cave Springs across the road -- such a beautiful escape for a few days. But perhaps the greatest element of our stay this time, like it was the first time, is the people at the Inn and the restaurant. From the woman (can't remember her name now!) who checked us in with such a great sense of humour and who took us personally to our room, to our breakfast and dinner servers (our waitress for dinner was so wonderful, even encouraging us, despite the fact that we were the last ones in the restaurant, to take our time and to enjoy every last minute and morsel of our dessert course long after all the other diners had left), to our checkout with the incomparable John, they all treated us so professionally and yet so warmly and with welcome familiarity. It was so nice to see them all again, to be remembered by them, and to know we'll see them again next year for our second anniversary, if not before then again this summer.

author: plchic
title: Perfect mini getaway
text: My husband and I wanted to get some R&R and enjoy the wine region. This was our first visit and upon entering the inn, the staff were extremely friendly and honest. We stayed in the Honsberger suite and we were so surprised at the space. The only downfall for this suite was the heating/air conditioner unit as it was loud. I was not able to sleep though the night. Other than that we enjoyed our stay. We also enjoyed this inn as it was close a winery, Cave Springs. We ate at the Inn on the twenty restaurant next day for breakfast. The service and wait staff were great. We had the salmon hash with poached egg and it tasted great.

author: NausheenPickering
title: Excellent Hospitality
text: Booking a room during Fall (November) was affordable compared to summer prices. The charms of a quaint little town where the townspeople were proud and happy to shower their hospitality on the guests. Free bottled water, warm blanket on the couch, current magazines in your room and attention to details to make you feel welcome. The stores promoted works of local artisans, beautiful art work on display. There was also an antique store with European antiques. Gifts and fashion choices to match your budget. It was definitely a lovely town to visit just 10 minutes away from QEW tucked away to be discovered for nature and serenity lovers and shopping adventurists. Food at the restaurant was excellent and there was free wine tasting as well. It Was a lovely get away close to the highway and a short drive to Niagara Falls.

author: HighcroftManor
title: Wine, luxury and fine dining: what more could you want?
text: We stayed here for just one night in late January (birthday treat) but it was absolutely delightful. We had often wanted to stay here, and had enjoyed lunch in the excellent restaurant more than once. But this was our first time at the Inn. And it was everything we had heard. The room (more like a suite) was perhaps the largest we have ever had anywhere. It was L-shaped, with the bed on one side, and a lovely sitting area around the corner, with couch, large chairs and a gas fireplace. An extremely comfortable room to relax in, and sip some of the excellent wine we had purchased in nearby wineries. Dinner in the restaurant that evening was first rate. Comfortable, relaxed, and luxurious - a perfect trifecta.

author: LindaG607
title: A Wonderful Get Away
text: My husband recently took me away for a night at Inn on the Twenty. The room was spacious and beautifully decorated. The king size bed was on a raised platform which was well lit for night time. The room included a sitting area in front of a gas fireplace and a flat screen t.v. Appetizers and a chilled bottle were in the room when we arrived. The washroom was ample and the jacuzzi was large as was the shower. A real spa like feeling. Would love to visit this hotel again in warmer weather as I hear there are some magnificent trails near by. The staff was very helpful and attentive.

author: mamarip
title: Wedding Bliss
text: We stayed at the Inn on the Twenty for a family friends wedding. The Inn was fabulous! The room we stayed in was stunning and extremely large. I wish we were there for more than a night as we really didn't get to appreciate all the Inn had to offer. It is not cheap, but you definitely get what you pay for! And I could only dream that I had the bathroom this room has. It was spotless and upon our arrival from the wedding the beds were turned down and chocolates placed on the nightstand. Jut another small touch that made the night awesome! We had a king bed, while our "kids" had the room across the hall with two queens, oh and they both had fireplaces too, something that came in handy as it was chilly out. Can't say enough good things about the place, really really nice!

author: tourist_TO_Cdn
title: Sidestepping Niagara Falls
text: The street was a little empty.. The village was one block end-to-end. Right across from the Vintage Hotel.. Once you stepped in, you will be attracted by the setting with big windows facing the entrance, green garden just outside, the sun setting with the Niagara Escarpment beyond the tree line. Appetizer: Salmon Tartar was franked by the crispy cucumber, very fresh & tasty on the thin toast while my wife had the browned sea scallop which was still very soft inside. Main course was a pan fried Erie pickerel fillet top with read & yellow cherry tomatoes, while my wife had a medium rare rib steak on top of a bed of mashed pumpkin. As for desert, the chocolate cake accompanied by a scope of mango ice-cream with a dash of strawberry sauce was just heavenly. Of course, my wife skipped dessert after endouging in such a nice dinner!!! Service was execellent especially with the waitress coming from Toronto...

author: L0ve_t0_travel63
title: Total Class!
text: We were at the Inn on the Twenty for a family wedding. Everything from the rooms at the Inn to the ceremony site at Cave Springs Vineyard and the reception at Windows on the Twenty was done with complete class. All the staff was very attentive, the girl setting up the ceremony site wanted to make sure she set up the site just perfectly, while we were there just checking on things. She was very pleasant. The reception dinner was superb! Many compliments to the chef, kitchen and wait staff! The Inn is located in a quaint village perfect for a quiet or romantic getaway. Add amazing food, excellent wine and a spa...what more could you wish for? Can't wait to return!!

author: Voyageuse038
title: Relaxing Getaway
text: If you are looking for a peaceful, very clean place to stay, this is it! Situated in the heart of Niagara Wine Country, the Inn on the Twenty offers huge, tastefully decorated rooms with high ceilings. The rooms are like a suite and also include a gas fireplace and a huge bathroom with a separate shower and a whirlpool bathtub. All sorts of amenities are provided in the bathroom, including in room coffee and tea. Across the street,they have their gourmet restaurant, whose huge panoramic windows face the luscious Jordan Valley. We enjoyed a beautifully cooked dinner and a free full breakfast there. The service was excellent. Next to the restaurant, there are all sorts of shops, including a wine store where we were provided with free wine tasting. Other cafes, shops and restaurants are also situated on Main St., where the hotel is located. In the evening, we also took a long walk in this peaceful little town and truly enjoyed our short, romantic retreat.

author: Busterthechihuahua
title: Huge Disappointment
text: We had had a beautiful lunch here the year before and were so impressed, we decided to book dinner and a room after a trip to the Shaw Festival. The room was absolutely beautiful with high ceilings, a gas fireplace, and a sumptuous bed. The bathroom had a gigantic spa tub that we were really looking forward to after our meal in the restaurant. Dinner in the restaurant was absolutely terrible. The only vegetarian option on the menu was a pasta, which we both ordered. It turned out to be so poorly cooked that it was inedible--a good third of the penne (if that's what it was--the noodles were apparently made in the kitchen and looked like misshapen solid tubes) was hard and stuck together. It was tossed with peas and some kind of flavourless oil. We went back to our room with a bottle of wine we'd purchased at the wine shop, and ran the spa tub....only to find that the jets didn't work and the entire side of the tub fell off while the bath was running (we kind of propped it back up). We half-heartedly had a glass of wine in the bath that was just a bath since it had no working jets, and climbed into our sumptuous bed....only to be woken up every fifteen minutes by the loudest air conditioner in existence. We were really expecting something special because it is very expensive, but it was an enormous disappointment.

author: KellyS492
title: Beautiful Inn
text: We stayed here for a weekend in early March to attend a wedding. From check in to check out, we were accommodated for everything we needed. They helped us understand parking, they provided us with little extra's when required and the rooms were amazing. Large, spacious, luxurious. Bathrooms are almost more luxurious then the rooms! It was romantic and quiet even thought it was full. The room package we got included breakfast at Cave Springs restaurant across the street the next morning as well. We loved the atmosphere and great customer service here. Well worth the money!

author: ItsMrsG
title: Beautiful property, decent service.
text: My husband and I stayed here as we were in town for a wedding. The hotel was very unique and had a lot of character. Free parking was great too! It was great to have a mini-fridge in our room. Our room was extremely spacious and clean. I found the staff to be okay. They weren't rude, but the service wasn't where I would expect for a boutique hotel. The worst was when we had breakfast on the day of the wedding and the server was not pleasant at all, until he found out that we were having breakfast with the groom of the wedding to be taking place that night and it was like he just flipped a switch and was completely 'on the ball'. So they have shown that they can have excellent service, but perhaps they just reserve it for some guests?

author: Canadian013
title: Exceptional service and comfort
text: Inn on the Twenty is the best boutique hotel we've ever experienced. Classy in every way: very clean, tasteful decor, very comfortable bed, and exceptionally friendly and attentive staff at not only the hotel but also the restaurant and Cave Springs tasting room. When we arrived, we were delighted to find a complimentary bottle of wine and wineglasses ready in our room along with a hand-signed 'Happy Anniversary" card: nice touch. The first night we walked a short way to the Jordan House tavern, where we enjoyed a live band as we ate a pub-style supper. We had the "Carpe Diem" package, which includes 2 breakfasts and one 3-course dinner at the beautiful Inn on the Twenty restaurant across the street from the hotel, a winery tour/tasting and a bottle of wine upon departure. All of the food was excellent, and the servers were second to none! The whole experience there was very pleasant and relaxing: it made our 35th anniversary extra-special. There is no question we would go there again!

author: travels4kicks
title: Slightly disappointing
text: Unfortunately our stay was a little disappointing, I was expecting much more for the price I paid. The room was nice we had a loft room, however just before we were going to sleep the toilet did not flush, luckily in the lofts you get 2 bathrooms. I'm sure they would have come to fix the issue but we were just about to go to sleep, so we didnt push the issue. The bathroom was dated and the coffee maker was in the bathroom close to the toilet. Only when we were about to leave did we notice what I thought was a brush was actually a plunger, which only says to me they had issues to begin with (as I read later in a review from Oct 2013, with the same issue). Because the bed is in the loft the bed area is very warm, the air conditioning does not reach up to the loft area they did provide a fan, but again not exactly what I would have expected from a top notch hotel. The staff was friendly and when we left we mentioned our issues, and she did give us a small credit but a credit was not what I was looking for, I paid to have an exceptional experience. I've read some other reviews and they seem to be positive, I'm only telling my experience so others can be wary. The Inn on the Twenty restaurant was a different story, the food was excellent, as well the shops in Jordan are lovely and quaint. I would visit Jordan but stay elsewhere.

author: Libandma
title: Extraordinary spa experience at half the price...
text: While searching for a mother-daughter spa get-a-away my favourite (high end ) spa was going to be $1,100 for one night. While looking for an alternative, I found a identical package at half the price. This is how I came across the The Inn On The Twenty. The whole experience was so pleasantly unexpected from check-in to our breakfast. Our room was spacious with a lovely sitting area and large bathroom with lots of counter space. The spa services were wonderful in particular my massage from Holly. The dinner at the restaurant was haute cuisine with a wonderful view of the valley. Service was so welcoming from the front desk to our breakfast server. Quality, value, service, these are the things that keep people coming back. And we will.

author: margaretf337
title: Not What We Expected
text: My husband and I invited another couple to join us for a fun evening in Jordan, however we didn't have the experience we expected. First of all, I was shocked when I realized our room was charged to my credit card the day I made the booking. I was told upon arrival at the registration desk (which was difficult to locate and at the top of a long flight of stairs) that this was standard policy. I have never encountered this before!! My friend gave her credit card to pay for her room, but I learned later that my credit card had been charged for both rooms!! I was not impressed!!! Then, we were sent down the street to the Jordan House Hotel -- not the Inn on the Twenty. The rooms were nice but nothing special. The Jordan House Tavern, next door, had great food and the entertainment was outstanding. The Inn on the Twenty website sounded much better than what we experienced.

author: JohnC15544i
title: Surprisingly Average !
text: My wife and I have been looking forward to a time where we could stay and experience the INN on THE TWENTY......we did just that on New Years Eve with another couple with great anticipation. The expectations of the property ; from the ambiance of the old INN , to the Spa to the much noted high acclaimed restaurant attracted us, along with our friends ; to bring in the new year (2014)in style . .....the room was very nice , quaint , comfortable ... could use an upgrade, not over the top by any means but rather old world charm which we enjoy. ......the Spa was quite sparse, and the relaxation area and change rooms were not set up to truly escape....the massage therapist (Rebecca) was very good ! .......the food our most anticipated part of this experience beginning with dinner was not that great and memorable only as being average! The breakfast in the morning however was fantastic. ...as for the staffing ALL were extremely , pleasant and accommodating, shout out to Paul in the restaurant and the ladies on the front desk. We have decided that only a return trip in the RIGHT SEASON (summer/fall) will satisfy our curiously, as New Years Eve may not be the best time to evaluate the INN on the Twenty!

author: dlr51
title: Charming oasis
text: The inn is located on a quiet street in a small village. Formerly a storage building for the local ag industry, it was rehabbed into a boutique hotel. Most of the rooms are mini-suites, well-decorated and very comfortable. Fireplaces and oversized bathrooms are also a common feature. My wife and I have been spending our wedding anniversary there for a number of years. The Inn is affiliated with On the Twenty restaurant across the street. A night's stay at the Inn includes breakfast at the restaurant. The village is surrounded by vineyards and there are dozens of wineries within 10 miles. It is also a short drive to Niagara-on-the-Lake, home of the Shaw Festival and many restaurants and shops. It's a great place to stay!

author: rieslingca
