I explained we don't have much use for air con in UK. All the staff at this hotel very helpful and cheerful. The rooms very clean, the food was good for a three star AI, something for every one. Just one thing that spoilt it the spirits on the AI not very nice. Would recommend this hotel value for money.

author: SophieE761
title: Does the job
text: I really enjoyed my time here, the staff couldn’t do enough for you! The food was edible, a bit samey towards the end as I find with all inclusive but I couldn’t really fault what was served, all hot and fresh and replenished quickly. The hotel is basic but very clean. The pool area is fantastic! Bar staff were lovely and friendly. Agios Georgios is definitely my favourite part of the island and perfect for relaxing and enjoying just how special the Greek Islands really are. My only gripe with this hotel is that they cancelled the Greek night, (which is what I was really looking forward to) for football. Other than that, we had a great time and would recommend.

author: 825alanc825
title: OUR TEN NIGHT HOLIDAY IN MAY 2018
text: We were on a 10 night holiday arriving on 13.05.18. We were in room 2018 which was on the second floor and had a wonderful sea view from the spacious balcony. The room size was OK and the bathroom had a bath and a shower which was very handy. There is a lift to all floors. The food was OK with a different variety each day and the dining room was clean and bright. The swimming pool and grounds are kept spotless and there is a bar with shaded seating when it gets to hot. The inclusive drinks package is limited to local wines,spirits and draught beer and starts at 10.00 AM and finishes at 10PM which I think is to early. You can still get drinks up to midnight but you have to pay for them. We were dissapointed that there is no beach in front of the hotel and you have to walk up the road for 250m where you are charged 6Euro for 2 sun beds and a brollie. Overall, the place is very good value for the money and provides a nice quite holiday.

author: sharontH7215BZ
title: Corfu holiday
text: Not good. 4 of us down with some sort of bug, as was every other person in the hotel. None of the staff seemed interested when I reported it and even denied it when a Thomas Cook rep phoned and asked reception. Food was awful. Scared to eat it after the 2nd day as had been ill for 36 hours. Paid all inclusive but ended up eating and drinking out every day and night as food and drink was terrible. In fact it has put me off all inclusive all together. Never never again would I return to this hotel. Even if someone else paid for me!!

author: 240cassiee
title: My family are currently staying here!!
text: My family are currently staying here and after a 3 hour flight delay arrived hoping this would be a dream holiday. But after only being there 2 days woke up with the worst diarrhoea and sickness!! The worst thing is the whole hotel has it due to the dirtiness of the hotel and lack of food hygiene! The chemist is a 45 min walk, the hotel is in the middle of no where! Food is kept in a hot server all Day! The hotel is old and dated and everywhere is dirty. Will be taking this further... EVERYONE THINKING OF BOOKING HERE DONT!!

author: Michal_Si
title: Honeymoon relax
text: We have spent our honeymoon in the Golden Sands Hotel. At first, we thought that hotel is rather old and it needs refresh but, what is more important, it was very clean. The best thing of the hotel was the personel - very positive, helpfull, and puting tourists in first position - as a example, during trip to Albania we had a huge delay at the border and it was obvious that we will be late to the supper. We decided to call the hotel, tell about our situation and ask to prepare us some sandwiches. When we got to the hotel, it tourns out that the kitchen has prepares for every trip member a full, warm supper. Food was variated, very tasty, however some dishes could be better seasoned (my own opinion). The pool bar servs mainly local alcohol that has is weaker than typical Polish vodka or brandy, but if you aks barman, he easly pour into glass more alcohol to maintain the power :). To sum up, we can recommend this hotel.

author: JulieH454
title: Not what it seems
text: Upon arriving at this hotel all seemed well, the staff were very friendly and helpful. However the following day we found that the all inclusive drinks were very limited not even allowing Diet Coke or hot chocolate, after speaking to the receptionist Diet Coke was added on,but the alcoholic drinks were very limited compared to any hotel I had ever stayed in before. The best meal of the day was the breakfast which was not amazing, the lunch and evening meal were not very nice. There was chips most lunch times but nothing nice to go with it so I had chip sandwiches, evening there was not any chips so we ate out for half the week. If you have children there was nothing no nuggets, pizza, burger fish fingers nothing. This hotel did not cater for the typical british family. The table cloths were very dirty and hardly ever wiped let alone changed. The most shocking thing that happened was on the morning of our departure we were not being picked up until after 6.00pm but our all inclusive bands were actually cut off at 12pm and we were told we could not have anything to drink from that time but could have lunch and then nothing after 2pm I have stayed in plenty of hotels and this has never happened before. If you are visiting this hotel especially if you have a family please save some euros for after they cut your band off. If you are thinking about this hotel look else where.

author: ivankovacek
title: Agency arrangement for 10 nights
text: Where to start - Summary; If you can please avoid this place! if you do not have money for something better spend it on your girl at home If you want to know why: The only bright point - personnel - they are really trying but you cannot fix this failure with nice attitude. Area is nice, cannot say. You want a car but not from LordTravel something ... Cons: -overly expensive for the service it offers -terrible food, you have to fight for that terrible food -All inclusive is utterly joke here. No really - I haven't heard better one long time ago. We are buying our water coffee and tea.. I have tried everything they offer as a package and I cannot refer how bad is wine, beer, even water. Vodka is pure alcohol. -rooms needs new furniture since 1950, Enough said

author: frogo2012
title: Can't wait to go back!!
text: Coming from the hospitality industry, this hotel is as stated "functional" Yes it is a bit dated and the bedroom is basic but honestly, you only sleep and change in it. Food, there is plenty of it and lots of choice both hot & cold. Grounds were lovely and everywhere very clean. Beautiful fresh water pool and well maintained every morning. Pool side bar has music playing all day and night yes there is some people who don't appreciate this but they are the minority. The best beaches are, Lakkies as it is more peaceful and Sandy beech for all your water sports. George and the whole team are fantastic and make the whole experience more memorable, can't wait to go back!! :-) Remember it is a cheap & very cheerful holiday hotel.

author: 327iang
title: Brilliant!
text: Fantastic place highly recommended. Food is lovely. Never laughed as much. The staff are extremely friendly and very helpful. Bar staff very entertaining. Reception staff couldn't help us enough with problems with our transfers etc. Cleaner was in everyday with fresh bedding and towels and the place was spotless every time. Love her wanted to bring her home ❤️Maggie never forget you

author: Mal-Nutrition
title: Great staff could not make up for the shortfalls
text: Excellent service. Food a real disappointment: barely any choice and just as little daily variation. Entertainment one night in our seven. Building fabric 'tired'. Nice pool with enough sunbeds for a late-September customer level. Inclusive drinks finished 2200 hrs. Contrast with Agios Giorgios town/village, where restaurant fare was very good and the welcome amazing. This experience demonstrates what happens when businesses try to do All Inclusive inside the EU economy: unhappy hoteliers; unhappy local businesses; unhappy customers.

author: ToonmanUK
title: Back in Time!!
text: In 1975 the Golden Sands would have been a jewel in St George's sand, fast forward to 2016 and it's lost nearly all of its sparkle, thing is it wouldn't take much to bring back a shine. The rooms are dated, the bed's are the most uncomfortable I've experienced in all my travels. The bathroom had an odour and how much would a newk shower curtain cost? Now the food, it's an all inclusive hotel it's 3* and this is Greece but...... It's repetitive, I'm by no means a fussy eater but I do like a standard of quality that wouldn't be hard to achieve the food here fails miserably. The quality of the drinks on offer aren't much better, "rola cola" and the weakest beer on the market. Poolside is ok no complaints there. There's no evening entertainment bar a "night of Greek Dancing" which to be fair was entertaining. Now why on earth did you book this hotel I hear you saying; well it was cheap and the money saved on the accomendation meant eating out wasn't an expense. Finally, a friendly Hotel, we met some really nice people Alan, Helen and Gary ,Bill and Lorraine And Karen .Its in a very quiet location (all be it a little bit past its sell by date).Would I return, no, would I recommend to a friend no sorry...I like to keep my friends friendly

author: donnamariap
title: 7 day all inclusive
text: Me and my hubby booked this as a last minute holiday. We couldn't fault the hotel staff or food. The only negative was entertainment we arrived at 4am on a Saturday and was picked up to go home at 10.50pm on Friday, the one night they had entertainment and it was a Greek night..... gutted as it looked like a really good night. Mosquitos are rancid outside I got bit alive and no matter what I used they still bit and I ended up with an allergic reaction. We had no mosquitos in our room and the room was spotless, clean bedding towels and room cleaned every day. All inclusive stops at 10pm but wasn't a problem for us as we where ready for bed by then. If you are a fussy eater then go self catering and dont moan about food choice. A lot of people have slated the hotel for this but we loved everything we ate. Big thumbs up to you all at Golden Sands because we absolutely loved our week with you and despite all the bites it didn't spoil the holiday.

author: katiepA7543WM
title: Awful
text: Horrendous!!! I went away with my family and 2 year old. Hotel advertises it caters for kids...does it heck!! Rooms are minging...dirty.... Really dated...and Smell. Food at hotel is shocking..no variety what so ever same food everyday... Pool area dirty and beds and chairs all falling apart!!! Bar tenders and staff miserable and rood. No entertainment at the hotel...and u have to pay for drinks after 10 pm. Crap

author: milenak483
title: Perfect vacation for family
text: I love this place. People are so nice and friendly. Food was tasty and fresh. Rooms cozy and clean. We're enjoying every minute of this beautiful part of Corfu.Beach is 50 meters from hotel. Small and perfect for kids. Warm and clean water. I think 10 days isn't enough for this kind vacation. We're definitely coming back again!!!

author: Derbyshiretravellove
title: Cecilia derbyshire
text: Stayed at this hotel the last 2 weeks in June. The reception staff are very friendly and checked us in very quickly. Our room was on the 2nd floor and had a lovely side sea view. The room was very clean, plenty of storage space, a fridge, a tv but couldnt get any english channels (even bbc world was frozen until the last day), but we were not there to watch tv. Room was cleaned and towels changed every day and the beds were changed several times. We are not fussy eaters and really enjoyed the greek salads, but the rest was fairly repetitive but always fresh and well cooked. All the staff, cleaners, reception, waiters, bar staff and especially George were all very friendly and helpful. We were always able to get a sun bed and umbrella, and the pool is great. This is a very good 3star hotel.

author: pomp1
title: Compliments
text: I was there now twice. When you go for a holiday - what do you want? Sun? Seaside? Food? Good friendly people? You have it at the "Golden Sands". If you are going to holidays only to look for reasons to critizise, better you stay home, where everything is perfect.

author: clegg5810
title: Just back from a lovely holiday
text: just back we stayed for 7 nights returning on the 28th + for what we paid we have no complaints it was a lovely quiet break which we needed. first off if you whant 5 star treatment then go + pay for it instead of complaning this is a 3 star hotel. will start with the staff from the lovely ladies on reception to the cleaners to the dinening room to the bar staff always got a smile on their faces + i found them very polite so thank you for that golden sands while i was there i had bad prickly heat rash + spoke to the lady on reception within 10 mins the doctor came + prescribed 2 lots of creams + tablets + i saw him again the next day. room cleaned towels changed every day. enjoyed all our meals found them to be warm +tasty if you can get a room with pool + sea view worth payin a bit extra we tried to up grade but they were full. 5 mins up the road is a nice little beach with sunbeds + parasols which belong to the pub XL they don,t charge you for using them if you have a drink there which was nice for cooling off in very plesent surroundings. 20 mins up the road to the right is a long sandy beach we did,nt go there because we were happy with the XL beach which is what we called it. went on a bus trip to corfu bus leaves about 10.25 + departure 4.30. hope i have given you some good information ps if you like busy busy busy areas this is not for you enjoy anway

author: steveharris4fs
title: Great Hotel
text: We stayed at this delightful hotel from 19th - 26th September. We arrived around 1am to be greeted by George on reception, he was very friendly and also provided us with a sandwich each, as they thought we would be hungry after our journey (very thoughtful). Our room was very clean although basic and dated, provided with a fridge and air conditioning, both free of charge. There is no kettle in the room, but we took our own travel one, so could still enjoy a cup of tea first thing and last thing! Breakfast has plenty of choice, from yoghurt, fruit, toast to cooked items, all buffet style so help yourself. The pool area is very clean and looks as though newly stoned around the steps. The pool bar serves plenty of choice of drinks from coffee to cocktails and during the day served by Katarina, who was very friendly. The reception desk staff were very friendly a big hello to Aspasia and Spiridaila and the hotel owner Dimitris. All were extremely helpful and very friendly. We would stay here again and would recommend this hotel.

author: CosminCandin
title: Great and relaxing holiday
text: We stayed ant this place in September 2015, we were surprised by the hotel location, room and facilities. The staff is very kind and helpful, the food is plenty and diversified, we found it to suit all tastes. The rooms are clear, the towels and sheets are changed on daily basis. The surrounding area is great, we liked it extremely well.... Tip1. If you go in the area be sure not to miss the Korissioni lake(hope i remember it right). Tip2. Also be sure to visit Zack's Restaurant(very close to hotel), there is a beautiful garden and nice staff, beside excellent food.

author: donna1969
title: Nice Hotel
text: We stayed here 18th September 2014 for a week, hotel is a little dated but had a great view over the pool and to the sea (room 221). Resort was very quiet (end of the season), there was entertainment at the hotel on 3 nights. (nothing to exciting). I feel the room could of been a little cleaner even though we saw the cleaners daily. Food, Breakfast was the typical bread and cheese you was lucky to get a boiled egg. Evening meal was OK though we ate out a couple of times, Try APPLE do a lovely steak and the portions are massive. For entertainment in the resort you have to see Elvis.......we did laugh. My favourite bar was Europa Bar best Pina coloda in Corfu in Europe I'd say :-) Overal this is not a bad hotel the staff are very helpful just a few small improvements would go a long way. And yes I would stay here again.

author: Sunshineluver2014
title: Great ,Relaxing hotel
text: My friend and I stayed 14-21 September rooms were clean and spacious . The beach is just across the road or you can enjoy the pool in the hotel with bar and free wifi . The staff are AMAZING !! And go out of their way to make your stay enjoyable. I would like to say a special thank you to Yannis, Espacia ,George ,Alex and Katerina they work tirelessly and really make you feel at home. The only improvement I would make is the bathrooms are a bit dated and could do with a face lift and evening meals could be a bit more versatile. However as a 3 star hotel you get good value for your money and you will definitely have an enjoyable stay. Andrea and Ellen.

author: 257janets
title: Much Improved from last year
text: We were very disappointed with this hotel last year but due to its superb position we decided to give it one more try. We are so glad that we did. The room we had was at the front of the hotel with a sea and pool view and was very comfortable. We stayed on bed and breakfast and there was a good selection of food. George the waiter is great, full of fun and very cheerful. Yuannis, the owner's son, manages the hotel and he and Aspasia on reception are fantastic, always willing to go the extra mile to help. The pool was clean and there were plenty of sun beds along with some hammocks and swing settees. The pool bar serves nice lunches at reasonable prices and the staff are very friendly and attentive. We have booked again for September we were so pleased with our stay

author: bajenleker
title: A quite good greek 3-star hotel.
text: This is a typical 3-star standard hotel in Corfu with a nice location, so do not expect wonders. It was built 1985, but has been renovated since, the the old radiators is still on the wall, and a fridge in the room, which can be noisy. We took a last-minute charter and picked this hotel despite some "not-so-good"-reviews on the travel-agency site. It was reasonable clean, the staff was very friendly and helpful. The breakfast was up and down, some days quite good, some days not so good, did not ate at the hotel at evenings. The pool-depth starts at 1,40mtrs and ends at 2,50mtrs plus a smaller pool for the children. A playground, tennis-court a small basket court etc. Location is a bit off from the center of Agios Georgios (South), 600 m, but close to a nice beach. Can be tricky to get down to the beach, do not use the nearest sign pointing "To the beach" just outside the hotel, instead take left and walk 50 meters and you´ll find an easier way down. I rate it between average and very good, but leaning to higher, due the friendliness of the staff.

author: KirstieD255
title: Just what we wanted!
text: We stayed here for a week from 20th September. It was just what we wanted and a bit more! The area is quiet but there are plenty of tavernas and restaurants to choose from and the beach is very close. The hotel was great, the staff were friendly and helpful. The rooms were a little dated but clean and the food was ok. The hotel were getting ready to close and guest numbers were low so the choice of food was limited. The pool, bar and restaurant were well kept. If you are looking for a quiet relaxing week this is a great place to stay 👍

author: LubicaM
title: Wonderful end of this summer
text: We spent here a nice week on 2-9 September 2013. Hotel is situated in a quiet part of Agios Georgios, a small village lying in the south-west part of Corfu. Its rooms are nice, sea view was worth money and food was also very good, everybody was able to find its own taste including the English breakfast - I understand while the English guests are so frequent here. Staff was very kind, they settled everything with a smile... At noon when it was too hot we could swim in a wonderful swimming pool in front of the hotel surrounded by palms and we enjoyed perfect privacy, really nice. It was a wonderful end of this summer season; we enjoyed large sandy beaches where you get on foot in about 15 minutes and then you have nobody on the beach! Moreover, you can go to the excellent "Taverna Malibu" a white-blue restaurant where you can enjoy not only fresh fish and Greek specialities but also wonderful sea view and kind service, even its menu is available in many languages! We were really happy to choose Golden Sands hotel with its hospitality and privacy instead of going to the all-inclusive hotel resort on another side of Agios Georgios - we simply don t support this kind of touristic industry and globalization... Thank you!

author: IlianaT21
title: Wonderful hospitality
text: Hotel staff offered us an excellent stay. They were hospitable, sociable, communicative and helpful in anything we ask them for. Our room was clean and decent and so the hotel’s common sitting area and the restaurant. I need to point out that the food in their restaurant was palatable! They also have a really nice outdoor bar near the swimming pool, which hosted different events. The hotel is located in a quiet district and nearby you can find beautiful sandy beaches. There are also bars and night clubs not far from the hotel. The hotel is approximately 40 minutes from the airport and 50 from the city center.

author: 957janc
title: Great holiday
text: We have been guests at the Golden Sands now for many years. The hotel is friendly and the staff are really great. Rooms are clean and serviced well by the cleaners - what more do you want clean sheets and towels changed regularly. There are rooms to accommodate couples and families and nothing is too much of a problem. This resort has one of the best beaches in Corfu - sandy and safe for children. Well done Ioannis and the team. See you next year. Jan

author: KandJEssex_England
title: Great Value!
text: If you are looking for a great value hotel with high standards close to a sandy beach then look no further. The hotel is comfortable, clean, offers great service and overlooks a great sandy beach. The restaurants nearby are numerous and of a high standard at reasonable prices. The Il Mare Italian has a super location in a small cove, right by the water and the Oceano at the far end of the resort does fantastic Prawns!, This resort is ideal for couples looking for a relaxing break. A trip into Corfu Town is easy as the bus stops right outside and only cost £2.50. The breakfast at Golden Sands is plentiful and typical of a hotel catering for a mix of guests from across Europe. We were booked on a B&B basis, but dined in the hotel restaurant one night due to a thunderstorm keeping uas indoors. The menu is limited and the food was average. With such good restaurants nearby at very competitive prices, i would not recommend the half board option. This was a great value holiday and we are already looking forward to returning soon!

author: randeet2018
title: Low budget resort for Brits
text: If I had small and hyperactive children this might be the perfect spot. There is close proximity to the beach, a big pool, loud music and a pool table. As far as enjoying anything particular to Greek culture, people or tradition - forget it. In general, I think we might've been happier at the Northern side of the island. This area seems to be only about Brits on cheap holiday. The hotel was average. I had made a mistake in booking a day earlier than needed and they refused to adjust the bill, saying "every other hotel wouldn't do it either." This was a drag and unexpected, as the hotel was far from full and we're basically talking about a typo. We've been to Greece often and never Corfu. My husband speaks Greek, so we had the best times leaving the area and going into smaller villages.

author: bruce050
title: great hotel and surrounding area, we will return
text: What a great hotel, lovely friendly staff and very helpful. Rooms are ok and there's loads of storage space (unusual in Greek accommodation), the fridge comes in handy. Breakfast is continental style buffet with ample selection. We have been to St.Georges before and love the sandy beach nearby. Lots of tavernas in the area, Makis and The Balcony are two good ones that are at the other end of the resort (turn right out of the hotel, about a ten minute walk, brings you to the slightly busier end). For lunch (and dinner) try Zacks taverna opposite the beach, we had lunch there every day . No sea view but the food is very good and the gardens are very pretty with lots of shade. We will certainly go back to the wonderful Golden Sands Hotel.

author: sandruljak
title: Relaxation =)))
text: On the coast of the Aegean, is the jewel of holiday hotel Golden Sands. I work with people like Hr Selector , and I needed peace, warmth and fresh air. All that I found through a travel agency GPR International at the hotel Golden Sands. Decent housing, clean pool, varied food and sandy beach. Are you looking for a vacation where there is no noise, where is peace?! This is my recommendation. P.S. All praise for the kindness and professionalism for manager of the hotel Ioannis Sourvinos. Greetings for the most charmihg waiter :))))

author: Danijela_DR
title: Great place for the families
text: My family and me have arrived at Golden Sands Hotel where we had 11 day half board stay, on 24th of June, Golden Sands Hotel is situated in the near the Central part of Agios Georgios, surrounded by shops, restaurant, and cafe bars. Hotel rooms are large, meals are rich, service excellent, But what makes difference among hotels worldwide are the people - personnel. Make you feel like you're home. It's very important that they're very tolerant for the children's misbehavior , as well as their avoidance to respect hotel's rules. Golden Sands Hotel is charming, a bit old fashioned place, and if you can't survive without Hi - Tech space shuttle like accommodation, this place won't suit you. But for those who prefer acceptance, warm family atmosphere, this is probably the best place in the world. For more adventurous spirit, Golden Sands Hotel is a perfect base for some further exploration of the Corfu island, due to the fact that there are plenty of the Tour operators offering sailing through underwater caves, Paleocaastritza, Bella Vista, etc. There's a large outdoor swimming pool, ( water is always clean), with a bar, and the possibility of having a meal on the pool. MR Ioannis, the Golden Sands Hotel's manager, is one of the nicest people you will ever meet and he goes the extra mile to make sure that each and every customer is happy and having the time of their life. We're looking forward to visiting that lovely place again.

author: IvanaanavIIvanaanavI
title: Low higiene, not for kids!
text: We spent 10 days in this hotel last June, and I cried for first three days and worried about the health of my two years old son. After that, we decided only to sleep in the room, and during the day we were discovering the town Corfu, trying not to think about the hotel. The room was not touched from the previous season, full of dust, with awful smell, the bathroom was dirty and old. When you take the shower you have water everywhere because there are no curtains! It was awful. The pool area is not cleaned once during our stay. Food is also poor and repeatable. It`s not suitable for the families with kids! If you wish to enjoy your stay on this beautiful place, choose other hotel!

author: JILLV395
title: Good location
text: This hotel is conveniently located to the UNESCO sites, within walking distance, as we didn't have a car. The room was adequate but nothing special although it had a modern bathroom. however the beds were very firm, but to me it is the same through out Europe, (I travel with an air mattress to put on these beds). The breakfast was basic European breakfast, good but not elaborate. The best part of the stay was the fellow at the front desk. He went out of his way to help us and our friends who stayed here to arrange travel after our stay in light of a train strike. Not only was he helpful, but hilarious and had us laughing out loud, (his English was very good). I would stay here again if back in the area.

author: 609FionaC609
title: Quiet hotel, but a lot of steps
text: We spent three nights at the Hotel Diana and found it very quiet in the midst of a bustling city. It is within walking distance of the main shopping and restaurant areas. Driving to the hotel took 1 ½ hours from the outskirts as Ravenna is a nightmare of one-way streets and with an 18 year old map we got lost many times. But eventually we ended in up the carpark near the hotel; the hotel provided a long-stay parking ticket for it for only a couple of euros. Our room was at the back of the hotel down a long corridor and up and down steps, but it was quiet. We found the WiFi fine (perhaps it's been upgraded) and had no problems with it at all. Our biggest problem was with the shower which was built into a corner of the bathroom - and the doors didn't open very far. Too many pasta dinners and one of us would have been stuck in a very embarrassing situation! The breakfast was good and I was impressed with the choice of honeys (not something you often see). The hotel provided a handy (up-to-date) street map with a list of local restaurants on the back - show the map when you pay in a restaurant for a 10% discount.

author: VictoriaL770
title: Super placed hotel for the Unesco World Heritage sites
text: While this is only a three star hotel it plays well with the big boys. Located in Ravenna centro it is within walking distance of the five sites on your all church sites ticket. It is very quiet, close to restaurants and interesting shopping choices with spotless well appointed rooms and clean bathrooms . They have a small fridge for your use, air conditioning you control and a flat screen television . Parking is only 2euros a day a short walk down the street. The staff is friendly and helpful and the breakfast was generous. Pastries , yogurt, dried fruit for the yogurt, a selection of cereals, rolls, toast , a huge selection of jams and honey, butter, cream cheese, Nutella, and meats and cheeses. I probably left out something but no one should start the day hungry. For Americans this hotel Eco conscious...electricity is turned on by inserting your room key in the slot by the door, you are asked not to waste towels etc. It was a wonderful experience.

author: SurreyGoldfinch
title: Hospitable and centrally located
text: Warmly greeted with a cappuccino, we enjoyed our stay at this hotel. The rooms are not fancy but are very quiet and comfortable. There is an elevator. The main sights with the magnificent mosaics are all within short walking distances. The included breakfast was varied with meats, cheese, cereals, breads, fruit. The wifi was excellent. Parking was easy and close by. The staff were very helpful and anxious that we should know where to go and what to do. I have no hesitation recommending this hotel and would stay there again.

author: marshypops
title: Lovely hotel.
text: We stayed here for 4 nights during July. The staff were friendly and helpful, they could not have been more so. We were able to borrow bikes from the hotel, Ravenna is a bike friendly town and I found it to be quite safe. We rode to Classe and back without any problems. The room was clean and tidy, we even had fresh flowers. It was a bit small but I don't spend time in my room so it wasn't a problem. There was a great range of breakfast items to choose from and a pleasant dining room. When we return to Ravenna then we would be delighted to use this hotel again.

author: HL314
title: Great Hotel with one suggestion to be greater.
text: My wife and I stayed at this hotel for 5 nights and really enjoy our superior double room, top class service and assistance from Fillipo and his team. Breakfast was really nice. The room was very clean as was the ensuite with one exception. The massaging arm chair was tremendously welcoming after long days of wandering through the interesting streets and lanes of Ravenna. As with some of the other reviewers, my wife was surprised by the amount of obvious black mold in the grouting between the tiles in the shower cubicle. At home, we use a mold removal detergent spray on our shower cubicles every month or so. It works. Just the same, a big thank you to Fillipo for an enjoyable stay. We'll be back.

author: TallSteve2014
title: Metallic Green.
text: Stayed for 2 nights. Convenient location for walking into city centre, but coaches not allowed in street meant a 200 metre walk with case to reach hotel. Hotel quirky in some respects. Despite lift, there are likely to be some stairs to rooms. Reception is up a short flight of stairs. Enigmatic decor in our bedroom - metallic green and a poem/quotation painted on the wall. Small balcony overlooked a very overgrown garden. Lovely pastries at breakfast.

author: pourgirl1
title: Great location, kind staff, tiny shower stall
text: Hotel Diana has a perfect location near the treasures of Ravenna, and it's maybe a 15 minute walk from the train station. The staff were always very friendly and helpful, and breakfast was excellent. Our triple room was bright and cheery, I assume in a newly renovated area. The bathroom was also fresh and clean, and roomy except for an insanely small shower stall. I literally could not get through the door. My tall slim husband was able to get in, but had to shower standing straight and tall. And don't drop the soap - there's no way to bend down! Lovely bathroom otherwise, but this was a real drawback.

author: Jagggs
title: Great location and price, easy parking
text: This hotel is very well-located for visiting the UNESCO sites (and all the other wonderful things in Ravenna) and parking nearby is not a problem (but finding the hotel is tricky because of the 1-way streets). Hotel Diana is adequately furnished, the bathrooms are modern, WiFi is free, and the beds are firm. The only toiletries provided are bar soap and tube of body wash on the shower wall. No tissues, no shampoo, no frills. Breakfast was fine and the breakfast room staff was pleasant. I think the much-admired Fillipo must have been away for the weekend as the "welcome" and hospitality were lack-luster. I was expecting the warmth described by other reviewers, but we didn't find it. What we did find, was a clean, comfortable hotel of the 3-star level, a quiet room and a great location. Not much tourist information in English. We could walk everywhere we needed to go, and after the hill-towns, the horizontal nature of Ravenna was very welcome!

author: ConnieM368
title: A stay to remember
text: I just returned from a spectacular trip to Italy with my husband, son and a very good friend. Staying at Hotel Diana will be one of our most memorable experiences. From the minute we arrived, the hotel staff was attentive and made us feel right at home. Our rooms were clean, bright and spacious. The breakfast was impressive and once again the staff was top notch. Flippio took it upon himself to arrange a city tour for us and recommend exciting and wonderful restaurants for us to visit. I wish all hotels had the level of service we experienced and I want to thank Fillipo and the rest of the staff for making our stay so remarkable. I for one can't wait to return.

author: esfesq
title: Refused to credit my card after cancellation
text: We had a very sick small child and could not travel. I called the Hotel Diana and spoke with a very nice gentleman who said it was OK, and we would not be charged. We were. I emailed the hotel referencing my conversation and requested a credit. Nothing happened. I called and spoke with a woman who said there was a mix up, and that she would have my card credited and would respond to my email. Nothing happened. I regret leaving this type of feedback, but I hate businesses that treat customers like this.

author: mariae955
title: Friendly but very simple hotel. Needs redecoration.
text: Friendly but very simple hotel. Needs redecoration. Breakfast with very little proteins but apart from that a wide range of foods. Lots of sugar though. Non functional minibar, warm inside. 2 bottles of water in it (warm). Friendly staff. Difficult to find the hotel with car. Get a map in advance ti find pedestrian zones.

author: Sharmiro
title: Lovely, large & bright
text: Although I did not arrive particularly early, the superior single use room I reserved was not ready, but the receptionist upgraded me to their "comfort level room" without hesitation. I had walked from the train station, in the rain, and I was ready for dry clothes. The room was lovely. Bright with a good window, and spacious, with a grand size bathroom ( by European standards.) I was delighted. Breakfast was on the sumptuous side, with lots of choices: fruits, meats, cereals, breads and more. Self served in a glass enclosed garden room, I enjoyed it both days of my stay. The pictures provided by the hotel are very representative I definitley recommend. If there was one complaint, a map to the hotel from the train station would be great, as it is an easy 10 min walk-unless you get lost!

author: EdwardRabbit
title: Clean and warm
text: We stayed 3 days in October. room was large and clean. Staying on top floor we found the room almost too warm and had to sleep with skylight wide open. Bathroom large and spotless, waterflow good. Breakfast ok would have appreciated a fruit option and a proper coffee with milk - the machine only provided espresso with or without powdered froth. Nice breakfast room in conservatory. Service helpful and efficient rather than friendly. Wifi good.

author: lektor
title: Nice, but poor A/C
text: A very pleasant and satisfactory one-night stay at Hotel Diana: Very centrally located within walking distance of all points of interest. Good beds, no noise during the night, fine bathroom and excellent cleaning, high-standard buffet breakfast including fresh tomatoes and green salad leaves, - something a traveller from northern Europe always finds regrettably absent from Italian hotel breakfasts. Very pleasant and helpful reception staff. Parking in the hotel garage at 12euros or at a public parking lot nearby at 6 euros. Two drawbacks however: Quite difficult to find when driving into the city and without a GPS. Spent an hour driving around, endlessly confused by the one-way streets, and had finally to park the car and walk our way to the hotel. Turned out to be quite easy when we got a map with driving instructions from the reception. Problem two: Got a room at the top, a loft room, and the A/C had virtually no effect on the room temperature. With a day temperature of about 30 degrees Celsius it made for a sweaty night indeed.

author: James_In_Italy
title: Nice Hotel at a Moderate Price
text: My wife and I stayed one night in a double ("Matrimoniale") room. The rate was 90 Euro. I pretty much concur with other positive reviews. The room was clean and quiet and included tv, A/C, and private bath. They also had a free internet point in the lobby (not working at the time) and wireless connectivity in our room. We were on the garden side, but there is not much traffic at night, so I imagine even the street side would provide a good night's sleep. The staff was friendly and the rate included a nice breakfast (served downstairs 0700-1000). Parking is made a little easier by a covered garage and large open parking lot both within one block. Hotel is an easy walk to the Tourist Office which is also very helpful and offers free bicycles for tourists.

author: RickandRos
title: An excellent choice
text: We spent a week here in May-June. I agree with the favourable comments others have made about the staff, the food and the location. We paid a bit extra for a Superior room, which was a good choice. Some of the rooms we peered into seemed quite small, but ours was a good size, as well as being clean and well-appointed. The hotel is only a few minutes walk from the centre and the sights. Don't miss the covered market. Driving in Ravenna is a real mystery. There's a network of one-way streets clearly designed to deter through-traffic (and a good thing too). So if you're driving, get the hotel to send you instructions on how to get there. Don't just think you can follow your nose across town.

author: ziadanna
title: Great value
text: The hotel is a short 4/5 minutes walk to the town center and max 10 minutes to all the amazing historical sites in town. There is a gated parking lot right next to the hotel (10€/24hours). A party of four, we booked two adjacent double rooms. Rooms were really small, but very comfortable: excellent bed, modern flat TV, a very large and clean bathroom. Breakfast is superb, wide choice, and pleasant surroundings. Staff was friendly. We had a great time. If i really really wanted to be picky, the temperature in the breakfast veranda was defintely coolish.

author: FionaBell
title: Hotel Diana was the best!
text: In July 2004, we spent a day in Ravenna to see the Byzantine mosaics. We arrived a little late and decided to spend the night. We'd heard of the Hotel Diana and decided to check it out. We were very glad that we did. The lobby area was very open, light and clean. The desk clerks were all extremely friendly and we had no problem communicating. Our room was large and slept four people without any of us feeling cramped. The bathroom was spacious, had a shower/bath that didn't leak all over the floor and also came with a basket full of amenities. The breakfast was also a full spread with meats, fruit, cereal. The hotel is not far from the center of town and is definitely worth staying at if you're in Ravenna.

author: JohnCracknell
title: A good hotel
text: The hotel is on a one way street next to the Parque de la Concordia. The middle of the street has tram lines. Their are no longer any trams - so, if you arrive by car, it is ok to leave your car their whilst booking in. The hotel has its own garage. The rooms are well equipped. The bed was a bit hard for me. One of the window hinges was broken, so it whistled with wind noise. Breakfast was varied and good quality. The wifi was good and free.

author: claire_walker12
title: Excellent hotel, food so-so.
text: The hotel is clean, comfortable and with its own secure parking. It’s conveniently located for shops and places to eat. Staff were very friendly and keen to help with advice on the the town and what to see. The rooms were large and the beds comfortable. Our only complaint was the food. We eat earlier than the usual Spanish nighttime meals and we were told that we could get light meals in the cafeteria earlier, only to discover when we got there that we couldn’t get anything until 8.30 p.m.. I refused to pay for one course after finding an insect in it, and the waiter’s response was’t helpful. The quality of the rest of the food was OK and the wine was good for the price. A good place to stay, but maybe eat elsewhere!

author: davey2828
title: Great value for the money
text: Great value hotel right in the center or jaen and walking distance to everything. Parking not easy but can pay to park at hotel12 euros.very unfriendly staff on reception but that was only down side. Room clean but no fridge, says it's 5 star so think we should of had a fridge in room. Room was ok but basic amenities seeing that it's meant to be 5 star. We have stayed in this town before and there are better hotels just outside the area but we tried this one for a change. It was ok and right where we needed to be. Price was great and included breakfast booked through booking com . I would not stay here again but would recommend it as the price was good. They just need to be a little more friendly and welcoming at reception as this is where first impressions are made.

title: Wedding Celebration
text: We had a lovely room with all amenities. Beautiful trrace for breakfast on main street. Noisy but lively. very well attended by locals and tourists. This summer the hotel had opened a superb roof terrace and bar where you could meet friends. Friday night was packed, but staff soon made seats available for those who wanted to sit down. Spectacular views all over the area and the castle on the hill, illuminated at night. A great place to stay if you want to be central.

author: danlE8512JA
title: Nice place to stay for a few nights
text: We stayed here in late January visiting our daughter. Very nice premises - marble lobby and nice restaurant for breakfast next store. Rooms are comfortable - nice firm bed. It would have been nice to have had some English language channels on television (although I'm a Spanish speaker). Also beware of rooms facing the plaza - there is a nightclub on first floor and noisy until 6 am over the weekend. Finally, I didn't think staff were overly friendly or helpful. They did their jobs well but didn't seemed that interested in greeting or conversation with guests. But central location and clean rooms and good value made this an all right choice.

author: marchamona
title: Absolutely 4*
text: Pleasant décor, must have been 'lightened' recently as not all brown. Good size rooms, very comfortable beds. Big bathroom with all amenities. Needs a bit of soundproofing though. Don't book breakfast, unless you eat a lot, the hotel cafeteria is excellent and serves passing public on the terrace, so prices are competitive. Continental breakfast pre-booked €9. Coffee, juice, croissant/toast, €4.30 on the terrace, slightly cheaper inside. I pre-booked the underground parking and luckily took a small car, or I may not have fitted in. Extremely tight. Bit of an incline on the street up to very centre of town/Cathedral.

author: senorita2013
title: Good Location but basic facilities
text: The hotel's in a really good location, between the historical centre of Jaén, and the new 'bulevar' area, so we couldn't fault it for that. However the facilities were very basic, and the hotel's really in need of renovation. There were car park facilities underneath the hotel, which you had to pay for on a daily rate, but it was very hard to drive in and out of. However this seemed our only option in the middle of the city. The hotel was very hot at night, even in February when it was very old down in the street. Hopefully they'd sort the air conditioning out in the summer months! As Jaén isn't a classic tourist destination we didn't really expect them to speak much English in the hotel, but they didn't seem to have a word between them, which was unexpected and difficult to deal with at times. Overall the location was good, but we'd prefer to stay somewhere else in future

author: 58Tinlady
title: Not What's on the Website
text: The picture on the shown on the website represents only a VERY few rooms that have been updated. Our room smelled of cigarette smoke, the carpets more than worn, the bed rather uncomfortable and the heating/cooling system old and antiquated. The wifi code is listed on the telephone only our phone had no placard. The curtains were falling from the ceiling and there has no doubt been a water issue. The hallways are outdoors so if it's winter time best be dressed warm. The elevator not only took forever but a few of the buttons didn't work and it's very warn. If you don't mind staying in a dorm listening to the folks next door pee in the middle of the night than this is your place. On the upside Phil who was running happy hour is quite nice and a pleasure to speak with.

author: JamieHtravels
title: Needs an Update
text: This hotel is in a nice location within walking distance of downtown, shops, restaurants, etc. There is even a train stop in front which I was worried would be loud, but wasn't. The staff was very friendly, we were given warm chocolate chip cookies at check in, and maps of the city. We were happy to see that they had their own parking lot when we pulled in but surprised that they charged $18 a night to park there. Breakfast was included in the price and was okay with eggs, bacon, bread, fruit, yogurt, juice, etc. As for the room and hotel itself it's in serious need of an update. Picture dirty floral carpet, floral bed spreads, heavy popcorned and stained ceilings, old tile in the bathroom, outdated lights and furniture, classic things that you would see at a Motel or old Super 8 style hotel. We did see a sign at the desk offering updated rooms for more money which I personally think is ridiculous because everyone wants an updated room and shouldn't have to pay more for it. We were there when school was out so it was pretty quiet.

author: nocellphonegirl
title: Do not recommend
text: Front desk staff is supremely rude and inept. They lost my reservation, then took my credit card but their machines were down so they told me to come back. I came back after a while and I'm not from this town. So I wasted my time, came back and then they told me they didn't charge me, lied about taking my credit card information all while acting very rudely, kind of like robots on steroids. I know sometimes mistakes can happen, but if I can't even get past the front desk people, then I know it's a crappy hotel. Judging from the other reviews, I'm glad I did not stay here after all. Maybe it was the universe protecting me from an even worse experience. I would not recommend a place where people are so rude to their customers.

author: 863mistys
title: It's disgusting. Will not stay here again.
text: Chose this place because of the close vicinity to OHSU but it's filthy. Outdated, old, that I can deal with, but this place is downright gross. I found black curly hair in the bedding, on the pillows, in the shower, the carpet is filthy and I won't even walk barefoot on it, seriously,and the mattress keeps slipping off the box springs whenever I move even the slightest bit. I'm not feeling comfortable crawling under the bedding. I'd leave but my room is nonrefundable and it's already almost midnight. I would have been better off in a $30 crappy hotel somewhere else. Also, there is an unexpected parking fee of $13 if I leave before 8am or be charged more if I stay longer than 8am. I'll be leaving much sooner. Oh yes, the staff didn't even remove the last renters key cards from the slot on the door. I just feel like they didn't make hardly any effort at all to clean between renters :( not money well spent.

author: 398michaelm398
title: More than just a bed for the night
text: A hotel in the centre of Portland including a full buffet breakfast for at the time under $70 per night.... amazing value.... so why isn't it full every night. Might have something to do with the dark and dreary corridors to the rooms, or maybe the fact that the bar closes every night at 9pm. The rooms are good the bed comfy the heating excellent, the bathroom dated but clean, the water pressure low. Now going back to the breakfast which I was looking forward to. Its in a room like a dining hall, no character, no feeling, oh and that includes the staff on the morning I was there. Oh and dont forget to clean off your plates and cup after you and put them in the plastic box, the correct grey plastic box. Small things could improve the experience like put some small spoons over where the tea and coffee is dispensed from, not over the other side of the room. At a good price this place is well worth it and an ideal place to see Portland from as the bus/Max stop is right outside the door.

title: Great value for a city escape
text: We wanted to spend a few days in the downtown area of Portland. This hotel was a great choice. The rooms are large, comfortable & clean. The hotel is in the university area & has convenient access to the tram & bus routes. An added plus is the full hot breakfast buffet that's included in the price. There are lots of things to see & do - arts, museums, restaurants, and of course locally made beer & wine. Staff are friendly, welcoming and kindly answered all of our questions. We would definitely stay here again. Thank-you!

author: Inspiration741705
title: Ok, but could use some attention.
text: Good hotel, but outdated. Shouldn't have to move the bed or desk to get to outlets. Bed was comfortable. Room is clean. Coffee and tea well stocked. Furniture comfortable. Staff were helpful. Breakfast comparable to other hotels in price range .

author: 736travisj
title: Great location
text: Fibe stars for location to south waterfront at the price. Nice landscaping around pool. Close to the trolley and buses. Very quiet. Clean. Good views. By university. Good staff choice for our room location. Pet friendly

author: BridgetT908
title: Great price and a great location.
text: We stayed here for a wedding. Couldn’t have asked for a better price. Because it was so good we extended for a long weekend. The location close enough to downtown to walk which was exactly what we we wanted. The rooms are a little outdated. The TV didn’t work when we arrived but they fixed it right away. Good breakfast. We would stay again!

author: anitakj1210
title: Nice hotel, friendly staff, good free breakfast!! Great stay!
text: We stayed at this hotel during our roadtrip from West Canada all the way to San Francisco. The desk clerk was very friendly at checkin, even asking us if we had a preference for a floor! Pleasant surprise was that free breakfast was included and also a complementary chocolate chip cookie for both of us. Very nice touch! Our room was on the third floor, 2 queen beds. Spacious and clean. Yes a bit outdated, nonetheless a pleasant stay! Breakfast offered many options and good way to start the day!

author: MamacitaMorenita
title: Great for PSU Visit
text: The hotel's location is ideal if you are visiting PSU. Every part of the campus is within easy walking distance from University Place. In fact, you have access to light rail, street cars, and buses. Traveling from PDX on the Max was super easy. We upgraded to a large and quiet comfort room. The furnishings and finishes were tasteful, and the room and bathroom were very clean. I would have rated the hotel higher if housekeeping had remembered to service the room. They didn't, so I had to remind front desk staff on two different days to send someone to clean our room. Other than that, I loved the hotel, its affordability, morning breakfast, and welcome cookie! Next time I travel to Portland, I plan to return to this hotel.

author: F4420BJemilys
title: My son had a procedure done at dornbechers in portland. We stayed in room 362.
text: Big mistake, The staff was not friendly, there was stains on comforter, the wallpaper was peeling from wall, it was pretty ghetto. The shower didnt really drain when we took a shower. We called the front desk to let them know we weren't happy,and tub wasn't draining...the receptionist informed me it was probably just because there were so many people showering at the same time. And they were super booked. There was a few spots of black mold on the ceiling in the shower. And burn holes by the sink in the carpet. I was very disgusted but after a long day at the hospital and having to be back at 6 in the morning, we suffered. so we were literally there for 8 hrs. On top of paying over $100 for the room, they tack on an extra $15 for us to park there. Do not recomend this hole!

author: M8206DJcatherines
title: Lots of good things, but some negatives.
text: I stayed here for two nights in 2018. I didn't really engage with the hotel staff too much but they were very polite, knowledgeable, and friendly. Restaurant staff were great and the food was excellent. The room was fairly standard regarding amenities and they upgraded me to a larger bed which was nice. My only real issue was with the building itself. Corridors (which are outside) were dark and kind of creepy late at night, as there appeared to be unlocked doors leading outside the hotel to the street. There were a couple minor negatives with my room: one drawer on the dresser was missing a handle and appeared glued shut; furnishings were a little worn, and the heater/air conditioner was very noisy. I wouldn't stay here if you are a light sleeper: I could hear traffic noises all night and sound traveled so easily between the rooms that I could hear the person in the room next to me passing gas and snoring. Overall, I think I would stay here again because it was a good location, moderately priced and had decent amenities, but if there was something in a similar price range and location I would pick that one instead (but come here for the food).

author: _lauraborelis_
title: Stay here! (and avoid wasting your money at over-priced boutique hotels)
text: This was my first time visiting Portland and I chose this hotel for two reasons: cost and location. It was significantly cheaper than all the other hotels in the area and it’s walking distance to Pearl District (or take a street car just a couple blocks away). I value a clean room, basic necessities and good customer service. This hotel ticked all those boxes. It also has a nice pool area and good sized complimentary hot breakfast. The concierge was very helpful at providing us some ideas of things to do. Yes, the building is old and it could use a paint job but it suited ourselves just fine. We’d stay here again next visit.

author: 431JB
title: Dirty
text: Was going to give it 1 star, but figure poor is a better description. Had black mold in health club, which they removed after I showed them a picture. The hall rug outside the room had dental floss on it entire stay, despite being reported. Room keys often took 3 tries, was told they will be replacing all locks. The elevator in b wing was dirty, had flies, smelled terrible. Room wasn't made up till after noon several times. Had to push door open with foot or shoulder. Little fridge and microwave nice. Front desk staff nice. Getting to hotel from airport took over an hour at 3:15 PM, told it was rush hour by taxi driver.

author: fayo400
title: Great central location
text: We stayed for a night on our recent trip to Portland. This property is centrally located and walkable from downtown or else the MAX rapid transit stop is right across the street.This is an old property that has had a face lift at some point in the past. They do a lot of conferences and meetings. It is right next to Portland State University. The room was fairly large. The bed and sleep quality were great. The towels nice and fluffy. The free breakfast was more than adequate - hot and cold selections. The service from the staff was wonderful. We will definitely return the next time we're in Portland.

author: Olenka1492
title: Stop on the way to the Pacific
text: Getting here from the airport was a breeze with a taxi service. Checking in took a little bit longer than usual because of a line, but we each got a warm cookie! Walking though the hotel, we saw the pool which looked clean and nice. People were hanging out there so it must have been nice, we just weren’t in the swimming mode. Breakfast was awesome because of the bacon and potatoes. The potatoes were literally the best ones I have had in a while. Not an updated hotel, but that doesn’t mean the room is not comfortable. I had good sleep even with the time zone change of three hours.

author: G5001OGlindah
title: decent price for area
text: My room was on the first floor, which was convenient for me. Stayed June 8-9th. Had a sliding door which opened to the parking lot, and that didn't seem safe. The hotel location is convenient to downtown, and my family and I walked to the festival that was going on. The King bed was very comfortable. I liked having the Keurig coffee maker in the room. Included Breakfast buffet, which was great to start our day.! Furniture, chair, and carpet was old and worn out. They charge extra for parking ($15) per day, and I do not agree with this practice, as is common in larger cities The hotel overall could use some refurbishing and through cleaning.

author: BunnieinOregon
title: 5 night stay.
text: Convenient to the light rail and plenty of car parking for a price. The upgraded rooms are pretty good and they keep them very clean. The halls are dreary but there are rooms with outside entrances. The pool is small - at least they have one! The breakfast room can be crowded and later on in the morning, messy looking. Both my husband and I had a piece of bacon which tasted like fish - it was so gross and I could get rid of it fast enough. Didn’t touch the way undercooked bacon after that. The breakfast is the same every day. If you are a walker, you can easily walk to Nordstrom and all over town and the waterfront area by Tom McCall Park is about a 12 minute walk.

author: Caliborngirl
title: Good location, very helpful front desk
text: This is a nice hotel that is part of the University of Portland. The buffet was well stocked in the morning. The front desk was very helpful. I had a double room and it was OK. The carpet was thin and had weird texture underneath - kind of lumpy? Everything was as clean as it could be and for the price was acceptable but this place could use some serious updating. WARNING - if you rent a car from Avis in the lobby only park in their spots. I didn't know this and was issued a $45 ticket from the University police. You MUST have a permit or you'll get one too if you're not in a rental space.

author: MOTAtascadero
title: Great location!!!!
text: We stayed her for 3 nights for my daughter's graduation from PSU. The location cannot be beat for walking distance to sites and the MAX line right out the front door!!!! We stayed in one of the upgraded Comfort Rooms that overlooked the city. The room, beds, location, and hot buffet were great. The pillows and tiny sink were not great. We had to get help with the TV and the broken iron. There is a liquor store, domino's pizza, and convenience store a short walk from the hotel. The ice machine down the hall made a ridiculously loud hum. I would have had to change rooms if I was near it.

author: HikeMDI
title: Disappointed
text: The front desk person was very pleasant and the outdoor pool looked clean and fine for swimming although we didn't use it. Otherwise, this hotel needs a good facelift. The lobby smells old even though it has a newly furnished sitting area. We had a room in the outer building and the glassed hallways leading to our room weren't well kept or clean. Our bathroom, linens and room were clean, but the room was very dated with old wallpaper and carpet with stains. The mattresses were also uncomfortable. As a side note, the location wasn't great either unless you need to be right near the university, but then we weren't big fans of the downtown area of Portland. The scenic day trip drives we took were great, but we will stay outside of Portland next time we explore beautiful Oregon.

author: Cary7227
title: Great location, Good value
text: University Place Hotel was exactly what I expected and met all my needs. It was close to the PSU and the transit system was within a couple of blocks. I had great access to downtown and everywhere I wanted to go. The room was clean, comfortable, and well maintained. The free breakfast was great, based upon the price of the room. The staff made every effort to serve. Those who expect luxury hotel amenities will be disappointed. Those, like me, who make a choice for a fair price and a good place to stay will be happy.

author: 434joyl
title: Dirty hotel & poor service
text: My husband and I are visiting this hotel for one night. We saw this place has a high rating according to Trip Advisor (4.3/5) so decided to give it a try. This place might be the worst hotel I’ve ever stayed in... The room was dirty... I found gum stain on the dirty gray carpet, yellow stains in the bathtub, and a dog hair on the blanket before we settled into the room. (Yet the hotel has a no pet policy.) The room has limited amenities and the elevator has broken lights. The hallways are very dark. The hotel resembles university residence but on the low quality side (as I’ve visited many typical residences that are neater/cleaner and better-looking). If you’re able to book another place, I highly recommend going somewhere else instead. So glad we are only here for one night!!!!

author: tsT8431KA
title: Simple special request wasnt honored. Room was mostly clean enough.
text: I booked through booking.com. In the Special Requests section, I typed: “Please draw a picture of a star fish and leave it in the room. Testing to see if this is read.” There was no such drawing, and staff didn’t even mention it. —— CONS: 1 of their 6 ice machines were working, but only one of them had an Out of Service sign, which was dated for March, not April. —— Apparently the pool is only open in Summer. Booking.com didn’t mention that part. —— Room was mostly very clean, except for about 7 hairs of unknown origin in the bathtub, which I had to extract by hand. —— PROS: Friendly staff, free breakfast, great location, great price, and I get a mug for this review!

author: ronaldmT8248YD
title: Portland trip
text: As we travel around, I always look for bargain hotel mostly downtown so everything is within walking distance. This place served it's purpose since we get up and out of the hotel early to explore the town and come back late just in time to go the bed. It has a complimentary breakfast and the Wi-Fi is excellent. The room is standard with a flat screen TV. Bed is kinda lumpy and there's multiple stains on the carpet. I also noticed that they don't change the sheets or dust it off before making the bed because I saw some hair on my side of the bed which looks like mine. It's located in a quiet area of town but it has thin walls and you can hear the plumbing next door and the guest. The front desk has an attitude problem as if they are not happy to work there because as I was sitting in the lobby waiting for our ride, the guest that would approach the clerks and ask questions. Overall we enjoyed our stay even though it needs upgrade.

author: 650KarinB
title: Seriously unacceptable!
text: Booked the hotel because their netsite said Airport Shuttle: But what they could do was give a shuttle company a call about yet more custumers. But we still would have to pay normal price. Well were tired after a long day of travelling, hauled the suitcases off to the room. Next unpleasant surprise: no hot or even lukewarm water in the shower! Clothes back on, to the reception where surprise number two was the suggested solution: Let the water run for 15 - 20 minutes!! Little signs in the room ask us to Save our planet and reduce water consumption? Seriously! We were offered to pack up and try another room, but as the idea with the stay was getting some rest, we declined. So: The shuttle to the airport comes with a costs and the mismanaged plumbing or faulty waterwarming costs the planet - and guests can only get a quick coldwater wash! Do not stay here!

author: kwsews
title: Nice location, dated hotel
text: Tried to find a reasonable priced hotel the week after the eclipse and found this place. The location is great, on the streetcar line, and walking distance to many restaurants, parks and attraction. The hotel room is definitely dated and due for some renovations. Beds were not that comfy but tolerable. The room did have a mini fridge and microwave and they did have a decent breakfast that included real scrambled eggs, bacon, potatoes. Also had a waffle maker with whipped cream topping and chocolate chips. Nice selection of breads and muffins and scones. Just felt it was a bit high priced for being so outdated but then again we were between the eclipse and Labor Day.

author: 955jonathand
title: Visiting Portland
text: This hotel is old but nice to get out of crazy downtown. Very close to orange and red trains and freeways. This place have breakfast buffet which That starts my mornings. When the hot weather I jump in cold pool to feel freshen up. Nice Gym to workout. And you can walk or ride rail to downtown within 20 minutes. I enjoyed my stay here and it's reasonable prices. Just to sleep, swim, eat breakfast and go out and explore. And return back relaxed which I like. You can be lazy to relax too as well.

author: summeralohanui
title: Motel not a Hotel
text: Came to celebrate my 30th birthday. Was greeted, well not until I spoke up and said "Hi" first with three people sitting there not even looking up, by Laura/Laurie with no personality, attitude and when I asked her to repeat herself about the $15 parking fee (ridiculous, since we were never told about that on the phone prior) she raised her voice and gave more attitude. Instantly irritating me and my boyfriend just wanted to get me out of there. Went to the nearest access door to where our room was and the key-card scanner was broken. Went to our room and the key-card sanner took what seemed like a century to open, sliding the card juuuust right. Get into our room and it smells stale, looks to be water damage/ mold on the ceiling, only options for the HVAC unit were fan constantly low or high (no temperature control), the shower head had one option (massage/hard-center stream) and the towels smelt stale & dirty. Pro- downtown Portland. Do not recommend, would not stay again and glad we booked only one night.

author: mas2764
title: Great price and location
text: I was in Portland (first time there) for a few days for a meeting I had at Portland State University and my overall stay at University Place was very positive. Price wise, the hotel is going to be one the best deals you will find. It was significantly more affordable than all the other hotels in Downtown Portland and nicer than the "Super 8" style motels. This hotel is perfect for people who will not be spending a large amount of time in the room (which i never do on vacation because whats the point on going a vacation if your just going to sit in the room all day). Its close to Downtown Portland and there is Max Line and bus stop right in front of the hotel. The staff was friendly, check in was quick and the complementary breakfast that comes with your room at the Lincoln Grill was actually very good. Not even hotels here in Las Vegas, where I work in a 5 star resort, who boast having 4-5 Diamond ratings offer a complimentary breakfast. Overall this is a small, affordable hotel with the perfect location. If your in Oregon and you just want to have a clean comfortable room to sleep in while you spend your time exploring this beautiful state I HIGHLY recommend this hotel.

author: 266samanthak
title: Dirty, Old, & Cheap
text: The price is still not worth the stay. We were using it as a "overnight pit stop" between Idaho and the coast. We knew we were really only going to be sleeping there and didn't expect too much... but it was even less then our expectations. I had to give my children a bath and didn't even want to because the bathroom and tub was filthy and damaged & tiny. We also had to pay for parking. This is not a HOTEL it is more like a MOTEL (rooms open right onto the parking lot/street) and you can hear noise everywhere. The pool was closed early as well and we were not allowed to use it. The only PROs are that the breakfast in the morning is nice & filling and it is close to downtown, the Zoo (where we were headed as well) and many other attractions. But next time we will spring for another place, even if it is just for the night.

author: bdrothschild
title: Older Hotel - Good Location
text: We enjoyed our stay here. It's clean and comfortable. The carpet in our room was not in good shape. The hotel is centrally located. Public transportation stops right across the street. Staff was friendly. Best value in downtown Portland. Breakfast was adequate. There was a lot of seating. There was a large group in the hotel and I think that the breakfast suffered a little.

author: MissGreekTraveller
title: Not amazing but not bad either
text: The location of this hotel is pretty good for the price. It's still walkable to downtown, there are some good funky eating options nearby and it's a pleasant walk to the downtown core. The hotel itself could really use some updating and a paint job but found it comfortable. The pool was a welcome respite during the heat wave and it is a good size. The most disappointing part was that the front desk person told us that breakfast ended at 10:30am but when we went down to find it at 9:30 the next morning we were told it ends at 9:30 on weekdays. The included breakfast was a major reason we chose this hotel so was not impressed when we had to go out and spend an extra $50. The front desk person obviously forgot that the next day was a Monday not a Sunday. Lastly I think they should include free parking for guests considering they have a huge lot and space. For such a tired old hotel, it would be a bit of a perk.

author: loannpowell1999
title: Decent hotel for a reasonable price
text: Rooms spacious. Beds more comfortable in updated rooms. Some odor in hallways and walls allow sound to be heard from adjoining rooms. Nice pool in inner courtyard. Good Keurig coffee and tea maker. Pillows comfortable. Staff seems unhappy in their jobs. Near OHSU if you need to come for medical.treatment, and need a reasonably priced hotel.

author: E8873AGtomh
title: Pleasant Place in Portland
text: Our 6 nights were very pleasant. The furniture in the good-sized room was fairly old. One dresser drawer was stuck, but the rest was adequate. The breakfast buffet is included and all you can eat. The well-maintained plantings in the courtyard surrounding the swimming pool offered shade and a restful atmosphere. The walkways to the exterior rooms are glassed in, helping reduce the freeway and neighborhood noise. Advantages of staying here are Portland's excellent public transit is right out front and the promenade along the Willamette River is within walking distance. A disadvantage-parking in hotel lot is pricey.

author: gmdesigns
title: A "Dingleberry" place
text: The worst! Seemed like a joke!! So awful and unfortunately the staff is all aware of it. Door security is busted Drains don't work A/C not working Dirt/Dust/Dander Yep! A "dingleberry" where it would make you shake and vomit! Need we say more. Went to Portland for an important OHSU appt. wanted to be close by for a very early morning appointment. Run don't walk away from this filthy/outdated/overpriced Petri dish of you can only guess!

author: doriss443
title: Great location! Quiet, clean, great staff, yummy cookies, nice people, popular stay
text: We were in Portland 2 days at the beginning of our trip, and stayed here, we were given a room in the older section, but quiet and clean, on the 3rd floor, away from the elevator, facing the inner courtyard & pool. When we returned at the end of 3 wks, we were pleasantly surprised with the newer area, just as quiet, & clean, just newer. The Metro was across the street, the Sat. Farmer's Market a close walk over. Wonderful food in the area, easy walk to the river, and fun on bikes. We will return, the location was perfect! Warm, friendly, helpful staff!! So enjoyed the quieter section of town, close to the campus, to the Cultural District, pleasant walks to anyplace we ventured to, public transportation very easy and convenient. We chose not to have a vehicle the 1st 2 or last 2 days, for it is such a pleasant and easy walk, and then you do not have to park the vehicle as well.

author: judiluvsjamaica
title: Should be called Motel 6
text: A simple answer , it's a dump. Carpets are filthy , room in serious need of an update, beds are extremely uncomfortable , bedspreads had stains on them , they don't clean rooms daily ( which is fine with me, but odd) TV is an 80's throwback, room smelled musty and felt like I was in a Rest area hotel. Don't, I repeat don't eat at the restaurant and be aware of the free breakfast buffet. Very cold nasty food. Now , I gave it a 2 star instead of 1, because the front staff was great and very friendly, and location of hotel is pretty good. Less then a $10 Uber ride downtown. It's a very inexpensive hotel but truthfully over $100 a night was too much for this hotel. I definitely was glad to not be in room. It kind of made me itch.

author: Elbye
title: A Convenient and Clean Place to Stay
text: We arrived in the afternoon by train and were able to quickly get to the hotel by public transportation. The city line lets you off right in front of the hotel and from that same place you can go virtually anywhere in the city. The check in process was quick and efficient although the lady at the desk seemed to be having a tough day. The room was clean and well setup with many channels available on the TV. I went in search of ice and found the first two machines weren't working. After finding out from the front desk that they are turned of in the winter, I was directed to a machine that was functioning. The included breakfast more than adequate and well-prepared. There was a problem with the toasters that seemed to indicate an issue with circuit breakers. Having said all this I wouldn't hesitate to go this hotel again. It's location near public transportation makes traveling around the city very easy and brings the beautiful city's sight within easy reach.

author: TravelPair1968
title: Convenient Downtown Location near Public Transportation
text: Rooms were nice sized and equipped with microwave, small refrigerator, and Keurig Coffee Maker. Our room was clean and had everything we needed including free internet access. Convenient parking on site. Hot breakfast included. We were disappointed that the outdoor pool was not ready yet. We had read there was "health club access" but found out it was $15 per person, too expensive for a swim in the lap pool for two. Would consider staying there again. Greeted by friendly staff and a warm chocolate chip cookie. Moderate accommodations with moderate cost..

author: WayneW329
title: Pretty good option
text: I think it might be owned by Portland State University. It's an old property and dated (60s/70s era) but clean and tidy. All staff were helpful and pleasant. Breakfast is included and hot buffet and usual continental choices - pretty decent spread. The bar/restaurant is the same location and has a very limited menu but the food was tasty. Wings, fries, burgers etc, reasonable price. You have to pay for parking at $15 a day. Light rail right outside that takes you to downtown for about $2.50 return. I understand the tariff is cheaper than a lot of other Portland options, and seemed to be good value.

author: Fermax
title: Good 3.5* in Portland
text: The Cinco de Mayo weekend was surprisingly busy in Portland and I was lucky to discover University Place that was great value. (Tip: Check their Facebook page for any current discount codes!) The hotel is clean, the staff are friendly and the location is well-connected. Things are not perfect (I could hear road noise from my room, you bus your own table at breakfast, it's hard to find power sockets in the room, I had to re-authenticate to the Internet several times each day) but the room was large and the bed was super-comfortable.
