The room has a mini-fridge and a microwave oven. The included breakfast was simple but satisfying. The Orange MAX light rail stops right outside the hotel, as do the 9 & 17 buses, making it very simple to get downtown ($5 all-day transit ticket). The Red MAX from the airport stops a block away (but this is only to May 20 due to track work - normally you'd have to change lines). In all, a perfectly fine place to stay.

author: suewoz
title: Very old and dated rooms
text: We stayed here 5 nights in April 2017. The outside looks nice and then you enter the room....The carpet is dirty, the bathrooms have mold, the furniture is beat up and the tv at least 10 years old. In the morning you could see daylight coming through our door because there was a crack. You can hear your neighbors and the people above you. I am not too picky but I pretty much kept my socks on the entire time. The breakfast was decent but the same every day. Pros: The people at the desk were always pleasant, there is a car rental right in the lobby, the train is right across the road, you can walk to several restaurants. I would not stay here again.

author: G5280FUandrewm
title: A good budget choice
text: I've stayed here three times, and I think it's about the best option on a budget with the given proximately to down town. It's easy to take the tram down town, and close enough to walk, albeit a longer walk. There's a pretty good continental breakfast buffet with eggs, bacon, sausage, fruit, coffee, juice, and random carbs. The rooms are clean, but aged. There's a pool, but I don't think there's a hot tub. I'll stay here again for sure. When you check-in they give you some cookies. Who doesn't like cookies?

author: sakik315
title: Good location and friendly staff!
text: It was my third time to stay at University place hotel. Every time I come here, staff members welcome me warmly and they are really friendly and helpful. Rooms are usually wide enough if you choose deluxe room. I stayed with a guy and two girls at deluxe twin room,but it was comfortable. You can walk to downtown in 20mins or take MAX which takes you there in 5-10mins. This hotel looks old but affordable if you would like to walk around or stay super close to Portland state university. Also they serve breakfast and it's okay. Overall, it was a great stay with this hotel! FYI-There is a car rent service at the lobby if you need.

author: mikim859
title: friendly, near PSU
text: Staff are friendly and there are some restaurants near the hotel. MAX orange line's station is in front of the hotel. MAX green line is also just 5 minutes' walk so that it is easy to go downtown and the airport. PSU is close, quiet area. A little bit old but a microwave oven, refrigerator, and a TV set are in the room. Queen size bed is comfortable. Complimentary breakfast is nice. Free wifi is available.

author: natashamV4889PT
title: Very average
text: I didn't expect much from this hotel from the very beginning. Stayed here with a friend for a short trip, and it was exactly as described in previous reviews. The building is older, grey uninviting hallways, room is functional, but could be better. For example, there was a used towel and soap in the room when we got there. Not ideal, but bearable if you're only staying to sleep at night. Otherwise, the location is great. The staff are nice. Breakfast gets really boring after two days, but at least it's free. Wasn't expecting all the extra taxes upon check-out, but I guess that's an Oregon thing. Overall, it's no five-star Marriott, but it works for what it is.

author: TheTJExperience
title: Great Guest Service in an amazing hotel
text: What to say about my stay? You are greeted at Front Desk upon arrival with a cookie by the super cute Alex - if you are lucky. I want to take a moment and dwell on this guy because he is a guest service all star! The sort of individual with invaluable recommendations on the area dispensed with a smile and amazing professionalism. Such a rare guest service treat! The entire staff, however, was amazing in every interaction. The property location is right across from the light rail, but an easy walk to everything if mass transit isn't your thing. The free breakfast is slightly elevated from your average continental. The only drawback is the property itself which is somewhat dated and in need of renovation (hence not all the available star rating). But if you know about the Portland hotel market and have the right expectations this place will exceed them.

author: Brucecher
title: Mom
text: Great Price, great location! Made a visit to PSU convenient and affordable. Room was nice. Staff were friendly and helpful. Will definitely return. Glad they are upgrading rooms. Saved money. Thank- you.

author: carolt343
title: Nice 2 nights stay
text: Great downtown location. Quiet inside and outside. Friendly staff. Nice beds and bedding. We enjoyed the free continental breakfast. Hot bath water. Decor and furniture not modern but still create cosy looking. Good value for money.

author: dallasmanta
title: budget priced hotel
text: This was the first time I have stayed in downtown Portland. This hotel was budget priced with breakfast included. If you are looking for place to sleep close to mass transit and you don't care what it looks like, this may be for you. The hotel complex is large and rooms are in desperate need for updating. Super hard beds and pillows, analog TV right out of the 1970 era. hot water in our remote wing took a long time to get hot. the bath vents were very loud. I would not stay here again.

author: ottog440
title: Perfect for our family trip into the city
text: In the city with 3 teenagers. Nice rooms. Street car right outside. Good place for the price. I would recommend it. The free breakfast is nice, the dining room is comfy. There is a lounge on-site where you can get a pint of local beer. Warm cookies at check-in. Reasonable parking. The staff is always very friendly and helpful.

author: ClintonWhidbeyGal
title: Old and Tired
text: Upon arrival we were greeting by very courteous hotel staff and our check in process was easy. Our hotel room however, was old and tired. As we entered our room I noticed that the bed cover appeared as though someone had taken a rest on the bed and not smoothed out the cover. The dust ruffle was very wrinkled and as I threw back the cover I noticed that sheets were also very wrinkled but they appeared clean!! Thank goodness. For the price (and I wasn't the one to book this hotel) I expected much more. It was as if it were a low budget one off motel. I was skeptical of the cleanliness of the carpet and kept my shoes on at all times. The bathroom was clean enough, the only negative comment would be the mold in the bath/shower. The trolley runs outside the hotel (an our room faced the trolley street) but I didn't find that it was noisy, I could tell when it went by but it was amazingly quiet.

author: robertf873
title: Robert F
text: I stayed here while attending a small conference in October, 2016. The hotel is well located on the streetcar line. The room was comfortable, clean and large. The staff was helpful and efficient.The conference rate was very reasonable and in checking the regular rate it seems to be very reasonable also. A breakfast was provided for the conference attendees. Whether breakfast is provided to others, I do not know. The breakfast was very adequate, however, the breakfast room was dark and crowded. Other problems with the hotel are lack of a business center which seem strange as this hotel calls itself a conference hotel, worn carpets on stairs, noise in adjacent rooms can be heard through the walls and the hotel layout is rather confusing. Nevertheless, as long as the rate remains reasonable, I consider this to be a good place to stay in Portland.

author: lillymania
title: Worth your money
text: I've read lot of reviews before I stayed here and have to say it's not that bad. Actually my room is quite in good maintenance. I really like that they provide microwave, refrig. and kettle in the room. Toilet is also clean. Bed quality is in average. Nice breakfast for this price! And good location to access to downtown or airport(there's an express bus that stop by right in front of hotel-per booking). Most staffs are trainees(I guess). They are helpful but sometimes a bit busy.

author: jp_edwards
title: Not bad but not great!
text: We were here for a conference which the hotel is well suited to but as for the stay, I wasn't impressed. The hotel staff was nice enough but not very motivated. Our room was not cleaned two days in a row so we had to call for service. The facilities are well maintained and things are in working order but it probably should have an upgrade. The breakfast was ok, but not great. But on the plus side, you couldn't get a better location. One block from the 4th street food trucks and a short walk to the Pearl district. Not gross but not great.

author: starrymisu
title: Great Location, Helpful Staff
text: My friend and I stayed 5 nights August 12-17, 2016 in room 272. Our room was not adjacent to the pool area and was clean and quiet. Everything in the room worked perfectly, really no complaints. The property was very busy with a girls softball team and parents but it didn't bother us because we have been there, too when our children were younger. We didn't hang out in the room we had so many things planned. What we really liked was you could catch the Max orange or yellow right in front of the hotel and be downtown in 10 minutes. Coming home late we got a snack and a flight of beer in the Lincoln Grill twice. That was super convenient. The breakfast in the morning is pretty standard fare but started us on our day. We would definitely stay here again.

author: S4529GOnatalieh
title: Never again.
text: The pictures make it seem like it's a grand-high end hotel. You enter and it's nice but the rooms are completely old fashioned, but still look okay. All of a sudden our sink bursts with water and gunk comes out, ruining our sink and our floor. We called the front desk 3 times until a guy came and checked it out and said "I can't do anything". So what were we supposed to do? Not shower or use the bathroom at all? That night we got sent to a new room, in an external hallway, but not as "comforting" as the one we first had. Not to mention they literally didn't do anything for the room that was messed up with the water incident. The next morning people were checked in. Never again.

author: gwens115
title: Convenient location near downtown and walking to the harbor.
text: The location of the hotel was great! We walked downtown to a brewery restaurant to sample some local beers. There was the typical city shopping stores and cafes. Right outside the front of the hotel was a train station. We had a rental car and were surprised to be charged $15 for overnight parking on their lot, but it was probably more reasonable than some places charge. We also walked down to the harbor nearby and ate at McCormick & Schmick's on the waterfront. The hotel staff seemed tired and not "with it," but they were nice enough. The hotel was very nice, with an attached restaurant and free breakfast (we did not eat), and a very pretty swimming pool area. Our room was on the outside, but it was enclosed by a glass walkway that kept it safer and quieter. The room was fairly nice and clean, and the beds were comfortable.

author: KalyanVC
title: Inexpensive, great location, not Hilton but ...
text: I found this place on Google as we needed a place to stay for one night in Portland. I liked the place a lot but my wife was freaked out by how "shady" it looked and by the fact that she saw a spider on the bed. The place, from the outside, in particular the corridor outside the door looks a little rundown. And it's Portland downtown so at any point you have a 10% chance some homeless man will run into you! But overall the place was good bang for buck. The wifi is great, no connection problems. They offered breakfast which we didn't eat because we had other plans but appreciated. The staff was courteous when they couldn't find my reservation at first but it was resolved quickly. Would stay again.

author: Vkirk00
title: Great hotel
text: Great hotel with a really nice breakfast! Clean rooms. Close to downtown. Right across from some type free transportation. Staff very friendly. Workout room small but has several cardio and free weights. Standard hotel room otherwise. Only stayed one night. Nice pool.

author: BunnieinOregon
title: Good deal if you can get in. 3 Star is about the right rating.
text: We stayed in a deluxe king with microwave, refrigerator, t.v. and coffee maker. It was a good deal compared to other places in the area. It takes about 30 minutes to walk to the Pearl District, 20 minutes to Nordstrom and a few minutes to the waterfront by Tom McCall Park. The parking is good and reasonable compared to other places. We had Friday and Sunday booked but they could not accommodate us for Saturday & I wish they would have tried harder or at least been nicer/friendlier in trying to accommodate us. The breakfast was the usual...not great but not bad either. There is a freeway close by and I'm glad I had earplugs with me.

author: AndreaRae13
title: Pretty disappointed with hotel
text: I stayed here as part of a conference (so my room was reimbursed) in late June. It was a warm couple of days, in the mid-80s, and the A/C in the hotel room was very loud and very inefficient. The hotel is quite run down, my non-smoking room had what looked like cigarette ashes near the sliding glass door. The carpet felt old and the place just hasn't been updated. The bathroom area was pretty run down, including stains on the floor and in the tub. The upside of the room was the bed. It was very comfortable (although I did bring my own pillow). Also the staff was very friendly and helpful when asked. If this is your only choice, or the cheapest choice, then go for it. Also, the location is great for PSU and the waterfront.

author: Joan1914
title: Rather disappointing stay
text: This hotel is owned by the University of Portland. The price is reasonable but I would say it hasn't been updated since the 1970s. It is clean but just run down. They offer a breakfast buffet, always the same, and a small restaurant/bar for dinner with a small menu of bar food. The wifi is free but keeps dropping. There is small pool here. If you stay here, ask for a "comfort" room and it will be slightly better quality and has a fridge and microwave (at higher cost). Old fashioned window a/cs that are noisy and thin walls. There are buses and a train that stops outside so it is easy to get into downtown Portland.

author: Ren1211
title: Good quality hotel with a decent price.
text: This was our first ever trip to Portland. The hotel was well placed near the transit system and little stop-in restaurants. When we first arrived they did not have our reservation (we booked through Expedia). After a half an hour or so of phone calls, and showing them various emails we were able to get a room. The room was decent with a large bed next to a 24 hour gym. It was too cold to have the pool open. The wifi was not that great, it was free though. Breakfast was complimentary and a buffet style with much to choose from. Overall, a delightful place at a good price.

author: 787abbyw
title: Poor quality hotel and poor service
text: Our rooms was very out dated with thin carpet and a old, musty smell. The first two days we were there housekeeping didn't come to our room until after 4pm. When they did come they didn't fully service the room. Lastly and most frustrating, it seems as though people live in the hotel and their rooms seem to be mixed in with guest rooms. Our room neighbors were very, very, very loud. We could hear screaming, cursing, and dogs barking well past midnight. The walls are very thin. Not a terrible experience, but if you can go elsewhere I would.

author: cal076
title: Nice place near downtown
text: This is the only hotel we stay at when visiting Portland! It's literally across from the Max! Rooms are cozy! They are dated, but we didn't care much. Beds are comfy and that's all that truly mattered. BREAKFAST IS AMAZING!!! Staff is nice! Great for a weekend getaway!

author: 798erins
title: Convenient economy hotel
text: I stayed here with a group of students in November with part of a national conference. It seemed a little bit run down, but not unkempt. The breakfast that was included with our room was decent and fit our needs. I found the layout of the building slightly confusing, but that was probably my own fault for being directionally challenged. The staff was friendly, and our room was always very clean when we came back in the evenings. The hotel is located right beside a train stop that comes from the airport which was extremely convenient for the group I was with--we hopped on to travel around the city every day. Overall, a good hotel for convenience and economy. You get what you pay for, and it's a decent value. I would stay here again.

author: ProfAragon
title: Economy Hotel
text: This is a budget hotel. There are no bells and whistles. Pack your own pillow and some ear plugs. The walls are thin and the public transportation can be loud. Do not eat here. Go around the corner to Tacos Del Mar or the Food Trucks. My tub would not drain properly and it took them half a day to fix it. Although the staff was really nice, I found that overall the rooms and hotel needs a good cleaning.

author: 208pickytravelguy
title: Excellent Price, Great Location, Nice Staff, Needs Major Upgrade
text: I wasn’t quite sure how to rate this property because really the only thing wrong with it is the very tired rooms and hallways. I originally had booked an “Economy” room and received a great price. The room was what I expected for something being advertised as such and I stayed the first night in it. I then upgraded to a standard room which was much cleaner (no smudges on the walls, no strange stains on the carpet, etc.), so in my opinion the additional fee was worth it. The wallpaper was peeling off in the upgraded room, but again it was much cleaner. I would stay again knowing what it’s like only due to the price. It wasn’t so awful that I could justify double or triple the rate other downtown hotels like to charge. Also the staff all seemed very nice and accommodating. A real bonus however was the hot breakfast however. Long story short is you get what you pay for—keep that in mind when booking this property.

author: TromboneAl
title: Hotel: Good. Wifi: Bad
text: Everything is good about this hotel, but if you want to use their WiFi, consider another place. At most hotels, if you want to use the WiFi, they give you a password, you log on, and you're set. Some don't even require a password. At this hotel, there was a complicated system in which you have to get things started with a temporary account or something, then you wait ten minutes, then you try again, then you put in a user name and password, and then it doesn't work. Apparently the system is tied into the university network. When it doesn't work, you have to call tech support and wait on hold, then they suggest that you go to the tech support office, which is in some university building. Just what you want to do on your vacation: Deal with tech support. My wife never got hers working, and I somehow got mine working by choosing the wrong server. I'm sure they've gotten a lot of complaints, and maybe they've fixed it. Check first.

author: kimpI8963JQ
title: Worst Place Ever
text: We booked for 4 nights, but checked out the next day because I could not sleep all night due to people slamming the doors near by rooms so loud all night. The place is dirty and needs total renovation. The front desk is very understanding, however, when I tried to check out 3 days earlier. The location is in Downtown Portland, but street streets are hard to drive around due to railroads, 1 lane streets all over town. Nothing to see in Downtown anyway, unless you are in the Pearl District which have something to do- but not much. Portland is the worst place ever regarding street signs and street numbers. I think the City does not like to put signs. On the way the Rose Test Garden, the streets are up the hills and winding and there were NO SIGNS to tell where to turn. I don’t think I will ever stay at this hotel or going back to Portland.

author: Culas
title: Good location. No frills...just a place to park your bones.
text: Stayed here for a week. Not good service at the front desk. The vendo machines were broken. The washing machines (they only have 2 for the hotel), broke down for a few days. Even with breakfast included in the price, I only ate there twice because they don't change the selections at all. Greasy bacon, greasy sausage, dry scrambled eggs and sometimes they run out of toast. The only good thing I can say about this place is the location. It's located at the edge of downtown so it's quiet with a lot of good places to eat nearby since it's right beside PSU's campus.

author: 96karir
title: An debunked old folks home?
text: Looks depressing from the minute you step in. Has recessed lighting with no lights or dark lights and just yukky looking. Three staff helped me. Two young women acted like they HAD to be there and hated their job. Not chipper, not upbeat. A young man who helped me though (Islander or Hispanic) was super friendly and did his best to give great service! The people who said you get more for your buck are just not as affected by their surroundings. If you need some cheer, or gross out easily, you don't want to stay here.

author: 320mrsw
title: Stay somewhere else
text: We booked a deluxe king room (I do not believe any room could be called deluxe), when we arrived they gave us a twin room and an 8 dollar discount as they said they were full. It is a disgrace that they think they can just throw you in any room when you arrive. The breakfast was mediocre at best. The room was clean for this type of hotel, but not really clean enough. Location is good. We had a wedding to go to in Portland and this was the hotel chosen, why I do not know I am sure there are better hotels. Staff unhelpful. Plumbing noisy. Would never stay here again.

author: 9world_citizen9
title: It's ok
text: Portland is really a city that works, and the hotel is perfectly connected by public transport. They offer also a shuttle for the airport for $14 ($24 return). The hotel is a typical American hotel, beautiful long time ago and never renovated. Thinks that there is no wi-fi in the rooms (just the cable). Breakfast is a misery, even if included. Rooms are big but not modern; noisy from imnplants. Some members of the staff are nice, other terrible. It is worth for what you pay.

author: TravelGuy72
title: Room is fine but hotel is stupid
text: The room is your average two-three star room. But don't stay here if you need to do business as there is no wifi in the room. They have an ethernet cable but last time I checked most phones and tablets don't accept a phone cord. Also, this hotel has the stupidest layout of any building I have seen. Miles from lobby/parking through heavy glass doors which is a pain with luggage. Room was never cleaned the two nights we were there. Apathetic, unfriendly, put-upon staff. Good location for PSU and downtown, and pretty good free breakfast. But extremely odd and rude breakfast attendant. If you have to stay here you'll be fine, but if you have a choice pick a modern building with usual amenities.

author: srh1234
title: Clean and served our purpose well
text: We have stayed at this hotel on several occasions when we come from out of state to visit family, who lives in an apartment directly across the street. In that regard, there is not a more convenient place for us to stay. The hotel is very average, not fancy and is in fact, pretty dated. It could certainly use an update. But the rooms we've stayed in have always been clean. We've not had any issues with hotel staff being rude, although they are not overly friendly either. They look to be mostly younger college students, which makes sense with the hotel bring practically on the PSU campus. The free breakfast is nice and plentiful. No complaints from me really. If I was truly on vacation, this would not be my hotel of choice, but for our needs when in Portland....a clean, inexpensive hotel near family, with easy access to transportation and shopping, this place works well for us.

author: 235LovetotraveL
title: Worst hotel in america
text: Me and my family went travelling through America in May 2015. Unfortunately this was a hotel we chose to stay in to save a little bit of money on our trip. The hotel front desk staff were the rudest people I have ever met. Pretty much ignoring you whenever you walked up to the front counter to ask anything. Anything you asked for they would say no without eye contact and not even offer to look into it or give an option. So frustrating and just poor service. I not recommend staying here ever. The breakfast was average, powdered eggs, Rock hard bacon, Toast and old muffins. Not worth a cent..

author: JeffS_Toronto
title: Dated but well located.
text: I only stayed here a night. WiFi is through the University and only available in certain areas. The room was clean. I don't think the building or rooms have seen an upgrade in over 25 years. The breakfast was included and was OK in dinning area. Parking was extra but convenient. The location was good for getting on and off the Highways and also for downtown. I'd probably stay somewhere else next time.

author: baseballjunkie
title: Still a great inexpensive place to stay in Downtown Portland!
text: This place is just a holdover stop. We stay here a lot for sporting events at Portland State University. This last time we stayed in the deluxe wing and it was clean and updated. The television was a flat screen and the rooms were comfortable and clean. The only complaint is the parking fee. The breakfast is hot and delicious, probably the best I have has as compared to other hotels I've stayed at. The hotel has a small bar/grill which made a great burger. Nothing fancy though, just good basic place to stay if you are out all day running around and want a place to crash that is safe, close and clean.

author: jogger1987
title: Disappointed
text: The staff did an excellent job to accommodate us that's why I gave it two stars instead of 1. Initially our room opened to the outside. For $130 a night that's ridiculous. I've stayed in multiple cities with a great room for that price. Our room had toenail clippings on the floor. After that and opening to the outside I requested a refund and they moved us to a much more suitable room. Breakfast was good and was a 10 -15 min. Walk from waterfront park and pioneer square.

author: jackiem55
title: Participated in block of rooms held for event off site
text: Horrible customer service. Either we are not worth treating... or the front desk man is lazy and smug. He did not welcome, he told me everything I could 'not' do as a guest, and I asked about wifi. He said, oh... here it is, and there is breakfast. Not where though.... not when. The front desk man on March 25, has no idea how to treat people kindly or respectfully. He acted as if I asked to crash at his house for free.

title: Pretty good
text: Stayed 2 night, King Room Wasn't sure what to expect after reading the reviews so I was pleasantly surprised. It was easy to find, good parking, and out room was updated. Pleasant walk into the downtown core – not very far at all. Convenient, quiet location, with easy access entering / exiting the city. We had a no fuss check-in (out was a bit longer), our room was spacious, updated (had read a review the larger rooms were) with a small seating area and a view over the pool. You can hear the outside pool noise but very quiet 9pm and onward. Comfortable bed, shower pressure and good amenities. Continental breakfast – buffet style: large and very filling. – definitely would stay again. Note: not a lot of dining options around the uni area but wasn't and issue for us.

author: mlokhorst
title: excellent choice
text: At the time of writing (January '15) the lightrail stop in front of the hotel was not open yet, but it looked like it will open soon which will make it infinitely easy to get from the airport to the hotel for $2.50. Right now it is about a 10-15 min walk to downtown with the lightrail you'll have another option. Checkin was efficient and arriving early was not a problem (I guess this is dependent on availability). The room spacious, bed comfortable. Wi-Fi is throughout the hotel, though the login is a minor inconvenience (you sign in get a 10min window to retrieve your email which contains a link for 24 hour access) it works and is stable. The room came with a free breakfast, which had a good variety of food (scrambled eggs, toast, bacon, sausages some cereal etc). All in all the hotel was great value for money.. good location, good amenities, friendly staff. If you find yourself in Portland you should consider this as a place to stay.

author: par_hoss
title: Nice and Affordable
text: I had an exam in Portland so I got one of the rooms in this hotel. There were better rooms but for the price and location that I wanted this was the perfect match. The room was okay with a good shower. It was also important to me that breakfast was included on the price and I enjoyed it. I was just not very happy with the Parking. I payed 15 dollars for one night for parking, when I wanted to leave I saw that I got a warning for parking there (although the ticket was 0 $ but still when I pay for a parking I do not expect to get a warning ticket! and the hotel said sometimes the officer will do this and I should be happy that it is 0$!. Any way for the price I payed I cannot complain and I liked it. My room did not have free Wifi but it did have internet with cable.

author: DavidB91
title: Excellent room in an excellent location
text: This was a surprise. The Portland University University Place (which is run totally as a commercial hotel) was very nice, very well-located. We had a large, clean and quiet room facing the interior courtyard and pool. The bed was great and the room was well-appointed, fridge, microwave and coffee-maker. Really could not have asked for more, and the wifi was strong and reliable. Very centrally located, tram and other public transport very near, and not far from the river and the downtown. Quiet location with excellent service and friendly, helpful staff. Highly recommend.

author: benl337
title: Good hotel in excellent location
text: I was using the hotel as a base for boarding the Amtrak Coast Starlight from Union Station. The hotel is close to the tram which goes straight to Union Station. The staff were friendly and helpful and the welcome 'smart' cookie was a nice unique way to greet you. The room itself was basic but provided everything I needed and more including a microwave and fridge. The is a self service laundry on site which is good for those on the move. Costing $2.50 (in quarters) for a wash and dry. Washing powder was available from reception. The location is excellent with lots of Portlands famous street food vendors only one block away. Only complaint I heard whilst staying was the charge for parking, but since I was not driving this did not affect me. Overall a good hotel.

author: gary053
title: Rough around the edges...
text: Easy, friendly staff...tipping is not allowed, so they're not "working" the guests. Glanced at other reviews and certainly would not categorize U. Plaza as "horrible" or "rancid"...it is dated, however--I'm guessing late 70's or early 80's. Our room had comfortable beds: Shelley was pleased (and she's picky!) but she also commented on how stained the carpet was. Hot breakfast was included and it was more than adequate. (Shelley thought the sausages were too spicy.) I do not agree that our room had noisy a/c; actually, I was impressed that it did not wake me (and I'm picky!) Thin walls: we had visitors and during our conversation, our neighbors knocked on the wall to "quiet us" and we weren't noisy...so is that our fault or the hotel's? The shower was ok: (not gucky, like someone else commented) but I appreciate a flow control on the faucet, which this place didn't have:you turn it on, and there's only one speed: full force. The price of the room was lower than many of the nearby hotels--but it is high-season and some of the other hotels were sold-out or priced according to demand. Some of the higher-end hotels nearby were hundreds of dollars more per night. I would stay here again if I could get a better price; it's ok to negotiate, isn't it?

author: LeonaLee618
title: Rancid
text: This place was extremely disgusting. There is NOTHING good about this place at all. The bed was harder than a rock, pillows and sheets smelled AWFUL and the carpets were filthy. Thank god I was only here for two nights. There was this non-slip mat in the bathtub and it was gross because it was complete stuck on there and this weird mold/gunk started to form on it. Spend the extra $30 and stay at the hotel Rose next time. OH and the free continental breakfast only goes from 7-930am because they're cheap. You are basically just paying for location and nothing else. The wifi is awful and kicks you off the entire time, no free parking and breakfast is at a very limited time.

author: ATerrapin
title: Average Stay
text: The lobby was nice and the staff very helpful. The layout was somewhat confusing - trying to find our room was laborious because of the various levels and outdoor walkways etc. Our room was clean and comfortable. The continental breakfast was not available to us because we had to leave for the Rose Parade. They did their best to bring some food out for us though. I think my biggest complaints had to do with location. There were really no restaurants nearby - although there were some food trucks about two blocks away. It was quite warm out, however, and we really wanted to find a sit-down restaurant with air conditioning. The restaurant in the hotel was not open for some reason. When we asked at the front desk, they didn't give us a reason for why it was closed.

author: 480jimw
title: An Adequate Place for the Money
text: I was in Portland for a wedding in late July. This hotel was convenient to their home, but otherwise was in a rather uninspiring location with very few attractions. It is right near I-405. I did not try the local transportation because of scheduling. It is owned and, I believe, operated by Portland State University. The facility is due for an upgrade as it is beginning to show its bare threads in the lobby and rooms. The room had a tube TV, a first for me in many years and stays at other hotels. The WiFi is only available in two wings and poolside, which worked for me as I was on the first level and thereby next to the pool. The staff was ok, but I did think the complimentary breakfast was good, perhaps because this place has a full restaurant kitchen and dining room...better than rubber scrambled egg "patties" and bottom shelf cereal in the budget chain operations.

author: GeoT
title: Good location for the South end of downtown Portland
text: We were going to a play at the Keller Auditorium and this hotel is just two blocks away. The parking was cheaper than most downtown hotels and we did not have to drive while we were there. It is also right in the mix with Portland State University. The service was great. The breakfast was good. The wifi is a bit tricky to set up, but once going was really fast with no dropping out or not being able to log in. The hotel itself is a bit dated and the room, although clean looks like it could use an update. When we got back from the play, there was no hot water for a shower, although there was plenty the next morning. Overall, we were satisfied, but not overwhelmed. Occasionally, when the rest of downtown Portland is booked, this hotel has rooms.

author: 310rizwana
title: sunny portland
text: not a very clean place. very old property, in a dire need of upgrade. wifi internet was good. breakfast was very good. location not very easy access from and to the highway. staff was friendly. they charge a parking fee :). lots of good places to eat at a walking distance.

author: Neil_in_Sheffield_UK
title: This hotel is becoming dated and needs upgrading. Draught-proofing room doors would be a good start.
text: The best thing about this hotel was its location - just to the south of downtown Portland. Breakfast fayre was also pretty good. But I have three significant negatives to report about our third floor room:- 1) The door was not draught-proof and so the room became very chilly. In the morning you could see daylight creeping in all around the doorway as the outside air continued to rush in. 2) When the lady next door got up early to have her shower we were woken by the noise. We heard her turn on the shower and drop her soap - that is how soundproof the room was. 3) Although I knew about this beforehand, I don't see why guests with cars should have to pay $15 a day for car parking. It is just a rip off and seems more so when I recall that in no other hotel on our North West Pacific holiday journey did we have to pay a car parking fee. University Place is a big hotel but it is becoming rather dated and needs upgrading if it is to justify its room prices. The TV in our room was chunky old school and so modern oblong TV images were incomplete on the square screen.

author: BonnieKeith
title: Under rehab, Not a pleasant room
text: We booked through a third party site for this hotel/motel. The room looked old and the furniture looked old too. The air conditioner unit was old and couldn't cool the room enough. The biggest complaint about this place though, was that after we booked it, we get to the hotel and they tell us that it will be $15.00 to park in THEIR parking lot outside our rooms. Ridiculous that it wasn't included in the price of staying in this place. The good thing about this hotel is that it was close to waterfront dining and street cars were right outside our hotel. We should have left the rental car at the airport and taken the railway/street cars to this place. This place did have a full hot breakfast that came with the stay. The rooms face in (courtyard interior), but you should be very aware that you will be there with college students during a lot of the times of the year.

author: billc145
title: Well appointed, well located, well priced.
text: Clean, well appointed, large room, with comfortable bed. Good facilities. Brilliant proximity to several public transport options giving quick access throughout city for low cost. Access to Avis/Budget hire car also a bonus, providing reasonably priced rental cars with free airport drop off. Breakfast selection was quite good, with cereal and selection of hot food. Reasonably priced evening meals available at the restaurant. Would stay again, and already recommended hotel to friends who were staying in higher priced hotels with smaller rooms. Thanks

author: jane_turner53
title: Great Value for Money
text: This hotel is in a great central location - close to the main trams and within easy walking distance of the river. The breakfast was plentiful and included (unusual in the USA) in the price. Our bedroom was clean and comfortable. The carpet and the decor was a bit 'tired', but not so as to spoil our visit. We had a very nice evening meal which was reasonably priced. Surprisingly, there is a notice on the next requesting that patrons do not give gratuities. Instead there is a form which you are asked to complete and to name a particular member of staff, if we have had good/bad service. I would be happy to recommend this hotel to anyone who is visiting Portland. It is great value for money, clean and with pleasant staff. What more can you want?

author: X8118TCdavidd
title: Run from this place
text: Does not even rate a star. they charge me for room. Then charge me again for the room already pay for. Then I check on the date that I paid up to and they charge me again! the rooms had no wireless internet. The floor were dirty and room was not clean when I check in. I posting photo of the room on my faceBook. It was the worst hotel i have ever stay in. This place stay away unless you like a nightmare like i had. I told them and all they say was sorry we will fix might take week on money.

author: Hannahebryant
title: A Little Disappointing
text: We read the reviews but were on a strict budget so we stayed here anyway. The good news is that they seemed to have fixed the wifi problem (at least if you spend the extra ~$10 for a deluxe room) and it is really close to the Max light rail station. Unfortunately a deluxe room is far from deluxe. We were there in November and the window did not seem to close properly but the heat only understood HOT so temperature was a constant problem. The room was very outdated and the lighting fluorescent. Lets just say I wasn't wanting to stay longer than necessary in the room. The breakfast was fine, nothing special but edible, ends at 930am. The staff was helpful though and there is coin laundry which I desperately needed and was appreciative of. If you're pinching pennies this is an option but you could probably find much better.

author: Road_Rage_Kmac
title: Good place to stay in S. Portland on a budget
text: We decided to stay here because of the reasonable price and location. This hotel is not too far from some local breweries so it worked out great for us. I didn't mind paying the parking fee, in October it was $15/day, I just rolled it in to the hotel cost. The complimentary breakfast was great, there was scrambled eggs, oatmeal, sausage, bacon, yogurt, etc. and all foods were kept stocked until the very end of serving time. Staff was friendly and polite. We stayed in a Deluxe King room which on the website said had a fridge and microwave in the room, unfortunately there was not, but we had not brought food with us so I did not raise a stink about it. Overall, I would recommend this place if you are looking to stay in South Portland on a budget.

author: CGJW
title: Great value, location, and staff.
text: Average+ rooms. Clean. Quiet - even on the front side and second floor. Nice modest pool. Excellent large free breakfast (but horrible coffee). Great parking. Friendly staff. Easy to find. We will return.

author: Awalsh58
title: Wish I stayed somewhere else
text: About the only thing to recommend this hotel is the low price, but you get what you pay for. I stayed here a week while attending a conference at Portland State in the summer of 2013. It has a very complex layout, which I found hard to navigate. I had requested a room on the first floor, since I have a mild disability. I did get a room on the first floor, but didn't realize until I got there that getting to it from the hotel lobby involved climbing several short flights of stairs (up and down) to get to it. Hotel was unable or unwilling to provide a more convenient room when I asked. The rooms themselves were very dated and didn't look like they had been upgraded for a couple of decades. It was basically clean, but not exceptionally so. Room air conditioner was extremely loud as it cycled on and off all night, making it hard to sleep.

author: ronaldl878
title: Softball World Series Trip
text: Previously being employed as a Hotel lead engineer/maintenance employee I have seen several things that could improve here. If you are a host hotel for an event such as this you should ensure that you have everything squared away prior to everyone's arrival to include that all of your ice machines work, all of your soda machines are being filled daily, your laundry facilities machines coin bins are being emptied daily, and that your bar/restaurant are not closing early or running out of things. During our stay on Friday and Saturday night the bar closed at 10 P.M. which meant that if you wanted a place to hang out for a few drinks you couldn't unless you left the hotel. unless you called and complained.... your room was only partially cleaned, your trash not emptied, no clean cups, nor is your toilet cleaned, the side walk would have had more cushion than your bed... you had to pay to park in the hotel parking lot on top of paying for your room.. the cook in the restaurant had a attitude when the waiter would ask about your food and because the cook didn't want to stay late the bartender had no choice but to close...so customer service being a restaurant manager for eight years myself they totally sucked and wouldn't recommend to anyone

author: southpugetsound
title: A Secret Hotel!
text: I dub this a secret hotel as you won't find this hotel on most of the major travel agency websites (Expedia, Priceline, etc.). This hotel is managed by Portland State University and doesn't adjust their rates for occupancy like most major downtown hotels do. Every hotel except for some 1-star dumps within a 2-mile radius of downtown Portland was sold out for various festivals/events going on EXCEPT University Place, which most tourist don't know about. Overall: older but good three star hotel. Pros: Has a pool, clean, very close to Max light rail station, easy walking distance. Cons: Wireless Internet was terrible. Every five minutes it crashes/times out and requires a new login. Fortunately Portland is a 4G area and I was getting better connection through the data plan on my phone than the hotel's (PSU) wireless network. Will I stay again? You bet!

author: d0nebeendid
title: Curse of the Keurig
text: This hotel is ideally located for a visit to Portland, and the price is right. We have stayed here several times and never regretted it. Just one caveat:Bring your own coffee pot and coffee. The single cup brewers might be ok for a lone business traveler, but when two or more people are staying in the room or suite, they are a royal pain. The first question for me in choosing a hotel: how much trouble is it going to be for us to have coffee together in the room before we go out to meet the day? But the Internet access has improved here lately. You only have to register, click the link in the email, and log on once a day now, not every 20 minutes. It would be nice if they didn't play the TV at loud volume in the breakfast room (or even better, no TV at all).

author: RWorldtraveler
title: A perfectly fine budget hotel
text: This is a moderately priced hotel that provides all of the basic amenities that you would expect, plus a few homey extras (e.g. a microwave next to the TV!). My room was clean and although the furniture was dated it was in good condition. Given the reviews I read (and given that just about every other hotel near downtown Portland was booked), my expectations were rather low, so I feared the worst. It is a perfectly fine budget hotel and I had no complaints about the service or the quality of my sleep while there. I was offered a cookie when I checked in - which I declined - and thought it really sweet that the person at the front desk tried to change my mind because "they are really good cookies." The continental breakfast included hot food as well as cereal and fruit, although the sight of everyone watching the overhead TV in the breakfast room as they silently ate their food reminded me of a nursing home. I had no issues with internet access once I figured out how to activate their wi fi and everything else in my room worked fine. As I prefer a more exciting and stylish hotel, I probably would not stay again unless I had few other choices and were on more of a budget. But really, the University Place hotel is perfectly fine.

author: PopRoxy
title: Good enough if you just need a place to sleep and leave luggage
text: I was really impressed by the spread at the continental breakfast, they even had soy milk, which I appreciated. The front desk staff was very kind and more than willing to help us plan our route to adventuring in Portland at all hours. The location is great, right by the Max Line and really only 20 to 30 minutes walking distance from downtown if you're a walker like me. Other than that the hotel was mostly very average. The cleaning staff did what they could with what they had, but it was obvious that giving a thorough cleaning to everything in the room was not part of their job requirements. I found drops of blood on the inside of the bed coverlet and the carpet felt so grimy that I just kept my runners on every moment that I wasn't showering or sleeping. I would neeeeever go here for a romantic weekend and I would probably be too germphobic to bring kids here, but if you just want to explore Portland with friends then it's very nearly perfect;y suited to your needs. Also, Portland is lovely. You should definitely stay here and have a nice mini adventure.

author: Chicky-Athens
title: Comfortable Room - Pleasant Staff
text: The room was, well, roomy. It had a chair to hang out in and a chair and desk to work at. The staff at the front desk were pleasant and helpful if not always knowledgable about the area. It was a great value considering the competition. If you want to feel like you are downtown, this is not the place, however it is not in the boondocks either. There is very good public transportation nearby and I walked downtown (although, I'm a walker). The hotel is very close to a food-truck area and a couple of university bars. I enjoyed staying here.

author: PLJ10
title: More of a motel than a hotel
text: The room was large, which was nice, but not very clean. It was cheap, though, and you get what you pay for. To get internet you have to plug your computer into an Ethernet cord that only extends a foot from the wall. Sounds can be heard very easily from the next room. If you stay here maybe ask if the construction is still going on. We had to drive in a big circle just to get to an alternative entrance. Continental breakfast is included, but not parking. I would not stay here again.

author: mrsktm
title: Average
text: We stayed here a few days ago at the end of a trip through the US. We chose to stay here as the Budget rental is here where we had to return our car. We had a very old room, very old (we didn't think we would). The wifi didn't work and we were told when booking the hotel had wifi - there was a cable to plug your laptop into though. When we awoke in the morning the roof was leaking on us, so we went down and complained and were moved after breakfast to a deluxe king room for a few hours until we checked out which was very nice. I thought the room we initially booked would look like the deluxe king room (which was quite nice). The breakfast was very average, served on paper plates with paper cutlery, quite odd. The night before we had dinner and drinks at the restaurant downstairs and the server (only girl working) 'kept' $5 on our bill when bringing the change. I'm not sure if she did this on purpose and decided on her own tip or didn't add what we gave her up properly, but we didn't tip her because of this, we thought it was quite rude, she would have got a tip otherwise. The hotel is quite old, we have had a lot better for less.

author: 247PaulS247
title: Not worth the money
text: My wife and I stayed here for four nights, attending a recent convention in Portland. On the positive side: the rooms were clean and the service was good. On the negative side: I was told of a $12 parking fee at check-in, which was not mentioned at the time of booking. There was no wi-fi in my room in C wing, only ethernet (which does me no good with an iPad) and no amenities like a 'fridge or microwave that one might expect at this price point. The breakfast offered looked nice but appearances were deceiving. The toaster took forever and the eggs were over-salted to the point of being inedible. Even the potatoes had a funny taste. I would never recommend this hotel to a friend and will not return on future trips to Portland.

author: blujaded
title: You get what you pay for here.
text: The staff was very friendly and the location is excellent for a visit to downtown Portland. Very close to free public transportation. The room was very clean, but with only minimal amenities. Unfortunately, although there is LAN internet in the room, WiFi is only available in the public areas which was very inconvenient. The room was very small and the beds (full size) were stiff and uncomfortable. They charge extra for parking ($12/day), which wasn't something they tell you when booking. The continental breakfast was bigger than most offer with lots of choices, but the quality & taste of most of the food was poor. All in all, I wouldn't recommend it to a friend, and I will spend a little more to stay at a nicer location on my next visit.

author: lennybruceisdead
title: Great place to stay if you're on a budget
text: Very acceptable rooms at extremely good prices (we were three in a room and paid $110 per night incl hotel tax). The location is good: if you don't mind a short walk, you can easliy get downtown on foot. Otherwise there is a MAX stop a couple of blocks away. The breakfast, while not exactly gourmet, is free - so no real complaints there. Parking is cheap as well at $12 per night. And the chocolate chip cookies that they gave us when we checked in may have been the best cookie I ever had. The hotel lobby and other areas could sure use a makeover, but then I bet the prices would rise. Anyways who cares what it looks like. The rooms are clean, the service is good, the location is prime, and the price is right.

author: verymary
title: Nice place, great value and awesome location- with an outdoor pool!
text: We were in Portland on business with Portland State University and this property happens to be owned by that school. Located on campus it is close to the museum and block parks, has easy access to public transit and is within walking distance of a really nice section of downtown Portland. Our room was lovely. Overlooking the courtyard and pool, it was well appointed and clean. Though obviously not new, it is suitable for any traveler(s) looking for a good value in a terrific location on campus. It is close to affordable restaurants and the outdoor pool area makes it a great choice for families with children. Of course, understand that this is a school campus so there may be college students present. Typically that could mean noise issues - but we did not encounter any problems on that level - even after passing half of a football team in the hall. The staff was helpful and friendly.

author: tws1
title: Not suitable for a patient from the hospital
text: Requested a quiet room because I was having surgery at OHSO and was going to need a night to recover. I got a room with a giant noisy machine directly outside the room. Next I had purchased the manditory parking passes for $12 dollars a night and WAS STILL TICKETED $80 dollars by the parking enforcement. The staff started an argument with me over the parking dispute even though they charged the parking passes on my AMEX. Remember, I had just under gone surgery for my inner ear. I was in no shape to properly defend myself and they took complete advantage of me and the situation. I called the police and my attorneys. I am never staying there AGAIN. If you are going to the hospital for any procedure and need to spend the night, DO NOT STAY HERE!

author: juanita_ash
title: it was dirty
text: We were sent to this place until our room at the Ronald Macdonald house. my daughter is ready to deliver and her baby will need an operation as soon as he is born. The heart specialist said to go there to wait. When we arrived the quilt on my bed had blood on it and not a little. The blanket underneath had white stuff on it and it was not milk!! They never cleaned the room the entire week we where there. We live 5 hours from there and we came home because we could not stand to be there anymore. we had to pay $25 for a microwave and a little fridge that froze everything. If you can avoid it do not go there.. Also it was $12 a day for parking.

author: cypanadero
title: Old and just Ok
text: Stayed here with my gf and some of my friends during spring break. We travelled from Vancouver Canada and spent 2 nights here, front desk seemed indifferent toward anything and I don't think I saw a smile on any of their faces once. The elevator was ancient, hallways were dark and dingy and looked like nothing had been changed since the early 90s. Our hotel room had filthy carpets and I would NOT walk on it without having a pair of shoes or flip flops on. Bed sheets need to be changed too since they are outdated. If you're looking for a cheap hotel not too far off of downtown, this isn't a bad place if you're on a budget and not picky about where you stay. Otherwise, i'm sure there are better ones out there. P.S. AVOID THE BREAKFAST!! ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING!!

author: NurseOR2009
title: Ugh! Stay away!
text: I was in Portland for an orientation at OHSU with three of my collegues and thought this place seemed like a convenient spot. We had 4 to a room with 2 double beds so things were pretty tight, but it made it worse that their ways of running things were completely ridiculous. Not only was it $12 a night to park, but they only "allowed" us 2 continental breakfast tickets per room and expected the 2 other guests to pay $7 for each of their "meals". All the breakfast included was carbs like muffins and some fruit. To top it off, at check out, they actually tried to charge us $25 for using the in-room microwave! There was no warning or sign to prepare us for such an unreasonable policy. The front desk had no explanation for their policies, but we managed to talk our way out of it. This hotel really put a damper on our trip and I'd suggest you go elsewhere.

author: palmera12
title: Dirty Hotel with Poor Service
text: Do not stay here if for no other reason than the service is terrible. This hotel was chosen for a function we were attending. Prior to arival, I tried to change our reservations over the phone; I was unable to speak a compentent person - so I gave up on the phone and decided it might be easier in person. Unpon check in the staff made it entirely to difficult for a simple room change. The customer service was horrible. Entering our room - it was dirty ( dusty, mold, and a used coffee cup); also, there were no wash cloths. We called the front desk and housekeeping for them to act like it was no big deal. I could go on on on....but bottom line is we will never stay there again, nor would we recommend it to anyone.

author: nickuw94
title: Horrible Hotel! Absoutely Ridiculous
text: This hotel was one of the worst I have ever seen. Pictures deceive you online. When I arrived for a conference I checked into my room and went to use the bathroom. I lifted the toilet seat, only to find that it had not been flushed, and therefore not cleaned. I called the Front Desk and said I would like housekeeping to come clean my room and her reply was "oh, I am talking with housekeeping right now and will send her to help you clean it." HELP ME!!!! Are you serious. The floor had stains, the shower was ridiculous, it took three ice machines before we found one that worked, my friends toilet didn't even flush (she had to lift the back and hook it back together). Food in restaurant was WAY over priced for the type of hotel and was not good quality anyway. Most of the other conference attendees felt this hotel was unbelievable. I recommend you spend your $125 a night in a place you know has been cleaned.

author: aronCA
title: Needs to revive setting and personnel
text: Unfortunately the ambience is dismally grey, and the personnel appear to reflect the setting. While they were polite, their responses were chilly and short. The rooms had no luggage racks so the suitcases remained on the desk top or on the one chair. The shelf for toiletries by the sink was taken up by the coffee maker, so there was no space for personal supplies. There was no refrigerator in room. The decor was unpleasant and cheerless, no color. Only one computer available near the guest shop with a charge of $3.95 for 15 minutes, most other hotels have one available at no charge for guests. No nearby coffee shop or diner, just a formal restaurant. The buffet breakfasts provided for the group were mediocre and often lacking (milk, jams etc). On the positive side, the beds were comfortable but the rest of the setting was inhospitable.

author: Vera1983
title: Amazing location, good hotel but poor service
text: At the entrance I've noticed that hotel is 4*, as actually experienced - it’s not more than 3* . Some renovation, and internal staff work would save the reputation of the hotel, as if you look closely - furniture is ok, but some bathroom facilities are broken, carpet in the room was burnt a little (while room was non-smoking), but the most disappointing was household services (sometimes forgot to bring tissue box, sometimes toilet paper, shower amenities were never refilled), and in very last days I’ve notices small black ants on the carpet, and you can only wonder how this room was made up. Internal walls are so thin – that you can easily hear what people in a next room are doing or talking about, especially it’s clear in bathroom. Choice of food on breakfast is also quite disappointing: free drinks are only water with lemon, and fruit flavored “something” which is called “Corange juice”, which tastes more like fruit powdered concentrated dissolved in tap water. Of course, scrambled egg is there, and quite nice haloumi cheese fried with tomatoes, small plane croissants, choice of cheese, olives and jam. But generally, the choice is so poor, that 4 mentioned stars are not applicable to such breakfast. If you’re lucky to get sea-view room – it’s breathtaking! Walls of ancient city, waves of Marmara Sea, sea wind- it’s all so beautiful, even when weather is not pleasant. If I’d decided to live in 3* hotel – I’d be extremely satisfied, but once you pay 4* - you expect equivalent service and conditions. And luckily, location and window view – are not the only factors which affect the overall rating of the hotel, good services and accommodation conditions still come first.

author: DejanSTQ
title: Excellent hotel on a perfect location
text: We stayed 2 night (only unfortunately). It is too short time to write a proper review, but also first impression is the most important. So, Perfect location, at the edge of old citadel near the sea, easily accessible with a car and there is private parking. The hotel is very clean, well maintained, "modern" architecture of 60's and 70's, but somehow it fits very well in historical environment. We have panoramic view room 2+1. Beds are very comfortable, excellent sleep quality. Bathroom is little bit small, but therefore shower box is big. Staff is very friendly. We will definitely come back.

author: ecekop
title: great service and food
text: It is an old hotel but I guess they keep up with most of the renovations, it looked all clean and nice. The staff is really nice and professional. We were there for a wedding and spent the night there. The wedding was really nice, all food and organization were perfect. We also had lunch before the wedding ceremony and breakfast the day after. Everything was really delicious, had no problem. The only downside was the bed for us, it might just because we got used to a certain type of bed and this one didn't suit for us. It was hard yet jumpy and made noise every time one turns. So cannot say that I had a good sleep, unfortunately. But besides that everything was just fine.

author: md9512016
title: Good hotel by the sea
text: While the hotel probably wouldn't make 4 stars in Europe or North America, it was still good. The lobby was clean and spacious. We found the staff to be very friendly and helpful. Our room (junior suite) was a little smaller than the pictures lead us to believe, but that seems to be the norm. It was clean but some areas definitely need redone (bathroom mostly). Our room was facing the ocean, which though nice, gets full sun until early afternoon. It was getting so hot that the AC could not keep up even with the curtains drawn, so choose your room appropriately. The bedding was not very comfortable, especially the pillows (too hard). The location is good, but down the hill from Sultanhamet and about a 15 min walk to Sultanhamet Square (hard with strollers).

author: Jamal29054
title: Disappointing food and food service but nice place though
text: The hotel has it's fantastic location. However, I have some disappointments and comments with one of the services which is the food service. I have booked the room with breakfast included but I did not find the satisfaction with the food as it lacked the turkish style. Fruits provided had been limited to 2 varieties only. One instance also was when I woke up at 7:15am and the food was not ready yet so I need to wait before I could have my breakfast. Also, the shampoo provided in my room has no smell at all compared to other rooms, while lotion has its good quality even no fragrance. Apart from my disappointments, the reception service and room cleaning service have improved from before based on my experience from my previous stay with them. I wish the hotel must take note of the comments from the guests on which service needs attention and improvements.

author: egons2014
title: Very nice and friendly
text: I was here with my wife. We had a pleasant room with sea view. The staff was perfect, friendly, accurate and always available when needed. The room was clean, bath room with shower, clean and useful. Since the mattrace as a bit hard the crew put a softening layer on it, which gave better comfort. Only neg. point was the street noises from the coastal road. But this has to be taken into account when you want to have sea view. I certainly would stay here again.

author: flybird40
title: Good
text: I stayed 2 nights its good hotel. For short stay it is nice. Room is ok. Bed is hard as my want. I slept well. I offer to sray here. Prices is ok not so expensive. Reception staff is helpfull. İstanbul is very good.. We enjoy so much.

author: MarilynS5
title: Location
text: The hotel is located on the Bosphorus, within walking distance to the Blue Mosque, Hague Sophia, Grand Bazaar. Room was very large, clean, modern, air conditioned. It has elevators, which is not always the case in all hotels. I did not like shower though, could not close the door all the way. We could watch the ships from our room. The hotel has nice restaurant and bar. Bar prices were reasonable, only 40 TL (about $12 US Dollars) for room delivery for four beers. Staff was helpful when our shuttle did not show up, especially night manager, Levent Olcaner. Breakfast buffet has wide variety and wonderful patio.

author: M2242RSmohammeda
title: Below par
text: I stayed there for one night. The hotel has no gym, and non are nearby. The rooms have very poor sound isolation and are pretty small. Internet was poor and the signal was not reaching my room. The hotel had one venue for breakfast and any other meal. The location was not the best for tourists but was very suitable for a sea side run. Breakfast was limited to few choices. Would choose a different property next time.

author: andrearobbiebebop
title: Excellent location to visit the Old City
text: I travelled with a large group and the hotel staff could not have been more helpful. The group check-in was very efficient, and we were all in our rooms within about 20 mins of arriving - impressive for a group of approx 40 people!! The reception staff continued to be very helpful throughout our stay and were always cheerful. The hotel itself has magnificent views over the water, and the breakfast is fabulous - good variety and high quality to get us going for the day. We also ate in the restaurant, and again, the food and service was of a high standard. As mentioned in previous reviews, the hotel location is very easy access to the Old City, and the Blue Mosque, Hagia Sofia and the Cisterns are all a very easy walk. There are a number of restaurants between the hotel and the centre as well, which all looked reasonable in standard - we ate at one, and it was excellent local food. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who wanted a good night of sleep and a very convenient location to this fascinating city.

author: 170rachelt
title: Great for tourists!
text: We stayed here for about a week last August. The location is great for exploring Sultanahmet and for accessing the tram to get to other areas of Istanbul. They have a backdoor which you can leave and enter through (via a buzzer) that opens onto the small hill that leads you directly up to the Blue Masque and Aya Sofia. The staff was very friendly and helpful and our room was perfectly comfortable. We could hear a bit more noise from adjacent rooms/the hallway than I would have liked, but ultimately it was not a huge deal. We had a window facing the back/garden area, which was nice (although I would have loved to have a sea view, we just couldn't afford to pay for it) I would definitely recommend this place to other tourists visiting Istanbul. It's nice that it's a little separate from the main tourist area, but still right there, if that makes sense. I liked having the short walk back to the hotel to wind down from our adventures and it meant that when we were at the hotel I felt very relaxed as well.

author: Ramialsaidi
title: 6 days business / touristic stay
text: I have stayed 6 wunderful days at kalyon. Great location with the sea view for relaxation and tourism within the beautiful old city. The hotel is modern and has business facilities for meetings. Extra helpful staff beyond regular service.. Specially in direct contact with Mr. Mustafa and Ms. Hulya The currency exchange also is very helpful and at a great rate. They had an internet connection issue that they will fix soon

author: Atmolex
title: Just perfect
text: The hotel is located in a few minutes walking distance from Blue Mosque, Aya Sofya and Topkapi palace which are one of the most beautiful and iconic places in Istanbul. On the way to Grand Bazaar from Sultanahmet park we enjoyed the spirit of old Istanbul with it's small shops and old buildings! And they are really quite close to Kalyon. This area is great for making photographs. We stayed in Kalyon in Executive room with a sea view which is really impressive due to huge glass windows. We also liked a design of the room and it's size - it's really big! The staff was very polite and the service was excellent! It's not the first time for us in Istanbul and I should frankly say that it's a rare example of such a perfect combination of service, value and amenities. The breakfast was good, a lot of fruits, varieties of cheese and sweets, fresh juices and bakery. We liked it a lot!

author: Chakal01
title: Good option
text: Not much to say apart from praising the staff's friendliness, good breakfast (average price), cleanliness, comfort of the room and location. It is in Sultanahmet, quite close the Blue Mosque and the stunningly inspiring Hagia Sofia, but not extremely central (if it's raining, you'd better be wearing a rain coat or have an umbrella). Taxi drivers don't seem to have heard of it, so if you are to take a taxi, make sure you have the address with you. By the way, I was told that taxi drivers are not reliable in Istanbul. I didn't have any bad experience with them (took only twice, but must confess that one of them made me think that he could overcharge me. He didn't in the end, maybe due to my 'switched on attitude'...) Anyway, I would recommend the hotel. I would only like to point out as well that the staff don't speak great English. Some of them speak better than others, but they are all very welcoming. Make sure you explain clearly to the chambermaid that your room is free to clean/tidy up, as they don't look at the notice card advising to clean or not clean the room. I had trouble locking the window of my room, but a member of staff sorted it out for me.

author: angelcakebaby1
title: Lovely, relaxed location beside the water.
text: Clean rooms, helpful polite staff and fabulous location for site seers. There is a terrace area where you can eat or lounge on the couches watching the boats come in. I honestly do not believe i have ever felt more relaxed than when i was sitting on those couches with a book and a glass of wine at sunset watching the boats make their lazy way. Absolute bliss. The hotel isnt exactly pretty on the outside but inside it is modern and well maintained. We didnt have a great view but apparently you can ask for a room at the front of the hotel which looks out onto the Bosphorus. The Blue Mosque is right around the corner if you are a good walker but if you are disabled or not so great on your feet its a bit of a trek i guess. Lots of great places to get food nearby too though the food at the hotel is great and the service is flawless.

author: BSahin
title: Lovely Renovated Hotel
text: I stayed there in November and found it charming. It has been renovated newly. I had a sea view room and has very large windows to sit in front of the view. Bads and pillows were very comfortable, my room was big and clean. Hotel is placed at the historical peninsula and it's 3 min walk to Sultanahmet, 10 min to Taksim by taxi, and close to the airport. It is also very close to the ferry port. On the other hand, hotel has a good restaurant and you may eat your lunch or dinner at the hotel. There were only one bad situation happened while I was sleeping, reception called the room in the middle of the night and they didn't say sorry for this. Hotel is highly recommended by me:)

author: uzmag
title: Great location, great hotel
text: We loved our stay here. The hotel was clean, the staff were very friendly and helpful. We were forever asking for advice on where to go, shop and eat and they were always happy to help. Easier to access main area of Sultanahmet from the back door which the staff were always more than happy to open for us. It wasn't an issue for me but theres no Leisure Centre or Swimming pool facilities. Overall very professional service and the staff always looked immaculate. Rooms were always cleaned to a high standard and they would leave chocolates and the weather for the next day everyday which was very nice! I loved my stay in Kalyon and overall in Istanbul and would definitely stay here again.

author: StantonJR
title: Not enough room to swing a cat!
text: The hotel was conveniently located, near enough to the old town but just 30 minutes from the airport. The hotel was clean throughout but our 'classic' double room was so, so tiny - there wasn't enough room to swing a cat. It was probably the smallest room I have ever stayed in and for the price that was being paid grossly overpriced and overrated. There was only 1 towel in the bathroom (thank goodness the cleaning trolley was just down the corridor) and you need to be a size '0' model to use the shower. We had tea and coffee but no kettle. We told reception who argued that there must be one in the room but they would check - they didn't and we went without. The TV remote did not work. All in all, thank goodness that our stay was one night only. I would certainly recommend looking elsewhere for your stay in Istanbul.

author: ia2T
title: Close to blue mosque
text: Good location and not far from the Blue mosque. About a 5 min walk using the back door exit. Staff are friendly enough. The wifi isnt great and drops out. The room is very clean and spacious. You can go for a walk by the water at the front of the hotel. We stayed there for 2 days in summer. Its a decent place for a short stay.

author: leeannj566
title: Fantastic stay!
text: Wonderful hotel! Great location with lovely view of Marmara Sea. The rooms are modern and spacious. We were 4 adults and a toddler. The staff are very efficient and friendly. They went out of their way to accommodate our child. Great food at the restaurant. A definite thumbs up from us!

author: arapuni
title: Great Position and super efficient friendly staff
text: The staff at this hotel were among the most professional, efficient and friendly that I have encountered in a 4 star hotel. I had asked my agent to book for myself for 3 days, and for 2 people for the rest of my stay. This had not happened, and I had a small room on the ground floor. Despite the fact that the hotel were not at fault, they organized for me to move into a room with 2 single beds on the day my friend arrived. Not only that, they moved all my things to the new room. Breakfasts were excellent, great variety, and extremely efficient staff. The view from the dining room and terrace across the Bosphorus was magic. The hotel is in a very convenient position, within easy walking distance of the Blue Mosque, Ayasofya, Topkapi palace and numerous other interesting spots. There are plenty of places to eat around the area, although I can recommend the menu and wine list at the hotel.

author: mikhenderson
title: Couple of little niggles, but good location
text: Negatives - not every room has a view of the Bosporus or Blue Mosque. Ours looked out onto a brick wall. You have to go out through a side door if you want to go to Sultanahmed (why else would you book this hotel as a tourist?), the staff buzz you through the first gate and then forget you are there! It happened more than once to me and I had to stand in a small walled garden waving at a locked door to get someones attention. The terrace bar is a nice place to sit for an afternoon drink. there are always 3 or 4 staff wandering in your general direction, they will happily take your order, and deliver it, but for some reason seem to find it impossible to produce a bill. You ask the nearest staff member - he nods, walks away and then comes back and starts moving glasses from one table to another - you wait 10 minutes, remind him you need a bill and he nods, smiles and walks away again. This didn't happen once, in a one week stay it happened 3-4 times. Positives - We paid not much for the room via Expedia, the terrace overlooking the Bosporus is great place to people watch, the staff are friendly, there are plenty of great places to eat in a close proximity and the Blue Mosque is a simple 200 metre hill climb away.

author: ChristianeV907
title: To be recommended
text: The Kalyon Hotel is very nicely located in fromt of the Marmara sea; so the view from the window on the front is very nice. Unfortunately there is a busy road in between, which you can hear in the room. By putting the airco on, this noice is removed. Nice rooms, you sleep well. The hotel staff is very good, friendly and helpful. The breakfast is very nice and the hotel has a nice lounge with view on the seaside where you can drink something and have a rest . Nice to sit there. I was very pleased with this hotel for my short business stay in Istanbul.

author: Swissmags
title: Room with a view...
text: On arrival we were disappointed to find we had a room at the back of the hotel when the Marmara Sea was right in the front. On looking out of our window we got the best surprise of all.... The most fabulous view of the Blue Mosque. We could see it from the (hard)bed and day or night it was stunning!! The staff were very helpful in the hotel but we never ate there.
