The first morning we walked into the dining room and found it to be very busy and stuffy. The food looked lovely but I preferred to try and find something outside. The location was good... a back gate from the hotel allowed a 5-10 minute walkto the main attractions of Sultanamet ( Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia and the Cisterns).

author: Williamw00
title: An appropriate hotel for working and visiting Istanbul
text: Stayed in this nicely decorated hotel for four nights in the room of no.265. The room was spacious, clean and stylish while windows facing the sea view making it even more cozy. The bathroom has nice bathtub with rain shower option. Location is very wise, exit through the back door is more convenient if you are planning to go into Sultanahmet area. However, you need to request the help from receptionist to unlock the back door due to their security policy and the staffs are always friendly to assist you. During my stay, I really enjoyed truthfully and I also learned that this hotel is more suitable for working or meeting as it has facilities such as meeting room and a decent dining restaurant instead of swimming pool, gym or recreation area for relaxation. The staffs and housekeeping are working according to managements and they did good but at times you may feel the lack sense of fun, humble and harmony that you always find in Turkish culture. However, at times, you also will feel very warm and sweet from the weather report that comes with chocolate treat.

author: gibboa
title: Excellent place both to stay and to tour Istanbul from
text: My wife and I stayed at this excellent hotel in April 2013 . From the moment we checked in we we're made to feel at home . The staff are super friendly and very efficient . The rooms are very well appointed and impeccably clean and the location is excellent . Just exit the back door and you are no further than 5 minutes from the Blue Mosque , the Haja Sophia and the the Topkapi Palace . All of Sultanahmet is just a quick walk away . This hotel is well priced and provides free WIFI that works to all guests . Well worth a stay .

author: JackieJ804
title: The Best of Both Worlds
text: This stylish & modern hotel is ideally situated for exploring the old town area of Istanbul. With the great advantage of being situated on the sea, the standards within the hotel are of the highest in every respect, the service is immaculate as are the reception areas and rooms. Breakfast was a delight with a fantastic choice of fruits, breads, cheeses and the best scrambled egg I have ever tasted in a hotel. There were also traditional Turkish hot items such as cheese pastries and savoury soups which were nice to try. After a hectic day in the busy streets of Istanbul, this hotel is like an oasis of calm with modern decor and everything you need for a relaxing stay. We had a room to the rear of the hotel which had no view, but a plus was it was lovely and quiet and had the most comfortable bed. There was also a safe, a well stocked mini bar and a very modern bathroom with glass surfaces, a trendy wash bowl and a powerful shower. We travelled with another couple and we all agreed we could not have chosen a better hotel for our trip.

author: HansELind
title: Good for meetings
text: Stayed 3 nights due to a work meeting. Everything functioned very well - quick check in. Nice room (terrible view of backyard but the pro is the total lack of noise). Breakfast - splendid! Good sleep. Bathroom with rain-shower. Good pressure on water. Meeting room facilities and lunches also very perfect.

author: Majstorovici
title: Where Bosphorous meets Marmara sea
text: There , on European side of Istanbul , just under Blue Moscue is hotel Kalyon. Perfect place for start exploring the old Ottoman history places and perfect distance from Ataturk Airport and ferry port. Hotel stuff on reception was very helpfull and profesional, always polite and ready to help. Rooms are spacious and have good free WI-fi, perfect bads with selection of 4 different kind of pillows, coffe maker, big flat TV and mini bar. My room was on the first flour and with a view at Marmara sea. Selection of wines in hotel bar is very wide , but the waiters are too young to help You with the choice. Breakfast was very European , with a little of famous Turkish meals. That is something that should be changed by my opinion. All the Istanbul historical places and bazars are near and easy reachable by foot and hotel share one slide of old Constantinopolis defending wall. After two days spent in hotel Kalyon, I strongly recomend this hotel to anyone has business in Instabul and wants to explore it history places.

author: weekenderpaul
title: Perfect location
text: We have stayed previously at the Kalyon Hotel and its location cannot be beaten. The hotel faces the Bosphorous and it is in the heart of Sultanahmet on the Golden Horn. It is classified as a luxury four star hotel, which I would say it only just about manages. The Superior class rooms are clean and spacious and the rooms at the front have excellent views. The rooms at the rear of the hotel have very limited views of the city. If you have a hire car, the hotel has excellent parking facilities; something of a rarity in Istanbul. The hotel is ideally located for all the attractions in Sultanahmet. The Blue Mosque, the Grand Bazaar, Topkapi Palace and Hagia Sophia are all just a few minutes walk away.

author: 919AmandaC
title: Great stay!
text: I really cannot say enough great things about this hotel. My boyfriend and I were very impressed by everything from our room to the staff to the breakfast buffet. You may read reviews on here that talk about small rooms, but I felt our room size was perfect. (And I've worked for hotels in the past.). The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful as well. In addition to the staff, The location of the hotel was wonderful. It's a 5 minute walk to the Palace, the blue Mosque and the Haga Sofia and only about 10 minutes to the grand bazaar. It's also on the water front so you have lovely fish restaurants within walking distance of your room. If I ever return to Istanbul, I know exactly where I will book my accommodations!

author: dorinser
title: ideal position and very good quality
text: I stayed 4 nights at this hotel. It made a good impression. Tastefully designed interiors, nice smell, large and comfortable room with everything needed in it, great beds, great sea view, discrete and helpful staff. Location is very good, from the window it looks as if you're somewhere outside the city but in fact you're right in the center of the old part of the town, with a 7 minutes walk to Istanbul's most important historical monuments.The street in front of the hotel is very active and often crowded, but I didn't find the noise too big. In fact, the hotel is not directly on the street, there were 20-30 meters from our window. However, we got scared by the voice of a muezzin from a mosque nearby, probably the Blue Mosque, who woke us up at 6.00 a.m. with his morning song. In case you come by car, they have a generous and free parking place so again a good choice. All in all if you're not on budget it's a hotel worth your short list for your next visit to Istanbul.

author: Nasreen123K
title: Loved every minute of it!!
text: Kalyon hotel has to be one of the best hotels I have stayed in, every corner is full of detail and style, especially the paintings on the walls. It was my first time in Istanbul and the hotel staff made sure it was a memorable one, as soon as we stepped in I was greeted by Serap with a warm smile, she showed us to our room and made sure everything was just perfect from then on-wards for our 7 night stay. Serap took out the time to get to know us and what we expected from Istanbul. I had done my research so had a list of the places I wanted to visit but didn't know how far one was from the other and also how I would get there, that's were Serap's expertise kicked in and she drew a daily plan of sites I could visit in a day, showed me how to use the tram system and marked a very useful Istanbul map for me to reference to on my daily journeys. It was also refreshing to come back to the hotel after a long tiring day and be greeted by Serkan he was amazing he made so many suggestions of brilliant places to visit, places I didn't know of and the same as Serap marked them on my map for me showing me easy routes to get to them. Every evening it became a habit to go ask Serap what shall I do tomorrow, overall the staff are amazing from the reception staff to the security guards outside who always helped me carry my shopping to my room!! The little door at the back of the hotel is a gem, it only takes 5mins to get to the main area were the Blue mosque and main attractions are, and there is always someone at the door no matter how early or late you walk in. The room service is brilliant, the hotel restaurant is once again amazing especially the setting right across the sea, early morning you can see the dolphins setting out and again returning in the evenings, so I would give this hotel and the staff a 10 out f 10 for everything!!Especially the lovely scent they have in the lobby area and the wifi connection!! I look forward to returning to Istanbul and staying at the Kalyon again, no other hotel in Istanbul would now measure up to the love and service I received from this hotel, so if you are looking for good service overall try the Kalyon trust me you will not be disappointed...

author: TravelmateDurham
title: Perfect base hotel for exploring the historic sites of Istanbul
text: When I lived in Turkey 14 years ago, I always stayed at the Kalyon Hotel on my way out of the country. On a recent visit to Turkey, I was overjoyed to see that the Kalyon had kept up with the times and was still the perfect place to stay to explore all the wonderful historic sites of Istanbul. Go out the back door of the hotel and take a short walk up the hill through the old picturesque neighoborhoods takes you to the magnificent Hippodrome where you can see the Blue Mosque, the Hagia Sophia, the Topkapi Palace, and the colorful gardens surrounding all the spoils of war brought back to this glorious city which was then called Constantinople. As a bonus, the wonderful Kumkapi with its many delicious seafood restaurants is only a short 15 minute walk away. A 25-minute walk will even take you to the Covered Bazaar. The hotel concierge Serap was a wonderful and generous source on restaurants, tours, vendors, and of things to do. The hotel staff was wonderfully friendly and were quick to satisfy my every request and even had umbrellas in case the weather turned rainy. And to top it all of, the wireless service was free! I highly recommend the Kalyon Hotel for the adventurous traveler!

author: moth123
title: Dolphins in the sea of Marmara
text: We spent an enjoyable six days here during our recent Istanbul vacation. The staff are wonderful and very helpful. We arrived at the hotel at 0830 way before normal check in. We were quietly and efficiently checked in and provided a temporary room and seamlessly transferred into our proper room later in the day. Extremely welcome treatment after a long flight The back door is a real treasure. Through it you are 10 minutes walk away from Hagia Sophia and Cadessi Akbiyik the food street. The rooms are clean and spacious. We had a wonderful sea facing room where the view included dolphins occasionally usually early in the morning or after 8 pm when the boat traffic was reduced. They could probably do a lot better with the food but at least they try hard to please. The lack of the gym is made up by an awesome sea side run on the 3 km beach promenade right in front of the hotel All in all a thoroughly enjoyable stay and we hope to return

author: SteveG116
title: Nothing Special
text: Stayed here on business. A colleague of mine wanted to stay here and I was expecting amazing things from his overview of the last time he stayed but I am sorry to say this is a very average hotel. Prices are very high for what you get and you are better off Asia side getting much more for your money. Room was tiny with 5' bed. Very little working area/power points. Nearby restaurants are good. Breakfast was OK but pricey. One review here says all the rooms face the sea, they do not, my room overlooked a rather rundown local street and the Blue Mosque is very close which means you must be prepared to awake early for the 'call to prayer' I won't stay here again.

author: AngelosX
title: One of the best hotels in Istanbul. Next to the sea and almost next to the main attractions.
text: Yes, yes, and yes. The right hotel in the right place. I've born in Istanbul and spend 13 years there, so I know the place in first hand. Everything you need is so close. Attractions, shopping, transportation, everything. Not to mention the luxury, and above all the hospitality of the staff. We spent one week in this hotel and it was just like home. Better than home for my wife who didn't have to cook! Even the restaurant has a fantastic - among others - local cuisine.

author: K6034MNianc
title: Good staff, mediocre hotel
text: Lovely communal areas, fairly good location for the old town, and very attentive staff. However, the small bedroom I was allocated, although spotlessly clean, really wasn't great. The biggest problem I found was the antiquated "air conditioning". Rather than cooling the room down it just seemed to move the hot, humid air around and had fan settings but no temperature settings. Given the heat of the Istanbul summer, not having decent air conditioning in the bedrooms of a modern hotel is a major failing. I also struggled with the temperamental room safe and the TV had poor reception with, strangely, no international news channel. The free wi-fi for guests is a nice touch, though painfully slow, and the restaurant is pleasant but serves very average food. There is nothing terrible about the Kalyon and the service is spot on, but I won't be rushing back - and certainly never again in the summer.

author: TrishW78
title: A delightful experience
text: What an absolute pleasure it was to stay in such a friendly, pleasant, helpful hotel. The staff, without exception, especially the ladies on reception, were always polite, warm, and ready to share a laugh and a joke, and went out of their way to assist us. The hotel was clean, airy, and comfortable, (although the bed was quite hard). The rooms large and well appointed, although the bathroom was a little small. The hotel is located in an excellent position with a short walk to many of the most important sights and very good restuarants. Our room at the front had wonderful water views, and the amazing piece of ancient wall helped dull the traffic noise, which was not a problem anyway. We slept very well. The terrace restaurant was excellent and a very pleasant place to eat and sit after a long day sightseeing, with a cooling breeze and wonderful view of the ships and water traffic, and occasional dolphins frolicking. We fully intend to return to Istanbul and the Kalyon Hotel.

author: Rosie2410
title: A Superb hotel!!
text: I have stayed here many times over the years. The rooms are very spacious, the staff are wonderful and the breakfasts are *amazing*. Yes, it is on a main road, but I think the sea views more than make up for it. It is a short walk by the Hippodrome to Sultenamet to the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sofia. Due to personal reasons, after many years of travel to Turkey, I have not been back to you since 2005 (couldn't put the date back that far...); my partner with whom I used to travel there with died a few years ago and I haven't been able to bring myself to go back. When I do, I will come back to the Kalyon and see you all again. Your hotel holds so many happy memories for me. Thank you, and I hope to see you soon.

author: ALeJune
title: Nice seaside hotel close to Sultanahmet
text: Just returned from a long weekend trip in Istanbul where we stayed at the Kalyon Hotel. The hotel is a 5 minute walk to Sultanahmet directly behind the Blue Mosque. Upon arrival at this hotel, they were unable to locate our room reservation and for the night the hotel was full. The staff were extremely apologetic and moved us to a room at a hotel directly behind the Kalyon. However due to the inconvience they upgraded our room to a suite for the duration of our stay. Although the situation was stressful the hotel staff went out of their way to ensure that we were taken care of and made sure the remainder of our stay was good. The hotel itself is very up to date and clean! It is 30 minutes away from the airport and a taxi fare to and/from the airport is only 35 Turkish Lira. I liked that the hotel was not necessarily in the heart of the tourist center, but close enough to walk to the sights! Overall a good stay and a fairly reasonable price!

author: kebe1212
title: Good location, service/rooms need improvement and training!
text: My Fiance and I stayed here for about 6 days and thought the hotel was conviniently located near Sultanamet square which houses tones of restaurants (with tourist price tags ofcourse) and the Blue mosque and the beautiful Hagia Sophia, cistern basilica, Topkapi museum etc.. We walked everywhere! Unfortunately, the room was TINY! Istanbul was the first stop of our 3 week vacation and had luggages to match, but the room barely fit our luggages! We had to improvise and that was a pain that took away the joy of coming to our hotel after a day of walking around. The food at the restaurant was average especially for the price they charge and coffee is super expensive (for instant nescafe!!). There were 2 ladies at the front desk who went above and beyond to help us with all our tourist needs, they really saved the reputation of the hotel staff, because almost everyone else had a horrible attitude. This is a tourist city and as such the hotel staff should be trained on warm reception customs that cater to their international guests! Smile, say "good evening" "good morning" thank you" ...these kind gestures will help your guests enjoy their stay in your hotel and city even more,and the lack therof could have the opposite effect!

author: kgrude
title: A tidy and quiet, good located hotel, with very obliging staff, who made you feel at home!
text: A friendly hotel where we had no problems to find our way around.It was clean and tidy both in the common areas and in our room. It was quiet in the hotel (perhaps not that many guests during newyear?) and we would have appreciated music in the bar in the afternoons. Though it was quiet, the room did not seem very sound isolated. The room was very tidy and clean, not big, but then we had the standard room. The bathroom was very nice, the hairdryer is not very efficient, though. The breakfast was absolutely very good, with lots to choose between and nice view to the sea, a cosy atmoshpere there too, with very helpful waiters. Also the staff in the reception was very helpful and kind. We missed a boiler/kettle to make our own tea or coffee:)

author: slakhany1
title: Great Hotel in SultanAhmet Area
text: Great Hotel! Since we have children, we usually book hotels we know like the Sheraton, etc. I read some great reviews on the Kalyon and decided to give it a shot. We saved a lot of money and weren't disappointed. The service is excellent and location is perfect for visiting sites in the SultanAhmet area. This hotel is sea-front and a ten minute walk from most attractions. My only complaint is, they don't have a gym. Other than that, the staff is very accommodating and tries to satisfy every need. hope this helps.

author: olyra2008
title: very good quality hotel very good service great Bosphorus views
text: Modern hotel with very good service staff, isolated from the hustle of busy Sultanahmet but still right in it this hotel offers spacey, large, comfortable room. If you get a sea view room it will only raise the pleasure of your stay. The building is nothing special from the outside compare to the beautifully decorated wooded hotels a few streets up the hill but rooms are well insulated, have air condition, space and are very comfortable. Service is very friendly and helpful. Breakfast is served in a covered terrace facing the Bosphorus (some tables even outdoor for the smokers). Quality is excellent. The hotel's entrance is from highway along the coast (which causes some noise if you have a sea view room) at night but there is a back door which lets you reach the Blue Mosque and Haghia Sophia within 10 minutes. Very safe neighborhood!

author: MikeSilva18
title: Expensive
text: We travel around the World and stay in many hotels. Prior to booking via the Internet the room was 900euro for two nights. The room was discounted to 300 for the period. I would have never paid the 900e. Only a shower which was small. The room average, the bathroom yes slippers provided but no Robes, no shower gel although shampoo provided. Coffe in the room I would expect of a 4star hotel. Nice view of the sea but not worh the 900e as listed. Clean and tidy presentation Mr and Mrs Homewood

author: myescapes
title: a safe choice
text: It's difficult to find hotels in any city, and particularly so in Istanbul. We opted for this for a large group and it was perfect. All rooms more or less the same, loads with a sea view (the 'city view' rooms mostly look onto a tiny lane at back so don't expect to see mosques against the skyline). We knew from research it was on a busy dual carriageway so were prepared for some traffic noise. The upsides are: double glazing, quiet at night and the sea is the other side of the road, so lots of sky, views of boats and breathing space here, in contrast to closely packed hotels up the hill right in the old city. Superb staff, huge breakfasts, reasonable price. Would go back, especially as we passed, on our travels, many of the other hotels on which we had done extensive research; most were in noisy chaotic streets and would have had v. variable rooms which is what we wanted to avoid. This is an established Turkish run hotel and we all would recommend it. 10 mins really nice walk through interesting streets up to the mosques.

author: mumbergen
title: Nice hotel, helpful management and staff
text: We have just returned from a trip to Istanbul.We stayed at Kaylon hotel and enjoyed our stay there very much. Before going, I checked TripAdvisor to find out what to expect and to my disappointment I read that the beds were very hard. But when I found out that it was possible to get a thin and soft madrass to put on top of the hard one, I was really looking forward to our stay. We found Kaylon hotel to our liking; the location was fine, in walking distance of almost everything, the breakfast buffet was varied, the staff helpful and polite. Imagening waking up to the sight of the Blue Mosque just outside the window and eating breakfast outside, watching the boats cruising the Marmara sea. My advice to future guests would be to contact the hotel prior to your arrival if you as we do, like softer beds. The management helped us with all our requests. If we were to go to Istanbul again, we would not hesitate to stay at Kaylon hotel again.

author: SamboUAE
title: Exceeded expectations
text: Kalyon hotel has an amazing view of the Sea of Marmara, and is perfectly located on the JFK highway that runs to the main international airport. It's at the foot of the hill where the Blue Mosque and Haja Sophia are located, so the walk up is a quick 8 mins stroll through the old town of Istanbul. The staff was very friendly and addressed every concern raised (room type, internet service, pillow/bed service). The room was clean and functional, with amazing views of the sea. The one downside was the bed - it's a bit short and the linens used were not the most comfy. Also, be sure to ask for a mattress sponge to be added to your bed - otherwise, it's a tough sleep. The breakfast is hearty and diverse. I didn't try the restaurant for lunch or dinner, but the menu is limited to western-type dishes. Near the hotel are pleny of options, so this isn't an issue. I will definitely stay at Kalyon again when I visit for business.

author: CostinP
title: Great location
text: We stayed at hotel Kalyon during the U2 concert in Istanbul. The standard room that we chose was very clean but also very small and the bed was too short (we slept with our feet hanging out - we are average hight). The bathroom ventilation was inadequate there was a moisty smell in the room every evening. The breakfast was good and there is a nice view of the sea from the restaurant terrace. We got a little upset with the staff because they wouldn't allow our friend, who was not staying in the hotel, to come up an visit us in the room - Hotel security policy they say. Kalyon has uses an expensive shuttle service that will charge you 50 euro to and from the airport for 2 people. The taxi costs about 17 euro..... This hotel's best asset is its location - 5 min walk to Sultanahmet through very picturesque alleys with beautifully renovated old buildings.

author: bucklander
title: Excellent base for sightseeing with great sea views to escape to calm.
text: Our second visit to the Kalyon in one year. Parents had lovely sea view room, only drawback is some roadnoise, but to have the view is worth it. Teenagers happy with room tucked away on ground floor, no view but same facilities as parents deluxe room. Charming staff, helped book hamman, restaurants and gave some tourist advice. Breakfast seemed less fantastic than visit 10 months ago. For 22 Turkish Lira a bit pricey, but lovely dining room and great service means the day gets off to good start. Clean, comfy enough, and central with the view. Bar in evening, low ambience. For some people this may not be in the heart of Sultanahmet, but 10 minutes walk uphill makes it a great escape from the hub.

author: gravitycollapse
title: solid business hotel
text: Stayed there for four nights. Chose the hotel because I needed a place I could do some work while traveling, and for that purpose, it served me very well. Wifi was included in the price, and was hotel-wide, not only in public areas...so many hotels advertise wifi in the rooms, but it doesn't work, or barely works. Hotel was simple and clean. Not luxurious, but for a traveler on a mid-range budget it will do nicely. Staff was courteous, and though I didn't demand much from them, they courteously and thoughtfully responded to my questions . Location was good but slightly frustrating; very close to Sultanahmet, but down on the sea, meaning you have to walk out and around, and then up the hill to some of the tourist sights. I had a room with a sea view, but actually wish I had paid less for a room overlooking the back alley, because the road between the hotel and the sea is rather busy. It is not particularly convenient to trams; it's a good hotel for someone who likes to get around by taxi, but when I return to Istanbul, I'll probably choose a place closer to a tram stop so I can more easily navigate the city on foot.

author: Juliet610
title: Lovely sea view. Great location. Very friendly staff
text: Have just returned from 6 day trip for my partner's birthday surprise. The executive, sea-view room was just as pictured on the website and lovely to sit and watch the ships passing. The hotel is not the prettiest on first sight but was very clean and nicely laid out inside. The staff were very friendly and helpful which is the most important thing. They gave us a selection of leaflets for local restaurants and trips and were happy to book trips for us. They even gave a leaflet for suggested taxi fares to the major sites and seemed concerned that people were getting ripped off by taxi drivers. The room was cleaned well each day although we didn't always get a refill of creamer or tea bags - strangely packets of salt appeared! The hotel is perfectly located for the old town although the 10 minute or so walk is uphill so maybe not suitable for everybody. The restaurant is also very good as was the room service. Also free Internet access was useful for airline check-in.

author: wonderwanderer
title: good food and convenient location
text: Although I did not pick the hotel and would probably have prefered something older and with a bot more character in a city like Istanbul, we really enjoyed our stay here. Agree that the rooms are on the small side, but the location is so convenient for the main sites (Blue Mosque, Agia Sofia etc) we hardly spent any time in the room. And it was very clean. Only complaint would be the poor lighting - could barely read the guide book at night! The service was much better than expected from reading the earlier reviews - no problems. The restaurant does excellent evening meals. I wouldn't normally eat in hotel restaurants, but am glad we tried this one. We enjoyed having the sea views, although it is a shame that the very busy main road is between the hotel and the shore (and it is a very rocky shore line, not somewhere you could paddle or anything). Altogether a very pleasant stay. Istanbul is fascinating.

author: ljg74
title: Decent hotel, good location
text: I just returned from a six night stay at the Kalyon. I was there with a large group for a wedding. Overall, this is a very decent, clean hotel. The location is excellent, just a short walk to the major sites of Istanbul, and a gorgeous view of the Marmara Sea (I really enjoyed sitting out on their patio overlooking the sea.) My room was one of the older ones - they've redone about half the hotel, and only a few in my group received the newer rooms. My room was in the corner, facing the rear street. It was spotless, though, so I can't really complain. A great shower and FREE wifi were definite pluses. The staff were, for the most part, friendly & helpful. The free breakfast was plentiful & quite good. Not all cab drivers knew exactly where to find the hotel, so if you stay here, make sure you carry a card with the map & address!

author: Matt_Giess
title: Reasonable, but be aware of their expenseive assistance
text: In general this is a clean, modern hotel reasonably well located. The bed was very comfortable, although two larger people may find it on the small side. I do however advise to be very careful when asking the hotel to arrange any trips, taxis, or to give recommendations for restaurants as it will always cost you significantly more. This is something you need to get used to in Istanbul in general as pretty much everything is a negotiation and you fully expect it in the markets, carpet stores, etc. but I expected more from a 4 star hotel. To give you an idea, if you accept the prices they give you at face value without negotiating you will pay about double what you should. I would expect them to gain something from the deal, but this was beyond reason for me and left a bad taste in my mouth. Also be careful to make sure when you book through the internet that you get the room you ordered. We ordered a standard room, but were allocated their smaller rooms and from what we saw there was a significant difference between the two. This may have been down to poor communication between the travel site and the hotel, we are not sure, but just something to be aware of.

author: Jonandgaby
title: Clean, Modern, Businesslike
text: The Kalyon is located nicely on the rather busy coastal road, a steep 7-minute walk away from the Blue Mosque and Aya Sofia. Most rooms have a view of either the mosque or the Sea of Marmara. Ours had 2 simple twin beds, was clean but sparsely furnished - no chest of drawers - with somewhat dated bathrooms. Quite attractive are the modern common areas: a large lounge, good size bar (beware the prices, though, a glass of red table wine cost $15! ) terrace and restaurant with sea view. Restaurant and most of the reception staff were friendly but not everyone spoke good English. Our main gripe was that the hotel has no rear exit. If you leave by the front door you find yourself on the mostly sidewalkless coastal road among cars going at 60 mph, not exactly a comforting situation at dark.

author: 975amye
title: Not a bad place
text: Have stayed here before. Helpful staff. Great rate for our team. Pools kinda small but was fine. Breakfast not the greatest. Our tub wasn’t clean in check in- looks like it drained slow and left behind gunk-but they cleaned it right away. Roll a way we used barely wedged into our room. Fridge was nice size and cold! Staff was very friendly and accommodating. I’ve certainly paid a lot more for the same or even much worse accommodations than what we had!

author: /undefined
title: A very unsanitary place to stay
text: The 1st. room I was given had crumbs from the previous guest on the desk. Not to mention some of their clothing laying under the desk. I was placed in the room next door. The manager had to change the bedding because their was dirty hand prints on the pillow cases as well as other dirt on the sheets. (Including the blanket) Apparently the bed was just remade for the next guest. Soap wrappers were on the bathroom floor with dirty footprints on the tile. I cleaned the bathroom myself.

author: nuttidad
title: Nice and relaxing
text: Is very close to main roads. Fantastic parking for lots and all size vehicles. Close to many places to eat and shop. Truck stop is really close. You definitely do not hear any road noise even with the windows open. Pool and hot tub are great. Would highly recommend for short or long term stay. Fantastic rooms.

author: HHJJSS
title: adequate
text: Stayed 1 night.. check in went smoothly. Room is ok, nothing outstanding. Everything worked well in the room. Adequate. Did not use pool so can't comment on that. Denny's restaurant is a short walk away. Motel breakfast is ok, had some toast and peanut butter with coffee or tea.

author: MikeB060
title: another good stay
text: We have stayed at this motel several times and have always been satisfied. The staff is friendly and the place is kept very clean. Our king bed was comfortable and the room was quiet. (top floor) We got 2 good nights sleep. We didn't use the pool but it looked to be well maintained. The breakfast is a little sparse. Bagels, cold cereals, fruit and some microwave foods. In this day in age, a waffle maker would be nice. This is a good place to stay at a reasonable price.

author: /undefined
title: Good but...
text: Our stay was okay. The guy in the front desk was very accommodating. He did his job very well by informing us about the hotel amenities, breakfast etc... However, when we get to our room, it feels like it was a smoking room, though I checked if it is a non-smoking one. Indeed, it is, but it seems that the whole room stinks like a cigarette. But overall. it was a good one night stay. We enjoyed the swimming pool and the hot tub.

author: /undefined
title: Overpriced Cigarette Motel
text: 3 nights at a hotel costing over $300 that wouldn't have been worth half that: CHECK. Not only was this hotel way overpriced, but the ENTIRE place stunk to high heaven like cigarettes. When reserving the room they asked, "Smoking or Non-Smoking?" which should have set off alarm bells to the tune of "they still allow smoking in Super 8's, anywhere???" So let's give it a chance, maybe they have a wing of the hotel seperate from others that allows smoking (as to limit the stink), WRONG. The bathrooms that clearly share some type of exhaust/venting system smelled like a permanent lit cigarette. Our thought was, well the prices online looked like $80 vs. the next cheapest option in Rogers @ $120/night. So we'd try it. WRONG. When checking in we see the first night is $86 followed by $100 for the second and third nights. Massively overpriced + heavy cigarette scented rooms = worth $50 more per night ANYWHERE else.

author: /undefined
title: Rogers, MN Super 8
text: We hadn't stayed at this Super 8 in several years. It was nice to see the remodeling, breakfast added, and a very nice pool and hot tub. Our room was clean, however, it didn't get serviced the next a.m. We stayed two nights. We asked for service when we noticed, however, the clerk could not give us assurance it would be completely serviced. It was serviced by the time we returned. This motel offers smoking rooms. Our non-smoking room was constantly smelling of cigarette smoke through the bathroom fan (only one switch for light and fan) and through the A/C. The lobby and halls reeked of smoking, as well. I left with a sore throat.

author: nicholasa62
title: Smoky, rooms just ok.
text: The manager at check-in was friendly and explained how the shower works, as they have a pull down lever in the bathrooms. The common areas were extremely hot and smoke smells were everywhere, and this was extremely annoying to me. One one area of the motel is for smoking and I know people in non-smoking rooms were smoking also. I did bring this to the attention of the front desk, but the manager on duty just told me since they were moving around a lot, there was nothing really to be done about the smokers. The breakfast at this Super8 did offer waffels, which was a first for the many Super 8s I have visited. Non-working A/Cs in the hallways made the areas outside my room hot and uncomfortable. They do have a pool, if you are into that, probably why their per night prices are more than most Super 8s I have been too. Overall, okay, but the A/Cs need to work and the room I was in needs work.

author: /undefined
title: Family stay for Easter
text: This is a nice Super 8. Our family stays here each time we visit my mother. They have a nice, clean pool and a decent breakfast. The Internet is good. They also offer smoking and non-smoking rooms. This time during our stay, I noticed the hot tub was in need of a scrubbing on the bottom and seats. We also had a bedspread that had a cigarette burn hole in it and a towel with the same. If there was a way to keep the linens separate for the smoking and non-smoking rooms, I'd give the hotel a top rating.

author: skylersgrandma
title: LOVE LOVE LOVE IT!
text: This is our 4th year staying here.,.. it cannot be beat ! We love the price,. the kids love the pool, the rooms are nice, and so is the breakfast, we always have dinner at Dennys using the coupons provided... this place cannot be beat !!... the staff is always Very very helpful and accommodating... they remember us from year to year.. WE LOVE this it here and wish we had to make more overnight trips so we could stay here more often... can't wait until next year !

author: 950keannap
title: Roof over your head
text: This hotel keeps you out of the rain, but if the stains on the ceiling are any indication, it barely does that. The beds were so hard we alternated between them and the floor. The person at check in and check were extremely rude, but the gal on Saturday was amazing. The blankets had burn holes in them, and the tv was so small we had to sit on the edge of the bed to watch it. Small room, small bathroom. Breakfast sucked. Some packaged cinnamon roles, lukewarm coffee and water, and thawed out eggo waffles on a plate was the meal-but they rotate out bagels! Basically, it's a place to keep you out of the rain and not much more. I will say the pool was amazing though. That and the sweet gal on Saturday are the only reasons this place got 2 stars.

author: /undefined
title: Ok
text: This hotel is overpriced for what is offered. The continental breakfast was very lacking in quality and substance. The water pressure in the showers and bathroom sink were very weak. It took forever to get a good shower. House keeping in the rooms was ok but I dropped something by the bed and I could see dirt and stuff on the floor between the head of the bed and the wall. I had a nonsmoking room but there was a cigarette burn on the comforter on the bed. The TV was the old fashioned tube TV, come on.... Lots of the times I could not read the words on the screen because it was not wide enough screen. $80 is a lot for a bare minimum room.

author: cherylr369
title: Acceptable for the price
text: For the price, it is exactly what you'd ask for & expect. Decent beds, decent amount of space, clean and nice looking. The continental breakfast wasn't fancy, but I've seen much worse. It was edible and sufficient. The only real 'complaint' we had is that the 1st floor lobby and hallway smell of cigarette smoke. Very odd. It was quite pervasive and annoying for a non-smoker. Other than that, I would definitely consider staying there again if the need arose.

author: MikeB060
title: a very nice super 8
text: We had a very nice overnight at this motel. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The check-in went smoothly and our room was what we expected. It was clean and the king bed was very comfortable. ( we like firm beds) There is a Dennys restaurant within walking distance and the 15% discount card, provided by the motel was a plus. There is a multi-plex movie theater nearby to help pass the evening. The breakfast buffet is a bit limited, could use a waffle maker. All in all, this property provides good value for the price.

author: 56nicke
title: Overnight stop in Rogers Minnesota
text: I would not recommend the Super 8 in Rogers. It was loud, understaffed, and took oner 30 minutes to check in. I was unimpressed with the fact that other guests attempted to enter our room after 10:30, believing that it was their room. This was followed up with a call from the front desk about half an hour later asking what our name was. Apparently there was some confusion by the front desk in determining which rooms were assigned to who. The room was to be a non-smoking room, but it reeked of tobacco smoke. Coffee was quite good in the morning, but the quality of the complementary breakfast left a lot to be desired. It is unlikely that I will stay there again.

author: /undefined
title: Nice looking motel driving up. Smelled like smoke in lobby...
text: Nice looking motel driving up. Smelled like smoke in lobby but didn't mind as we asked for nonsmoking room. Got into room and smelled like smoke. Opened window and people were smoking outdoors. Noisy all night long with doors banging. People parking in spots that were marked off. Will never go back. Rather sleep in the car, than here. Got home and clothes in suitcase smelled like smoke!

author: /undefined
title: Stayed because we had to.
text: I had made reservations a week a half prior to us arriving. I knew we would be driving will into the night and that we would be arriving late. I booked a king non smoking room, when we arrived the man behind the desk took over 5 minutes to come greet us (he was on Skype in the other room) and then when he went into his computer he said your queen room is ready, when I informed him that my reservation was for a king he said in a very rude tone " well we don't have any kings left". I showed him my reservation print out and he just acted like it was my fault and told me that I could take the queen or go elsewhere. It was 1230am and we really didn't feel like hotel hunting other wise we definitely would have gone elsewhere. Now, a king or queen bed really doesn't make a difference to me, however the rudeness of this man about the whole thing just turned me right off. To top all of that off, the heater/air con was soooo incredibly noisy that we opted to just open the window and have the loud semis over this machine. The sheets were also stained with something I'm glad I don't know what, and the shower head was so dirty I was afraid to open my eyes in the shower.

author: /undefined
title: Friends shopping weekend
text: This hotel was great! The staff was extremely friendly when checking in and out. We got a great shoppers package for the local Outlet Mall and nearby restaurants. The pool area and hot tub area are awesome! The rooms are quiet and ours was very spacious, but we were at the end of a hallway so our room was a little bigger than most. The only slight drawback was the faint smoke smell in the hallways, but there was no smell in our non-smoking room. Great location, only about 5 miles from the Outlet Mall with easy access to the hotel and good restaurants nearby. The tv's could use some updating.

author: Purple8084
title: Stayed August 31, 2012
text: The guy at the desk was very nice & helpful. The room was dirty...hair on the bathroom floor & in the shower. Room smelled musty. They had a OK breakfast, but the problem was there was not an attendent sitting in the breakfast area. The person restocking the breakfast items was also cleaning rooms. The problem with no attendent was theft...their was a group of Asian Ladies that would wipe out all of the breakfast items...by this I mean they took 5-6 oranges at a time, 5-6 cinnamon rolls, stacks of bread, the condiments back to their rooms & they also filled several empty water bottles with orange & apple juice. I've never seen anything like...they didn't even care people were watching them. I was doing laundry so I sat their for over an hour & these Asian Ladies made at least 5 to 6 trips taking most of the breakfast items.....WOW is all I can say!

author: AuntyMo
title: Air conditioner lousy, breakfast area pathetic
text: We stayed at this hotel two nights. The outside weather was in the 90's and the airconditioner didn't seem capable of overcoming it, as well as being noisy. The room was very warm and humid - the linens felt damp. The breakfast bar was a joke. They have this tiny little counter in an area where there are also several snack and drink machines and a washer and dryer. Two people couldn't get breakfast in this are without banging into each other and there wasn't much selection anyway. It was a shame because the outside of this building is reasonably appealing and the lobby is very nice for a Super 8. It's also about a 10 minute drive from the Albertville outlet mall.

author: 368stacis
title: Good hotel, beautiful grounds, very helpful manager
text: I really enjoyed my stay at this hotel. My only problem was that my room was not ready upon arrival at around 500 pm. The woman at the desk asked me to go to the restaraunt to wait. I thought this was not great service. When I mentioned it to a fellow traveler, the manager overheard me and told me that he would take care of it right away, which he did. He also gave me a couple of drink tickets and some awesome guacamole. The brunch on Sunday was truly amazing and even live music by the pool. It isn’t a cheap brunch, but really worth it. The waiters and the bar staff were great! I really enjoyed my stay and will always try stay here when in Cuernavaca

author: pattayainsider
title: Perfect, great value too
text: I was here just one night, but it was a great choice... just a few minutes inexpensive taxi into the center of town... room was super clean and comfortable, everything worked fine. I only used the restaurant for breakfast, but it was nice and great food, especially the fresh fruit. I wish they had fresh squeezed orange juice available... Staff were all very friendly, especially Concepcion (spelling?), who very nicely called all the bus companies to get me local bus schedules to/from Mexico City and Taxco. This hotel is actually an amazing value... nice pool area too. There is a 24 hour convenience store on the corner. Enjoy lovely Cuernavaca here.

author: Plog60
title: Nice hotel in great location
text: The hotel is centrally located and relatively easy to find. I think it's surprisingly nice for a "regular" Holiday Inn. We were upgraded to a suite, which was extra nice, but I believe the regular rooms are good also. The room was a bit dated, but everything was nice and clean. The bed was very comfortable. The AC worked fine. The pool area is very nice, surrounded by a bar and the restaurant. The breakfast was terrific. The full Mexican breakfast offering :-) We will definitely be back.

author: 109cliveb
title: A Holiday Inn that might surpise you
text: A Holiday Inn might not be every one's first choice for a romantic get away or a week.end visit to Cuernavaca, but this Holiday Inn might just surprise you. Don´t expect a luxury room, but the bedding is very comfortable, and the bathroom is spacious and functional. Ask for a room with a view over the pool área (a little more expensive but worth it). Our room (444) had a good work area and a king size bed. We enjoyed a Sunday breakfast-brunch that was included in the room rate and this was spectacular. The waiters were efficient and very friendly. The pool area is not large but is is very nicely designed and children and families all seemed to be enjoying themselves. The hotel offers excellent parking and valet service, and the staff are all pleasant and helpful. The lobby area is not attractive, and recent remodelling efforts have detracted from the overall "look" of the place. But still it's an option offering good value for money.

author: Chapinero992
title: Horrible customer service
text: I stayed in this wonderful hotel and wish I could continue to consider it wonderful. However, the staff at this hotel have been absolutely terrible helping me recover from a stupid mistake. I left my driver's license in the room and thought all would turn out well after I called and they located it. It took about eight more phone calls, with some staff saying they had the license and others saying they did not, to arrange for them to have it at the front desk for a friend. Yet, when he showed up, the license was mysteriously not there. I called an hour later and my license, which was at the front desk on Friday, was still missing. Honestly, these people have been giving me the run-around for a week now. I understand that I made the mistake leaving the license, but the lack of customer service has been absolutely appalling.

author: grappa135
title: Some difficulties, handled exceptionally well
text: Sometimes, when hotels advertise that they are 'pet-friendly' the booking process fails to take this into account. The reservation we made for this, very pretty hotel had us booking our small dog through the 'comments' section. when we arrived we were informed that the 2 dog rooms were occupied ( not by dogs) and we were put in a double-bedded disabled persons room, instead of the King room we had booked. After informing the reception desk that our dog was very clean and well behaved - probably more so than many travellers' - the extremely competent manager gave us a good room for our additional 2 nights. This hotels held breakfast functions in its grounds daily. These were superbly organized and catered, by very skilled staff - especially Luis ! Overall, the Manager, her reception staff, and all of the catering staff perform to a high standard of efficiency, but the IHG booking page needs to give a confirmation on pets if they continue their pet-friendly policy. This hotel is ideally suited to travelers with well mannered dogs.

author: SeenByMyEyes
title: GREAT HOTEL. GREAT SERVICE
text: Thanks for a great stay. The hotel is very modern and quite quite nice. Beutiful garden. All the necessary amenities. Magnificent service. Just don't ask for the handicapped room of you may be uncomfortable. Cons: Too much noise in the morning coming from the servie staff. But everything else is nice nice nice. Will always go back. Thanks again.

author: blondepenguin
title: Paradise found!
text: We had to stay at a different hotel for 4 nights for a conference prior to arriving here at Holiday Inn. We hadn't slept well because of hard beds and heat. We were sooooo happy when we found Holiday Inn to stay at for the rest of our visit once the conference was done. We have 3 small children with us, and they did not charge us extra like another hotel we checked out wanted to charge is 40% extra PER CHILD! AND here, kids eat free one per paying adult for breakfast! The kids loved exploring the gardens, seeing the kois & turtles & playing in the pools. We have a 6,2,&1 year old & the pools have several levels of depth that was great for each one. There are people working everywhere & the place is spotless. If I ever return to Cuernavaca I will definately stay here again!! Good job Holiday Inn!

author: 759PaulL
title: Nice clean hotel.
text: Surprisingly good place to stay in Cuernacava for a reasonable price.. This hotel is located in a nice part of Cuernavaca and is close to access roads. The building and pool area is well maintained.. I particularly liked the shutters they have in front of the windows that can block out 100% light.. I have seen these kind off shutters in Europe but never before in Latin america. I would have appreciated some facilities like coffee-maker and small fridge... Even though the online room description said the room is equipped with a fridge I arrived to find that is not true, I asked for a fridge and they brought me the smallest fridge I've ever seen.. Right next to the hotel is a OXXO convenient store which was really nice.

author: BillE124
title: Pricey but nice
text: Good location, nice room with good lighting - you need to place a card in a reader for the lights and ac to stay on - be sure to get an extra card when you check in. Desk staff (one spoke fluent English) were helpful and pleasant. All staff were always attentive and hard at work. The breakfast buffet was good with a large selection but very expensive - $500 pesos for two with the tip. Grounds were impeccable and attractive, secure parking. The lights in the hallways are on a very short timer, they go on when they sense movement and go off very quickly. Electricity must be extremely expensive here. The pool didn't have enough chairs - they were all taken despite fairly cool weather.

author: Daddytobe
title: Great business stay
text: Very nice hotel with well taken care of grounds. As others have said, it's kind of tucked away in a basic village, but overall it's not bad. Friendly any helpful even if you don't speak Spanish. Breakfast buffet is good with a little variety, but it is a bit pricey, about 150 pesos per person. There is bottled water provided in your room and the size of the room was perfect. The hotel even had a Mexican soap opera filming in their dining area, apparently they film many scenes there, but it never felt intrusive. Many great restaurants are a simple cab ride away, but it helps if you know basic Spanish. I'm sure I'll be back very soon!

author: Gabriel_Gecko
title: Beautiful facilities, very kind staff.
text: You won’t believe there’s this nice hotel inside, since you are in a regular neighborhood whit nothing that makes it special, but once you are inside, the ride begins. They have this forest like landscapes with waterfalls, fish and turtles. And 2 pools in the middle of all of this nature. It’s nice to have a walk at night after you have had dinner and hear the sound of the water and the crickets; you just forget you’re in the middle of the city. You are close to the downtown where you can visit several museums, and you can also buy a bus tour to either inside they city or outside and visit some small pyramids and know more about the foundations of Cuernavaca. You can also find nice local restaurants in the main square or stay in the hotel for a more expensive food rate though, it’s your choice. A plus in this hotel is that they will take you together with your pets for an additional cost so you are not worried if your pet is safe at home or with the vet. Definitively, you can trust you will enjoy your stay in this hotel.

author: pianograd99
title: Expensive in US comparisons
text: We stayed here for two nights on a weekend. The hotel takes advantage of the exchange rate and you end up paying more for the room than was listed on the website in US money. I would definitely recommend buying a room through Expedia or Priceline and paying in advance. At least that way you don't end up paying more because of the exchange rate. The beds were sooo soft and comfortable, and the A/C worked amazingly well. The pool is incredibly small. There is a second pool, but it is located a good ways away from the hotel rooms. The grounds were very well-kept and everything was very clean. We had great food and service at the restaurant. Overall, a good experience, but a lot more expensive for the room than what you would pay for something similar in the US.

author: chrisman48
title: best place in Cuernavaca for the money
text: The gardens are gorgeous, the pool fabulous, the rooms quite nice. (But beware of housekeeping staff -- they enter without knocking! which means you should lock your belongings away when you are not in your room). We stayed here 4 nights and easily would stay here again on our next visit. For some reason, the hotel doesn't advertise that it is very centrally located, and a short distance from the historic zone. This place is MUCH better than any place you could find immediately in the historic area. Try it, you'll like it (I think). Be sure to get the breakfast buffet as part of your package.

author: julietten683
title: Fantastic hotel in the heart of the Gredos mountains
text: We love the Gredos Parador and have stayed here numerous times because we so enjoy the experience. The hotel itself is in the style of a stone mountain lodge, the bedrooms having wooden floors and warm, comfortable surroundings, and the ample public spaces such as sitting and games rooms being equally comfortable, with open fires from autumn to spring. The staff are incredibly helpful, friendly and efficient and we often see the same faces in the bar and at reception in particular, who always do a great job. The food has, without exception, been excellent and the trout, cheese and beef (cooked rare), all local, are particularly good. The bar serves a delicious local beer too; the microbrewery is nearby and can also be visited. We also enjoy sitting either on the open terraces or indoor terraces to enjoy the spectacular views of the mountains that flank it. Many of the rooms have these great views, but even the other side overlook the pine forests that surround the Parador. The main attraction is the stunning location, in the heart of the Gredos mountains: there are nearby drives and visits to caves and local villages, but most recommended are the walls, suited to all abilities, right from the Parador door. The staff at reception are very helpful and will give you printed maps and suggested itineraries from a gentle walk round the pine forest, a longer walk along the river past cascades, or one of the signature Gredos walks from the Plataforma to the Laguna Grande (which, whilst needing some hiking stamina needs no technical equipment other than perhaps crampons to complete in the snow). In all, this is just a warm, welcoming hotel, in a beautiful rural location, and if this is your kind of thing, really shouldn't be missed.

author: solotravellerCanada
title: Wi-Fi doesn't work, reception staff poorly trained
text: This is a beautiful property, but it is poorly managed. The Wi-Fi system only works intermittently. The staff know all about this and admit that it has not worked well for a long time. It is impossible to rely on having internet connectivity in this hotel. The Paradores website advertised a price of €70 a night, but the young man at the front desk (Marco) could not figure out a way to get his computer to give me this price. He suggested I book it online... which I could not do because of the intermittent Wi-Fi. The housekeeping staff are very noisy in the hallways, like a flock of crows in the morning, chatting with each other up and down the halls. This place needs new management.

author: RichardCSimpson
title: Dog friendly, fantastic break.
text: We went to the Parador in Gredos with a group of people. The hotel offered a very good deal for two night, dinner, bed and breakfast, for around €250; they added a supplement for our dog (which is not unusual). We arrived at the hotel and there was a welcome pack for the dog, which included 1kg of good quality food, a small bed liner and food bowl. For me as a pet owner (we are worse than parents of children), this was an astonishing gesture. I have been to hotels before with my dog, and paid the supplements, but I have never had a welcome pack or made to feel that my dog was part of the family - the Parador changed that. In general the hotel was good, the food was very good, with a wide variety of options for all tastes. Dinner was a menu with a good selection and breakfast was a buffet. Overall a good experience and I shall look for other Parador hotels that welcome pets.

author: stephenwF8014GN
title: Superb Location
text: It was the first Parador in Spain and sits on a hillside overlooking the valley and pine forest. Its quite large and busy. Our room was quite small although clean and comfortable. We were there however on a Saturday night having failed to get into Salamanca, Segovia or Avila and I am sure the rooms overlooking the valley are a little more spacious. It was nevertheless quiet .There is not a lot of choice in terms of eating locally unless you are prepared to drive. Food in the restaurant was ok without being particularly memorable. Breakfast as usual in the Parador's was very good. Its great strength however is its location. There are some superb drives in the local countryside on roads which have little traffic. I would not rush back again unless using it as a stopover on the way somewhere.

author: darrenb885
title: Lovely hideaway
text: I had the pleasure of doing some cooking at the parador. A beautiful hideaway. Even though it snowed!! Rooms clean and tidy. All the staff were so helpful. Eva the manager could not do enough for you. If you want no mobile reception and peaceful days. Try this place. Can't wait to go back and just do nothing😎

author: ibanejm
title: Ideal staying for a break
text: Parador de Gredos is a very good option for a break and get relaxed by the scene. Located in a priviliged area surrounded by Sierra de Gredos, this Parador keeps the essentials for having a relaxing staying. If you are into hiking, trail running, mountain bike or just walking is a perfect choice. Having trail routes departing from the Parador from all levels of difficulty. After a long hiking session you can restore your energy in some of the good restaurants around the area or in the Parador itself, and delight yourself with famous "cochinillo asado" or roasted lamb. Milano Real restaurant is close by and could be a perfect option. Austerity is dominant, so don´t expect luxury but Parador preserves the essentials to make your stay very enjoyable. Rooms are very clean and having comfortable beds, you have several terraces with breath taking views, buffet breakfast is very good (fresh orange juice, fruits, eggs,...)

author: ciaracat1
title: Mid level parador set in beautiful wooded scenery
text: I was amused by some of the earlier rather negative reviews. Some of the criticisms, i suspect is that the design is more for cold than for scenic views. On arrival was put in a cigarette drenched room and, on request, was switched to a back room facing garbage area. Turned out that the following day most rooms were booked for a very large wedding party - well at least we hD free disco music! Front desk staff seemed overwhelmed, all internet access was off, including direct connected pc. Despite this , there is nothing much wrong with this parador, all other staff, bar restaurant worked hard and were friendly and attentive, food fine although hardly gastronomique. Location is excellent with lots of hiking. It is not one of the more charming Paradors but perfectly acceptable and the Parador circuit is wonderful and not to be missed.

author: jeminab
title: Small room but nicely furnished
text: We stayed at this Parador for the first 2 nights of a "Ruta" and were allocated a small room on the same level as the entrance. There was only one case rack and, as we have 2 cases, we had difficulty walking around the one on the floor. It is a noisy hotel as the floors and doors creak. This was the only parador where eau de toilette was provided so I suppose this rather nice additional touch is being discontinued? There are plently of lounges with comfy sofas; small seat areas on each floor and 2 lovely roof terraces to catch the sun. We enjoyed our meal in the restaurant but other people were not so happy. Very good choice at the hot and cold breakfast buffet. Free wifi, games room, tennis court and plenty of parking. Good area for walking.

author: MartinDG61
title: Wow what a location and hotel
text: Our first visit to the area and a Parador, the building is fantastic (the original Parador we found out). We only stayed 1 night but wished would could have stayed longer and will be back. Our rooms overlooked the mountains and the view is spectacular, there are sitting areas on each floor and the lounge is worth a visit. Dinner was excellent and even the teenagers enjoyed something different. There is even a games room and a tennis court to keep you occupied when not looking at the scenery. Rooms are large and comfortable, with a large bathroom. The hotel was very quiet while we were there (mid week in October is not busy), and we had good service throughout. Definitely going back in the future.

author: EuroJapanFamily
title: A great getaway in the middle of nowhere
text: We stayed 5 nights in this hotel in August 2008 while visiting a friend in the area, and everything was very good. The Parador de Gredos is a large stone building in the middle of nowhere and you can spend long hours just lying on a long chair in one of the terraces while watching the wild and peaceful Sierra de Gredos landscape. In particular, it is great to be on the terrace very early in the morning to see the sun rise in an absolute silence, except the sound of the bells coming from sheep herds in the distance. The room was quite large and very nice and quiet, though with no view at all and a bit dark due to the small size of the windows (it is no problem during the hot spanish summer as it keeps the inside temperature cool during the day, but I imagine this can be quite depressing during wintertime). The breakfast buffet, like in the whole Paradores chain, is spectacular. The only weak point we found is that the place can get very crowded and busy during the weekend, as locals from the nearby villages often come to hang aroung and have a cup of coffee at the hotel. There doesn't seem to be enough waiters to ensure an appropriate service during that peak time. We tried to have a snack in the main cafeteria on a Saturday evening, and gave up after waiting more than 20 minutes at a table full of durty dishes as no waiter showed up. Otherwise, the hotel staff is kind and efficient, the facilities are very clean and there is a nice atmosphere. This is a good place to stay with small children (you will see many spanish families coming here and the staff is very helpful with kids).

author: Alf
title: Great position and good facilities.
text: A great example of the benefits of staying in Paradors. The position is wonderful providing access to the excellent countryside of the Gredos Sierra, also offering direct access to explore the ancient pine woodlands that lie below. The rooms are very comfortable, nice and warm in cool weather and surprisingly quiet considering the number of guests. The restaurant is very good and the food is of very good quality with the usual offering of local produce common to the whole Parador group. Dinner is served at a pace that suits your needs and the food is all freshly prepared and delicious. the breakfast caters for all tastes and requirements. A real bonus is the number of quiet and secluded places to sit and relax amongst beautiful surroundings. I look forward to returning in the future.

author: Curious31794
title: Amazing place
text: Stayed here in May/04 - it was amazing. Beautiful grounds, great rooms and bathrooms although you need to decide if you want a bigger room or better view. The mountain views are generally smaller rooms while the views to the front of the hotel are of nice outdoor surroundings in much bigger rooms with much bigger bathrooms. There are PLENTY of public balconies, sitting spaces and views to contemplate the surroundings for hours, so if a big room is important - go for it and spend time reading a good book in one of the public areas on every floor (available both indoors and outdoors.) The service was impeccable, the food in the restaurant very good and the staff sweet in all respects. You need a car to do some exploring of the nearby town, but the hiking around the hotel is excellent and you can hire guides, do bike trips etc. directly from the hotel. If you would like to spend a few days "away from it all" in an amazing building with gorgeous surroundings, check this location out. I'm told all the Parador's in Spain are just as nice.

author: jamesallardice
title: A good hotel, better for business than leisure
text: Given the fact (I believe) that Brasilia sees far more stays for business than leisure it probably makes sense that the Brasilia Palace hotel feels a bit like the typical business hotel found in any major city. From the outside it is a striking building, as are many in this city, but once in the room there is little character. Breakfast, served in the Oscar restaurant, is good (the pão de queijo was one of the best we have tried in Brazil!) but quite impersonal. For a hotel of this style you could normally expect a little more in the way of table service even at a buffet breakfast, for things like coffee. Our stay was short, over a weekend and in winter so it's hard to say what the place would be like during the week in high season, but it was very quiet (not a bad thing). It was easy to get transport (you can't walk anywhere in Brasilia) either via Uber or normal taxi booked via hotel reception. The staff on reception were always helpful and spoke some English. All in all, I'd recommend this hotel mainly for the fact it's the only one designed by the architect of the city so you get that true Brasilia experience. But you might find better elsewhere.

author: CtheK
title: A Niemeyer hotel in a Niemeyer town
text: Our stay here was pleasant enough, but the real reason we came was the Niemeyer architecture. We were in town to see his works, so it made sense to stay at a hotel that was drawn by him. It didn’t disappoint. We loved the underground foyer/reception that is accessed via a ramp, furnished with period pieces and nicely lit. The rooms were functional and ok, but nothing to write home about. The place has a 50s Niemeyer feel, we we were happy. Breakfast is excellent in the place that functions as the Oscar restaurant at night. Just don’t go there at night, as that DOES disappoint.

author: cord246
title: Tranquility.
text: If you are just looking for any top end hotel you might wanna look further rather than stopping here. You can get more luxury for this money. But why should you? In the end all those hotel are kind of the same aren't they? Not this one. If you have any sense for architecture, for perfection in design, then this is a place that will stick in your memory. Take ample time to wander through the corridors, the emptyness of the public spaces and the premises to observe the outside building in it's context. This hotel radiates a deep tranquility that influences your state of mind. Try it!

author: 94priscillac
title: Beautiful MCM hotel by Oscar Niemeyer
text: This is a beautiful MCM hotel designed by Oscar Niemeyer is a dream for those looking to travel in style. The rooms have been modernized, but the hotel retains the clean lines and simple designs of the past. The restaurant had very tasty Italian food and the egg-shaped pool begs to be photographed. Most impressive of all though, was Tiago, the gentleman at the front desk who checked us in. He went above and beyond to ensure that we had a wonderful stay, and single-handedly saved the rest of my Brazil trip, by getting me the urgent medical attention I needed, quickly and efficiently. Tiago is the epitome of amazing hospitality and I will always be grateful to him for it. I would like to nominate him for a promotion! Thank you Tiago and Brasilia Palace Hotel!

author: suite-tools
title: Business and pleasure
text: The building is a great historical hotel if you like mid century modern. The total interior is classical long wood line halls. The furniture is all keeping with the style. The room is comfortable with outside balcony. My room overlook large grass area ending at a lake. The service has been great has gourmey restaurant called Oscars. If you like privacy and quiet this is the place. The negative is it isolated maybe 15 to 20 minutes from other venues and restaurants.

author: johnaP5996IM
title: Worth a night
text: We stayed here for one night on a two night architecture sightseeing trip to Brasilia. Our first night we stayed closer to the Esplanada Dos Ministerios for the convenience, but wanted to give this gem designed by Niemeyer a try even though it's a bit far from the center. A single night stay was about right. Front desk staff is fastidious but welcoming. We were given a small room for two on the top floor. Didn't seem like many people were staying there during our wintertime trip. We only bumped into a handful of other guests while having dinner at the nice restaurant and at breakfast the next day. We had the large pool to ourselves and never saw anyone else using it at other times. It's worth a wander around the property to take in the many design elements, both inside and out, particularly in the afternoon light. One night is all you'll need.

author: janicetrotte
title: Very charming and good value for money
text: The hotel is located in a very nice area, by the lake and away from the crowd. But bear in mind you will need to drive from there to wherever you go in Brasilia! The rooms are very comfortable, spacious and clean. Internet service is not remarkable. They charge you for Wi-Fi in case you need to use more than one device; this is unacceptable nowadays! Hopefully they will provide free Wi-Fi services in the near future... Buffet Breakfast is splendid and served at the well known Oscar restaurant where you can have a nice meal as well. In general, I would recommend staying there, if you're well accompanied!

author: EG-aloha
title: historical building! great breakfast! roomy property and pleasant staying!
text: The bedroom i stayed wasn't that roomy but was ok, clean and had a little lanai that wasn't really furnished to be used to it's potential. But we could open the back door to have fresh air. Great parking lot. Nice historical exhibition showing this was the first Hotel in Brasilia. Very well kept! After the nice breakfast we walked around the property. The architecture is very much from the modern period. I recommend!

author: 28Tom
title: Stay in a piece of history
text: Staying in Brasilia is all about discovering modernist architect. So it seemed appropriate to stay at one of the very first buildings of the new city. It was designed by Oscar Niemeyer, opened in 1958 and hosted the guests of President Kubichek who wanted to fly in and see the new city as it rose from the dust. In it's modern incarnation at lot of the 50/60s effects have been kept and it's not hard to imagine yourself alongside staying Eisenhower or Che Guevara. There's an outdoor pool. The restaurant is excellent and modestly priced. The only real draw back is that the hotel is a little out of town, which makes for a very peaceful stay but does require a taxi or bus every time you want to head in. The hotel staff are very friendly, efficient and attentive.

author: spanishguy
title: Great Niemeyer designed Hotel in Brasilia
text: I've stayed there for 2 nights with friends on a leisure trip. I liked the hotel very much. Great Niemeyer design everywhere, friendly and helpful staff. The hotel is not really centrally located, so you need a car or taxi to go into the centre or you're looking to eat at a restaurant outside of the hotel (Oskar is their own restaurant). The rooms are "basic" but minimalistic design - all works well. Unfortunately the shower didn't work properly in my room - but I wasn't bothered too much and too lazy to change my room so I've lived with it. It's not a boutique hotel - but for those who appreciate the "design" of Oskar Niemeyer - they will like the place. I would return there for sure if I am back in Brasilia. The Wifi was a bit slow - but worked more or less ok

author: solid_smile
title: Like one note Samba
text: I truly enjoyed staying at the Brasilia Palace Hotel. The luxury encountered here lies not in plush interiors but in a well orchestrated combination of spaces and views of the outside. Some of the common areas are refreshingly "empty" giving space to the artwork of Athos Bulcão. I also particularly admired the craftmanship of the woodworkers which went into the various wooden furniture in the simple but tastefully furnished rooms. Service was not overwhelming but absolutely ok. Breakfast is served in a lovely area and was the best I encountered during my travels in Brazil. Even though the hotel is located somewhat remote (that's actually not a term to to be used to describe a location in Brasilia...) - this guarantees the hotel to be a quiet spot to relax during siesta or in the evening. Taxis are always available on the spot and not too expensive.

author: LaLiga16
title: Loved it, but not for everyone
text: We loved this hotel. Probably not for everyone as it has the simple "modern" design. Spartan rooms and the amenities are not what you might expect (e.g. the fitness center is in a separate glass enclosed space in the middle of the turnaround driveway). However, it was really comfortable and quiet. Breakfast was great. We were there during the 2014 World Cup and discovered the teams stay there during matches. Security getting in and out was very tight, but didn't detract from our visit. It is quite a distance away from the monuments, restaurants, and sights, so you'll have to take a cab to everything. However, if you are in town only a day or two, it is well worth it to stay here if you appreciate the architecture and quiet setting.

author: chowzinha
title: Great Hotel
text: I booked the hotel so I could enjoy it with my fiancee on Valentine's Day. We absolutely loved it! The hotel staff is friendly and kind, and the hotel itself is an absolute delight! The design is amazing and decoration flawless! Oh, and the breakfast! It's wonderful!! The only downsize for me was the "cable tv", which wasn't cable at all (only a handful of channels and with very bad reception). But other than that, it was an amazing stay!

author: belinova
title: Comfortable with Style
text: The hotel, built from Oscar Niemeyer, got style of course! It's also a typical star hotel with all the trimmings: clean room, balcony, minibar, 24h room service and a really great swimmingpool with service too. Unfortunatly the restaurant was closed when we have been there. Instead it took place in the hotel lobby, what is not the best place for a restaurant. But the service was nice... Nonethless we mostly ate on the room because of the horrible atmosphere and the remote location of the hotel. The receptionists are a bit grumpy and not very helpful. All in all we had a good time there... you just have to except the anonymous atmosphere!

author: Haidhauserin
title: A true orginial in Brasilia - not impressive, but unique
