text: As 1st time tourists in Brasilia, we felt we had the choice between some very standard business hotels and big chains or a true design icon. We chose the latter. This Niemeyer hotel is certainly a must for design fans, but don't expect it's been treated as a legend. Certainly some renovation in the rooms would do no harm, especially the wooden doors and balcony/window fronts. The standard rooms are standard and the rececptionists were less welcoming than anywhere else on our trip to Brazil. The hotel breakfast was in a nice restaurant, but again here the staff seemed overwhelmed. It's highly recommended to go by rental car as Brasilia in general is hard to get around without. With the car, we felt the hotel had a good location and we were happy we didn't stay in any of the other nameless chains.

author: meduniv
title: A rather uncomfortbale landmark with bad service
text: The hotel is a landmark building in itself, as it was designed by Oscar Niemeyer. In my opinion, it is not a good design for a hotel. The rooms are located along one very long corridor which makes for very long walks from or to the elevators. The rooms are appropriately sized with modern bathrooms and balconies, although they feature a rather shabby looking carpet. The hotel only has one restaurant, Oscar, that can be reached either by walking through the conference facilities (impossible if there is an event taking place, which was so at every day of my stay) or by walking outside around the building. When the restaurant is closed, there is no chance to get a drink anywhere in the hotel, as there no other restaurants or bars, not even poolside. Although restaurant staff was inside the restaurant between 6 and 7 p. m., they told me I could not get a coke to take it to one of the poolside tables.

author: rlunardelli
title: good choice
text: very good hotel. is based in the 60's design. good service, food and rooms. the only thing negative are the showers!! very weak! but stil a excelent place to stay! i'll definitely come back!!! (on the confederation cup, the brazilian team stayed here)!

author: rrporto
title: close to government buildings
text: Hotel is located beside the Paranoá Lake (which is big by the way) so you will be in north part of it. Is kind of far away from everything (but close to government buildings) ... you will have to get a taxi even to get dinner, because there is nothing close to there. It is roughly at 2,5 km from Brasilia's landmarks = government buildings and cathedral. It is a historical building therefore they do not have a "star category" classification ... but I would rated as 4 stars. Staff is helpfull and rooms ok (simple and clean). they have a big swimming pool and a fancy (and expensive) restaurant beside it.

author: RAlanHertz
title: The Only Place to Stay in Brasilia
text: For anyone interested in 20th century architecture, Brasilia is an amazing place to visit. Built in five years and opened in 1960, it features the architecture of Oscar Niemeyer, who brought the sensibility of Le Corbusier to Brazil. We stayed at the Brasilia Palace Hotel, which was designed by Niemeyer. We were fortunate to have it recommended by our guide Maria Joo, who has lived in Brasilia for thirty-five years, has a thorough knowledge of its architecture and design, and opened doors throughout the city. She can be contacted at maria.joo57@yahoo.fr The restaurant in the hotel is named OSCAR and serves outstanding food, the best we ate in Brasilia. The rooms are spare and sixties elegant. The staff was attentive and helpful. We loved it!

author: andorbln
title: design icon
text: if you go to brasilia for the town planning and architecture, this is the perfect place to stay. the hotel was designed by oscar niemeyer and beautifully restored in 2006 after it had burned down and been abandoned for almost twenty years. although some elements of the original design have been changed and some of the newly added furniture is awkward, the overall impression is still of elegant simplicity. the location is a bit away from the city centre, but we didn't feel this was a major disadvantage as you mostly move around the city by taxi anyway. there is a gorgeous egg-shaped outdoor lap pool in the garden. service was excellent for brazilian standards. the price is unbeatable on weekends - we paid 165 reais. all in all, highly recommended!

author: dannlaly
title: Good Hotel
text: My husband and I spent one weekend at Brasilia Palace. As usual, it was hot and sunny in Brasilia, so we were able to enjoy the pool - and that was great. I've read some reviews complaining about no pool service and I can say that's no longer a problem. Polite waiters offered us whatever we wanted to drink and we were able to enjoy cool bevarages by the pool. The room is also good (can's say great since they still have those huge tvs and the shower was not the best). Breakfast was delicious. We rented a car, which is a good idea being in Brasilia, since everything is far away, so the distance was not a problem for us, but the hotel is a bit far from downtown and in the middle of nowhere - but with a great view of the lake. It's also a bonus that it's a historical building, with beautiful panels. Overall, it's a very good choice, specially if you get a great deal for the room (we paid US$ 100)

author: lennoxheadfamily
title: Retro style heaven!
text: This hotel is heaven for anyone who appreciates style in architecture and decor. The 1960s design of Oscar Nemeyer has been perfectly restored to its elegant modernist vision. The location by the lake is cool and a respite from the dry Brasilia winter, and the building design channels the breeze... we didnt need to use the air conditioner. The beds are superb, the breakfast offers a wide range of fresh fruit, pastries, Brasilian specialties, the restaurant is first class, and the staff are friendly. The location is a little out of town by the lake. If you have a car this is the best place to stay in Brasilia. Even if you don't have a car (we didn't) its still only 10 minutes in a taxi to the centre, and its a far better atmosphere than the main hotel sectors. We also did the city tour offered by the hotel which was excellent.

author: Luiz_Sobrinho
title: Achieved the requirement
text: It`s a fair hotel. Not too good, not bad... Breakfast at Oscar restaurant is fine, nothing AWESOME, but with good products. Room is large and so is the bathroom, both looks really clean. Internet connection is free if you have patience to use a 200Kbps, to have a 2Mbps connection you have to pay U$10,00 for 24hs. For an average rate of U$100,00 and due to the location nearby where I had to go, it was a good option. There is absolutely NOTHING nearby the hotel, so, either you order food in the room or a cab to go somewhere. I ordered a sandwich that was acceptable.

author: SjurOslo
title: I would recommend this hotel
text: The great virtue of this hotel is its architecture and design, which is obvious to everybody. This is Brasília modernism at its best. A second argument is its location by the lake. The area is beautiful and dead safe (the presidential palace is just down the street). I have done a lot of jogging on the roads surrounding the hotel. True enough, the hotel does not have very upscale amenities; only one restaurant, no exercise room etc. However, this is more than compensated for by its location and design. I have stayed in many of the more "central" hotels in Brasília. They are located in the dreary "hotel sectors" with little opportunity to walk around and to relax. This hotel provides you with more such opportunities at a good price.

author: pbergama
title: Yeap, OK.
text: I stayed here in a business trip, on a 3-day stay, on room #218 on second floor. The left wing of the hotel (viewing from front outside), you stay on the side of the Jaguaré Avenue and in front of a helicopter parking, which makes everything very noisy. The air conditioning was loudy also. The hotel does not have service room, the dinner costs R$ 32 (US$ 8.20), the wifi have a weak signal at the room. The bathroom is small, and its sink stays outside of it. The windows open only 12 cm (4.7 in). The cable TV hadn't good options. So, it's a business hotel. Do not expect great facilities.

author: vvdantas
title: Not for a long stay
text: Clean, regular breakfast, minimal facilities. Bathroom really small and sink is outside of bathroom. My room was cleaned every day. Not possible to use the phone as hotel does not allow calls. Also keep the window open will let in the stink from the Pinheiros river (behind the building). Elevators take too long. The building has 3 of it. I do not look forward or plan stay in this hotel again. It was not my favorite at all.

author: 288bb
title: Not a Favourite
text: The hotel is clean and well maintained. But the breakfast is sparse, the air conditioner in my room did not work and very few of the front desk reception speak or understand English. The restaurant does not let you charge to the room and there is no room service. The fridge in the room is not stocked with water but the store in the restaurant carries water. The Wi Fi is free but is not strong enough to work in your room. You must go down to the lobby area in order to do your work for the next day. The rooms are quiet if you stay opposite the front. At the front and across is the street is a helicopter landing pad so it would be noisy at the front.

author: Bowlover
title: Good Value, Great Location
text: This hotel appears to have been quite recently updated, and tastefully so. Located right next to a four block long covered shopping and dining area, it was especially good for us because it was raining and we were on foot. The room size was large for Japan and for this price ($100/night), as was the double bed. Breakfast buffet, at $7.00, was also a very good value. I've certainly never found anything close in the US! The big shortcoming, resulting in a one star downgrade, was rather coarse bedsheets. All cotton, I believe, but scratchy. Even so, highly recommended for the price.

author: brown-and-cony
title: Noisy room in a convenient location
text: This hotel was in a convenient location with an adjoining Lawson, and really close to Obiyamachi. The car parking is right next door for ¥900 per night, which you pay for along with your room charge at check-in. Check-in was quick and staff were friendly. There’s also a counter where you pick up any amenities you need. They say you don’t get any amenities in your room, but they have pump bottles of shampoo, conditioner and body wash, and there are also toothbrushes. The room was large with lots of space to walk around, but the bathroom was quite small, like other Japanese hotels, but it was nice and clean. While we didn’t get lots of pillows, the bed was still comfortable. We also got quite a nice view of the city from our room. One negative was that the room was pretty noisy – firstly from the street outside (you can even hear the beeping from the pedestrian crossing!), and then from the air-con unit. Also, we were in an end room, so the wi-fi was quite weak in our room, so if you’re relying on wi-fi, ask for a more central room.

author: JW8188
title: Modern Clean Hotel
text: Stayed here for a business trip. It takes a few days to figure out the elevators but the view from the lobby is stunning. Lobby bar seemed to be very small and crowded most of the time. Sadly the wind was blowing strong so we were unable to enjoy the rooftop bar. Rooms were very nice and clean. Much like the elevators, it does take a few days to figure out the light switches in the room. There was a glass wall between the actual room and the bathroom. The night light really shined through the "wall." Was a little too bright for us.

author: mbstwins
title: Great hotel in a good, and maybe not-so-good location
text: Now this hotel is interesting: you get there and take the elevator to the 70th floor for the lobby- which has be beautiful view of LA (be sure to walk toward the bathroom on that level so you can see the Hollywood sign). You then check in and go down to your room in this elevators that you request on a kiosk. There is a roof top bar and restaurants. Now, the 7th Street Metro station is right there, next to the hotel. You can take a trip to Santa Monica pier for next to nothing and it takes the sam amount of time as an Uber (about 1 hour). Target, Nordstrom Rack and a food court are across the street. You can walk to many sights ( I walked to the Cathedral about a mile away), but be forewarned _ there are many mentally ill and homeless people on the streets in the area. I am not exaggerating that a homeless person literally walking into the Starbucks I was in and while I was preparing my coffee, he walked in and grabbed my food. When management noticed they just said " he did it again".

author: jeansV4075PO
title: From DC
text: Stayed here many times but very frustrated with inconsistent benefits, food choices, and general lack of professionalism. Something has changed here making me to move on. A food desert on Sundays and ordered bar food never delivered- will I be charged? Two days no water than two days of turn down. Why the disparity? Paid for club access and no drinks when they were promised. Just an un professional response. I am moving on to RC.

author: love2travel79
title: Once Again Amazing!
text: I had a short staycation to celebrate my birthday and had an amazing time! The rooms are very spacious and luxurious. Even the basic room is quite large with an amazing soaking tub. Bed linens are high-end and matress/pillow comfort is on point. Room service was fast and did not disapoint. Many TV viewing options. Excellent costumer service. The lobby is on the 70th floor but have to travel back down to the guest rooms. It seems a little incovenient, but did not present a big issue, just some getting use to (having to go up first in order to go down). I would definitely recomment this property and return with pleasure.

author: jw2018939
title: Beautiful New Built Skyscraper 40 Mins Drive from LAX
text: It’s convenient for my business trip from Los Angeles international airport to downtown LA. Very new skyscraper. It’s reception is located on 70th floor with magnificent view day and night. Be very close look at doorman to help you hire a ride to airport. They gave me an out of dated Lincoln charged me 60 from Hotel to LAX after I saw driver tip doorman. Flat rate charged by yellow cab is 46 from downtown LA to LAX airport. It’s an awful image on my leave. In addition, the bell desk charge you for receiving mail for you. Not free as many other InterContinentals.

author: Artherine
title: Unbelievable experience
text: The hotel is two years old and the highest building in Los Angeles. The service is 5 star and everything inside. The pool, fitness center, rooftop bar and music, restaurants, and the list goes on. Guest parking is a little expensive but the area is secure . The view from the room was priceless. Every day I could see the Hollywood sign. If you want to have a great experience and not worried about $$$ this is the place. Also there’s a little mall next door: Target, Nordstrom Rack, CVS, Starbucks just to name a few.

author: Susanloves2travel
title: Great with a few gliches
text: The hotel is beautiful and sleek. The rooms are lovely and the views with ceiling to floor windows are a treat. Only here for two nights and would return. For two nights the bar had no Sauvignon Blanc wine-why when it’s on the menu. The roof bar music was deafening. Went to the lower bar which wouldn’t let us in as no room. Ordered in the lobby from a menu. Can you believe a chicken sandwich is $29 and pastrami is $25?!

author: TravelPickier
title: Upscale Hotel with fantastic services, but elevators are inconvenience
text: We booked a King Deluxe Club Intercontinental corner room with parking package (Valet parking only, charge for $48 per overnight, no self-parking allows). First, they gave us a small corner room with a shower only in the bath room, after I raised up the requests that we wish to have a bath tub, they switched to a suite corner room. Intercontinental club is a fantastic lounge, it’s worth the money to book a room with club InterContinental (highly recommended), it service breakfast (light), afternoon tea, and cocktail, refrigerator has bottle soda, ginger Ale, water are open for all day long, the self-service coffee machine made a very good Flat white (much better than Starbucks). We will appreciate the peace feeling to enjoy the breakfast, the afternoon tea with a view for downtown L.A from 69 floor (if clear sky). We have the Saturday dinner buffer at Dekkadance, ($55 per person), variety are not as much as other same class hotel (not comparable to Las Vegas buffer on price and food), they do not have king crab, instead of cold shrimp, Clam, Mussel. New York Strip and Roast chicken. Pizza suppose is A+, but because of not many customers visit, those pizzas has been out from the oven for a while. As many previous comments said, the elevator is the most confusing, they have at least five elevators (maybe six), in order to check in, the lobby is located at 70 floor, you will need to go up to 70 stories and come down to your room, if you need to pick-up your car, you will need to take the elevator to the ground floor, and walk out to the elevator and take another elevator to the P1 (underground parking area)level, it is inconvenience. There is another elevator (all glass) from the lobby to the highest floor, but it was closed due to the rain. Overall every staffs are very kinds and polite, they have been provided as a five starts hotel services.

author: Odyssey603630
title: A superb stay
text: The quality of the rooms is excellent. Beautiful furnishings, sumptuous soft beds and very well kept. The bedrooms are very quiet and all have excellent views. We stayed on floor 43, west side, and the view was excellent. Once you get to floors 65 and above, the views of LA, Hollywood etc are breathtaking. As for the food in Dekkadence, it was very nice, lovely breakfast selection, fresh fruits and a wide variety of savoury dishes. A special mention goes to David Valencia, who was a consummate professional and provided excellent service to us front of house, resolving in a most helpful and swift manner an issue which arose. A wonderful stay and would definitely return.

author: millenniumflyer
title: An Incredible Stay
text: I’ve stayed at a lot of hotels and was extremely impressed with this property. In fact, it is actually one of the best hotels I’ve ever stayed at. The views are nothing less than magnificent and the guest rooms are modern and well-appointed. I was lucky enough to have access to the Club Lounge, which featured breakfast, afternoon tea, and hors d’oeuvres/drinks in the evening. The service throughout the property was outstanding and the staff was consistently kind and friendly. I really can’t say anything negative. It is certainly a hotel I will return to in the future when I am in the LA area. I give the Intercontinental LA Downtown my very highest recommendation. You won’t be disappointed!

author: iancarswell
title: The best of everything
text: Currently we are 4 nights into a 5 night stay and will miss the place when we leave . We have a one bed club suite and the room is perfect, plenty of space , the best views and a huge bathroom . The club lounge is one of the best I have been to as the views are stunning and the food exceptional. The location is great for a tourist as is a small Uber to all the tourist hotspots or across the road for a metro. Also as it’s downtown the broad is a short walk as well as restaurants and shopping galore . Working in travel I have stayed at many exceptional hotels all over the world and this one sits with the best . I read that people had issues with the lifts and was a little worried but the way it works saves so much time not stopping on every floor to get to you floor. I highly recommend this hotel

author: barbaracU1473MC
title: Anniversary getaway
text: Loved this property! Upscale and elegant along with also being comfy and cozy! Staff professional and friendly! Location perfect , shopping and dining at your footsteps ! The view from the room was breathtaking ! View of the mountains, Hollywood, downtown and surrounding areas. The 73rd rooftop bar was so nice! The layout was beautiful and the view was fabulous ! Overall this property was modern and elegant and exceeded all my expectations !

author: CBTLoudLive
title: Recommended!
text: After a long day of travel and meetings the staff took great care of us! Lovely room and appointments. All new furnishings. Super comfortable bed. The next morning at the Club we took a breakfast meeting and several calls. Horacio took care of our double espressos and made sure we had everything we needed. Great experience from arrival to departure. We’ll be back!🙏🏼

author: ModernMichael
title: A pleasure...
text: This hotel is wonderful. The staff is first rate and very helpful. I had ordered an Uber and the valet opened the door, and then moved the front seat forward so that I would have legroom in the back seat. The views are insane -- if it is within your budget, I would definitely upgrade to one of the Executive Suites. They are significantly larger than the regular rooms and have large expansive windows on two sides of the room (they are in the corner). Ask for a room with a northern exposure as those are the best views, although the sunsets from the west are beautiful. It was a pleasure. Some people complained about the elevators. It is fairly simple -- you have to go to the lobby on the 70th floor and go down from there. It's a bit unintuitive but it's actually quite simple.

author: Victorradaelli
title: Worst package handle in world
text: Worst experiencie in an hotel that I ever had. I made some purchases in Amazon with the same address of the hotel. Intercontinental accepted one box and rejected others boxes for the diferents orders with no reason. When I tried to understanding why, nobody couldn't help me. I couldn't buy it again because it's a short trip so I went back to Brazil without my items. I really didn't recomend this hotel if you will use this type of service. The hotel have three different zones of elevator that is very annoying because if you room are in the higher levels you must go to the lobby in the 70th floor to change elevator. It's crazy and boring.

author: alexandersY5402GQ
title: 25th birthday stay
text: Amazing from start to finish! Room was not ready so we were given drink vouchers while we waited. Then also they upgraded our room. Amazing view from the 63rd floor. Service was great from valet, check in, concierge, bar tenders, room service, etc. I was also surprised with a birthday dessert and personally signed birthday card! Perfect staycation hotel. Definitely will be back. Thank you for everything!

author: hammyone
title: Overall great with a few big not so great features
text: Was at the InterContinental for four days over New Year's. The hotel is new and modern. As other reviewers have noted, the reception is on the 70th floor which was fine for me as the entire floor is a bank of floor to ceiling windows facing West, so lots of fabulous light. The bar area on 70, the workout room (and full service locker room) and breakfast buffet were highlights. The elevators and key card lighting system in the room had their frustrations. Waiting at the elevators got to be a "thing." Check in was a bit rough - rooms not ready, luggage missing. We had a large group to be sure, but they've known we were coming for a long time... staff seemed to be uninterested. I liked the hotel but would check out something different next time in LA.

author: ZipsnBucks
title: New Years stay
text: We stayed at the hotel for the Rose Bowl. The hotel is very nice and had everything we wanted. We arrived early (11:30 am) and while our room wasn't ready yet we checked in and dropped off our bags. We walked around the downtown area and had lunch. We came back around 2:00 and our room was ready and our bags were already in the room. The plusses for the property were the number of restaurants, the staff were always available and helpful, the rooms were spacious. The only minus would be the elevators but we go used to them fairly quickly. We will recommend the IC to anyone that will be staying in the downtown LA area.

author: chac94
title: Great Hotel
text: One of the nicest InterContinental’s I’ve been too. Was upgraded as a Spire Ambassador. The hotel has spectacular views from pretty much every angle. The rooftop Spire bar is a great place to relax. Club also had beautiful views. The complaints about the elevators are true. If you want to go to your valet parked car from your room you have to take 3 elevators. Confusing but I got the hang of it quickly.

author: 550la
title: Trendy, downtown
text: We spent one night at this hotel and found it a hip and trendy hotel. The check in was flawless - thanks to Sharon. The concierge took time to recommend some great eating options organized by distance which was extremely helpful. We would have been lost without him. One thing to know - you have to access the lobby on the 70th floor and take another set of elevators to your room which makes navigation a little tricky sometimes. The price was well worth it. After several unsuccessful attempts to meet Uber at the right place, Jereal from valet hooked me up in 2 seconds. Thank you Jereal!

author: csanchez1203
title: Anniversary trip
text: I am a couple days late but i just had to write a review! Stayed here on December 3rd room 4031. Check in was so fast and Chris at the front desk was so kind and funny! Everything about this hotel is so exciting to see, every employee smiled and made me feel so comfortable! Will definitely recommend to family and friends and we will be back soon! Thank you Chris again for the nice room! Saw the Hollywood sign from my room which made my husband so happy! Great way to relax and spend our anniversary here! I swear every time i went on the elevator my husband and i got so excited mind you were adult haha, 73 floors is crazy though!!! Thank you guys so much for the best service ever!

author: JustinDOF
title: Dec trip
text: Good hotel. Scenic rooftop bar, nice pool/spa area, and large fitness room. The room was spacious with a large bathroom area. Bed was comfortable and the lighting/storage area was sufficient. I though the tv was a little small, for the size of the room, and I prefer the fridge to not be stocked. Also, the bottled water was not complimentary. The elevator system is a little annoying but manageable. I would stay again.

author: dysphorichousewife
title: Beautiful! But alot of time spent in elevators to get to lovely rooms
text: This is a wonderful property in a great location in DTLA - I loved my room and hotel overall and would give this an excellent rating if it were not for two things: 1. The elevator situation - you need to ride up to 70 to check in and then go up/down to room. To get to gym is a long ride also sometimes requiring an elevator change. They should consider a checkin kiosk in lobby for regular guests. You can switch to express elevator on 31 so request a room on that floor or one that is close to 31 or 70. 2. Service - the staff needs development to make this a consistent 5 star experience. I know this is a newer hotel so hope they are working on it! I highly recommend and will definitely return.

author: AnyaI11
title: Modern new hotel with beautiful views
text: The hotel was beautiful, designs were chic and modern. Located on main street and relatively close to go around downtown. Design of room was nice too i loved how they put cool and quirky paintings on the walls. Only downside was that service was not too good. I had a housekeeper come in twice to my room without me requesting it. Also when asked for check out for 1pm as an IHG rewards member they should be able to grant it when the hotel is not busy (it did not seem 100% occupancy). Request was not granted. I work for an InterCon property as well and i know how it works. Dissapointed but I let it go because i know how much pressure and work the colleagues experience during work.

author: carawasthere
title: Takes Forever to Get Anywhere
text: This hotel is beautiful and the service is impeccable. Rooms are nicely maintained with comfortable beds and nice showers. Some rooms feature high end bath products while others do not, which is disappointing. There doesn’t seem to be a method as to why. The biggest frustration in this hotel is the elevator system. You have to go all the way up to the lobby on the 70th floor to then go down to your room. It takes forever and quite frankly, is just annoying in general. There’s several restaurants and bars in the hotel. Spire 73 is the rooftop bar and while it’s worth a visit, it’s fairly windy and the views are fairly obscured by the dirty windows (same in the rooms).

author: Seamus_NYC
title: Brand New Hotel with Amazing Views
text: Stayed in Downtown Los Angeles. Brand New hotel. Great sky lobby. Nice bar with great view. Excellent brunch. Nice pool and fitness center. Highly recommend. The hotel often has rooms for a reasonable price.

author: sharnise006
title: Sisters Trip
text: The hotel was very nice. The view is amazing. I could see the Hollywood sign from my room. Also, the beds are so soft best sleep ever. The elevators were always packed, and most if the time had to wait for it to open. Check in is all the way on the 70th floor. Alot of stuff was within walking distance. I will keep this place in mind when I visit again.

author: Gorilla23
title: Best hotel in the West Coast
text: I’ve stayed at this property a few times since it has opened. My wife and I decided to celebrate our 30th Anniversary for four nights here. I’ve stayed at over 35 Intercontinental hotels around the world and there is none better than this property. Great, hip theme. Awesome restaurants. Fantastic outdoor bar (73 stories above street level!), and absolutely fantastic service. Kudos and thanks to Sylvia Gomez and her guest relations staff best on the west coast. I can’t recommend this hotel enough. It’s a must stay in LA!

author: Chineham-traveller
title: Stunning Views and Service
text: This hotel has the best views you could image. I was given a room with a view of the Hollywood Hills and Sign, it was amazing with floor to ceiling windows. The room was perfect and hi-tech, loved the controls by the bed for the lights and heating. The TV was huge and the fact you can stream from your iPad to the TV (Netflix) is brilliant. The bath room and shower are the size of a small apartment. The hotel is right by the Subway, so easy to get to from Union Station - if flying you can get the bus to Union and then the Subway...Easy, even with JetLag ! The team at the hotel are very friendly and welcoming. The reception is on the 70th Floor with views stretching LA. I wish I had tried the food as it looked amazing - I had some by the pool and this was very good.

title: Recommended for LA Downtown
text: Strangely enough, last time we were in LA, we stayed in the hotel that *used* to be on the same spot and yet I booked this not for nostalgia for that time 8 years ago, but convenience to downtown, both in terms of offices and LA Live. The hotel is new. It's very swish, very LA (as in what you expect from TV), has a complicated lift system in terms of floor access, but the whole place runs like clockwork. The staff were good and knew their stuff. The breakfast was terrific. We had dinner on both nights in the hotel: the first in the fine dining restaurant - very good - and the second at the lobby bar - what you'd expect from a lobby bar. The room itself (which wasn't the cheapest option available) was on the small side. While the bathroom was large and included a bath (waste of space) and separate shower, the room itself was small and awkward for two people to unpack bags, walk around, check out respective computers etc. Overall, I would recommend it and, if wanting to stay in LA Downtown next time we visit here (probably in another 8 years!!!), we'd return.

author: Spottypudding
title: Amazing hotel
text: We have recently stayed here for 2 weeks and we didn't want to leave! The hotel is amazing, from lobby to room and we got upgraded to a corner room and it is really worth it. The rooms are so modern and a decent size and the bathrooms are lovely. The only problem, is pulling yourself away from the spectacular views of LA! Though, it was always somewhere, we looked forward to coming back to. Every member of staff, we came across, where very friendly and helpful and we even got 3 phonecalls during our stay, to ask if we needed anything. Attention to detail throughout the hotel, was perfect and even little things like a clock next to the bed, made a difference, as most hotels don't provide one. Housekeeping were great and the room was always done to a high standard everyday. We found the lift system very easy to use and don't know why people complain about it, in other reviews. We had breakfast here, one morning and very nice, though wish it was cheaper, as we would of gone more.

author: keithgH1078QT
title: In town for business meetings
text: In town this week for business meetings and decided to select this hotel for convenience to my local office. Have stayed in the LA Downtown in past, so was curious on difference. When arrived was surprised by fact that the lobby was o. the 70th floor, but was amazed when I arrived to check in. The layout is very inviting and location of hotel is great. Was immediately greeted at lower level and upper floor when getting off the elevator. Check in was perfect and then took elevator down to my floor. ( only real interesting part from other hotels) I was on the 32nd floor and entered my room and was overwhelmed by the view and layout. Facilities are perfect and will look to stay here next time in town.

author: alhamdank
title: Perfect Hotel
text: Quite hotel, spacious clean room, large comfortable bed. Super tall building with great view. Stunning lobby and 73 rooftop overlooking the skyline. Wonderful swimming pool area at 7th floor. Helpful friendly staff, and security staff was everywhere. 1 minutes walking distance to Fig at7th mall with lots of restaurants, shops and walmart. One thing I don’t like ridiculous elevator system go to 70 or 31 floor then change to other elevator to reach your room. Overall it’s wonderful Hotel .

author: caz389
title: Amazing hotel is a perfect location
text: My husband and I got to enjoy 6 nights here earlier this month. Our room had an amazing view of downtown LA on the 55th floor and it's location right opposite a metro station made it so easy to get about. The Staples Centre is walking distance and would highly recommend the Grammy Museum, also within walking distance. We loved the rooftop bar which is stunning and the staff were helpful and polite. Don't understand why people moan about the elevator system -it's not rocket science! The reception is on the 70th floor and the rooms are below this so you have to go up to go down but is so quick and there are a good number of elevators so we never waited for more than a couple of minutes. You access the elevator with your key card to stop anyone else gaining access and you press your floor number and it immediately indicates which elevator is yours. We rarely stopped at any other floor on the way and you arrive in a few seconds! Highly recommend.

author: smrpenn
title: Excellent well located hotel
text: This brand new stunning tower is great. It's well located downtown so if you have business in that area or in DTLA it's a great choice. The rooms are very large with a stunning lobby and rooftop bar over looking the skyline. Further the lobby bar and restaurant are excellent. Views are unparalleled as this is the tallest tower west of the Willis Tower in Chicago. The elevators are a journey as is getting to parking but that's to be a expected for this mixed use building. As its new you'll get a good deal. I'd stay here again.

author: rl508
title: Great location and treatment of elites
text: The front desk staff took good care of this Platinum Ambassador and assigned me a nice room (too bad it was facing East LA and the building where I work). Interiors are new and clean, and at 60 floors up, we didn't hear too much outside noise and hardly any hallway noise. We did hear our loud neighbors at 2am banging and dropping things and shouting for a while. The club lounge is ok. The offerings aren't too great, and I didn't like how the staff hounded us down every time we walked in to ask for our room number. They should put a card scanner at the door. Sometimes we would walk out of an empty lounge and come back in like 30 minutes later to an empty lounge and somehow they forgot who we were in that short time and chased us down again for our room number. I'm glad they check to prevent unauthorized entry, but there has to be a better system. At least the view is better (facing West).

author: kitkit1
title: Very good service &a wonderful views!
text: My family & I had 2 adjacent rooms - the kids (12 & 14) loved that we could see the famous HOLLYWOOD sign from our rooms. They also loved the excellent WiFi & the food, both room service as well as buffet. This speaks volumes because 1 is a very picky kid. We all loved the beds & pillows. It was quiet at night, which is a rarity in a big hotel like this. The reception at checking was fantastic. I'm sorry I can't recall the name of the gentleman who checked us in but he was French, from Marseille. It was a lovely stay.

author: heatherdB7853BX
title: Woah! Amazing views
text: I loved this hotel so much, I hardly wanted to leave. While the elevator system was a little confusing to work out at first, I loved being treated to a spectacular view of Los Angeles every time I crossed the 70th floor lobby. The My corner suite on the 53rd floor was spacious and elegant. I am now obsessed with Santal 33-- the bath products from Le Labo provided in the bathroom. The gym was very well equipped with many machines. While the furnishings and views are stunning, service leaves some room for improvement. Unfortunately my Nespresso machine stopped working on the 2nd day and was never repaired even after I reported it (morning coffee!!!); room service and service in the restaurant was slow on two evenings (long waits to order, for food, and for the cheque). Service during the Sunday brunch was quick, which made me think they might not have had enough staff on the other nights. I'd still stay again, as overall its a beautiful property.

author: ellent447
title: New modern skyscraper with great views!
text: Stayed one night for work, on the 40th floor. Took me a few tries to get used to the elevator system as the lobby is on the 70th floor, restaurants are on the 71st and 69th while the rooms are on lower floors (different elevators) and you cannot go directly to your room from the ground floor. Either change on the 31st floor or go to the 70th, then change to the other elevator to get to your room, You punch in your room #, and the system tells you which elevator to get on. I only had a view of the accounting firm from my window, but the lobby and the Dekkadance restaurant which serves breakfast, had fabulous views. I thought the $35 breakfast buffet ($43 with tip) was steep for what you get, and I did not see any fresh berries (except strawberries) which I would have expected for those prices. I walked down Wilshire Blvd (take escalator from ground level to the second floor and you're right on Wilshire) to walk a few blocks to dinner, and noticed several groups of homeless folks on the sidewalk. It was a warm summer night and this neighborhood seems safe to walk around at night but I was a bit surprised so close to many of the nicest hotels. I noticed there was a bath robe but no hand soap (there was shower gel) and no slippers in my room, which I would have expected for a quality hotel such as this.

author: waiake1
title: A great hotel with one small niggle
text: Stayed two nights in a Club suite. Should have checked in a club lounge. The room was great. Staff very eager to please. We were on 62nd floor. This is the crazy bit. to get anywhere we had to take one elevator to floor 70, then go to different one to get anywhere else. The lobby on the 70th floor is inconvenient to say the least. so that aside the place is great and worth the cost.

author: DuckTails2013
title: Excellent in all aspects
text: The hotel is Downtown directly opposite the Metro station and on the sightseeing hop-on-off bus route. Getting around LA was easy from here. The view from the lobby is simply breathtaking (70th floor) and from all the bedrooms (don’t look down if you’re not good with heights!). The staff were all very friendly and helpful (esp Charles and Yolanda on Concierge desk). The hotel was only built last year and is bright, clean and well furnished. The lift system is a little tiresome though as you have to switch lifts to get to different levels. The breakfast is excellent and we would’ve eaten in the restaurant in the evening but they had a shellfish buffet on with no alternatives which didn’t work for two of our party. However we were able to get to good restaurants within a 10 min walk on all three of the nights that we stayed. We stayed with three teenagers and they made good use of the gym facilities! We were really impressed with this hotel and will definitely stay there again.

author: Sherlock_bcn
title: Good hotel but .....
text: The hotel is the tallest one in LA with great views of the city. Nice roof garden on the 73 floor with well-organized bar amenities. The location was one of the reasons why we booked (it is on the Downtown area) nearby of many restaurants and other facilities. On the less positive side the hotel was very crowdy during the week-end lacking from the required number of employees to attend your request (specially at the reception). It was impossible to get room services or even a person to talk with by the room telephone. Last but not least some services were not at the level of expectation. The breakfast lack from many products that now a days in an hotel of this category should be considered standard (fish, tomatoes, vegetables, etc). In summary we felt that we paid too much for the services we finally get.

author: alyf38
title: Great hotel, except for its confusing address
text: Have stayed in the here for 5 nights. The lobby view is amazing. The staff are helpful in general. The room design is good especially the lighting arrangement. The lifts are fine except that the touch screen is not sensitive enough sometimes hence the need to re-press again. The key thing for the hotel to fix is its address. Have been going out a lot by calling Uber. However majority of the drivers couldn’t find the drop off point which is accessible from 7th St not it’s official address of Wilshire Blvd. the hotel needs to consider how to talk to Uber so that the directional routing can be right.

author: 137arlenep
title: A Happening Place
text: Stayed at the Intercontinental for 4 nights in a club lounge corner room while a family member had a suite. Breathtaking views, excellent rooms, great linens, good toiletries. Extremely pleasant and helpful staff Club lounge was superior with terrific choices, especially breakfast and cocktail hour. Worth every penny (probably saved money were I to buy food elsewhere). Gorgeous bathrooms BUT no grab bar, slippery shower floor, soap dish with large grates so soap and amenities fall through unless you line it first with a washcloth. Elevators provided an opportunity to chat with fellow occupants who also wondered why this odd system was instituted! Bizarre but bearable. Popular hotel, busy. Worth a stay!

author: Lugano1980
title: Brand New in Downtown LA
text: A large property that works well. Check in on the 70th floor provides striking views but keep in mind going to different floors can require changing elevators. Was there for a conference. Huge and well equipped gym, rooms are standard with good sized bathrooms. Conference spaces are effective. Did not try restaurants, though CVS/Target/Macy’s and many restaurants are within walking distance. Very nice staff. Close to highways.

author: BrooklyniteLA
title: Great luxury hotel
text: This is one amazing luxury hotel. Brand new construction with a nice bar on the 70th floor overlooking the City of Los Angeles. If you are not staying here at min take the elevator to the bar and have a drink. We stayed during the BET week so the hotel was packed with rappers and the valet area was full of Royce so prices were around $680 min including tax. Hints: You can buy a day pass for the pool online at resort pass for $35 or $50 Tell Uber guy the valet entrance is on 7th not the address on Wilshire. There is no resort fee. Gym and Pool are included for free with room. Elevator situation is not my favorite basically for every move you have to go to 70th first.

author: Bnizzle76
title: Unbelievable Views
text: This property is absolutely gorgeous! The views from the lobby, pool, and rooftop bar are ahhhmazing! However, the checkin/checkout time is waaay too long. Our room wasn’t ready even after the suggested time. The mgr did try to make it right by giving us Concierge floor access. The complimentary food and drinks were wonderful, and we truly appreciated her effort. But, the lines are long and understaffed. Definitely needs improvement. Location is terrific- walk everywhere and metro a block away.

author: AsakaPanda
title: Beautiful
text: What a beautiful hotel! I love the check in on 70th floor and the views are breathtaking. The rooms are elegant and modern and very clean. The bathtub was awesome to take a soak in. The room service was great (24 hour) and the maid service was exceptional. I liked the lighting in the room was controlled via consoles on the wall and by the bed so you can turn off all lights, partial, etc etc. There are a few restaurants in the hotel - Sora was my favorite (Japanese). Very pleasant stay here and will definitely be back.

author: Timtan123
title: Nice city hotel, a little chaotic
text: We stayed at the Intercontinental LA Downtown for a three nights in March this year. Staff was professional and efficient, as you should expect. This is a business hotel given its location, we spotted one other family with kids like ourselves at breakfast. We had a corner room, and enjoyed the full glass windows. The subway is just across the road and a shopping mall is really closed by too. With our toddler we walked and took the subway and the Intercontinental is a good base if you want to be in the city. One small dislike was having to walk through the crowd of people having drinks at the reception level to get to our floor. There was no way of avoiding this, as we had to change elevator at the reception level to get to our floor, and that elevator was at the opposite end of the floor.

author: SarahB9209
title: Amazing view and friendly service!
text: Stayed here for two nights for my b-day trip to LA. The moment you entered the lobby, I was wowed by their beautiful scenery. Check in process was quick. Front desk agent appreciated me for being a IHG and gave me a nice room upgrade. She also explained me how their elevator system works. Too bad that we had to come all the way to 70 floor and transfer to guest elevator. When we came back from short trip, Jaelen from Guest Relations sent me a nice b-day dessert in the room along with a big sparkling water. I was so happy by her kind gesture. She did make my day and made me so happy after 5 hour trip from Toronto.

author: VikaasK
title: Loved it
text: One of the best if not the best intercontinental i have stayed in around the world. Big rooms. Superb service. Amazing views. Great location. Helpful staff except for the lady during the checkout she was rude. But the overall experience was amazing and worth staying again and again at this property. Dont even think twice if you are in los angeles just make this your 1st and last choice. Love it

author: KateL943
title: Spectacular views
text: We had almost a week at the this very modern hotel. It had magnificent views over LA. Check in was very professional for our first stay. My husband is a spire elite IHG member and we were given an upgrade. The room was large, which was greatly appreciated as we were staying for 6 nights. The concierge was extremely helpful. The lifts were irritating though, reception being on the 70th floor, then you had to take a lift to your designated floor. We came back and stayed one more night, but unfortunately no upgrade, the room we were assigned was the smallest we encountered in our whole month long trip!

author: CarlaM560
title: Sleek hotel
text: This hotel is trendy. Great rooms. Courteous and friendly staff. The rooftop bar has a good vibe and view. Convenient to restaurants, bars, shopping and LAX. The rooftop pool is good too. I would definitely stay here again. I was on business so didn't have time to use all the amenities. Next time.

author: Arrendajo
title: Unique experience
text: At first I was put off by the fact that I had to take two elevators to get to my room: one to the lobby and one to my room. But it turned out I really enjoyed my stay. The room was spotless and comfortable, and the staff was very attentive. I enjoyed passing through the lobby and taking in the view whenever entering or leaving. The fitness facility is a big plus... it's free, open 24/7 and very well equipped. I liked being able to watch Netflix on the big screen in the room. I did not like things for sale scattered around the room... wine, snacks and a minibar fridge, but no fridge for guests.

author: matthewj513
title: What a view!
text: Everything thing about this hotel is first class. From the rooms, (very quiet) the bars/ restaurant options/ it’s central location/ and of course the roof top view and bar. The gym is as good as you would find anywhere, it is really top notch. Excellent pool / spa area. Wifi was fast and constant, brekkie had a good range and the bed was very comfortable. I did not have a vehicle. You are required to use two lifts to get to your room which is a slight frustration so best to stay on floor 31 to avoid two lifts. The view from the room (fl 34) was helped by extra large windows however if you go to the rooftop bar the view is spectacular. I will stay here again.

author: Roslyn28wantagh
title: Superior Hotel.
text: New, posh, beautiful. This hotel is really gorgeous. The rooms are a generous size and very modern and plush. Loved all the new electronics. Fun rooftop bar and restaurant. The prices are surprisingly low given the quality. Convenient downtown locations. Friendly staff. Very accommodating.

author: NitinDawar
title: Luxury property
text: 1.) Polite Staff. 2.) Clean Property. 3.) Good Views. 4.) Nice And Spacious Rooms. 5.) Hotel Should To Keep Maintain As Like. 6.) Good Location. 7.) Property In City Centre. 8.) Good For Families. 9.) Nice.

author: BellaFromLA
title: Beautiful Instagrammable Hotel in the Center of DTLA
text: I stayed at this hotel for a meeting, while POTUS was visiting and even with all the craziness with secret service and the extra security, they did everything they could to make our stay comfortable and as easy as possible. The staff here is wonderful and I would definitely stay here again. The hotel rooms are spacious while everything is modern and sleek, it is also comfortable. The rooms have amazing views and are well appointed. The restaurants have delicious food and you eat while overlooking the city and the view. Also, there are so many interesting finds that photograph well throughout the hotel so your social media addiction will be fulfilled. Each bathroom and public space has a unique surprise so it’s a fun hotel just to explore. They also do a great job with their outdoor spaces to show off the downtown area, which has changed so much. The only thing this hotel didn't have that I wanted was a spa

author: 729brianc
title: INSANE VIEWS, EXCELLENT SERVICE, GREAT HOTEL
text: As this is the tallest building west of the Mississippi, its no surprise that the views are INSANE!! But wait,......there’s more!! Service is EXCELLENT and the accommodations are superb! It’s interesting that the hotel lobby is located on the 70th floor, which is very popular in Asia at the moment. The elevator set up can be a bit confusing but everything else about this hotel is incredible. Very modern feel, all the bells and whistles you could desire. You can really see that they paid great attention to detail when building this place. As a bonus, I hear it’s built to withstand a 9.4 earthquake. SOLD!! You must check out this spot, even if you are local.

author: JDA60
title: Deserving of Five Stars
text: The first thing you notice is how friendly the staff are and how good the service is. The rooms are nice and you have bedside control of climate lights etc. The staff seem to care about you as a guest. The room rates are reasonable but the restaurant and bar pricing is high but not unexpected for a luxury hotel. Beer is $9.00. The elevator system take a bit of getting used to, the lobby is on the 70th floor and you have to go to the lobby to get the elevator to your room or to exit the hotel, very secure but get to you after awhile. You enter the floor on a keypad and it tells you what elevator you will take. Do not get into an elevator unless the floor you selected is on the display by the door, there is no way to select a floor once the doors close. The mini bar in your room has some interesting items but a word of warning, if you take an item out of the minibar it will automatically bill you even if you put the item back.

author: joejnyc
title: GROUP TOURIST HOTEL
text: Where is the bus?? This place is a laughable, both the hotel and the guests. The hotel, the eleveator on the 70th floor sounds like a winde tunnel...all day & night. The staff are young and no hotel experince setting. The rooms are small and smell like the artfical spary they love at the hotel. This place could have been the place to go in downton la but they really screwed it up. The guest, hotel.com kind of people who want a free botttle of water or french toast. Korean tourist are everywhere, that should tell you the story. One korean guy was asking if there was a dog bbq place near the hotel.

author: FabrizioLV
title: Stunning hotel DTLA
text: I spent 2 nights during New Years Eve at this new Intercontinental downtown LA. It is I believe the tallest building in the city. From the moment you arrive with the lobby positioned at the 73rd floor you understand this is not your average hotel. I don't think there is one spot in the whole hotel where the views are not stunning. The standards are very high being the hotel brand new. There is roof top bar that is amazing being the tallest bar again on the city. The service has been impeccable. Having being open only for a few months, not everything is still well oiled but all the staff tries to make it up to you, especially Jean Baptiste that followed all of us very closely making sure we enjoyed our stay. At walking distance to the Staple Center, it is simply a beautiful property.

author: CJchina2
title: Almost but not quite
text: Considering how new the Downtown Intercontinental Hotel is, I was surprised the room was in such poor shape. The desk lamp and toilet paper holder were both broken. The room is very modern and bright with a great big TV. Gorgeous view all the way out to the ocean. I was forewarned about the elevator situation and it's not that big of a deal. I had asked for a room near the elevator but I was at the farthest point from it. I also waited twenty minutes for my car at the valet and I was the only car they needed to retrieve. So just not quite there yet. Room service was pretty good, but I waited an hour for both dinner and breakfast, which is just ridiculous.

author: kimwit11
title: Amazing hotel! Great staff
text: Was at this hotel for work and it was great. Staff was amazing and accommodating went so far as making sure I looked at the eclipse when I walked though the lobby. Room was beautiful and clean. Gym was the best I’ve ever seen in a hotel. Pool was great. Rooftop bar had amazing views. Not a complaint and I stay in a lot of hotels. Great hotel!

author: golflad69
title: Sureal!
text: Checked-In on floor 70. Above the clouds! Brand new hotel. As an Ambassador was up-Graded to corner suite with lovely views of city, mountains and ocean. 73rd floor outdoor bar was fantastic. Great pool, hot tub, cabanas and pool bar. Club Lounge one of the best I have been in with great service and selection. This property has so much that you need not ever leave the premises. Staff was all around excellent, Will now stay at only this property when in LA.

author: Stefan79
title: Great Hotel
text: The location of the Intercontinental Hotel is perfect. Many restaurants and shops are within walking distance and the metro station is right across the street. The change of the elevators on certain floors is a little annoying and during peak times it takes a long time to get to your room. My room was stunning.Very modern yet cozy and comfortable. The modern fixtures in the bathroom need extra care and cleaning -this was not the case in my room. I loved the view from my room, the lobby, the restaurant and the rooftop bar. Restaurants and bars delivered what one would expect from an Intercontinental Hotel. Every staff member I have met was very friendly and keen to serve. The gym is world class and worth schedule extra time for it.

author: Truth1914
title: On the 70th floor with great views of Los Angeles
text: Great views of LA. Wonderful stay in downtown LA. The food on the 69th floor was yummy. enjoyed drinks at the bar. Great service. Easy Lyft ride to Little Tokyo. Easy walk to shops. 24 hour fitness center.

author: Riley74
title: So disappointing
text: The disappointment just kept coming with this hotel. We don't mind paying 350 dollars a night for great experiences but this wasn't one of them. Once you get over trying to navigate the lift system which I find terribly annoying (call me old fashioned I like a ground floor libby) the check in was not special at all just felt like everyone else and not first time tourists to L.A.. Room was lovely but only 1 robe, had to ring Down. Breakfast was very disappointing - 900 rooms apparently and only one toaster! There were frozen lumps in the milk which I had to ask for when the tea came without it. Had to ask for ketchup twice, everything took so long. The roof top bar was unbelievably dirty and when the woman asked for 37 dollars for 2 drinks I nearly fell off my seat - again I don't mind paying big prices for memorable experiences but this was memorable for all the wrong reasons - you cannot charge huge prices just because of location etc you have to have the experience as well - sorry intercon you have a lot to do 🤥

author: Michael-Traveller-JP
title: Very new and stylish hotel
text: The InterContinental LA downtown is a very new, modern and stylish hotel. The lobby on the 70th floor offers great views over the greater LA area. The elevator system is unique. Need to key-in your room number on a pad in elevator lobby and you will be informed about the elevator taking you to your desired floor. Rooms are very modern. Especially some switches a bit too modern for my taste, since design was obviously more important than functionality. Breakfast is good. Some good and popular restaurants and bars, including a rooftop bar. All in all very recommendable and probably one of the best 5 star hotels in LA.

author: andreejune
title: so high
text: NICE beautiful, minimal and well laid out hotel. the check in on the 70th floor is very impressive as there is nothing else like it in downtown LA. rooms are clean and large with everything that you need and nothing you don't. bathrooms are also large and well designed. this is a modern hotel but not what i like to call the cheesy modern that you seem to find so often right now. it is a no frills business hotel but gets the job done. i like the many bars and restaurants in the hotel for convenience sake. this beats the tired JW marriott and the boring ritz on the other side of downtown. NOT SO NICE the double elevator ride that is required for all movement in and around the hotel - it can also feel somewhat corporate.

author: glc_11
title: Worth a stay
text: Brand new and impressive; tallest building in LA. Check in on the 70th story with spectacular views (bar there too); rooms lower but still great vistas. Good sized rooms for a downtown hotel. Rooms very modern and well equipped; as clean as only a new hotel can be. Good service. Went to business functions but food for large group very good. Elevators it odd-access sign in then take different elevators (which don't go to ground floor) to your rooms. Exercise area looked great but did not use.

author: J6185HLwilliama
title: Impressive building
text: You enter on the first floor and take an elevator to the lobby on the 70th floor; then you go down to the floor your room is in on either of 2 sets of elevators. To go back to the street you must return to the 70th floor and catch one of the ones that brought you up from the first, ie, you can't go directly down from your room floor. Who thought of this arrangement? There is a lovely view of LA from the lobby. The edifice is nested between others in such way that from the street one has to look up from limited angles to appreciate its modernistic magnificence. The rooms are nice and spacious but not beyond expectations. Yes, the personnel is very courteous. A practical location if you need to be downtown.

author: aldop470
title: Favorite hotel for Downtown LA for sure!
text: I give 5 ⭐️ for this Hotel. Start from the professional , helpful and friendly doorman! Great management staff with great service too. The view is just amazing .. it take your breath away start from the lobby, bar, breakfast restaurant and the rooftop bar. The room is modern and spacious. Room service food is 9 out of 10. The only negative feedback is lack of complementary mineral water in the room, we have to ask for more then they will deliver. But definitely will comeback for stay next time i visit dowtown LA. Cheers!

author: xxlauren3xx
title: Amazing!!!
text: What a hotel!! I am super fussy but I am super impressed with this hotel. The staff are friendly. The hotel is modern and clean. The views are out of this world. The beds are comfortable and luxurious. The best part is the view...incredible. Would visit again in a heartbeat

author: PeterFelix
title: Great Place
text: I had a meeting in Los Angeles. I selected the New Intercontinental hotel in downtown Los Angeles because of its proximity to all my meeting places. The hotel is beautiful! The room was superb! The front desk services were great! They were very, very helpful. Now there are several restaurants and lounges at this hotel and the food was amazing! We were able to move some of my meetings to the hotel:) Don't forget to try the breakfast brunch. It was outstanding! I will definitely be back!

author: bmmartino
title: Good with the potential to be much better.
text: We stayed here back during the end of August when we were stuck in LA due to Hurricane Harvey on the way back to Houston from Hawaii. We knew going in that this hotel was basically brand new and at the time we stayed it definitely was still working out some kinks. The elevators take some getting used to as its a system different from most hotels. Its important to remember this building isn't exclusively a hotel and they try to keep the hotel traffic separate from the business traffic. The room was great, very modern with a great view of the surrounding city. There's definitely a cool factor staying in the highest building in LA. A note on service, the hotel did check us in very early, which was great, but otherwise the service was a miss for us. At the rooftop bar, the service was very slow and they probably need more staff there to speed things up a little. We ate at Sora, the sushi restaurant on property, and we were pretty disappointed. The sushi is more like grocery store quality than what one would expect at a high end hotel property.

author: seunghyunw2017
title: Beautiful hotel with HORRIBLE service
text: The hotel is very new, so it is very clean. This is the only positive thing about this hotel. The service was horrible in general (front desk and phone service). I made two simple room service type requests, and one was completely ignored, and the other took more than 45 min to be completed. One more negative thing about the hotel is that the hotel lobby is on the 70th floor, so you have to go through the 70th floor every time you want to get out and to get back to your room. It's very inconvenient. Also, if you don't get out by 12pm on the checkout day, you will get locked out. We left something in the room on our checkout day, and we couldn't get in because the hotel terminated our access right at 12pm. To gain the temporary access back, it took close to an hour to resolve. Horrible service.

author: 981rickyg
title: Fabulous New Hotel!
text: Intercontinental DTLA is a very welcome addition to Downtown LA. I had stayed in DTLA once prior at a nearby lifestyle hotel and did not enjoy my experience; however, my recent stay at Intercontinental DTLA has changed my opinion of downtown - I look forward to returning! First, the check in is on the 57th floor with a fabulous lobby and almost 360 degree views of LA. I highly recommend booking a club level room as I enjoyed this daily for breakfast as well as in the evenings when catching up on emails. Despite many of my clients being located in Beverly Hills and Santa Monica, the driving in and out of DTLA was easy and simply by LA standards. The design of the rooms are immpecable and the floor to ceilings windows are the icing on the cake. Last, but not least - the service, everyone was friendly and both the Hotel Manager and Guest Services Manager made a point to greet my husband and I while in the club lounge. All and all - well done Intercontinental DTLA!

author: usckww
title: Great view, 70th floor lobby, then downhill from there
text: Hotel with a cool atmosphere and a lobby on the 70th floor, but after the initial wow, everything went down hill. Housekeeping was very poor. Dirty carpets, chrome not polished, floors not mopped and cleared of water? spots and sheets with holes. Spent $42 on a cold flavorless pizza and 2 diet cokes. Room service delivery person was very nice. Too bad the food was terrible. Very poor execution by a top tier hotel.

author: stevefowler
title: Aaaaagh - those lifts. And poor service, too
text: This should be so special - great location and views. But two things spoilt it for me - having to go via the 70th floor to get in and out. Why take one lift when you can take two? How infuriating! Rooms are comfy, but not special. But if you're going to provide a turn down service and towel refresh on nights one and two, why not do it on night three, too? The breakfast room is too small for such a big hotel, too. All-in-all disappointing.

author: jnlv2trvl
title: Great views
text: The hotel is on Wilshire Boulevard, but the main entrance is actually on Seventh Street. To enter the hotel, you come in at ground level and take express elevators to the 70th floor sky lobby with beautiful views of the L.A. Car valet is $42/day, the staff are very friendly. Check in was quick and easy. Room is modern and clean, but the shower does not have a handheld and water pressure is light. Nice room view, but the windows are very dirty. I guess it's hard or costly to clean the windows outside. It is located minutes walking distance from Target, Starbucks, tons of restaurants and venues. Very good hotel in downtown.

author: Kirkpatrickorion
title: Wonderful hotel
text: I’ll make it short. Very nice hotel. Lobby on 70th floor room was on the 64th floor. Awesome view. The service was really nice. Hotel is new, elegant but also trendy and hip. My wife and I got up-graded as it was our first time and we were only staying for one night. Room was biggish and very clean and neat. One of the best hotels in LA by far. Great location near LA Live.

author: daithieoin
title: Fantastically beautiful hotel finish, but service a little cold
text: So the Intercontinental Los Angeles Downtown has been open for four months now, and it is build and furnished to a high standard. However the building is startling to a regular traveller and a little confusing on arrival, which is compounded by the “Uber cool” yet “freezing cold” customer service on offer. I know hotels; I work in them and stay in them a lot, I can naturally find my way around a hotel as they generally follow a common sense plan. This place bamboozled me and every staff member made me feel uncomfortable and awkward about this in my interactions with them, all with the exception of Denys a sweet young man who did my check out. Reception is accessed by high tech smart lifts on the 70th floor, bedrooms are all below it via other equally smart lifts... but to get in and out you need to go up and down to reception etc. It’s almost as if they don’t want you to leave the building. A great hotel for one night in LA for a Morrissey gig at Hollywood Bowl, but would I want to be based here for two days or more? Probably not as I would need a warm jacket to survive the arctic breeze of service and interaction.

author: 129sylvies
title: The in-place to be at the moment
text: The minute you arrive at this magnificent building, you know you are in for a treat. The lobby of the hotel is on the 70th floor, which offers breathtaking views of Los Angeles. LAPD choppers fly close by, so close that the pilot waives at you. La Boucherie, on the 71st floor, offers a memorable refined experience in French cuisine, and the roof top bar on the 73rd floor is unlike any other rooftop bar. Our room was spacious, beautiful, and offered views of the Hollywood mountains. Service was impeccable. Having to switch elevators to go up and down is the price you pay for staying in such a remarkable building, and phone service can be spotty, especially in the higher floors. I wished the fitness center had been opened so I could have enjoyed it. Overall, a splendid visit.

author: AndyB728
title: Incredible Views!
text: I spent 5 nights at this new hotel and it was very, very nice. The staff was wonderful and very attentive. The check in and check out process was very quick and smooth. The room was very nice and was on the corner so that I had a spectacular view of the city as well as out towards the Hollywood Sign and Griffith Park Observatory. The outside of the windows were filthy though, so that made the view not quite as nice as it otherwise might have been. The room had a king sized bed, and all of the other types of things that one would expect like a desk and chair, etc... The bathroom was very nice and I really appreciated the amount of glass and having a separate walk in shower and as well as a tub. I would highly recommend this hotel.

author: RFk900
title: Interesting Intercontinental
text: New modern high rise office building hotel combination in downtown LA. Ground floor consists of a coffee shop and sitting/gathering area with an outdoor plaza. Main lobby, check in on the 70th floor with stunning LA basin views. All elevator transfers are on this Lobby level. For instance my room was on 55th floor, requiring a trip to the 70th floor to visit the amazing 73rd floor outdoor bar. Elevators have NO controls inside, you chose your destination floor on the panel in the vestibule. Room comfort and amenities AAA+++. The finish construction quality, wall covering, paint is some of the best I have seen. Hi Tech room features require inserting your access key card into the power control adjacent to the lighting controls.

author: yellowsunsun
title: Wow!!
text: Wow! What a beautiful hotel! Lobby is on 70th floor lol so if you don't like heights, this hotel is not for you. Staff was phenomenal :) Room was beautiful and fancy :) which I love! Plenty of restaurants and bars to choose from. Hotel is in great location close to LA live, just a short uber drive. Would definitely recommend. Was a lovely stay and comfy bed. Enjoy!

author: matauh
title: Good place to stay in the city center
text: The check in is on the 70th floor unlike other places where it is on the entry level. Rooms are all below this floor. New hotel with a good view of the city. Good attempt at room automation but not very user friendly. Crowed rooftop bar. Have to wait in queue for entry which is a bit of an irritant. The maintenance seems to be little poor even though the hotel is new. The wash basin had a water block which has made me give this property only a four star rating.

author: BobPhibbs
title: Their Elevator System Is A Deal-Killer For More Than One Night
text: I wanted to love this hotel. I saw the WG being built and thought the views would be amazing. They are. Unfortunately the crazy elevator system of having to go up to the lobby on the 70th floor, cross over to a new set of elevators to go down to my room on the 35th each time keeps me from recommending it. It's a new property so furnishings were all clean and great. Abundance of staff at the first floor to guide people and in the lobby was helpful but I stayed 4 days and found any time I thought of going out - and having to do all that extra work to get to the street - made me think twice. On the last day I did find out there is an additional set of elevators on the 31st floor that can take you straight to the street but unless you stay on that floor, you'd have to go up to the 70th first. Big miss. Big.

author: JoleneH218
title: Stellar Hotel
text: This is a grand hotel in every sense. The staff is fantastic! They are so helpful and pleasant. The rooms are comfortable and luxe. The only thing that was a bit confusing was the elevators.. you must take particular elevators to the lobby and another set of elevators for your room and then one particular elevator for the restaurants and rooftop lounge. Other than that everything is great. Oh except that the building does sway a bit but that's for safety and it being earthquake proof (that's a good thing in LA)!

author: noturkey
title: ..La Boucherie on 71
text: If I could give 6 stars I would, This place has to be the best ive ever eaten at, the decor amazing, apparently its Marie Antoinette meets Cowboy very elegantly done, muted colors , very detailed, everywhere you look including the silverware pink or black/grey, Everything ties in the attention to detail is amazing,even the music is detailed, mood changing music as the night wears on., We were welcomed by the manager Aloyes , very friendly charming, best window seat in the place, he made a couple of recommendations for dinner and told us to sit back relax and enjoy whats coming, We certainly did Aloyes, thank you. Joaquin our waiter was super friendly, on top of everything, he anticipated our needs, very experienced and friendly, Phillip , charcutier introduced out platter of delicious cheeses and cold cuts. Loved the wild pig ham, "the pig that loved rolling down the hill that he did it all day" Frogs legs, giant shrimp very well presented in rich broths, the piece de resistance was the tomahawk cut prime rib aged 42 days to perfection melted in my mouth, huge, looked like it came from a dinosaur i thought a very nice touch Joaquin brought out a selection of steak knives to choose the one you prefer,(your weapon of choice?)also very nice touch, a large selection of mustard to choose from, must have been at least 16-20, the lobster, one of the largest ive had very tender, then the perfect dessert, |Flambeed table side Joaquin performed a fire act over this baked Alaska style banana and cake , i normally dont eat dessert, this one I did, delicious, Chef Alessndro came to the table and chatted , a great Spanish import, loved his creations. Matthew the sommalier was super knowledgeable about every wine you can imagine and very interesting and funny person to talk to. The view of course is spectacular, we watched it go dark over dinner, all the way to the pacific, Downtown looks very different from above. Overall a great restaurant a fine dining experience , the rooftop bar, the Spire 73, open air musicand drinks and view of course. Be sure to check out both mens rooms, you literally urinate on the glass window overlooking downtown, A big thank you to all the staff that made us so very welcome, a memorable evening. Good luck,

author: bethliew
title: Beautiful Hotel
text: A relatively brand new hotel with great city view (almost 360 degree view) from the hotel lobby on the 70th floor!!! Our room as big and the bed was so comfortable. Plus the management surprised us with a bottle of wine and chocolate dessert to celebrate our 20th wedding anniversary which add a wonderful touch to our stay ( thank you guys!). It is very nice to have an evening cocktail at the lobby bar even though the service was not very good but it was still nice to sip my glass of wine with the surrounding city view. Wished the bar wasn't so bright though, so we can view the city better. Metro station is right opposite the hotel which made moving around LA very easy. Walking distance to Grand Central Market ( 15-20 mins walk), there is also a nice mall next door ( 3 mins walk) very convenient location. Overall we enjoyed our stay and hope to stay there again in the future.

author: ramogon
title: Amazing new hotel
text: Excellent service by everyone I interacted with. Large room and bathroom (with a tub!) and great amenities. Fun bar on 70th floor and the rooftop. Amazing views. Great steakhouse on the 71st floor. Unfortunate that steakhouse was closed on Monday. The whole elevator experience was not fun at all (having to move from elevator to elevator, going to 70th to then go down to 57th - very messy). VERY expensive valet service.

author: wocyee
title: Nice view and friendly to kids
text: I had a family trip stay at this hotel last week at LA. Their front desk is not professional to serve the customers. Concierge is very knowledge of LA city and give you excellent advice. I stayed up to 62 floor and the view is to city. Very nice view at night time and especially their club lounge, food quality and different kind of cultures food to provide to the customers. You also can sit their to work at the private room for meetings. The swimming is very clean and nice view, manager helped my kids to blow up the floating toys. Will definitely return to this hotel.

author: Nikon
title: Spectacular building and beautiful Hotel with some minor issues
text: Well, the building is spectacular. Frendly staff, beautiful lobby, beautiful and comfortable room. Great location if staying in downtown. I could give it 5 points but there are still some minor problems. The rooftop bar had a surprisingly slow (reallly really slow) service even with very few guests. Another issue is the bathroom. The bathroom itself is superb but if you need to go there in the night the bathroom light will lighten up the whole sleeping area of the room. The need to change elevators can be little bit annoying but that´s not a big issue.
