title: Great accommodation
text: Great accommodations! Clean, quiet, friendly staff and above all walking distance to great restaurants! Very nicely appointed. TV was great, WiFi was free and great. Air conditioner was QUIET and worked wonderfully. On staff's recommendation, dined at the Red Raven. WOW, EXCELLENT FOOD and service. Just a short block and a half from the Lodge. If your going to the Grand Canyon or just passing through and need accommodations, don't even think twice. Go to The Lodge on 66!

author: 0ut4Fun
title: We keep coming back and love it every time.
text: We recently went back to Williams to get out of the heat of the summer in Phoenix. We have had a lovely stay here before and this time was no different. The rooms and linens are crisp and nice. We stayed three nights and the maid service does an outstanding job. They have a great continental breakfast that is very busy when it opens at 7 am. Unless you're in a hurry, wait a little while and then go and enjoy. They have free wi-fi, but I noticed it was very slow, often disconnecting when their occupancy was high. It's within walking distance (a block or so) of downtown and a nice place to stay. Overall, highly recommend.

author: mrsoto
title: Best hotel in Williams, Arizona
text: We held a family gathering (50 souls strong) in Williams, Arizona. The Lodge on Route 66 was wonderful! We were visiting the Grand Canyon. Williams was the perfect staging point for our trip. The Lodge on Route 66 was newly remodeled, well kept and extremely comfortable. The staff was professional and friendly and catered to our every need--we felt welcomed. Not one member of our group had a problem. Several members of my extended family have vowed to return. There is nothing like a good night sleep in a comfortable bed followed by a complimentary continental breakfast in the morning. Thank you to the staff at The Lodge on Route 66 for making our stay enjoyable.

author: austin_autumn
title: Great spot in Williams!
text: This hotel was one of the highlights of our trip! The prices were very reasonable, the rooms were clean and nicely updated, the staff was friendly, the breakfast had a variety of choices and was tasty, and the overall atmosphere was very nice and relaxed. Our room was well furnished and quiet. I was worried I would hear a lot of commotion in the morning, as the parking lot is very close to the rooms. However, I didn't hear a thing! They also have a covered patio with lots of comfy chairs and some tables that are great for relaxing! The hotel is located about a block from downtown Williams. We were able to walk to dinner and shops, which was a great perk. You definitely don't want to miss this hotel!

author: 392hollyb
title: Suprisingly wonderful hotel in adorable, small town USA
text: My husband & I really enjoyed our recent visit to Williams, AZ. After doing a lot of research of the area, I was so pleased the reviews backed up the pleasure we found in The Lodge on Route 66. It was so wonderfully decorated, updated and serene. The bed was super comfortable and the room was clean & spacious! We appreciated the friendly staff, satisfying continental breakfast and location within walking distance of the train station and several restaurants & shops. We highly recommend this as your lodging destination when in the Williams are! I wish it was a chain so we could stay again elsewhere! Loved it!

author: Honeymooners014
title: Perfect stop-over to the Canyon
text: This motel style lodge is perfect as a stop over place between Vegas and the Grand Canyon. I found it by going on Trip Advisor and we weren't disappointed. Williams is such a traditional cute town with a lovely high street and a few western bars. In the evening at the end of the road they have wild west shoot out, which is well worth watching. This motel is excellently located on the main road through the town. The staff were very helpful and friendly and happy to recommend places to go, one being the Red Raven restaurant, which served delicious food. In the morning they leave out a lovely selection of breads, jam, waffles, fresh orange juice, fruit and pastries, which sets you up well for your hour drive to the South rim from here. I would definitely recommend this motel.

author: Touchous
title: Great, but not cheap.
text: The staff and accommodations, room 6, are equally nice. But really... a 50's style motor court in which you are dishing out WELL over 100. I know, it's a tourist trap - generated by the Grand Canyon traffic, it's summer and the city is small. We plan to avoid Williams in the future, but if you must stay and $$ isn't an issue, then by all means -- enjoy the cute setting, small - but nice - room. Enjoy the town stroll, restaurants and live entertainment, and by all means, enjoy the zip line! Cons: for the amt of money, the "free" breakfast could/should have been special. It was sparse and you would miss little if you skipped it.

author: 377JohnK
title: Skip this one
text: The only good thing about this motel is it's location. It is pretty much centrally located and within walking distance to all the tourist happenings. The rooms are tiny, if you are not careful I guaranty you will bang your knee on the bed post which sticks out beyond the mattress. Oh yes, I did twice, my wife did once. Amenities are practically non existent and the price is crazy. I have stayed at Holiday Inns, Hampton Inns etc. that didn't charge this much. I will not stay at this place again simply because I will not be going back to Williams again. The whole town has turned into nothing more than a tourist trap.

author: dkperreira
title: Guess I was expecting a little more for the price
text: We stayed here 1 night on the way to the Grand Canyon, end of May, 2013. The people at the front desk were very nice and gave us advice on where to eat,etc. We had dinner at the Red Raven, which was great & I would highly recommend it as the food was great & the place itself had great character. Our room was small(room named Oklahoma) as the bed took up most of the room, but it was clean & comfortable. The only complaint I have is the room was stuffy so it was hard for me to sleep & I would suggest they put fans in the room to circulate the air. The continental breakfast was good, making your own waffles was a nice surprise. We loved walking around the town on Route 66-there's a lot of shops & history here. I've never stayed here before so also don't have anything to compare it too.

author: JerryMast
title: Great little motel!!!!
text: Cute, cozy, clean and nicely redone. Office staff are friendly and efficient (she had all the paperwork neatly organized for the days check-in's). Rooms have the lodge theme on a small scale. Sleeping bags as extra blankets are a nice touch. Within walking distance to heart of Route 66 shops and diners. Williams is alive, glows at night with all of the neon lights. A great experience to revisit a piece of americana. Overall, very friendly town and proprietors seem geniunely happy to have visitors. Would definitely stay again at The Lodge again when returning to Williams.

author: Wagz1601
title: Clean, modern hotel with great character
text: Recently had the opportunity to stay at The Lodge on Route 66 in Williams, AZ. All I can say is, wow. The room looks to be recently updated with large, comfortable beds and lots of Southwestern U.S. furnishings, style, and charm throughout. The bedding, towels, carpet, etc. were all exceptionally clean. Extensive continental breakfast (with "make-your-own waffles") was also included. Very pleased. Will be my first choice on my next visit to Williams, AZ.

author: PamelaJReid
title: Worth Your Time and Money
text: Found this place on Tripadvisor....looks to be an old motel, but renovated. Price very reasonable at less than $100 a night for a queen room. The decor is awesome, we were pleasantly surprised! The dining area for the complimentary breakfast was great also! We really loved the place, and definitely would stay again! Very clean! Great decor! Stroll through this little town...it's worth your time!

author: FawnP_13
title: A Hidden Gem
text: At first glance you wouldn't think the Lodge on Route 66 was going to feel like a 5 star hotel. Once inside the room we were pleasantly surprised by how spacious and welcoming the room was. The queen suite has two VERY comfortable beds with luxurious linens and the living room was nicely appointed with comfy furniture and a pull out sofa. The kitchenette made it easy for us to have our snacks in the room and every thing was spotless! The pictures on their website don't do it justice! There were lots of restaurants to choose from within walking distance and the train to the Grand Canyon is only 3 blocks away. I would highly recommend the Lodge on Route 66 to anyone who wants a relaxing place to come home to after visiting the Canyon or just for a place to escape the heat! Thanks to the friendly and helpful staff for making our stay a wonderful experience!

author: Northslickers
title: Awesome beds, Excellent Location
text: We really enjoyed this hotel. The rooms were very nice with modern decor and very comfortable beds. The bathrooms were clean and had plenty of fresh towels. The breakfast was excellent with waffles, a good selection of yogurt, 3 kinds of bread for toasting and a wide variety of fruit. The location was great, within walking distance to downtown. The whole downtown is a 1960's Route 66 and western theme. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We would definitely stay here again.

author: Happy_Traveler_1970
title: A little gem!
text: Well worth the trip into town past the usual chain hotels. We loved this place. The service was really friendly. Great Value! Free wifi. Cont breakfast included. We would definitely return. As a bonus we woke to fresh snow.

author: issyluna
title: Great find!
text: Awesome experience! Stayed one night in the Chicago room which has a separate living room with a fireplace. There is also a cute bar height table with four chairs, fridge, and microwave. Bed was extremely comfortable. Room was very clean and well decorated. There are heaters/air conditioning in both rooms so it was easy to keep the temperature right. Located on the main drag so it was easy to walk to dinner. The internet worked well in the room and the hotel front desk staff was friendly. I would stay here again for sure.

author: BlakKat
title: Cool place to stay.
text: It's certainly not a cookie-cutter accommodation. The rooms have fun little bits of kitsch all over, and the furniture is not ordinary. Loved the touch with the sleeping bags as decor/extra warmth on the bed. Rooms feel small with the oversized beds, but it makes it cozy. We even managed with small children. Fixtures are all modern and average quality. Nothing special at the continental breakfast, but it's a good place to grab some snacks. It was nice to sit outside at night on the benches. Walking distance to anything in town. Favorite thing: the cute little door that hides the ice machine!

author: Rachelav
title: A little disappointed
text: We were on route to Grand Canyon and decided to spend one or two nights in Williams. It was January, low season, and almost every motel or hotel had vacancy. However we chose this motel because it was the first position in Tripadvisor. We're really disappointed. The room was tiny. We couldn't almost open our big suitcases. Besides, it wasn't clean at all; the quilt was really dirty so we couldn't use it although it was a very cold night. Breakfast was poorer than in other similar motels.

author: 4tomorrow
title: Very clean hotel and restaurant, with pleasant front desk clerks.
text: We stayed just one night in this hotel, and found it to be very pleasant. The room was quite small, but extremely clean and comfortable. The desk clerks were very accommodating and helpful. They helped us locate a nice restaurant for dinner, and helped arrange our train tickets to the Grand Canyon in advance, when I made the hotel reservation. The breakfast was nice and the dining area was very clean. The hotel is on the main street (Route 66) and in the center of town, making it very convenient to walk to the restaurants and shops. The parking is free, and it looked like it would be very nice to stay there in the spring and summer, as they have a covered patio with a fire pit and outdoor patio furniture to enjoy in the warm evenings. We were there when their was snow on the ground, so couldn't take advantage of the outdoor atmosphere.

author: DAYSX4
title: Williams is wonderful
text: We enjoyed our stay in Williams as a stop over on the way to the Grand Canyon. We booked in and went for a walk up the street which I highly recommend. The beds are comfy but the rooms are small. It is well refurbished but the bathroom is older in style and there is not much storage space. The motel is within easy walk of all points of interest. The continental breakfast was average and I would eat elsewhere if you have to pay extra. When going for a walk I highly recommend stopping in at the Pine Country motel for a slice of pie. We also had dinner at the Cruiser Cafe and they were cooking a BBQ which was also very tasty. It is a very quaint town and we enjoyed our little slice of Route 66.

author: Bex_K
title: Great Motel, Great town
text: I loved Williams. We had read about the train into the Grand Canyon, which was our purpose for stopping. The rooms were clean and tidy and beds were really comfortable. The Reception staff were really friendly and helpful. Breakfast was also good. It was on the Main Street, so just walked out of the Hotel to the Railway Station, and did a little window shopping along the way. I have to say Williams was the biggest surprise on this trip and I would love to go back and explore the area some more. It is at a really high altitude though, I did sometimes have problems catching my breath.

author: JW_1190
title: Good Clean Hotel
text: Our family of four stayed one night on our way from the north rim of the Grand Canyon to Las Vegas. Really clean and comfortable hotel on Route 66. Free parking right by your door. The complementary breakfast was very good as was the breakfast room. The fruit bread was excellent, it was clearly from a local bakery. The hotel is in a good location, you can stroll to the best places on Route 66, in Williams. The rooms are very good however with four people in them they are quite small. We would would however stay here again.

author: chicphx
title: The CLEANEST hotel ever!
text: I recently stayed at The Lodge on Route 66 as a surprise getaway for my birthday. The front desk clerk was very friendly, and when asked if there were any upgrades, she gave us a suite with NO hesitation. The "Chicago" room was the cutest little 'casita-type' room. BY FAR the CLEANEST room I have ever seen (I work for a world-wide hotel company AND have a cleaning business of my own). I tried looking for dust or something wrong with the room...I couldn't find anything! Great location in Williams and extremely convenient to the Grand Canyon Railroad. We didn't have utilize the free continental breakfast, but being in the hotel industry, I wanted to see what they offered. It seemed very nice. I cannot wait to return to The Lodge in the future.

author: AWLKLL
title: Comfortable Route 66 Motel
text: Stopped in Williams, AZ for 2 nights to ride the Train to Grand Canyon. The outside of the motel was a normal 50's era rest stop establishment, but the inside was a surprise. Very modern and well maintained room. Wonderful bed, flat screen TV, WIFI, and a great shower! Staff was very pleasant and informative. This motel is within walking distance to numerous world class eating establishments and the train depot. The wife and I loved the motel and Williams. We will return.

author: Kiwidreamer
title: Very Charming
text: We enjoyed our one night stay here on the way into the Grand Canyon. The town is very charming and worth a wander through - you can easily walk from the hotel into the heart of the town. The hotel itself is charming as well. The room was small but comfortable. Breakfast was one of the best we had in 3 weeks of touring - make your own waffles, yum. There is a laundry just diagonally across the road - can't see it from the hotel but ask at reception, they'll point it out to you. Plenty of dining options just down the road. All in all a very satisfactory stay for a reasonable price.

author: 0ut4Fun
title: Great stay!
text: Stayed at the Lodge for a three day getaway and had a wonderful time. They've done a very nice job of updating the motel. The beds were nice and comfortable, the bathroom had lots of towels and a gas fireplace as well. It was perfectly located in town within walking distance of all the shops and restaurants. They do have wireless (although their website doesn't mention it). They have a continental breakfast with the usual fare of breads and some pastries and also one of those waffle makers. They have a general seating area outside for gathering and lots of places to sit outside and watch the activity of town. We'll be back with a group of folks to enjoy the area and the motel again.

author: TerriA399
title: Great place for the family!
text: The Lodge was a perfect stop for our 1 night stay on our way to the Grand Canyon. We traveled with a family of 6. The room was clean & comfortable, with a very cozy decor. The furniture is a bit large for the space, but it served our needs very well (I'd much prefer 2 queen beds over 2 full beds any day). I must admit I would have not chosen this place, with its less than desirable curb appeal, if it wasn't for all the positive feedback from Trip Advisor; and yet again it did not disappoint! The staff was very friendly and helpful. And the continental breakfast was AWESOME! The kids loved it; especially the make-your-own Belgian waffles. I would highly recommend staying here to anyone.

author: katmcw
title: No wonder it's ranked #1.
text: We stayed here for 2 nights for our trip to the Grand Canyon. The room was very clean and nicely decorated. Big, heavy furniture (no generic furnishings) but watch your shins around the beds! Soft, comfy bed linens and good mattresses. We had a queen suite because no other rooms for 3 people were available, so it was a little more than we wanted to spend, but it was very nice. They have a pretty patio with tables surrounded by a liitle vegetable garden, so you can sit outside and enjoy the cool mountain air. There is a nice continental breakfast. The motel is within walking distance to the Grand Canyon railroad depot, as well as to restaurants and shops. We really enjoyed our stay here!

author: AlejandroAB
title: For the price is an excellent choice
text: It is cute and clean, classic and romantic in route 66. Rooms are small, but ok for a couple of nights. Good choice for route 66 and for visiting grand canyon. Breakfast was quite poor. Staff very friendly.... Just in front there is a coin laundry... For those long travellers. Visiting williams takes a couple of hours, therefore thos motel is for short stays.

author: TicketyBoo
title: Route 66 Motel with character
text: We stayed in this motel on route 66 for 1 night in April. It is a traditional American roadside motel which has been restored. It was full of character, and a pleasant change from the chain motels which are everywhere. Parking is in a central square with the rooms opening onto the parking lot. Our room was very small with little space for luggage or seating, although for 1 night stopover on the way to the Grand Canyon this was not an issue. It was clean and the high double bed was very comfortable. Breakfast was available in the small reception area and was adequate. The motel is located on the historic Route 66 and within a short walk of the diners and shops in Williams. Staff were very friendly and helpful. It was a pleasant stay and we would happily stay here again.

author: greer_girl33
title: 2nd time just as Awesome
text: This is the second time my husband and I have stayed here. Of course we got the same room because we love it so much. Room #1 the Santa Monica. It is a king suite/kitchenette. There are lots of complaints of the size of the rooms in this hotel, which seems to be its only downfall so if its avaliable spring for the suite. Its not that much more. Its so fabulous you may not want to leave your room and explore all Williams has to offer. Everything about this place is great, location, comfort, service. The beds are amazing you sink right in. It deserves to be a top rated hotel in Williams.

author: shutterbugshell
title: A true Gem!
text: We recently spent a night at the Lodge on Route 66 and from the moment we called to request an early check in until the time we check out we were pleased with everything! Sadaly the pictures I took were lost so I can't share those but what a gem of a place. The room are quite small, the room we were in was just big enough for two people. It was decorated with an outdoors theme and the bed was VERY comfortable! They provided nice organic soap and shampoo and a decent continental breakfast. The breakfast has a make your own waffle station, pasteries, cereal, yogurt and oatmeal.Not a hug selection but enough to please just about everyone. Perfect location right on the main street in town- and what a GREAT town, I can't wait to go back! Williams was the perfect palce to stay we only wish we had planned to stay longer. We will be back and we will stay at the Lodge on Route 66! Thank you for such a lovely stay!

author: adkandbeyond
title: A pleasant surprise in Williams
text: Why stay at a chain hotel when you have this gem in downtown Williams. We arrived late afternoon to a motel that had obviously be totally remodeld, just check the photo album in the lobby. The room had nice pillow top beds, and every nook and cranny was clean. The most enjoyable part of the stay was morning coffee under the covered porches and gazebo. It was very relaxing. The hotel was located on route 66, two blocks from everything in Williams. Continental breakfast was included. I'm glad that I took trip advisors advice and booked this motel. Other guests I spoke with were also impressed. Warning, watch your shins on the solid wooden beds.

author: DeborahnJack
title: Great Place to Stay
text: We stopped here on our way to the Grand Canyon. We made our reservations on line and everything went really well. This place has been completely remodeled and is just lovely. There is no closet, but since we didn't really unpack it was no problem for us. Our room was very clean and had a western theme. It was quiet and comfortable. Check in was quick and effecient. Our room was toward the back. Williams is a great town. It was fun walking around shopping and sight seeing.

author: toy4cannon
title: great value
text: We needed a place to just spend one night before taking the grand canyon rr the next day. We picked this due to excellent reviews posted here and were not disappointed. We got the cheapest room size which is indeed small but no problem for two people for a night. It was very clean and comfortable and quiet. There is hardly any traffic on this segment of 66 and the speed limit is about 20 so noise is not a problem here. The continental breakfast was a nice surprise as there was enough to keep us full for a few hours. The staff that we did meet were friendly and helpful. We will stay here again if we need a night in Williams. From the location of this lodge you can walk to about any restaurant in town.

author: R2K3
title: Great
text: What a wonderful place to stay in Williams! The owners are very nice and have a property that is pleasing & comfortable to all. We had 2 rooms for our group of 5 (my husband, me, our 21 yr old son and 2 of his friends) and we were VERY pleased with them and the cool parking lot patio. You can walk everywhere - shopping, dining and enjoy the Route 66 town. One thing that surprised me most was the bedding which is a big deal to my husband and me. The bed were very comfortable and we loved having SOFT SHEETS! We only stayed one night but we all wished we could spent more time there. The boys preferred this property over the Rim Cabin we had in the park the previous night. We will stay at The Lodge again and I tell everyone if you're going to the grand canyon - stay at The Lodge!

author: toastedmallow
title: Great base for sight-seeing.
text: Stayed here for 2 nights to take in the Grand Canyon railway trip and were not disappointed. The motel is right on Route 66 but no problem with road noise. The room was a bit small to try & fit 2 suitcases in and to negotiate around the very large bed. However overall it was spotless, nicely decorated and very comfortable, and we weren't in it for long periods of time. If so it might have been worth upgrading to the larger rooms. The continental breakfast was great with a wide choice and made for a very welcome start to the day. A great choice for anyone wishing to spend a few days in this area & we really liked Williams which is a characterful little town with a good choice of restaurants. All-in-all a great place to stay.

author: GermFreak
title: Somewhat overrated.....No privacy
text: I was super excited about staying at The Lodge. The girl was very nice when we checked in and gave recommendations for a restaurant Our room was room 3 - two queen suite. The room was very clean. The wooden bed frames are VERY large for the room - it would be easy to stub your toe so be careful! There is a road inches from the bathroom and kitchen windows but the noise was not bad. The beds were comfy. My major complaint is that we put up a "Do Not Disturb" sign but the maid came into our room and completely disregarded the sign and put it inside the room when she cleand!! I was appalled that someone would do this. Our personal items were handled and straightened. I would not stay here again just because of this one thing.

author: corinneg661
title: Great accomodation
text: We stayed at The Lodge 3 years ago and decided to try it again after comparing other hotels. We had only booked one night and decided prior to arriving that we would like a two night stay. They were more than accomodating changing our booking. Also, we had booked a double queen room but after viewing it we decided to upgrade to a suite (larger room). This decision wasn't based on the size of the room as it was a standard size but we wanted a little more room as we have a 3 year old son that needed some room to play. The rooms are clean and the continental breakfast has been upgraded since we were there last. The train whistles can be heard all night long but as all the hotels are along the tracks I don't think it would make a difference as to where you stay; you would hear them. We certainly would recommend it for a one or two night stop!

author: Fepeaux
title: Quaint Awesome Motel Made Our Gramd Canyon Visit Even Better!
text: The Lodge on Route 66 is GREAT! We stayed in Room #1 Santa Monica which is a King Suite in early April 2012 as our headquarters for 2 days of Grand Canyon visits. (First day we went with Marvelous Marv and second day on the train- both great!). Our suite is 2 separate rooms with a sleeper sofa, 2 chairs, huge flat screen tv, kitchenette w table and 4 chairs in 1 room, and then one step down thru french doors into a room w king bed (very comfy) and flatscreen and a double vanity sink separate from toilet and shower. Pullout sofa was great for our 9 yr old. You can walk to anything in Williams. Service is top notch. Contintental breakfast is just juice, coffee, & off the shelf pastries plus yogurts but a good start each day. We would stay here again in a heartbeat!!

author: ushela03
title: Nice cheaper alternative than staying at the grand canyon
text: Everything seemed nice... Big bed, clean room, new feel. However we just didn't sleep well. Don't know if the hotel is to blame as it was a one night stop. We stayed here and drove to the grand canyon, an hour long drive. Williams is a nice little route 66 town and you can walk anywhere from the lodge. We had a terrific dinner at the Red Raven. The grand canyon railroad begins its journey just down the street. One complaint: breakfast was carb heavy, prepackaged donuts and bread with a toaster. They can do better.

author: stlamc
title: Experience Much Lower than Reviews
text: The Lodge has some of the positive features as described by others, but next time we would definitely choose another hotel in the area. I think we got caught in a TripAdviser review trap. We stayed here (Williams) as a stopover between Grand Canyon and Las Vegas. Positives: homelike feel and nice theme to rooms/hotel, fluffy towels, easy parking (it's a motel), reasonable toiletries, friendly staff. Not so positive: *very* small (standard) rooms, beds too high and too soft (base seemed higher than middle or top, and we are fairly lightweight people!), minimalist breakfast (e.g., prepackaged muffins, styrofoam cups), heater/aircon was a bit too noisy even in "low" position, some sort of noisy fan/motor behind motel unit (not bathroom fan which is also noisy, but keeping bathroom door closed reduced noise a bit and noise was gone by morning). Also, internet didn't work -- wireless connected fine, but diagnostic analysis indicated that there was no internet response due to an internet service provider problem. We stated this to reception soon after arrival, but internet was still not working throughout evening and next morning. Internet did work at another location in Williams (i.e. not a computer problem).

author: MrsOrnay
title: Wonderful, wish we could have stayed longer!
text: We stayed in this hotel after riding the Grand Canyon Railway and wished we didn't have to leave in the morning! We stayed in a queen suite which had a small sitting room and small dining area with fridge and microwave. The room was very clean and there was enough space for my 20 month old son to play without being underfoot. The bed was really comfortable and cozy! The breakfast was your standard continental: fruit, cereal, pastries and donuts. The staff was very nice and made us feel right at home! I wish we could have stayed longer, THE place to stay if you are nearby. I am looking for reasons to plan a trip out there just so I can stay there again!

author: DWVL
title: So charming!
text: We loved our stay! The place looks like a 1950's motor lodge with a mission style flair. The owner checked us in and handed us our room key, yes, it was an actual key! The room was small but cozy, well appointed, and updated. It had the warmth and charm of an older room with the modern finishes that made it feel clean. Overall it was a fabulous stay. The only drawbacks would be small rooms with no closets, and they advertise free wifi but it is only available in the lobby or patio. Would definitely stay again!

author: haani808
title: Awesome hotel for Polar Express trip
text: Williams is a really small town and this was an excellent small hotel. I believe it is one of the pricier choices, but you get what you pay for here. We had a double queen room, decorated in the rustic decor. Everything was clean, new beds and the heater worked so well that we had to turn it down during the night. They offer a cold breakfast in the lobby and it was better than we thought, oatmeal, toast, muffins, donuts coffee, oj, yogurt. The staff were really nice and helped us with everything we needed. We were walking distance to the train station and all the shops in the main square. The same family owns the motel directly across from this hotel, it is called the Rodeway Inn The Downtowner Motel and is a bit cheaper to stay in but I'm not sure why.

author: trailersrfun
title: Grand Canyon Road Trip
text: We live in California & decided last minute to go on a road trip to the Grand Canyon. We had heard about Williams for other friends/family, so we decided to spend a night there. We booked The Lodge On Route 66 - it was so cosy we stayed the an extra night. It is warm, quiet (the walls a solid block!) and the service was great! An extra bonus is their breakfast in the morning - a great selection! The rate is reasonable. I would have liked to have stayed in their family room but it was already booked. The rooms are cosy, warm & inviting but a little tight on space! I will stay there again if I an going to the Grand Canyon, which is only 40-minute drive from Williams. Also check out my reviews on Bearzonia & The Polar Express (both in Williams)

author: mrsb060
title: Fantastic
text: Also stayed at the Lodge after reading reviews, had two rooms, the queen suite and a single room. The suite was great, roomy, separate livingroom/kitchen area. Very comfy as was the single room, though very small. The breakfast in the Cabana included fresh orange juice, yogurt, toast etc. The young lady at reception was very pleasant and helpful and checking in was a breeze. The Grand Canyon is less than an hour away; Williams is a wonderful place to stop enroute. Great little shops and places to eat. Would stay again without hesitation.

author: RichardT216
title: Great Modern Lodge
text: My wife and I stopped here for two nights as paert of our Route 66 honeymoon trip. We booked in advance which I think is recommended as this place gets very busy. The staff were very friendly. The room was clean and mdern. We had a queen room. We did find it very small. struggled to find room to open our suitcases etc. The complimentary breakfast is excellent. Great location if you are taking the Grand Canyon Railway like we did. Highly recommended just a shame about the room size.

author: jnjm
title: Great Place
text: Made reservation at The Lodge after reading Trip Advisor reviews and finding the price to be very reasonable and have to say we werent disappointed. Truthfully I was a little hesitant as we pulled into the area, because it was a "strip-style motel" with outside access doors. Unfortunately I guess I'm a bit spoiled by newer Courtyards & Best Western's. But this place more than met our needs and expectations. The staff/gentleman that checked us in was friendly, pleasant and helpful (& a great sense of humor!). Our particular room (king bed/regular room) was small but had everything we needed, furnished attractively and definitely clean and looking new. The continential breakfast was served on central outdoor patio - although we were up early and there was a bit of a chill in the air, so we ate in our rooms. But the idea, in warmer weather, was very inviting. We stayed here on our way into the Grand Canyon. Someday we hope to do a "Route 66" trip, and if we pass thru Williams again, would definitely stay here.

author: mjcSING
title: Best choice for staying overnight on way to Grand Canyon
text: This is a nice hotel. The rooms are very comfortable and well-appointed. The building itself shows its age but that doesn't take away from the modern rustic feel of the room. The beds are very comfortable and I sleep very well before an early start to the Grand Canyon. Williams itself is interesting. Get to dinner early or make reservations. The restaurants fill up quickly. We went to a bar in town and played pool with cowboys. Lots of fun.

author: McSwain
title: Nice and friendly Motel on Route 66
text: After checking Tripadvisor and other sites, we decided to stay at The Lodge On Route 66, Williams, after checking out Grand Canyon. We were not disappointed. We stayed in a room/suite called Newberry Springs (all rooms have names of landsmarks on Historic Route 66). We parked right outside our door. The motel is nice, clean, and is well run (by what it seems) a friendly and helpful couple that makes sure everything is in order. The room was big and clean, and everything was fine. Wi-fi signal a bit weak, but much better on the patio, and in the outdoor breakfast area. Breakfast was simple, but great: Pastries, bread, youghurts, and wrapped muffins and other sweet baked stuff, as well as coffeee and juice. I would deninitely stay there again, and it is ideal before or after av visit to Grand Canyon. We drove all the way from Williams to Santa Monica after our stay.

author: Mountain300
title: Nice place - Good Choice
text: Arrived in Vegas 18 Jul 11 and drove to the lodge via a quick diversion to check out the Hoover Dam. Easy location to find, Audrey checked us in to shamrock room 11. The room is small but for 2 nights it fitted the bill nicley. The top of the mattress may be 300 feet from the floor but you will definetly have a good nights sleep. Breakfast is continental style and can give you a high sugar rush if you are not selective on what you eat, but there is sufficient to set you up for the day. The outsdie central eating area is a good place to meet and chat to other travellers. We ate at the Red Raven which was recommended to us. Good service and great food, they will cook you a steak exactly to your requirements and if you like spicy food try the sausage & pasta.

author: DanioCal
title: Great location, beautiful room but a bit small.
text: We stayed 2 nights in mid-June 2011. The front desk person was very nice and informative. The location was prefect. Close to the all the shops and food but not right next to the noisy spots. The Albequerque room was beautiful. It's like spending the night in a model home but it was a bit too small for 2 big queen beds. You really have to be careful to not to bang your knees and shins on the beds and there's little room for luggage. I think it'd be fine for a single King but with 2 Queens, 2 big bags and some groceries it was a bit too tight. Having said that the staff was great and the room was generally very nice and a great deal. We'd definitely stay again next time.

author: Millard74
title: If you are near the Grand Canyon, this is the place to stay!
text: Booked the Lodge based on TripAdvisor reviews, and we were not disappointed one bit. Audry at the front desk was great, helpful, friendly, and effticient. We stayed in the Riverton room and it was clean, cute decor, modern tv and satellite. The bed was comfortable and had a Coleman sleeping bag as a comforter which fit in well with the fishing decor of the room. No in room telephones but didn't miss having one. Wi-fi available in the office and outside seating areas. Good breakfast bar outside in the cabana, it was a beautiful morning to sit outside and enjoy Gods creation. We took the train to the Grand Canyon and would recommend it, if you don't want to drive and if 3 hours is enough time at the rim. Great stay, would definitely return and would highly recommend to all. If you are one of the lucky ones, maybe the ice machine will talk to you☺

author: ladysheff
title: The perfect stay on historic Route 66
text: This hotel (motel) was recently renovated and was more than adequate. We were extremely comfortable during our stay and had no problems. The staff was very friendly and the room was clean and had all the necessities. It felt like you were staying in a guest bedroom of a friend or relative. Williams is small, of course, but you can walk to everything (restaurants, a sundown showdown, shops, etc) easily from this hotel. There is a coffee shop, with excellent java, directly across the street. We had an excellent time here. We would stay here again, without a doubt, and highly recommend to friends and family.

author: gonicki
title: Fantastic Value!
text: What a great little hotel! The rooms are beautiful (may have been cleaner than our apartment!)--nothing "motel" about it. Everyone who mentions in their review about how comfy the beds are ain't lying, either. We had very little interaction with the staff, which was fine. We checked in without a hitch. We stayed 2 nights--exploring the town on the first evening (didn't take long). The next day we took the train to the Grand Canyon and had a nice dinner back in Williams. Then got up at the crack of dawn on the third day and headed home. This is the perfect amount of time to spend in Williams--a quick little road trip on the last little perfect stretch of Route 66. Go see Larry King and his Country Legends show at the Sultana Theater if you get a chance!

author: marilynjoy
title: Our Williams Experience!
text: We were on our big roadtrip driving Route66 , and decided spend a couple of days in Williams, to go to the Grand Canyon. We read about The Lodge, here on TA! We were very pleased with our suite!! So beautiful and extremely comfortable. We had the added enjoyment of a snowy day, and loved sitting in our room , toastie and warm watching the snowflakes fall! (May) A real novelty for us, as we are Aussies and don't see a lot of snow. The rooms are a surprise, as the outside looks just like any other motel, but inside very clean a tastefully furnished. This motel was a highlite of our trip! Oh and the couple that manage The Lodge were very helpful and friendly too, thank you!

author: Andymt
title: A true GEM on Route 66
text: We loved everything about the Lodge on Route 66 - location, rooms, staff, breakfast. We stayed in RM 12 and it was great - it didn't have lots of space but it was lovely, clean and comfortable. The Lodge was really relaxing, in a great location on Route 66. We loved walking out to at night to find some where to eat and wandering around all the shops in Williams! It is just a short drive to the Grand Canyon - we were so glad we based our selves in Williams and at the lodge on route 66. We didn't want to leave! We had no problems with the wi fi either! We plan to return with our family soon. If you are doing Route 66 then stopping here is a must! If you are just visiting Williams then this is the place to stay.

author: gracielufreebush
title: Very comfortable night sleep and clean
text: I stayed here 2 nights the staff were super nice, very clean and oh my gosh the beds were amazingly comfortable after hiking in sedona 2 days before i went to williams. They have wifi on the grounds. The coffee across the street is not good i dont recommend it. the hotel had a great outdoor party place to sit and chat and grills to cook out. The town is charming. The only thing i did not like was the heat/air unit is not temperature degree monitored but old fashioned wall unit low,med and high and in a very awkard place very close to the bed and hard to get to. I would stay there again for sure. This town has no nightlife though but a great place to stay if you are visiting the grand canyon about 45 min to an hour drive

author: westcoastgal35
title: Amazing Lodge - Amazing Town
text: It was like we stepped back in time being in Williams and at the Lodge on 66. We had read all the good reviews and chose to stay at this motel. I booked the cheapest room that they had and it was wonderful. Check in was smooth and the clerk was very helpful. Our room was fully renovated and was gorgeous albeit a bit small. It was also imaculate which was great. There was a wonderful courtyard in the parking lot that had lots of seating, a gas fireplace on either end and lots of patio heaters. Although the weather wasn't great the combo of patio heaters anf the fire allowed us to have drinks on the patio and enjoy the comings and goings of Williams. It was a great way to end a day of touring the Grand Canyon and I would highly recommend this Lodge to anyone.

author: tjbeaches
title: Tasteful and convenient
text: We stayed in a King suite here and loved that we could park in front of our room. The room itself was very tastefully decorated and cozy. The beds were big and comfortable. The heating was very hot and we turned off the one in the bedroom. The owners are friendly and available. The included continental breakfast was simple and adequate, but I would take it to your room to eat since it is a very small breakfast area. Looking around Williams, this seems like the best bet for a stay. It is centrally located so we could walk to restaurants, the train and cute shops.

author: desertdescover
title: Would hold it's own in a much bigger city
text: We spent one night here in January and we're very impressed. I usually avoid motels, but the reviews on trip advisor convinced me to try. We weren't disappointed. The motel was very well done on the outside, and the interior was tastefully appointed. The furniture was good quality and aesthetically pleasing, as well as the decor. The bed was thick and comfy, and covered with high quality sheets. In the evening, our friends and I spent hours out on the patio. They had patio heaters, gas fireplaces, and string lights for ambience. The only thing that could have been better would have to be the breakfast. Is was okay, but pretty plain.

author: StarJade
title: Best hotel room of our entire trip!
text: We stayed here two nights to break the journey from Las Vegas to Page. We had room 10, the Amarillo room. Expensive for a motel (same rate as we paid in the Bellagio in Las Vegas) but well worth it for the comfort. I was suffering with a bad back at the time and this was the only room of our entire trip with chairs and a sofa in which I could sit comfortably for hours at a stretch, Indeed, the sofa was so comfortable I wanted to take it home! Our room consisted of a sitting room with large sofa, an armchair, small dining table and chairs and a kitchenette; and a bedroom with kingsize bed, two really comfortable swivel armchairs and a large bathroom leading off. The bathroom consisted of outer room with large tub, his and hers basins, separate toilet and a large walk-in shower. My only criticism would be that, in common with many American motels, the heating/air-conditioning was very noisy. The bed was very high off the ground but once you climbed in it was extremely comfortable. About 100 yds from the motel we found the Red Raven restaurant which I would highly recommend for dinner. We also found several native American jewellry shops nearby which were well worth a visit.

author: teafour2
title: A warm welcome
text: Due to a car problem that day we arrived extremely late to check in at the motel, but after phoning ahead we'd spoke to a lovely lady on the check in desk who was very reassuring and true to her word, we got a warm welcome and no problems when we eventually arrived. It looks like a traditional all american road side motel from the outside, helped out by the group of touring bikers who had stopped off on the same night as us. The room was a little small but had everything we needed. It was very clean and looked as if it had recently been made over so felt quite modern. Breakfast was served in the gazebo located in the middle of the courtyard by the owner - toast muffins, fruit and coffee. The place had a very family-run feel, and the staff were all lovely. Sadly we didn't have enough time to see the rest of Williams as we had a tight schedule to keep to. A few minor criticisms were that the wifi only worked as far as the gazebo (and not in-room) and there weren't really any amenities to speak of (such as a laundrette). but if you're after a clean room for the night, a good breakfast and a warm welcome then this is a lovely place to stay.

author: Lady_Road_Warrior
title: Enjoyable Stay
text: We planned to travel the Arizona portion of Route 66 from Williams to Oatman and wanted to find a place close by to stay so we could start the trip in the morning. After spending a lot of time looking at options with very mixed reviews we chose this one and have no regrets. Yes, the rooms are very small but they are clean, modern and comfortable. The location is great; within walking distance to just about everything. The morning continental breakfast was adequate, not special, but that was just fine with us. The hotel rates are good for this area and we were told they also own the Rodeway Downtowner across the street which looked pretty good, too. (Don't confuse it with the other Rodeway!) We were going to eat at Cruizers but it was too hot, full of flies and the menu was way overpriced for a burger joint. Instead we ate at the Red Raven and could not have been happier.

author: BillB1948
title: Great Visit
text: We were assigned an handicap room for whatever reason. Room would have been a little difficult for someone in a wheel chair, but overall we had a great stay. \ Hotel is in easy walking distance of nearly everything you want to see. Great restaurants and shops. The room was clean, very nicely furnished. Owners and staff were great. Breakfast was basic but served in a nice gazebo area with fireplaces and heaters. Great place to hang out in the cool mornings, or even sit in the evenings. Overall It was a great place to stay.

author: leticiateliz
title: Do not hesitate to book this motel!
text: My husband and I stayed here for one night during our trip to the Grand Canyon from Las Vegas. Very charming, beautiful room. The staff were very very friendly and helpful. The location is great. Everything was extremely clean. My husband loved the fact that they had satellite tv! The only thing we would comment on is that there are no phones in the rooms, we wanted to call a few local places to ask some questions and we couldn't find a phone so we had to use our cell phones. I would definitely recommend this motel to friends, worth the money!!

author: ClareGoWest
title: Clean, neat and close to everything!
text: This is an adorable small motel. The staff was very attentive. We stayed in a Single Queen Room. It was small, but no smaller than expected, comfy, clean, and neat. The Lodge is located within walking distance of everything. The continental breakfast was perfect for us. It included cereal, fruit, toast, drinks, and yogurt. JD’s Espresso is directly across the street if you want more than coffee to start your morning. We would definitely stay again!

author: no1nanaCa
title: Little Gem
text: What a great place!!! I wish that more old motor lodges would be saved and remodeled. WOW!! We were in Williams to enjoy our grandkids on the Polar Express and decided to spoil ourselves and stayed here at The Lodge. When we checked in we were upgraded to a suite, thank you...... It was very clean and comfortable!! We will definately stay here again.... Just one question, where is the phone???

author: rjnet
title: Charming
text: We booked a trip to do the Polar Express train ride with our 2 little boys. We canceled the over-priced and over-hyped hotel package that comes with the train tickets, and decided to just get the tickets and stay at the lodge. The accommodations were great! And the morning continental breakfast was perfect - the kids had oatmeal and we got our morning coffee. We stayed in a suite - which allowed enough room to sleep and let the kids play a bit, too. Our cousins and their kids stayed next door, and it worked perfectly. The staff was very helpful - even had the pull-out bed made for us after I called and said we'd be getting in very late. The lodge is a great "mom-and-pop" stay, that fits perfectly with Williams.

author: Weave2u
title: Best on the route 66
text: This is by far the best accomodations on Route 66, Williams AZ. The room was superb, with very nice appointments. It was great because it was so quiet. They really sound proof their rooms. The staff were terrific and quick to help out their guests. I read a review about the small towels, LOL... and they are, but they are just the standard towels you find in most hotels... they do give several of them though. I highly recommend this hotel if you are in the Grand Canyon area.

author: versejer2911tim
title: What a great find!
text: My wife and I stayed here for two nights during our 25th wedding anniversary trip. We had spent three nights staying at the Paris in Vegas, and were rather diappointed with our stay there. When we got to The Lodge, we were instantly more comforatble. We stayed in the St. Louis room and were so amazed at how cozy and comfortable it was. We loved the decor and were delighted by the warm hospitality shown us by Rob & Carol. The morning breakfast was nice out under the central pavillion, while we looked at the picture album of how the Lodge was renovated from its former state of disprepair. There are some cool things to see and do in Williams and if with the Grand Canyon only 50 minutes away, and Sedona about 40 minutes, this place is a great choice. We would difinitely stay here again and will be recommending The Lodge On Route 66 to all of our friends who travel west.

author: elephantsyeah
title: Loved Staying Here - Cleanliness, Comfort & Friendly Staff
text: After determining to do things on the cheap in the US & have more money to eat well my mum, dad & I arrived late afternoon in williams - very nice little town - chosen for it's location (1hr drive to grand canyon & 1hr to sedona). we scooted around looking at some of the other motels in town, which had good prices but didn't compare with the room standard here - newly decorated, big comfortable beds...and very friendly lady at the front desk (i think she was the owner/manager & the gent there i guessed was her husband). the room cost a little more than we had planned on spending, but we were all tired from a lot of travelling & wanted something we could enjoy relaxing in as we were staying for 3 nights - and they gave us a good deal :-) i think i just read someone scoffing at the term 'luxury' in ref to this motel, but we saw it as a nice little treat & it's cleanliness, the fact that the rooms looked like they'd just been redecorated, the wooden-cabin look of the place, the solid, comfey furniture were in great contrast to everything else we saw in town (i think we checked out about 5-6 other places which were cheaper but a bit on the shabby side) - i personally prefer this family-run kind of atmosphere to the 5 star tack which is not what i imagine one would be looking for if staying in williams.... a simple breakfast was included - which was fine for us - just enough to get us through till we went out for our filling all-american pancakes bonanza! really loved it & have no hesitation in recommending the place - hope to return one day! P.S. - there's now a great restaurant - apparently new - in town, which we only managed to go to once due to our excursion schedule....the Red Raven - lovely food!!! we were sorry not to have been able to eat there every night - but i guess 9pm closing is pretty usual in most small towns in the US. & the kind gentleman called 'chuck' at the photo shop was first-class at helping me burn a disc with all my holiday pic's & films for a very reasonable price :-)

author: WesternModern
title: Vintage Motor Court, Done Up Right
text: We stayed here for one night in October of '08. We had room #5-"Seligman"- which has a single queen bed. When you compare it to a chain motel, the room could be considered small,but it was still PLENTY big for two people, decorated in a "Pottery Barn" style, and was very clean. The bathroom, which IS of good size, was spotless! The friendly manager as a plus. After dinner,we were sitting in front of the patio fireplace and she came over and chatted with us for a while. We like her a lot. Since we had an early start the next morning, we can't report on the breakfast. Next time.

author: SeychellesDream
title: Nice Hotel
text: Positives: Friendly front office staff. Clean room/bathroom. Spacious room with 2 double beds and a pull out couch. Easy to find location and relatively close to the Grand Canyon. Not so postives: Had issue with shower initially, but was resolved. We had to leave by 6 am, so were not able to get breakfast. Early option not offered. Over priced.

author: Realfamilyvalues
title: Cute, comfy, a pleasant place to stay.
text: We pulled into a rustic atmosphere welcoming experience, went into the front desk and spoke with the gal in the front she was very friendly, we had booked rooms for our group and had to change two of our rooms from a two night stay to a one night stay, no problem no charge just a nice smile and a thankyou. We recieved actual keys for our rooms, opened our door to the Kingman and it was very cozy, felt like i was in at a small cutely decorated apt. Kitchenette, microwave dinette set, electric fireplace, two tv's. Large king size bed, nice sheets felt like 600 thread count. Nice romantic lighting option also french doors seperating the livingroom and the bedroom was a nice plus, so when my husband woke up he could watch tv while I slept very convient. Our friends stayed in the flaggstaff, quite happy , two queen beds and cozy feeling also. The newberry springs ins really nice for a family two queen beds and a hideabed will sleep 6 comfortably. One other thing I would like to point out It is definetly motorcycle friendly you can park right outside your room and if you smoke there are nice benches right out side of each room to ad to your comfort. Definately would recomend.

author: BuddAZ
title: Great find ....
text: We stayed here on 5/20/08, and found it to be delightful. We had a Queen suite, which basically consisted of two of the original rooms. The living area had a sofa bed, dining table for two, TV, micro, refridge, separate freezer ... a very large countertop area (maybe for more kitchen type expansion?) ... the bedroom had a queen bed, and very large bath area. Overall, we loved it ! There were a few "quirkey" things, like no ice machine, but did get it from their sister motel across the street, so we did not "suffer". We would recommend this motel .. have fun !

author: sarena_c
title: Wonderful place in a beautiful small town
text: This place is a gem. We stayed in the Queen Suite. It was very well appointed with a very comfortable bed, a small but useful fridge and microwave. We used the sofa bed as well and it wasn't bad at all. This place really made our trip because while it had a higher level of comfort - it also celebrated the area with it's decor. The central breakfast area is a fun way to meet the other guests (most of them were children while we were there because of the Polar Express). The staff was very friendly and helpful as well. There is nothing that I would change!

author: kathiPDX
title: Great find!
text: We stayed a couple of nights at The Lodge on Route 66 in October and loved the charm of this motel. It doesn't look like much on the outside but the inside of the rooms have been completely remodeled and were quite cute. We stayed in a single room for $79 a night which is a bit less than the Quality Inn's we stayed at getting down there but this motel was much nicer!! The room is kind of small but it's really all we needed. The only complaints we had is that there isn't a closet so the only place to hang your clothes is on a few hooks in the bathroom and the heater is quite loud. The free breakfast leaves something to be desired but that was typical for all the free breakfasts we had along the way except for the B&B we stayed at in Sedona. The motel provides easy access to the Grand Canyon and is at the center of things downtown. We would stay here again.

author: TravelingJen
title: Best Motor Lodge on Route 66
text: My husband and I stayed here for two nights recently in a single room with one queen bed. We arrived much earlier than expected as the pouring rain ruined our plans to walk around town first. The staff was nice enough to check us in and welcome us regardless. As others have said, the single, non-suite rooms are really tiny. However, our room was spotless and well-maintained. The bed was super comfy. There is certainly some noise from being right on the main drag but, we figured that was part of the Route 66 ambiance. Overall, it was everything we need for a quick stay. It definitely appears to be the best of the motor lodges right on the Route. Would stay there again in a heartbeat!

author: Monisia
title: Great Place to Stay in Williams... Very Nice & Clean
text: We were occupying a single room with 2 queen beds. We spent here 1 night on our way from the Grand Canyon. The place has been very nice and room was extremely clean. It also looked like it has been remodeled recently. Rooms are a little bit small but cozy. There was not much of extra space but it was enough for us. A complimentary breakfast was very good. The motel is also within walking distance to all shops, bars and restaurants. Highly recommended.

author: VeryRarelyVacation
title: Good Experience Overall
text: My husband, I and our toddler stayed here our first night in Williams. This place is very clean, upscale for a motel!! The problem was that the room we stayed in was very small for a family. We had 2 queen size beds and it was cramped, especially for a family of 2+1. My husband kept calling it "the closet". They also have suites that were not available at the time and those are beautiful. I would recommend this place for families only if the suites were available, but this place is perfect for couples!! Great time overall and would stay here again!!!

author: werberzicke
title: great stay
text: we had a great one-night stay in this little motel, after hiking in the grand canyon. the room was nicely decorated, everything was clean, not really spacious, but ok. breakfast was served in a seating area in the middle of the parking lot, with two fireplaces - nice! if you need to stay in williams - do not hesitate to book this motel. its really good. the only thing we really missed: a hairdryer! btw: rods steakhouse is just across the street - but we weren't that impressed with the food or the service. it was just ok.

author: kjjones
title: Clean, cute, convenient
text: We were very pleased with our stay here. Rooms were very clean, comfortable beds, ,all new bathroom fixtures, very clean, did I mention it was clean? We booked a Queen room which didn't have a lot of extra space, but there was enough room for what we needed, which was a quick night's stay after touring the Grand Canyon. Note that there are no phones in the rooms. Short walk to all restaurants and shops in town was nice. The breakfast is served outside in the covered patio, coffee, tea, juices, yogurts, danish, granola bars, fruit, etc. Was good to fight off early morning hunger. There is some train traffic overnight, but it was nice to hear and rather nostalgic, being on historic route 66. Overall, we thought the accomodations were the highlight of the stay in Williams, would definitely stay here again and recommend it to anyone traveling through the area. Great place!

author: eurotourist75
title: Lots of character at affordable prices
text: We were 2 occupying a single room with a queen bed. There wasn't much space but it was enough for us. The style of the room was at 4-star level, with solid wood furniture, nice decorations, and travertine tiles in the bathroom. There were no coffee making facilities and the hair dryer is provided upon request. It was nice to stay downtown in lovely Wiliams and feel the atmosphere of Route 66 at walking distance to all shops, bars and restaurants. The hotel is not on the road facing the railway but one block behind it, so trains were not too noisy and there weren't too many anyway. Continental breakfast in the pavilion was ok but we like Starbuck's style coffees and we found them at Java Coffee Cycle which also has internet access. For dinner we had good quality bbq meat at funky Cruiser's Cafe'. Both these places are just a short walk from the hotel, on the main road.

author: desertrat2
title: A lovely last stop on our trip
text: Williams was the last stop after a nine day loop through Texas and New Mexico and we were very happy to find a lovely room in a lovely town. Williams is quite historic and is the Gateway to the Grand Canyon. The Lodge is completely renovated and is nicely located. We stayed in a suite with a king bed including a nice sized bathroom. There was a large refrigerator and a microwave next to a kitchen counter, but, oddly, no sink. The nice part was the car was parked right outside the room and we didn’t have far to drag all our luggage into the room- a real bonus for a trip’s end. We ate dinner at a new Italian restaurant, Donna Bella, and had a lovely meal. The only down side was the continental breakfast was not served until 8 and we were long gone by then.

author: JuliG1
title: Great accommodations!
text: We stayed at the Lodge on Route 66 at the end of March for three nights. I was extremely pleased with our stay there. My son and I stayed in the suite. It was immaculate and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was very spacious and the living room/kitchen had a refrigerator and a microwave. The only thing missing that would have been beneficial would have been to a closet. Nice decor! I felt very comfortable there. I was a little disappointed that the fireplaces in the plaza were not in use while we were there. Complimentary breakfast was okay.

author: Scenic40219634267
title: Tired 3* accommodation
text: This is a very well located block of apartments with great access to the slopes and very convenient ski lockers. HOWEVER it is very tired, in need of redecoration, and not staffed all the time. We arrived at noon just after reception had closed. A 'phone number was provided to call for out of hours assistance, but the man who answered said we simply had to wait until 4pm and there were no other options. Once we gained access to the apartment we found it was very compact. Fine for just two of us, but it was advertised to sleep seven which would have been very cramped. The extractor fans in the kitchen and bathrooms did not work, so cooking smells lingered, and bathrooms steamed up. One bathroom ceiling was covered in black mould. The TV did not work and the WiFi did not support Apple devices (odd...) Overall it is in need of a bit of TLC

author: 777markd777
title: Great access to slopes, ski lockers, beds and rooms
text: Came for a long weekend. Access was easy even though were late - keys in locker just outside the sliding doors. The lifts are good and the rooms clean with good beds and locker space plus good clean linen. Showers were ok - water not really warm enough. Cooking was easy. There is a supermarket about 50m up the street which is good. The view was awesome from the window (see picture). Heating was ok, not brilliant and the TV didn’t work until a service man came to fix it a day later. It is only 100 m from the ski lift and is virtually ski in and out with 2 ski hire shops right next door which is great. So overall one of the most convenient places I have stayed to ski - recommend.

author: 506nadjaf
title: Nice, clean apartment close to the piste
text: A good place for a family, group of friends or a couple. Friendly staff that is helpful enough. The reception isn't open 24/7 but it was easy enough to check out by dropping the key in a key box. No bread service any longer (has been described in previous reviews) They call it ski in/out but you'll need to walk 50-100m to get to the closest slope/chair lift. An easy walk though. We didn't pay extra to get a view so our window faced a small road, a drag lift and a steep tree littered part of the mountain. Not bad but maybe a bit claustrophobicIt. It could be worth paying for the view.

author: /undefined
title: Good basic accommodation close to slopes
text: Our third visit to these apartments and no real change since 2006. Decent accommodation but could do with redecoration as a little dated/worn now. Reception is not open noon-5pm mon-fri, but is open 8-8 sat. We arrived at 12.10 on a Friday and were expecting a 5 hour wait, but a kind female receptionist saw us waiting and came out with our key immediately. Very helpful reception staff.Tourist tax to pay on arrival was 60 euros (5 adults 8nights). Also the safe is not free (15 euros per week). Beds are very hard and pillows very soft but excellent room heating.Ski set hire shop next door and apartments boot lockers are downstairs.High level south facing rooms are the best for views and sun.Close to foret slopes and lifts and only a short walk to funicular to access the forum area. Shops also a short walk away.Free bus stop outside which gives access to top of resort.All in all a reasonable apartment in a good location.

author: Merbau
title: Decent Accomodation in Excellent location with Great Staff
text: Stayed here towards the end of March, and booked via a third party app. The Positives: Excellent location, 2 mins from the Ski Lift, and equally near shops and the Forum Reception Staff were excellent, v friendly, helpful, they were a real asset. Apartments appeared to be well equipped, (we didn't cook, but it looked fine) WiFi worked Good Storage Ski storage rooms in the basement, good size and worked well. 2 Ski Shops next door They were also kind enough to offer Late Check Out without any extra costs The Negatives: Our apartment really wasn't very clean, not terrible, but definitely not hotel standard. Also, at the end of your stay you're expected to tidy and clean. That wasn't a problem, as it's a basic clean, but as per the above, I do wonder how much cleaning happens after you check out. Maybe that was bad luck on our part? To conclude, It's not quite as nice as the photos look, but all in all, was pretty happy with our choice, and would stay again.

author: rachelp995
title: Great value self-catering apartment a stone's throw from the piste
text: Stayed here with a 4-person family in a 6-7 person apartment with a view across the valley. This was a great choice. The apartments are not as spacious or luxurious as the online photos but good enough for a holiday where you're out all day. Particularly good = flexibility to add extra time at start and end of the trip - good if you want to catch a few more hours on the slopes. Lovely reception staff. Good range of kitchen goods - although no oven. Supermarket a few steps down the road. Would I stay there again? Definitely

author: /undefined
title: Very enjoyable last-minute stay!
text: We are a family of three and we were on a driving holiday. We booked two nights here while on the road and got an excellent deal. The accommodation was relatively easy to find; we were met by a friendly and helpful receptionist, who, without being asked, upgraded us to a spacious sixth floor apartment with a stupendous view of the mountains. The apartment could sleep six (!) and was very well kitted out. The apartment block is situated in a pleasant valley with other blocks and a range of facilities (shops, cafes, restaurants, play areas, etc) within easy walking distance. There are also good walks from the accommodation, as well as a cable car up to breathtaking views of Mont Blanc and the Grand Massif. Overall, very difficult to fault this accommodation for a short stay like ours; or for a longer holiday. PT&A from Devon, UK

author: dmlatham
title: The Alps in Summer - for a good price
text: The place is sound - nice keen staff, decent accommodation. The building's not pretty from the outside - blame the architect. But the high valley it's set in is superb. 5000 feet up - already higher than Ben Nevis fellow Brits - and it was still glorious Summer, T shirt weather for walks outside and it looked like young kids get lots of fun activities. You can walk in a couple of hours (I'm a not especially fit 50 something) up to 8000 feet and there's a vision of Mont Blanc, eternal snow up to 15000 feet. Awesome. Or shorter walks get you at sunset looking West at views so beautiful I should have stayed and starved rather than come home after the trip. Lots of lovely villages and towns within easy driving distance, though it's the same winding road for the first half hour to get to them. We had a wonderful two weeks. And...glorious Summer is out of season for a ski resort so the price was very good.

author: MikeA24
title: Weeks Easter ski holiday with family
text: Booked with Sunweb and had a great time. Everything was just as described and was ready for us on our arrival. Ok the apartments are a bit tired and maybe could do with some upgrades and refurbishment but everything was spotlessly clean and serviceable. The apartment was a good size and the kitchen adaquate. For the price paid it was excellent value and I would return. Staff were very friendly and helpful. The apartment was very warmth lots of hot water unlike some places I have stayed while skiing. Our friends stayed at the Hellios Pierre et Vacances Premium which was plush and had leisure facilities. This hotel was much nicer in decor etc but was considerably more expensive.

author: Carve_the_Piste
title: Enjoyable Ski Base
text: Stayed here during 3rd week in March, with Crystal Ski. Accommodation much better than anticipated. Check-in really smooth thanks to Margot's professional attitude. As we'd arrived very early we were informed the room wasn't ready which we expected but they texted to say when it was. Apartment was set up for 5 which for 2 of us was very spacious - a wee treat compared to what we've endured in past years. Big sitting area, small kitchen but more than adequate, separate toilet, bathroom, good shower, plenty of hot water, spacious bedroom, beds a little hard but perfectly comfortable, tons of shelf, hanging and storage space. For skiers, apartment complex has the best boot/ski locker system I've ever encountered - in the basement each apartment has a big locker with enough room for all skis and sticks and a boot heater. Walk out the boot room and onto the street for a short 70m walk to the pistes. Easy access to all the major runs from this point. All-in-all, a very comfortable place to stay and would certainly consider returning.

author: walterf570
title: Great top apartment, great beds, great views
text: We stayed in this place last week (3rd week March) with fam with two kids (10/12) and payed a bit extra to get a top floor apartment. It was definitively worth it: the views were fantastic. The furniture in the place is nothing special, but the beds were great, and that's is important. The main lifts (starting with a little baby 'magic carpet') were about 100m away. The kitchen was well equipped (dishwasher, microwave, coffeemaker). The living room was nice and big enough. Staff were friendly and helpful. 15 meters from the main entrance is a lift to Flaine Forum, with plenty eateries. Tip: Go down to Flaine forum for shopping (Sherpa) as the Spar in Flaine Foret is very expensive.

author: lazygit
title: Perfect
text: Stayed here for 2 nights last weekend. There was 4 of us in a 2 bed apartment, sleeps 6/7. If there was 6/7 of us then maybe this review wouldn't be so good but as there was only 4 then it was perfect. After reading mixed reviews we weren't sure what to expect but being 4 blokes we weren't too bothered as we knew we were going to be close to the slopes and we had a bed for the 2 nights and for the price we paid we weren't expecting too much. The apartment had a toilet, a shower and toilet, a bathroom, a bedroom with 2 single beds, a bedroom with one double bed and a living room come kitchen/diner with 2 sofas which could sleep 3. A nice large table with 6 chairs and all the bits and pieces you would expect in a kitchen minus a cooker. You could go round with a fine tooth comb and find fault like a little crack in the ceiling and a bit of paint chipped on the skirting boards but in general the apartment was clean, plenty big enough for 4 blokes, nice lockers for skis and heated boots and a nice balcony with nice views and great location. All 4 of us were very impressed and we would not hesitate to stay here again if we ever return to Flaine.

author: RichC591
title: Great accommodation and location
text: Having stayed at the Veret next door a couple of times, I am so glad we changed to the Foret ,superior in so many ways. The ski lockers are dry warm and well lit, the accommodation is of better quality with TV ,towels included, a welcome pack ,comfortable beds ,with the sofa bed a proper bed. Free basic wifi which we found adequate without having to pay for the upgrade (much to the disgust of our teenager) The location is great for both lift to the forum just across the road and close enough to the Bissac slope that my kids had no problems skiing to the door of the ski lockers. A few maintainance issues like a broken microwave ,missing kitchen cabinet door and ill fitting hob which we didn't report till last day as the hob still worked fine and we managed without microwave. 5 minutes after reporting these a nice polite gentleman replaced microwave and began addressing other issues. Reception staff were also very helpful and there is locked storage for cases should you arrive before 5pm check in, if your room is ready earlier they text you to let you know. As to the review from Amsterdam Suzie if it was you that was causing the noise above us keeping the kids awake then I'm glad you got fined, this isn't a hen do Travelodge! We have booked again for next year 😀

author: T2945GGpaulh
title: Staff rude.
text: Stayed here over new year. So many issues with the place. Phone broken. Wireless not working. Poor instructions. No staff during check in. Staff were rude when complained. Staff incompetant. The list goes on. Would strongly recommend against this place.

author: 769kateh
title: Perfect for a ski weekend or longer
text: The 2 bedroomed apartments are very comfortable and spacious although it might be tight with 7 people. It was great to have 1 bathroom and 1 shower room with WC and a separate WC. The double bed was a decent size too, more like an oversized double, not like other P&V places where we have stayed where only 1 normal sized person can fit on the bed. There were plentiful towels and sheets, lots of hot water and the residence was very handy for the slopes being only 100m away from the Grand Vans chair on the same level and where you can also purchase your ski pass. It is all opposite the 24 hr funicular that takes you down to the main village where most of the shops etc are located. Each 2 bedroomed apartment has 2 lockers in the ski room, one for skis and the other with heated boot racks. The WIFI set up was confusing as there are 2, one which is free and one which is a paid for service. I think you need to click the grey box when signing in to get the free version. I wish the residence provided a bakery service at reception like other P&V residences and a couple of extra keys would have been good but overall I would recommend these apartments if you are coming to Flaine.

author: 320debraw
title: Clean and comfortable apartment, perfect for a base for skiing
text: Our room was clean and warm, and the beds were very comfortable. The kitchen and bathroom were in pretty good condition. So we didn't have any problems with maintenance that other reviewers seem to have experienced. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Some of our group could not get WiFi to work all week - not a problem to us as we didn't want it, but if you needed to keep an eye on work it would be difficult. The location is fabulous; just a short walk to the lift. This was our first time in Flaine and it was a lovely ski area with plenty for all of our family to enjoy. Lunchtime restaurants were not cheap, but not extortionate either - London prices really. Drinks were probably the biggest expense at meal times. It was an excellent holiday and we will be likely to return.

author: Hi-Qs
title: Excellent location, good base for great skiing.
text: We've stayed here during numerous February half terms since 2009. Good clean(ish) appartments. Nice warm boot rooms although, like most similar places, they can get congested first thing in the morning. Very close to ski school meeting points so perfect for groups/families with novice/improving skiers.
