Easy access from slopes so you can pop back for lunch etc. Close to shops and lift down to Flaine forum. We prefer south facing rooms but have stayed in north facing room once - ok but missed having balcony. Don't know about parking as when we've driven there we've stayed next door where there is an underground car park and pool. We love Flaine and these apartments are fine if you're wanting a good base for a great skiing holiday (shame there's no pool).

author: bobtbell
title: As it says on the tin
text: Everything is fine. It's a good choice. We had 3 adults and a nipper in an apartment for 6/7 so we had plenty of room. Well- equipped apartment and having a shop/bar/restaurant in the block was a godsend in dodgy weather conditions. The wifi is rubbish don't bother - just buy half hours from the local networks - they usually work. As is the case in many ski resorts the 'après' can be a little noisy and the double-glazing in the apartments doesn't offer enough sound insulation. Reception staff are helpful and the ski store rooms are the best I have come across. Flaine is certainly not very scenic or a retail heaven - but the snow is OK and very accessible. Trips further down the 'Grand Massif' are great fun. Yes it's a good well-functioning family ski destination and La Residence will not disappoint.

author: JonnyM779
title: Perfectly acceptable for the pricepoint but looking tired on the inside.
text: "Does what it says on the tin" pretty much sums this place up. Reception staff are helpful but you can't help but feel you're being slightly ripped off for some things (having to pay to use the safe that's already in the apartment, paying to store your bags, the choice to pay an extra 100EUR for a south facing apartment etc.). The apartments are of good quality although the paintwork is looking tired and they could do with some new furniture. Well equipped kitchens which are rare in these kinds of places. Good location but it is by no means ski in - ski out (100m walk to the lifts along a road). Well situated for access to Flaine forum via use of the lift. Interesting set up with the "in house" "supermarket / pizzeria" on the ground floor. One of the girls working there needs a personality transplant, while the other is very pleasant. Don't expect there to be a limitless supply of pastries in the morning and be prepared to wait a while for a coffee. Overall, had a pleasant stay in comfortable accommodation, but I certainly wouldn't pay anymore than I did for it.

author: W3469XDjamesk
title: Family Ski
text: Good accommodation, comfortably near to the slopes. Very helpful staff. Not disappointed. Recommend it. However Wi Fi is poor. We have stayed at this location twice, both of which had stunning South Facing Views. On the last occasion we were on the 5th floor. Balcony included on both visits.

author: Wayne070
title: A lovely place to stay and right next to the slopes
text: Just spent a week at Residence La Foret for our first family ski trip. The staff were friendly and welcoming and the accommodation was perfect for a ski holiday with everything you need after a long day on the slopes. We had a one bedroom apartment which was spacious and fine for my family of five. The apartments are right next to the slopes and the snow was great as most reviews suggested and the variety of ski runs was excellent for all levels. I am very pleased that we picked Flaine for our first family ski holiday and also that we stayed at Residence La Foret and with Pierre Vacances. There are in my opinion some pretty unfair reviews about these apartments. They offer good quality and well priced family accommodation right next to the slopes. We had such a good time that we are already planning to head back to Flaine and to stay at Residence La Foret next year.

author: Jamboys
title: Fantastic
text: This was my third time in flaine. On the other occasions we stayed in the hotel beside this...Madame vacance terrasse de veret. There is no comparison. This hotel and its facilities are far superior. Better equipped and more comfortable rooms, with English tv and wifi in rooms if required. Last, but be no means least, a fantastic heated ski/locker room. Not the dreaded nightmare of the hotel next door!! Heaven!! With 3 kids, who needs that stress on top of getting everyone out in military precision!!

author: GarethA135
title: Great facilities, great location, very little noise
text: Stayed at the Residence La Foret last week, and I must say I was very pleasantly surprised. We were in a two bedroom fourth floor apartment which was listed as being for up to 7 people, we had 4 adults and it was very comfortable, any more and it would have been a squeeze but these places always come up small so if you're booking remember to look at the layout of the accommodation. The apartment itself was clean, well looked after and well appointed, the addition of a filter coffee machine being very welcome. The facilities within the building were excellent; we had two ski lockers, one for boots and one for skis/boards, and there's direct access to Skiset, a small market and the local pizzeria from the lobby. Twinner is right next to the ski room exit too. The building is two or three minutes walk from the Grand Vans lift, making it very easy to get up the hill in the morning, it is directly above two bars; The Flying Dutchman and the Diamant Noir, we were aware of noise coming from the Dutchman on one of the evenings however it wasn't enough to keep us awake, a friend on the 3rd floor reported the same level of dull background noise emanating from the bars below, he didn't have any trouble sleeping either. Overall it was an excellent stay, my only complaint is that the wifi was a little flaky at peak times, if I'm paying EUR15 for the privilege I expect the internet connection to be up to the task. Flaine itself has excellent skiing/boarding for all levels, the bowl offers fantastic on and off piste opportunities. It was our second visit there as a group and we had just as much fun this time as last.

author: CharlotteM605
title: Great location close to the slopes, tidy and functional
text: We went on a last minute break before Christmas to take advantage of great early-season snow. booked direct with P&V which saves loads on standard UK prices. This residence does what it saysnearer time - near the slopes, clean and tidy, with ski hire in the building. The shop and restaurant cater for a captive audience with breathtaking prices. It's almost cheaper to eat on the slopes than self-cater. Good selection of games kept the children occupied. Flaine is a good fun, family friendly resort, with great snow records and stunning views of Mont Blanc. Some of the buildings are spectacularly ugly, but the views from them are often breathtaking. Would go again.

author: Matt2525
title: Amazingly convenient
text: Decent size, clean apartment. Modern + well furnished. Said it slept 7 but I think 6 would be pushing it! Location great (lots of snow so ski'd 100m down the road to the pistes in the morning and walked back at the end of the day. Ski hire (Skiset) in the building - access door next to reception. Supermarket - in the building - access the other side of reception (fresh bread every morning without going outside!) Cafe / Pizza restaurant - again - accessed from reception corridor Ski lockers on lower floor included boot warmers and easy access to street to get to skiing. Ski lift 100m away is a fast chair to the centre of the Grand Massif. Only downside was wifi. 15 euros a week would be ok but it was slow and connections seemed limited (+ required a log on every time it was used). Overall - great for a long weekend or cheap week.

author: CanucksAbroad62
title: Good Family Holiday
text: Well located P & V hotel just steps from the meeting point of the ski schools. We took the 2 bedroom apartment for 1 week in early Janaury. The rooms were basic but adequate and fairly decent for a P & V. Our 3 children all under age 12 fit comfortably in one of the double rooms although the 2 sofas in the living room can also be used. One thing that did bother us was the noise form the pub downstairs. We wanted a south facing room and paid a bit more but all that was left was the one 2 floors above the pub. The noise on the weekend was loud but it was fine the other days. Next time we will try a higher floor. Flaine is not the prettiest resort in the Alps but the snow which eveyone comes for did not disappoint!

author: AndyP000
title: Location, Convenience, Good Price- what else do you need
text: P&V is only about 100m from one of the two main lift areas in Flaine and has a easily accessible ski and boot locker area in the basement area, which is conveniently also at street level for an easy walk in. P&V is on the upper of the two main levels in the middle part of Flaine but is right opposite the lift down to the lower level with the larger number of shops. The reception is not always open during the day in the week, but they left our info available for us to pick up anyway so we could still get into the room. The rooms are fine and our studio appt easily fitted 4 with lots of storage and a decent sized kitchen. There is a small market in the main foyer area (so you can easily nip down for your morning bread), and a SkiSet ski shop also accessible from the foyer, which will give a 20 disc if you are staying at P&V. Other shops are about 200m down the road. Don't bother looking for the pool - apparently closed for 2 years so far over an argument about the heating bill. The Flying Dutchman pub is directly below one wing of the hotel, but we heard nothing at night from this - possibly the steep prices put off anyone from going out. You can buy some beer in the market for a fraction of the price and hang out on the balcony for "almost" the same pub experience...

author: MidlandsJules
title: great location
text: The apartments are spacious and situated in a great location opposite the lift down into flaine forum. Just a short walk to the supermarket, bakery, butchers take away outlet,there is also a small shop in the apartment block as well. Only a 5 min walk to meet the ski school lift pass office chair lift ect.You could ski in and out if enough snow. We stayed in a 2 bedroomed apartment which had 1 double room 1 twin room and the lounge area made up into extra beds there was 2 bathrooms and i seprate toilet. Kitchen was well equiped 4 cooking rings microwave but no oven. Plenty of pots/pans and crockery. There is a ski room on site and next door is a ski hire shop very conveinent. The ski school also hold there presentation in the reception area at the end of the week.

author: Salyt141
title: Stunning hotel in a hip part of Sydney
text: Stunning hotel with high-end quirky decor. If you love something a bit different this is the hotel for you. Unusual decor, fabulous high ceilings with all original windows and walls. Spacious bedroom with open bathroom and seperate toilet and walk in shower. Everything is a bit left of centre but still delivers what a great hotel should. Right next to Spice Alley and a dozen of various restaurants. A great hotel with impeccable service. We will be back for sure.

author: RealDS
title: Rustic
text: Possibly one of the nicest hotels I’ve stayed in asthetically & service wise. The managers were thoughtful enough to have left a cute memoir regarding my work travels and being away from my dog. They also left some dog toys for me to bring home to my dog. I found the gesture rather overwhelming. It’s in the heart of chopping ham and you can literally get to most places easily. Bondi Beach is a 20 minute drive. Sydney Harbour is 2 stops away from Central station. I’d definitely recommend staying here if you’re going to Sydney

author: azmagicmountain19
title: Amazing find!
text: I booked this hotel looking for a place with a bit of character for our overnight stay in Sydney to attend a theatre show. Wow, it delivered and more! Our 6 year old daughter was truly fascinated by the many crops around the hotel - the detail is just amazing! I felt like a tourist in this hotel. This hotel has been so well done, keeping so much of its character. We loved it! The roof top pool was also a massive hit, almost had the whole place to ourselves. So reasonably priced, such beautiful character, amazing location with so many eateries at your doorstep. We will be returning if we ever need to stay in Sydney. ✔️ ✔️ ✔️

author: lord_splat
title: This is what a Sydney hotel stay should be...
text: Fantastic sympathetic refurbishment of the old site, with patches of exposed brick and wooden beams that make the rooms more interesting, along with the hilarious fake stained carpet in (what was formerly) the Clare Hotel. Regrettably, I’m old enough to remember the real thing. The already sizeable entry level O’Connell room was made to feel even more so by the double height ceilings. The glass fronted shower wasn’t an issue for me, staying solo, but may imagine it to be so if you were sharing with someone who wasn’t Scandinavian... Fantastic breakfast - spanner crab XO omelette had to be the best breakfast dish ever - across the way, but it got busy, even immediately on opening on Christmas Day. Pool was a bonus for an inner city hotel, but the surrounding building meant that it was in shade by the early afternoon. And cold. But thankfully only open to hotel guests. Great staff, willing to do that bit extra.

author: Sambasing
title: Great location!
text: Hi I was in Syndey only for 2 nights. I took at taxi from the airport to the hotel. My taxi driver had some issues trying to find the hotel as it is located in a small lane. But we finally managed to locate it. It is a small boutique hotel with great amenities. It has a great location and you have access to a great choice of restaurants as soon as you step outside. The service was good, the rooms were clean. A bit expensive, but worth it- as it gives you the freedom to decide what you want to eat and where you want to drink, due to its location. Cheers mate! Amit ------------

author: catherinepW8919MU
title: A Real Treasure
text: What a wonderful hotel!!!!! Every staff member we met was oustanding and extremely friendly and helpful. The room was super with divine beds - quality linen, duvet and pillows. Loved the industrial features - lamp, lights etc Beautiful toiletries. Nespresso coffee machine, jug and a bar fridge (drinks and snacks avaialble for purchase). A truely unique hotel. Location is perfect - spoilt for choice with numerous amazing eating and drinking venues on the doorstep (literally on your doorstep). Definitely a hotel to return to - looking forward to July. Thanks for a wonderful stay.

author: Mobile535340
title: Loved It
text: Hubby and I enjoyed our stay at Old Clair. Great location....walked from central station. Heaps of great restuarants near by, shopping if u want. We spent hours by the rooftop pool.... very relaxing. Staff were lovely... hotel clean...comfy bed...huge bath...retro feel. We will come back.

author: 687zoer
title: Beautiful rooms & great location
text: We love to stay somewhere a bit ‘different’ and the renovated Old Clare is really lovely! Our room was very spacious with a super comfy bed and bathtub in the room. Bar downstairs also did great cocktails! Can be a little bit tricky to find, took us a couple of drives around the street until we figured it out but not an issue. Only small thing was the room service ... called down in the morning to order some breakfast for the two of us. Asked for scrambled eggs with avocado & bacon, and poached eggs with bacon. We received literally 1 scrambled egg and 1 poached egg, 1 slice of toast, avo but no bacon at all. Obviously something got confused along the way and they missed the whole second order AND the bacon but we got over it and had a laugh about it later! Would definitely stay here again in the future though!

author: AMSully
title: Brilliant
text: I was attending a conference at Sydney University for a few days. I was staying on my own and this hotel was perfect. Fantastic service in the hotel. A great room. Great bar down stairs. Right next to Spice Alley (my new favourite place to eat in the area). Walking distance to UTS and Sydney Uni. I would definitely stay again.

author: Macgillthegreat
title: Nice to be back
text: New restaurants. Barzaari and A1 are both phenomenal. Food are fresh and delightfully delicious. Kudos to A1 with their uniquely lically produced green juices. Nice to be back in this vibrant part of Sydney. I love the quirky stylish but traditional style of The Old Clare. New faces at reception. Renato always look after us with the perfect amenities and our favourite Abercrombie room. My partner and I really enjoyed our stay in this hotel while in Sydney. Looking forward next year to experience the rooftop bar.

author: Agro1799
title: Mr Grahamme McDougall
text: Well what a find???? We drove past and thought was a dump, then we remembered the reviews and didn’t realize it was heritage listed till we went inside. Concierge was superb, very helpful carried our bags, parked the car and showed us to reception into reception. Reception lovely young lady. Explained the heritage parts of hotel. The hotel has great ambience, great choice of beer and all original. The rooms well appointed and well equipped. Checking out same concierge again helpful and courteous. Receptionist again very helpful and friendly. We will be back.

author: BaconXXX
title: Great unique hotel with much charm
text: We were very lucky to have 2 upgrades to two very unique suites. The first was a very large room that was an original room that was admin area of Carlton and United Brewery many years' ago. One whole wall was like a museum of shelves behind glass featuring a history of bottles and glasses in the original wooden joinery etc. The bed was enormous, as was the TV. Very large bathroom with freestanding bath, and large shower room. Alas this room was right on Kensington Street a very noisy street at night and especially Friday and Sunday nights. We couldn't sleep and the hotel was sympathetic - moving us to a loft room on the other side of the building - and this was perfect in every way. Helping us through all of this was a very helpful person at front desk - Charlie (Thank you!)

author: RonWamberal
title: The ultimate in design and style
text: Unless you absolutely have to be in the CBD, this is the place to be. Have loved the area since I first stayed but it has grown and changed over the years; now the area includes a multitude of eateries around Kensington Street and Spice Alley, retail and theatre at Central Park and White Rabbit is only a few metres away. The Old Clare itself is THE place to stay if you have the slightest interest in style and design - each room is spacious comfortable, design focussed and has its own art and character. The overall hotel has so many fascinating artifacts and is almost an art gallery in its own right. While I love most of the rooms , the only one I would avoid is the Chippendale Loft which is upstairs downstairs with a few steps to traverse. Appreciated the upgrade to the Mary O'Shea suite which is fascinating both for the space and design and the history of Mary O'Shea who was one of Chippendale's characters - worth googling to better understand what Chippendale was like before it became such a fashionable area. This suite is perfect whether you are enjoying a foodie few days at Automata and A1 Canteen or needing a room that will also assist with business - luxurious and practical with a stylish separate room for meetings. The hotel has a wonderful roof top pool although it is perhaps a bit too early to fully enjoy - Sydney at the weekend still had some elements of winter so dining at A1 had more interest than a cold swim.

author: jessied558
title: Beautiful Hotel!!
text: My husband and I stayed here for the weekend for our anniversary. The staff were so friendly and accommodating. We stayed in the Chippendale Loft which was gorgeous, very stylish decor. We were surprised to find an Instant Polaroid camera in the room for us to use with film which was just great, a beautiful touch to help us remember our stay. Great central location it wasn’t too far in a taxi or an Uber to get to where we wanted to go. Very pleased with the whole weekend! We will most certainly be back. Thank you to all the staff who helped make our stay so memorable, a special thanks to the man that worked in the bar (we didn’t get his name) who went out of his way to make our drinks when a cocktail my husband wanted wasn’t on the menu he did his absolute best to recreate it for him which was just so nice! :)

author: wendy77BB
title: Good location for universities , good service
text: We stayed here for 2 nights and enjoyed our stay. The entrance is hard to find and not signed - the only entrance from the main street is the bar, but the hotel entrance is actually round the corner in the side street. The staff are excellent, very friendly and helpful. We stayed in a loft room, which is in fact 2 stories with steep stairs connecting the rooms. The decor is unusual with old machinery as decorations, and quite spartan. However the bed is very comfortable, and the shower is hard to leave - excellent! Room service was excellent, and not expensive. The food was really delicious. It was expensive even on special, but I'd stay there again. Short walk to Central Station.

author: d-tsianakas
title: Hotel experience
text: Staying at the Old Clare is kind of a hotel experience. The hotel is probably the hottest kid in town right now, urban style, minimal aproach with a smell of 50’s-60s, a design paradise. The room we stayed was actually a small apartment! You could sleep, rest, work or even have a meeting! We loved everything about this hotel, friendly staff, excellent location, ultra clean, it really uplifted our stay! You can also enjoy breakfast or a late glass of wine in the beautiful restaurant in the ground floor. Old Clare is not at all old, in fact it is the newest “in” hotel one can imagine in Sydney! Very stylish, very New York(ish), but with the light of the Aussie sun! Definitely recommend!!

author: juliamorris2018
title: I must say this
text: I became sick with stomach bug on the 19 hour flight to Sydney. Upon checking in, the staff noticed my illness and promptly offered to call a physician for me. During my 4 night stay, they constantly checked on me, offering any and every bit of help they could. They offered to fetch the scrips, chicken and rice soup, and always asked me how I was feeling. When 2 days went by and I was not better, they made an appointment at a local clinic so that I could get iv fluid. On the last day, I was quite down, and renalto, the awesome reception manager, had the chef make me 2 types of juices to help get my strength back. He then refused to charge me for it! I will never forget the kindness of the concierge, bellmen, and of course Renalto! This is what a hotel SHOULD be like:) Thanks again everyone!

author: madchester76
title: Chic boutique hotel in Chippendale
text: Have stayed at the Old Clare a number of times now and it does not disappoint. Rooms are lovely. Staff go above and beyond to make sure your stay is as perfect as possible. Best hotel beds in Sydney in my opinion. Food from room service was not only fast, it was delicious and not overly expensive. Fantastic location, close to everything. Am yet to use the roof top pool but hopefully will be back in the warmer months to check it out, it looks stunning. Thank you for taking such great care of us time after time!

author: murphy3692018
title: Exceptional
text: Was lucky enough to have my birthday celebration at the Old Clare. Was booked in for a night to enjoy the final night of Vivid. From the moment we arrived, every possible need and expectation was met and exceeded. From the warm welcome at the door to the reception, I was greeted with smile, and a lovely room upgrade was organised for me by Reynaldo on reception, as it was a special occasion for us. The room was breathtaking, and did not disappoint. Beautifully elegant, yet understated, with all comforts catered for, and the most magnificent the heritage feature of the room. We were so excited as to what the evening would hold. But not before being taken down to the Automata where a mouth watering Champagne was organised. Decided to stay for another night. Thank you Old Clare.

author: thisisgus
title: Beautiful hotels and room, poor checkout experience
text: Fantastic rooms - high ceilings, exposed brick, a big bath, beautifully furnished - great for a couples staycation in the city. Perfectly located next to Spice Alley food, and a short walk away from all public transport. The two let-downs for me were: 1) when you pre-authorise a booking (the cost of the room + $100 possible incidentals) on checkout, cancel the original transaction, and clearly itemise the transactions that you're making for the checkout (one was for the room, the other was for the restaurant bill). It will make it less confusing and a more seamless checkout experience for customers. 2) Please don't email me the next day with $20 of minibar charge that I did not make, and then not bother to explain how the mistake was made in the first place. I appreciate that you refunded me, but the charge should not have existed in the first place. So, all in all, definitely stay here if you like a nicely furnished and located hotel, just maybe take a photo of the minibar before you check out! Also - there is a little bit of street noise as some rooms are on a major road.

author: Brisbane_Catlady
title: Character hotel in a great area
text: I chose this hotel as it was an area of Sydney that I hadn’t stayed in previously. I was given a room on the ground floor. I liked the room, however as it was on the ground floor I did hear a bit of noise from the restaurant, and people leaving the bar. As others have mentioned, the bathroom is glass so it’s not ideal if you’re going with a friend, however I was staying on my own for business, so it wasn’t a problem. I love the design of the hotel, it’s such a refreshing change from the cookie cutter style hotels that lack character. The bar was great, it had the feeling of a traditional Aussie pub but modernised. The hotel is in a good area with lots of bars and restaurants in the vicinity. It’s also close to central station. All staff I encountered were friendly. I’ll definitely be back!

author: lis4068
title: Good, but not amazing
text: We stayed here for a conference weekend. Room was clean but very different to that pictured on website - they do say the rooms vary, however it was nothing like the one pictured on the website. The architecture of the Old Clare is beautiful, and position was handy. Bed was too soft for us so sleep wasn’t great - but each to their own. Finally the restaurant was average. We attended for breakfast 2 days in a row. Paid $18 for 1/2 an avo on 2 pieces of toast with butter. Personally the Old Clare didn’t live up to expectations and I was left disappointed. Had high hopes as it appeared so charming. Oh well.

author: EmilyH97214
title: Up and Coming Area, Friendly Staff, Comfy Beds
text: Spent 2 nights at The Old Clare in a double bed room on the second floor. Beds were incredibly comfortable and the room was fine but not high end as the price suggests. I really enjoyed the unique and fun branding of the hotel and their slogans throughout. Bathroom is all glass to make sure you are comfortable with your travel partner if sharing the room. The staff were wonderful and helpful. The leaf blower to clean the open air lobby every day was a bit annoying, could be heard clearly in my room. Bar gets packed at happy hour but it's worth it the drink list is all my favorites (mojito, margarita, aperol spritz). Area is very up and coming and near a very nice mall, lot's of restaurants and public transportation. Roof top pool is only good for laps or wadding, not very deep but with a nice view. Overall I enjoyed my stay.

author: MerchantAdventurer
title: What a joy to find!
text: I stayed at the Old Clare Hotel in Sydney while on work. I selected it at random as it was close (easy walking distance) to Central Station and close to where my business meetings were. What a serendipitous choice. The hotel is wonderful. The staff are brilliant, friendly and welcoming. The room was spacious, tasteful and included some wonderfully whimsical touches (such as the desk lamp made from a part of a motorcycle). Delicious breakfast and great coffee. Excellent location. On my list of top hotels for 2017 and 2018.

author: Madcooki
title: Fab hotel, wonderful district
text: Great Hotel...designed to integrate a former archetypal cnr Aussie pub, and the brewery next door. Beautiful restoration and detail. We stayed in the Clare Room...spacious, beautifully appointed, fun, groovy, special and well worth staying in. Rooftop pool is a really nice touch...gorgeous breakfast, great vibe overall. Rag and Bone Man UK...hand made the special industrial lamps...everything available for sale...and if the beds could be folded up and popped in luggage...I'd have been in like a robbers dog. The are Chippendale, is a newly regenerated inner city district...full of spirit, good restaurants, and fun bars...a must see area. Safe, fun, great vibe. A really fun weekend.

author: 1natashaw
title: Modern, chic and treny
text: Architecture buffs heaven and millennials delight. This modern, chic and trendy hotel is in a great location. Loved the architecture especially keeping the old brick parts of the former building and very trendy accessories. I thought it was a bit overpriced for what it was. I was upgraded to a loft room - lucky I did not have mobility issues as those stairs were steep and I would have preferred to have one level more spacious room as I did not really use the bottom area, preferring to sit on the bed. The bathroom was very modern but no free standing bath tub as advertised in all their photos. The lift was very slow to the third floor. The staff were Ok but not overly knowledgeable - when I asked about buses to the city the girl had no idea. Happy hour cocktails - well I have never seen such a small glass - very disappointing. The pool is very small.

author: in0uei
title: My favourite hotel
text: This is my third time to visit sydney and also my third time at the Old Clare. My partner and I are very fond of this hotel because of its character. Automata is always a standout especially Abigail, she's very professional but Kensington is no longer the same. The service and food quality is disintegrating. The reception is always alive and welcoming. Good to see rento and Martin. The amenity is a bit boring. Maybe you should change the portrait and substitute it with fruit or chocolate.

author: GeorgeT1588
title: Super amazing staf
text: Checked into the The Old Clare last week after a long flight from Buenos Aires, although they had made us aware of check in time they actually did take into consideration an early check in request if possible. When we arrived, Rento from front desk did his best to accommodate us since we were only there for one night and arrived exhausted and made it possible for us to have a room asap! Loved the flexibility and empathy he showed to us whereas in some hotels don’t care and make it easier for themselves to stick to schedule as is. That gesture alone really made our trip! Otherwise, location is fantastic. Breakfast took a little longer than expected to come so the gentleman serving us apologised and did not charge for it. There are many 5 star hotels anywhere you go but it is the people who make it what it is. Thank you so much for such a pleasant experience.

author: djheini
title: Nice boutique hotel
text: I stayed at the Old Clare for 2 weeks while in Sydney on a business trip. The location was convenient to my office, but would require a train ride or about a 30 minute walk to get to the central business district or Darling Harbour areas. There are a good number of restaurants, bars and cafes if you want to explore other places to eat other than the hotel restaurant/bar. Including Spice Alley, which is right across the street. The boutique hotel had great, friendly service, and comfortable rooms which all seem to be unique. My room had a lot of open space (it seemed to be a handicapped accessible room based on the bathroom), but I visited my colleague's room and it did have less space but was still plenty for 1 or 2 people. I did notice some noise that sounded like people racing or otherwise making loud noise driving down the street outside my window, but it wasn't too frequent or something the hotel could really control. My only complaint with the service would be that they charged my credit card for part of the stay partway through the trip without any warning, including a 1.5% fee for paying with a credit card. I would have paid the fee anyways, but it did leave a bit of a sour taste in my mouth to see it without any prior warning.

author: markj498
title: Urban Sanctuary
text: Stayed only one night, but that was certainly enough to appreciate this hotel. The staff are friendly and calmly efficient. The room I stayed in was comfortable, clean, and spacious enough (given the high ceilings). Breakfast next morning was tasty, well presented, and a fair price. The design of the hotel is welcoming and engaging.The special attraction of this hotel , though, is its location. It's part of a well imagined planned urban renewal project, transforming a derelict brewery and surrounds into a vibrant and spacious urban zone. There are eateries everywhere outside of the hotel, with such a variety of cuisines and budget considerations. Cinema is across the road from hotel.Public transport just nearby. Three university campuses are also nearby. In summary, Old Clare is a great place to explore a vibrant part of Sydney away from the usual tourist spectacle, but so very close for Sydney's usual attractions to also be easily accessed.

author: kiwiphil47
title: Wow an amazing experience
text: We wanted to stay somewhere different to the standard luxury hotel that in reality are all the same. Then we found The Old Clair. This hotel and experience was the best we have ever been to. As it was a special occasion i advised the hotel a week prior of a couple of things i wouls like the team accommodated these requests and unexpectedly we got upgraded into the CUB suite. Photos attached do not do this room justice. It is incredible. The dining options at the hotel were suprerb infact the whole area is getting revitalised and when you are a 5 min walk from central station you realise just hiw beautifully located this hotel is. Thank you helping us have a memorable weekend in Sydney. The Old Clair....what an incredible woman

author: 89peachw
title: Unique
text: I recently had the pleasure of visiting The Old Clare Hotel for a business trip. Check in was a breeze and a room was available immediately. I had booked a Connell room based off the photos on the website but it turned out to look a lot like their Chippendale Loft without the living room. Unfortunately the Connell room wasn’t available however they were happy to change me to a proper Chippendale Loft. Upon moving to the new room I was pleasantly surprised by how spacious the room is. Both downstairs and upstairs is fitted with its own tv. The only issue was one of the remote had flat batteries and still and issue when it was replaced. The room is slightly noisy with the room facing the main highway however it quietens down as the night goes by. Within a few steps from the hotel is an array of cafes and restaurants for you to choose from including “Spice Alley” where you can experience Asian Street food for a reasonable price.

author: stevengaohk
title: Good location & room with negative service quality
text: My first experience on DESIGN HOTELS. Location - Good, as it's closed to central station. Room - Good, quite cool, with nice decoration and premium amenities. Facilities - Gym is located on basement with quite small space. Service - Worse than my expectation, even basic requirement. I tried to call Reception for 10+ times on 3AM with no answer, I went downstairs and nobody was there. On check-out morning I reported to FO officer, just got a "Sorry" as official feedback, eumm. A premium hotel with below-hostel-level service quality is just like a "snail" with only shell. I will not recommend it in future, maybe I will still consider Marriott or IHG as I don't wanna be upset with a cost of AUD600+ anymore.

author: danielkI9742CJ
title: Fancy hipster hotel downtown Sydney...
text: The Old Clare Hotel is not the typical 5⭐️ hotel. It is definitely a luxury hotel but in an absolutely other way. It provides all the amenities of a deluxe hotel but the whole hotel design is so different, very modern, a bit edgy, chic and all this combined in a stunning historic building. The service is great and friendly, the rooms cozy and comfortable with all a guest needs to splurge. The bar offers great drinks and in the adjacent restaurant delicious breakfasts are served. The area is quite different to the one of the Sheraton on the Park but it has its perks. I definitely will stay again at the Old Clare Hotel in Sydney. I big thank you to all the staff that made my stay unforgettable.

author: D3612ZAstaceym
title: Horrible dirty place
text: The room in reality didn't correspond to the pictures on booking. Certain things that were promised in the ad were absent. It was really dirty. Since we arrived late and tired we anyway stayed there for a night. But it was noisy, because the window of the bedroom faces to the public corridor. The whole building gives me an impression of an old prison converted into apartements. Plus mobile phone didn't work in our apartment. For almost 200 euro it was a rip off. So, stay away.

author: 727luke
title: Luke & Rachael Review
text: We loved The Old Clare Hotel. Staff are extremely friendly, helpful and genuine - they have lovely personalities and are real characters. Lucy and Martin (the Super Concierge) are who we met the most and they are both excellent. Martin spent a lot of time with us and really helped us with a few things. The building is beautifully styled. Very impressive. Great rooms & decor. Just great!

author: traveldude225
title: FKG Fantastic!
text: REALLY impressed with my recent stay. I found the neighborhood to be great and I loved Spice Alley which is a 10 second walk from the hotel. The rooms were well appointed, functional, spacious and clean! Loved the robes as well. Room service was always reliable and good. The bar had a great scene (not too quiet or too loud) with great cocktails. I'm also aware there's a pool but it was too cold for me to check out. Overall - I'd highly suggest it.

author: singaporegirl2016
title: Great boutique hotel
text: Great charming boutique hotel. Stayed there for 5 days for a business trip and it was great. Room is nice and comfortable but I had to ask for a soft pillows as all the 4 pillows on the bed was hard. All the rooms in the hotel is different and that is cool. Location is central and near the train station. The downsides is the gym... its small and dingy and the breakfast at the Kensington street social was not that good... BUT Dinner at the same place is great and I had the best dirty martini in my life there!

author: warehousestyle
title: Great revitalisation of an iconic building
text: Luckily the charm, character and quirky design elements of the Old Clare Hotel help make up for where it lacks in service and comfort. After specifically booking a Clare Room I was checked into a Loft Room by the guy at reception. When I returned to question the error I was assured it was Clare Room, however not convinced I checked the website again and the description and photos most certainly did not match what he was telling me. Begrudgingly I was offered another room which perfectly matched the description of a Clare room - lovely timber floors, exposed concrete walls, great lighting, a plush bed, lovely soaps and shampoo, an nice modern bathroom, overall a memorable and unique designer room. There's a rooftop pool with bar which would be a lovely place to hang out in summer. The hotel is in a great location, close to nearby restaurants and walking distance to the heart of the city. Sadly the comfort of my stay was spoiled by noisy, loud music and stomping from the floor above which went on until 3.30am, combined with the bed which was way too soft for my liking, resulted in a very poor nights sleep. Generally the staff are lovely and helpful, although there's a couple with bad attitudes who spoil the experience. Dining at neighbouring Kensington St Social was disappointing, and the Old Clare Bar sadly still treats customers like uni students rather than 5-star hotel guests. While I really wanted to love this hotel, I probably would try somewhere else next time.

author: leonieg848
title: Industrial chic
text: This hotel is amazing, Industrial chic, artfully refurbished walls and floors and repurposed machinery as details in the rooms, like lighting. The rooms are large and have lux bathroom essentials. Great in room coffee pod machine. Big plus-one of the darkest hotel rooms I have ever slept in, when the lights go out, no light coming in from the hall under the door or windows-great for sleeping. The staff are extremely helpful and friendly.The front bar is comfortable and lots of fun. Great location short walk to Central train station, about 20 minute walk into town or Surry Hills. Fantastic choice of restaurants both in the hotel and street beside the hotel. Definitely staying here again.

author: leeshamaree
title: Great newly renovated hotel, close to everything!
text: I travel quite regularly to Sydney, but as I was up for the weekend I wanted to try somewhere different to stay. The Old Clare was a pleasant surprise from start to finish. The industrial decor and the quirky art in the foyer are the first things you notice. I arrived super early but was pleased to find there was a room ready for me (Great if you've had a 6am flight and are desperate to freshen up!!). There was plenty of room and the bathroom well appointed, with beautiful fittings throughout. The beds are super comfy, you are assured a good night's sleep, and the blinds block out the light when you're after a sleep in! Located 5 mins walk from Central station, you're also a quick walk from the awesome cafes of Surry Hills - if you want a change from the delicious fare offered at the hotel restaurant, Kensington St Social. Would highly recommend for a cheeky weekend away, or a mid-week break!

author: steve7124
title: Excellent!
text: My wife and I stayed at this property twice during a visit to Sydney and found everything beyond compare! Staff wad helpful and friendly, rooms immaculate. They even had OPAL cards (for mass transit) that had $ on them so we could take the train and Manly ferry. We were going to board a cruise after our second visit, and they were kind enough to keep our large suitcases in storage while we toured Australia. When we returned, the luggage was waiting for us in our room. The biggest problem was cab drivers have no idea how to get here...so you might have to help them. It has a central location, very close to the Central Train Station which makes it easy to get around.  I would stay here agian, and in fact recommended this hotel to a business friend that works here in Sydney.

author: HKMH
title: Unique, Designer Hotel, Close to Everything!
text: This hotel is definitely unique in its design and presentation, which we loved. Good: Cool, one of a kind design. Very clean. Beautifully comfortable beds and linen. Great location between CBD, Glebe, Newtown and Surry Hills. Bad: Lack of privacy regarding the toilet in the room - only frosted glass wall dividing you from the rest of the room. The Bar called last drinks at 11:40pm on a Friday night. Apart from the building itself, the experience didn't really feel "5 star" compared to other hotels we have stayed at, especially given premium prices.

author: 354katieo
title: The best hotel in Sydney
text: My partner and I live in Sydney and stayed here for his 30th birthday last week. There are endless complements I can give this hotel and it's staff. The hotel itself is beautiful right down to the minor details. We stayed in the Connell room, it was impeccably cleaned, the bed was so comfortable and the bathroom was modern and romantic. All the staff were so lovely and welcoming. In our room, when we arrived, was a little coaster with a hand written message welcoming us to the hotel along with a donut time donut! Every detail was so personal and unique. The only negative was that we live in Sydney so only stayed one night. I would recommend this hotel to anyone, for tourists it's location is fantastic, just outside the CBD but still close enough to walk in and for sydneysiders a great little getaway for a couple. Thank you everyone at the Old Clare Hotel!

author: kfongy
title: Great Location, Quality Accommodation
text: Being from Hawaii, I was very impressed by the high ceilings and spaciousness of the room. We definitely felt like we could spread out, and relax. As mentioned by others, great wi-fi and desk and items to work and think. The rooftop pool was gorgeous, and a nice place to look out on the city. The staff was very friendly, and helped us with our various needs. We didn't get to try the Clare Bar, Automata, or Kensington Social, but it was always crowded, even early in the week. I would say the best thing was the location, as being a short walk from Central Station, we were able to all the train lines. That helped get us to Bondi, Featherdale, Newtown, and Business center easily. Also, the town of Chippendale is great as Spice Alley had delicious street food (5 min walk), Central Mall had a fun atmosphere and more well-known food such as Din tai Fung, Ippudo, and Sumo Green Label (5 min walk), with many other smaller places around since it is a college town it seems. Thai Town itself is a little north of Central which was delicious too (15 min walk).

author: Justine928
title: One of the best boutique experiences
text: Easily one of my favorite hotel experiences ever. I booked through my SPG points and it was worth every one! I arrived very early and the check in service was great as they had housekeeping do a rush so I could get into my room early. In the meantime, I ate breakfast at the Kensington Street Social restaurant in the hotel, typical hotel prices but nice quality coffee and food, and went to the pool briefly. The pool is on the rooftop and has a great view of the city and adjoining building. While the pool area isn't huge, since there's not a huge number of guests it wasn't crowded at all. The location was in Chippendale, which is up and coming and conveniently located to Central station, making getting a number of places very easy, and also near Surry Hills, which has tons of restaurants. While it's a bit harder to get to Sydney from New York, definitely hope to stay again at the hotel.

author: lalaloula
title: Overnight staycation - wonderful!
text: High quality & service, bursting with character & personality. Room & amenities were impressively pristine & clean. Very comfortable bed & bedding. The request for a toddler bed was not only effortlessly arranged but they even left a personalised welcome with some baby/toddler amenities which was an incredibly welcoming & thoughtful gesture. Rooftop pool was a wonderful experience for our short stay & in the neighbourhood of some fabulous places to dine, shop & explore. Spice Alley being a particular favourite. Breakfast at Kensington St Social was a great experience also (although the coffee was surprisingly poor). Fabulous hotel & welcome.

author: Breadsticks
title: Super wow!
text: Our first stay and I fell in love with this hotel. From the warm welcome and helpfulness of the front desk staff to the super cool, large room everything was spot on and beyond. The room was spacious without clutter, stylish design led furnishings and a bathtub for a pre-evening out soak. A huge and comfortable bed. The attention to detail in retaining the details of the old building during renovation are amazing and the way these have been incorporated and 'celebrated' by the features to preserve them is superb. The hotel bar was buzzing and equally retained the old charm of its past history as an old city pub. Having a Jason Atherton restaurant in the hotel, Kensington St Social, was an added bonus and a brilliant dining experience. I chose the hotel as it was close to Surry Hills an area I'd heard many great things about as Sydney's latest hipster area. Location was fantastic and a short walk away from Central station for travelling further afield in the city. The Old Clare did not disappoint, well done on creating a wonderful place that's a home from home.

author: fearanti
title: Up-and-coming area, nice room/building, restaurant service slow.
text: I spent a week in Sydney and this was my home whilst I was there. The hotel is a renovation of a couple of buildings and it's situated in an area called Chippendale, which is convenient enough for walking downtown, but it's more of a cab ride to the financial district. The hotel The room (I had 206) was really 'well appointed' and worked well for a single person to use as a base, otherwise I'd say it's a little on the small side for a couple. The shower was a glass enclosure just offset from the centre of the room, which works pretty well for the room aesthetic. There was the usual stuff: an iron, a hair dryer, a safe, a mini-bar and a little carry bag for 'stuff'. If you are in a rush out in the morning then beware of having breakfast in the hotel: It's expensive and slow (not a great combo!) and that was when there were only a few customers. Options abound around the hotel, we ended up frequenting a nearby place called Mezbah Central for breakfast. The trendy roof top bar and pool were closed for renovation which was disappointing...it wasn't a criterion for us choosing this hotel but it might be for many people so it would be better if that was made known in advance. I didn't have a lot of reason to interact with the staff, but when I did they were friendly and helpful.

author: Jean_T_12945
title: Doesn't get much better than this
text: Landed at the Old Clare for a few days of work and play. Check-in was friendly but vague. However, that was the only slightly off part of our entire stay. Our rooms were beautiful and we had trouble just getting the teen-ager out of hers (she was showing off the room via Skype to all of her friends back home). Great location near nice cafes and shops as well as a block from Sydney's excellent public transportation system. One of our party needed medical attention and staff could not have been more accommodating to get us the help we needed. We felt like part of the Old Clare family by the time we left and major props to the staff, from front desk to housekeeping for making us feel so at home. Bonus points for excellent Triumph and Disaster bath products. I can't imagine staying anywhere else in Sydney.

author: 813JohnE
title: Relaxing short break away from the rugrats
text: Great spot. They have used the space well and the finishes to the room were well done. Had a very enjoyable dinner in Kensington Street Social. We sat at the chef's table area which had a good ambience. The sommelier was excellent and appeared to be well across a good wine list. Attentive waiters and front of house too. Service in the hotel was good. The bar was quirky and cool if you like that sort of thing but we didn't hang around there. I agree with some of the other posts that the "pool bar" is a bit of an oversell - wasn't open - but the pool area itself is compact but nice. We'll definitely be back.

author: Debbiepettl
title: Style over substance
text: There is no doubt that this hotel is stylish and has a great cool bar vibe going on which they seem to be very proud of - actually one of the first things they mentioned when we checked in was that they had been voted Sydney's bar of the year. However, I think they have their priorities wrong - they are a hotel and customer service should be at the forefront of everything they do. We arrived late as our flight was delayed and the room we had paid for was no longer available - they upgraded us to a two storey room which was lovely of them but it meant our son was sleeping on a floor below us and has a habit of sleep walking so I called down and asked if we could have the room we paid for - we couldn't as the hotel was full. As we had arrived so late and showered we also asked is we could use the restaurant, sadly the kitchen closed at 10pm so we couldn't eat there so I asked if there was a room service menu - there was which had 2 types of sandwich and a dessert on it - we asked if we could eat it in the bar but apparently we couldn't do that either - we had to eat it in our room if we wanted a sandwich. I asked what the alternatives were and they said we could walk to the casino or order food online and have it delivered to the hotel - we ended up at Macdonalds which was not quite what we planned for our last night in Sydney. The beds are amazing and bathrooms very well appointed. The staff are all cool and trendy types although we found the staff in the bar miserable. They did let us have a later check out the next day and also refunded the extra amount for my sons bed but I really would have preferred to have just secured the room we paid for and for them to have some empathy around us not being able to find anything to eat due to our flight delay. This was the one hotel of our trip I was really looking forward to and didn't meet our expectations at all.

author: Tal99
title: Brilliant Sydney hotel!
text: Stayed here for 5 nights on a Sydney holiday trip. The hotel was a brilliant success and I will definitely return in the future. Rooms are functional, comfortable and design-driven. Public spaces, including bars and restaurants, are each unique and amazing. Hotel is located a couple blocks from central train station with easy access to CBD, Harbour/Opera House, Bondi, etc. Super cool neighborhood with Sydney's best bakery (Brickfield's), awesome contemporary Chinese art museum (White Rabbit), grocery store a block away. And the hotel is across the street from Spice Alley, a laneway (alley) with various Asian eateries and common seating. While this hotel is not in the heart of the downtown area, it was worth it to be a little ways away but in a super cool neighborhood with great transit access.

author: dr_gasman88
title: Live in a brewery....
text: The heritage listed administration building of the old Carlton and United Breweries in downtown Sydney has been stunningly transformed into an eclectic and ultra-luxe boutique hotel - and it's great fun! Each room has a distinctive character - I was lucky enough to be upgraded to a Showroom Suite, which used to be an old bar within the administration offices (the executives of CUB apparently lived quite well...). The room was enormous at 53sqm, and a beautiful mix of the old mahogany walls and bar area with modern and (equally big) bathroom and supremely comfortable bed. The cabinets contained historic artifacts of the old brewery. Not being a purpose-built hotel does present some issues, with some plumbing noises and outside street noise being apparent - although certainly not enough to ruin a great night's sleep. Some expected touches of a 5 star property were also missing - no bottled water, no morning newspaper offered, lack of bedside controller for things like curtains and lighting - but these were minor and insignificant given the quirky luxury of the room. The hotel is located about 5 minutes walk from Central Railway Station, the main train hub of Sydney, in a closed-off pedestrian street which is fast becoming a go-to foodie area, with a mix of casual eateries (including a hawker centre style area, and a dessert bar run by a former Masterchef finalist) and several fine dining establishments (which offer charge back arrangements with the hotel). The rooftop pool area is pleasant and sunny, with ample lounges, although somewhat exposed to the surrounding apartment and office blocks. The rooftop bar is not currently operational. If you are looking for something different from a standard chain hotel room, but still wanting a 5 star experience, put The Old Clare on your list - you won't regret it!

author: bec_233
title: Beautiful rooms
text: We stayed here for 2 nights in a Clare room. The room itself is lovely and spacious. The bed is huge and comfortable, but the pillows are too high and hurt my neck. On the Sunday morning we called room service 4 times and no answer. Very poor service there and definitely something to improve on. We went elsewhere for all our meals. Highly recommend Spice Alley for hawker style street food and the Brewery yard markets were another Sunday attraction in the area where you could get coffee, brunch and small hand made crafts - both worth a visit! As there is no information in the room about local attractions in Chippindale or places to eat this was also disappointing for visitors unfamiliar with Sydney. For the price the room was nice, however the service was lacking, not sure we will be back.

author: foodietravellers888
title: Perfect for family trip!
text: I stayed here with my grandparents for 5 nights and the staffs are really accommodating. We booked the wrong room with stairs inside the room and as my gramps are 70+, I asked if they can change the room for me, and they willingly did so. They always helped me book a maxi taxi too. As we're staying for 5 nights, we also got the complementary newspaper delivery. The design of the hotel is awesome! (This is the place to check out if you are in Chippendale, as it's featured in Sydney Architecture Festival). The location is very convenient too, Woolworths (supermarket) is just on the Central Park mall in the opposite, and there are lots of other few restaurants down the block, very convenient. We really enjoyed our stay here! It's perfect for couples, and even family with gramps like us. :)

author: nzphotog
title: like staying in an interior design magazine
text: This was my second stay in The Old Clare Hotel. Since then the restaurants in the front building have all been completed. Along the alley by the hotel have sprouted several posh restaurants, and there is some noise until after midnight, if your room faces the alley. However one does do have to travel far to dine. I don't remember the name of the room I stayed in, but it had a bathtub by the wall, and a searchlight made into a lamp in the corner lounge area. The space was huge. As I mentioned above, it was like staying in an interior design magazine. Wifi was free, which is a great advantage. The hotel is just behind Central Station, and Chinatown is a few minutes walk away.

author: Oggie575
title: My New Sydney Hotel
text: I stayed here in May for a few nights for business and to be honest had never heard of this hotel. Well I'm very glad I did stay here. I don't believe that the hotel had been opened very long at all when I stayed, but every thing about this hotel I liked. The bar downstairs, the staff, the restaurant were fantastic. The rooftop pool looked great but unfortunately I didn't get a chance to use it, next time. I love absolutely love how they have not only kept all the original features of the building (which I believe was an old brewery office) but to also incorporate it all into a modern hotel. Top marks to the owner and the design team it must have cost a heap but the results are brilliant. Definitely my new hotel to stay in Sydney. Looking forward to staying here again. Highly Recommend

author: ChiefsBTB
title: Nice rooms but too noisy
text: I love the way they have retained the heritage of the building. However when you are located in chippendale you should put some effort into soundproofing. The noise from someone running a bath at midnight on the floor above made sleep impossible. Lots of loud street noise. Staff at reception were indifferent and didnt even enquire as to our stay. Definitely not a five or even four star experience. Given the high priced rooms i expected more. Standards have dropped since or previous stay and we are unlikely to return. A shame as some improvements and focus on a customer service ethic could make this place great.

author: AndrewWinterPropMan
title: Love it, fantastic BUT!
text: This is an awesome hotel in every way, character building, so stylish, so chic and young. WOW love it in every way BUT the beautiful room I had I could never stay in with my wife. Open plan ensuite shower/vanity no problem, but the toilet clearly visible from the bed with a thin bit of frosted glass still see through as the only visual barrier. Sorry but NO. I asked around and it seems I'm not unusual toilets need to be out of sight and out of 'hearing'. So no matter how wonderful this place is and it is. Unless I could be confirmed a different style of room I will never stay here again. Maybe it is not all rooms? If you can get a private toilet, then it is 5 out of 5 all the way!

author: 57saraj
title: Meeting and a child free weekend! Great Hotel but...the bathrooms?
text: We stayed here while Vivid was on and Mum was minding the children! We had a lovely time. Great room, although the bath by the bed was a bit unnecessary and Very Barry Lyndon! Also the toilet and the shower doors do not go to the ceiling but they also open straight onto the bedroom. Disconcerting if you need some private loo time, if you get my drift. Aside from that, great bar and cool looking pool area although it was closed for winter when we were there. Great location with a couple of good restaurants in the area as well as a great chinese contemporary art gallery. Fab bed. Will definitely return.

author: A6416SPjustint
title: Architectural and design dream.
text: The hotel sits in a great part of Sydney near Frank Gehry's UTS building and next door to PTW's Central Park One. There was plenty of considering for natural light passing through the room with the glass shower and frosted toilet. Beautiful furnishes and accessories. Everything looked hot! So much consideration to design and branding. The best part of the place is probs the friendly staff. Very helpful and geniune folks. Will be back (hopefully)!

author: shinraemonsam
title: No format review
text: Writing again after experiencing some of the best customer service I can remember. I will always have a soft spot for The Real Claire, the one where wild memories were created, where the toilets overflowed. That said, it is a losing battle fighting against the gentrification of Sydney, and cynicism isn’t sexy when you are in your 30s. Enjoy the great customer service from the bar staff, and try and find if there is more than one single unisex bathroom to cater for the whole bar. I couldn’t find it, nor could the 5 others dancing in line. It is too often we see terrible import beers being served at inflated prices, so big ups to management for supporting the local and getting Marrickville’s Batch on tap. Tasty. And good to catch up with Benny.

author: mastermuzz
title: Comfortable preservation of Sydney history
text: This hotel is part of the Starwood ( Sheraton ) chain. The similarities stop there. This is an exceptionally well preserved part of Sydney history, right down to the bespoke carpets. The rooms are comfortable, quiet, and spotlessly clean. The staff are super friendly and the industrial features on display were the reason for our visit. We found ourselves in an interesting part of Sydney surrounded by eye catching architecture, and great shopping. Every wish is well looked after. Yes. The beds are the most comfortable we have found.

author: nsdc2015
title: Unique and interesting in a less touristy part of town
text: They've done a really super job renovating this historic building. It has a great vibe and a lot of personality. Our room didn't have a ton of natural light due to its location, but it was enormous and quiet, with a lounge area and a well-designed bathroom (if you want a lot of privacy from your traveling partner perhaps not the best setup). Staff is great and as others have said, Martin the concierge is a treat. Bar is fun and the breakfasts were actually fabulous. Worth a splurge. The immediate area is in the midst of a surge of new development and energy with Spice Alley next door and other things on the way. There is a shopping center a block away which is helpful for practical issues, and it's an easy walk to Surry Hills and Central Station. We split our time in Sydney between the CBD/tourist area and the Old Clare, and I'm glad we did. Very different part of town and worth exploring; the Old Clare makes a memorable base.

author: je120
title: Nice hotel in the heart of Sydney
text: Stayed here for 1 night. Hotel was well done and rooms were nice. Missing a few minor necessities you normally expect from a hotel of this standard, like facial tissues, alarm clock or other method of seeing the time at night, music system/iPod dock. These items are relatively inexpensive and seem to have been overlooked. Would be 5 stars with these things. Communications from hotel prior to stay were excellent. Pros: - Well located for city and Central station - Nice choice of restaurants at the hotel - Rooms well done Cons: - Missing a few essentials as discussed above - Beds super soft. You literally sink into them. (Some people may like this) - Mini bar extortionately priced (relative to normal over priced mini bars) The closest hotel in same category I can think of is QT in the City and I think this is slightly better, but still well worth a look!

author: Beanie94
title: Most comfortable bed ever!
text: The hotel is a fabulous architectural fusion of the industrial bones of the brewery combined with the Art Deco sensibilities of the pub seamlessly styled into modern comfortable practical design. Staff are all welcoming informed and helpful. Our room was gorgeous and the glass shower gave a real feel of spaciousness in an average sized hotel room. But the bed has to be the utter highlight. A king size slice of bliss. Superlatives such as floating on a cloud do not even begin to describe the perfectly soft sheets and pillows balanced with a mattress which makes your body feel weightless. Great location. Don't miss Spice Alley.

author: lifeoftravel08914
title: Stunning renovation... front rooms are noisy
text: I loved the beautiful and sympathetic (true to the style) renovation of this hotel. It's stunning. The rooms are beautiful and big, super comfy beds and lovely linen, really nice bathrooms, good amenities, great service, access to good food, efficient valet parking - all good. My only complaint is that I was there for 5 days and I was put into the front room facing onto Broadway - and it's noisy (traffic, as to be expected). If I was staying for a shorter period I probably wouldn't have minded but as I was there for 5 days, it was disappointing to be put in this room given the noise levels. I did mention this to staff, also asked to get the music system working properly to drown in out (didn't work), but nothing was done to move me and rectify the situation which given the length of my booking was disappointing. So just ask for a room that's not at the front of the hotel and it will be great. It's really lovely. Pool gets shady fast so don't expect tonnes of sunshine.

author: PadreJose
title: We didn't want to leave
text: The Old Clare is nothing short of wonderful. Stunning decor with a great industrial chic twist and a fantastic location. I found myself not wanting to leave our room - especially the bed. The bed! Oh my, what a comfortable, pampering place the bed was! We extended our stay for a night because we were so comfortable. Food options are great as it is next door to Spice Alley and just a hop, skip and jump from Chinatown. One morning we even strolled the seven minutes over to Brickfields Bakery for breakfast. I can't speak highly enough of the staff who were wonderful and went out of their way to make our stay wonderful.

author: jacquit423
title: Unexpected Unique Delightful
text: When I heard the location of this hotel I was not impressed. To me it was a run-down sadly neglected part of town, but I must have dozed off for a year or so because this section of the city has suddenly turned into a bit of a cool mecca. The Old Clare is perfectly positioned in the centre of things that happen, and it's got the goods to go with the territory. Eclectic and contemporary, I love a unique stay and I would say this fits the bill. Our loft room was super comfortable and stylish, and the bed was quite heavenly, but it was the little extra touches that really made the stay. Quirky additions to the usual touches show a sense of humour, and some extra thought, and good customer service rounded it out. My only bugbears were the fact I couldn't open a window, not even a teeny bit, and what is with the light switch for the bathroom being at the opposite end of the bedroom? Small challenges in an otherwise lovely stay.

author: drichia
title: Boutique Hotel
text: Good renovation of an old building into a charming Boutique Hotel. Nicely appointed room with good furnishings. Nice coffee machine. Modern bathroom. Friendly reception staff. Nice roomtop pool that unfortunately we could not try as it was raining. Close to Central Railway station. Next to shops including supermarket, nice eateries and Daiso

author: kuklas2016
title: Stunning!!
text: The location is fantastic as are the rooms . we were in a Chippendale loft. The concierge service was exceptional.. always helpful.. and smiling. A big thank you to Martin .. as well as the others at the concierge desk... Renalto, Alejandro .. I would highly recommend this gorgeous property with a stellar staff .

author: 346jennifert
title: Comfortable and cool (in all the right ways)
text: This converted brewery and pub is a cool, stylish and slightly quirky place to hang your hat. The designers did a great job renovating the hotel, all areas are stylishly done up and very current. Clean industrial with warm touches that make a stay here enjoyable. My room was really a studio with soaring ceilings and enormous windows, a glassed in shower and a comfortable bed. Staff was accommodating and friendly. Room service was beyond prompt. Literally, my toast and tea were ordered at 7:18 am and arrived before my 7:30 am call. The food is done by Kensington Street Social. Will definitely return!

author: Wanderer_Pete
title: Brilliant Hotel
text: My wife and I stayed here for a function we were attending in Sydney and we will certainly be back ! Stunning architecture and design in the rooms, which are furnished simply but beautifully. We had a Clare room and despite being quite close to the street we weren't disturbed too much my noise from outside. The shower was great, big enough for 2, which is a bonus. The bed was just perfect, Super King Size and unbelievably comfortable, one of the best I have ever come across in a hotel and certainly a step or two above the sort of stuff on offer in the cookie cutter big brand hotels. Breakfast was incredible, I can highly recommend the watermelon salad, perfect start to the day. We wandered down the Asian Street market next door for lunch and got a great value and tasty meal in a great atmosphere with lots of families around. Service was first class. A great stay in a hotel that should be on everyone's "must do" list.

author: FlicL
title: Luscious oasis of old world charm
text: I was lucky enough to be booked here for a business trip, and stayed in the Chippendale loft. The charm comes from the details: the glorious retro sofa, the impressive one of a kind lamps, the marble bathroom with the deep bathtub and the rain shower head. I had room service one night which took over an hour to arrive - so this taught me not to think it's a quick option after a long day. That said it was tasty and I went to bed with a full belly of steak, salad and chips. The only comment I have that isn't 100% positive is that the kettle and cups and coffee machine are all on the lower level, but as far as I could tell the only source of water is from the taps in the bathroom - upstairs. Perhaps I should have used the bottled mini bar water for my cup of tea? I also used the gym each morning, which is small but had enough gear to see me through - a couple of bikes and treadmills and some weights as well as space to stretch etc. Hopefully I will get another chance to stay in the future.

author: pauldE4870RB
title: WOW - What a Sydney Hotel Should be
text: It's funky, edgy and incredibly comfortable. Stayed in a King Clare room which was perfect in all aspects. Beautiful comfy bed, spacious, quiete with top class amenities. The toiletries are all top shelf. The staff were attentive and real whilst not being over the top. The area around the hotel has lots of great restaurants and bars which gives a better feel of what Sydey is about. If your looking for a a place that is typical of one of the "five star" international hotel chains feel, this is not the place and thank god for that! If you stay, take time to look around at all the little details left behind as part of the transformation of this old brewery in to this beautiful hotel. How they managed to design the carpet in the main bar to look like the old stained floor of the original pub is amazing. Great job Old Clare Hotel.

author: ThomasSavill
title: A Real Find....
text: The Old Clare came as a recommendation from my sister in-law who is a Sydney resident. She has witnessed the transformAtion of the Chippendale area in recent years and had visited the hotel in its second month of business for a work function. The hotel lived up to its reputation and provided a fantastic three night stay for my wife and I. Very attentive and knowledgable staff ensured that our time at the hotel did not leave us wanting. Large rooms with a unique style made for a very comfortable stay. The rooftop pool was fabulous in a sunny morning, although did not receive afternoon sun during our stay (April). The location is superb with a brief walk to central station and some outstanding restaurants nearby (koi desert bar, spice alley, Kensington st social, automata). This hotel is a real gem and one which will no doubt go from trench to strength.

author: geoffhead
title: Different from the standard 5* cookie cutter hotel, in a very good way
text: I chose the Old Clare because the My normal hotel, Four Points Sheriton, was full and the Westin was charging crazy rates. The Old Clare was a little more than what I'd pay at the Four Points, had good reviews of TripAdvisor so I thought I'd give it a go. And I'm glad I did. It's so different from the standard generic rooms you find in every other 4/5* hotel. My room is double floored with the bedroom and bathroom upstairs, and living room/desk downstairs. Quick note about the bed, it's one of the most comfortable I've ever slept on. The pub downstairs is excellent, if a little busy. And the adjoining restaurant is outstanding with beautiful prepared and presented food. In summary, if you want something a little different, give the Old Clare a try. I'll be back here again soon.

author: jacquiet202
title: Superb!
text: We stayed in the hotel on two different occasions over a ten day period. On both occasions, the staff were amazing - couldn't do enough to be more helpful. Each trip to the front desk was a pleasure. The rooms are quirky, very airy and the attention to detail very precise. We found the two different rooms we stayed in more than comfortable and very relaxing. Kensington Street Restaurant is not to be missed. A culinary experience not to be missed! With Spice Alley just across the road, the location couldn't have been more perfect. Highly recommended and we would return there without hesitation.

author: N0v0c6str16n
title: Trendy hotel in handy location
text: I stayed here for 2 nights with my partner. The fit-out of this hotel is fantastic and very unique. The rooms feel very large thanks to the high ceilings. The bed was extremely comfortable- perhaps one of the most comfortable hotel beds I've slept in. We unfortunately didn't get a chance to try any of the restaurants onsite (next time!) but do recommend trying the cocktails in the hotel bar. Similar to what other reviewers have mentioned, the rooftop bar/pool was closed both evenings that we stayed- we had hoped to be able to relax by the pool after a busy day. We did have a morning swim which was pleasant (the pool is very shallow although sufficient for lap swimming). Great location, very close to central. We also used the valet parking which was $50/night & quick/easy. Would definitely recommend staying here!

author: hakuna3
title: One of the best - highly recommended
text: We stayed for one night mainly for sleeping place as we were in between moving house. Old place was actually across the road to this hotel so was very acquainted with their bars. Amazing is all I could say. Immaculate stylist luxurious room - though with glass-wall bathroom, it would probably suit best for couple. Service was professional, polite and warm. The rooftop bar and the one downstair are great but of course upmarket crowd means expensive drinks. Overall we'd pick this over any other fancy 5-star hotel any day. In fact, already booked a return for a special occasion!

author: Alastair61
title: Very nice Boutique hotel
text: I stayed here for one night on business, the hotel is quite new and in an area of regeneration (there is a lot of work going on around it). Check-in was easy (although I really don't like the $100 charge to your credit card). The room (122) was for me the highlight - very large comfy bed with a good selection of pillows. As others have noted in this room the shower is glassed walled and therefore open to the bedroom, the toilet has a frosted glass wall. This is a room for one person or a couple! I didn't try the roof top pool or bar but the main bar was busy and nicely designed. Two very nice bathrobes were provided and the room had a safe and free Wi-Fi. I would definitely return (in fact I would have this week except the rooms were over $100 more expensive!).

author: aaronn279
title: Superb hotel, indulgence
text: Spent a Thursday night at the hotel and had a superb experience, its a classy place for sure. Stayed in the Abercrombie Room, which was fantastic. The bed was absolutely amazingly comfortable and the bath worth spending time in. The design of the room is nearly perfect, except for the toilet which is only seperated by the rest of the room by frosted glass door. At night it was quiet and the room was prepared to a high standard. Value for money, it is quite good. Didnt try the restaurant but did peak my head into the bar. Super design, great visuals, but poor acoustics and very loud. Location is just right, close to Surrey Hill and lots of places to eat. Parking is a pain and not cheap for the valet service.

author: NathanV380
title: Just popped in for a drink and went back
text: Stayed in the mercure round the corner and found this bar. Loved it. Cool atmosphere and pleasant staff.
