text: Firstly, let me say this review isn’t about the service - which was friendly and efficient. But the staff were having to serve food that had not been prepared with love! Breakfast - a cooked breakfast that was mostly just reheated in a microwave - which included a field mushroom that arrived on the plate in a puddle of grease. Just not an appealing or appetising meal. Likewise, dinner was disappointing. The fish platter looked unappetising - consisting over overly and very heavily battered calamari and whitebait. A dish of salmon with Mediterranean vegetables consisted of very over cooked - and therefore chewy - salmon covered in a far too rich creamy sauce that made the dish almost inedible. My daughter ‘s steak and chips weren’t much better. A medium rare steak arrived burnt, the chips were dry and limp and the onion rings, as with the fish, were overly battered and oily. For a pub that describes its food as outstanding, this was a very disappointing waste of money!

author: 133gillh
title: Lovely pub to stay in great location
text: We recently stayed for 3 nights with our dog Milo! We had a great room with a very comfortable 4 poster bed. The room and bathroom were very clean and had everything we needed. We had breakfast and dinner at the Kings Arms every day and the choice and quality of food was very good. The only thing that wasn’t good was the porridge which was awful! We had fantastic weather so were able to sit in the garden for dinner each day. We loved the village of Otterton and all the fantastic walks by the River Otter. One day we walked along the river to Budleigh Salterton for a swim and another day we drove to Branscombe.

author: RRyel
title: Such a disappointment for a Sunday evening meal
text: We arrived just after 7 and asked if the carvery was still available and was assured it was. We went to the counter and the man behind the counter walked away without speaking we assumed he was replenishing vegetables. On his return he advised us it was finished and we could have leftovers with a free pudding. We declined and reordered from the menus. My wife’s dish turned up minus the coleslaw. We were told it had run out. After complaining we were refused a discount. Surely that is not ok to short change like this. No other salad was offered only a free pudding. Will never visit again as the young Staff were unable to get the manager to speak to us

author: itsme016
title: Pretty village. Nice pub
text: We walked from Budleigh Salterton to Otterton along the beautiful river Otter, a walk of around 2.5 miles. Otteron is an unspoilt, pretty Devon village with thatched cottages and a lovely church. There are two possible places to eat in the village; Otterton Mill and The Kings Arms. We decided to have lunch at The Kings, they trade under the name of Greendale Leisure which is a local company running farms, fishing boats, holiday parks and hotels. The use high quality produce which is produced by them. We had the cod and chips, served with either salad or mushy peas, which was cooked to perfection, tasty fish, very light batter and non greasy chips. We did not sample the desserts but there was a good choice, the coffees were really good. We did not book but there was plenty of space, in the comfortable restaurant. The bar has a good range of beers and ciders, including the famous Otter Ale. The prices were slightly on the high side but ok because of the high quality of the food.

author: marksL2500SS
title: Night away with our pooch
text: Chose this , from reading reviews off TripAdvisor, it was in the area and most importantly, was dog friendly . The room was a touch small, but nicely decorated and the bed was comfortable. The en-suite was fine except we had one of those toilet maceration fittings that was incredibly noisy and would sort of pre-set itself even from us turning a tap on . Hence , fill the kettle, a quick blast of noise . They had dog-friendly tables in the dining room and that night we enjoyed a lovely me. I had the pie; excellent, my partner had the fish and chips; again it was lovely and our dog had a doggie meal of sausage,potatoes and gravy for £2. He was as happy as we were. Breakfast , there was an excellent choice and I ,as usual, went full English and my partner had pancakes,maple syrup and bacon. Yet again , we were very pleased . So , we had a lovely night and the pooch did to.

author: mpad
title: Great Steak but . . .
text: I popped into the Kings Arms for a quick evening meal while on business. A most odd welcome, plenty of empty tables but some confusion as to whether they could fit me in. I suspect that a couple of big parties arriving at much the same time was the problem. Thereafter everything was slow, I had to chase to order and to pay. The fillet steak was excellent but the chips were dull. I also discovered a feedback card on the table which had been completed by a customer 11 days previously and was still uncollected - popped between the cruet. Hmm! I guess I was a sole traveller and a bit unlucky, amongst bigger parties, but, Kings Arms, every customer is important.....and so is their feedback!

author: MargaretW1568
title: Very nice place.
text: Stayed for one night b&b plus evening meal with relatives on 1/10/17. Very friendly and helpful staff. Food excellent. Room spotlessly clean. Plenty of parking space. Picturesque location. Highly recommend this place. (one downside - hopeless mobile reception in this locality!)

author: ShepsterUK
title: Few Beers Whilst Staying @ Local Caravan park
text: Visited this great pub twice whilst staying at a local Caravan Park.. Both visits where more than welcoming.... it's great when you can walk into a pub frequented by the locals and made to feel welcome... I would have visited more... but had my car both times ... & really didn't fancy the steep walk back home to my caravan site ... as no doubt ... lots of ale would have been supped.. I shall definitely visit this pub next year when the nearby site is open for the season... Thanks to everyone 😎

author: Zafrirgoren
title: Good but not a typical pub
text: Pros: Good food, variety of dishes. Clean, fresh and tasty. Large portions. Fish n' chips was excellent. Staff is very friendly. Located in a beautiful village on the River Otter. Cons: It is more a restaurant then a pub. Dinning area is a too crowded

author: littleme281979
title: Best few days ever!!!
text: After 5 days of awful camping in woolacombe we wanted to find some where to relax and enjoy for two days.. we booked to stay here! Elaine, was so helpful and accommodating as the booking on line didn't state we were bringing a dog, and had booked their best room which didn't normally accept dogs. She didn't turn us away and told us that it would be fine. From the moment we got there it was amazing, the room was perfect, the staff were friendly, the atmosphere was brilliant. We ate in the restaurant both nights and the food was amazing, they even catered for our dog. The breakfast in the morning was very nice and the lady serving was so nice. We will definitely be coming back soon and also bringing our parents! Our dog Rocco enjoyed it that much he didn't want to leave he planted himself down and wouldn't move so we had to carry him to the camper. Thank you to Elaine and all her staff for making our stay so perfect and we will see you soon xx

author: RAW1966
title: Lunch with Very Good Food
text: A large place, acoustics in the extension a little loud as we were placed in same area as a large party with very noisy children which somewhat marred the whole experience. Quite a few Veggie options which was nice and light bites as well. My Dad had the Mussels which he said were very good. I dared the beer-battered Halloumi and for a change it was quite tasty and the best version of that dish I have so far tasted. Well done Chef ! The minted peas that came with it were excellent and my only quibble would be the less than average amount of chips. My mum had the cod and chips which she said was very good and my partner a Jacket Potato with Coronation Chicken. All in all very good food and overall very good service

author: steveprotheroe
title: Lunchtime visit to The Kings Arms.
text: We celebrated my sister in laws birthday here and all had a very enjoyable lunch with drinks. It was quite busy there but we found a nice table for 4 by the door to allow fresh air in. The hot food arrived in good time and presentation was fine. One of the waitresses checked that we were pleased with our food. The toilets were clean and tidy. Overall ambience very good too. Happy to recommend this pub/restaurant for meals - they do a Sunday carvery and seating outside. But on our visit the weather was not warm enough.

author: Haircut4a
title: Jolly good find
text: This is a great base for exploring this part of Devon. We met up with family and had a thoroughly good stay. Peter and his team are very welcoming and fun. The rooms are clean and spacious. If I had one gripe about the rooms which is minor is that the hospitality tray could have been better stocked i.e. full fat milk bottled water and fruit/herbal teas (I did get these without a problem from the bar but it would have been good as an option on the tray). Our room 15 had an excellent en suite with waterfall shower. The food was very good along with the hearty breakfasts can strongly recommend the muesli and yoghurt knickerbocker glory aka Bavarian breakfast. The full English certainly was "full".

author: BrightonBelle22
title: Food very good but service serious lacking, thought we would give them a second chance but sadly no better, left hungry
text: Went for Fathers day. Items forgotten. Wrong drinks order, hair in the salad. Staff didn't understand simple requests. Did go back but no improvement on the service so left without eating. We chose this place because it wad dog friendly and also offered a digs menu we ordered but they failed to deliver. Wrong beer provided and then when we alerted them they kept us waiting and gave us the same pint back. Poor poor service

author: julietA1272LU
title: A bit disappointing
text: I was looking forward to staying here as it had very good reviews on Tripadvisor. The room was clean and comfortable and the staff quite welcoming. We went for a lovely walk in the area and had a nice beer in the garden in the sun afterwards. We'd booked a table for 7.30pm as it was Friday night and likely to be busy. It was busy and the service was awful! Well, in fact there was no waitress service - we had to go to the bar to order drinks and grab a passing waitress to insist on ordering food. We waited an hour for our food and it was just average when it arrived. I mentioned this to the proprietor the next morning and she said they had been extremely busy, fair enough but an apology or a complimentary drink the night before may have made it less annoying. I'd like to come back but wouldn't risk a weekend evening.

author: fairy_whiskers
title: Disappointing visit- Sunday lunch
text: Having visited the Kings Arms many times over the years (although not recently), I decided to book a table for Fathers Day lunch. We had a carvery with it being a Sunday at a cost of £11.95 per head. We had reserved a table in advance but had been allocated a tiny table in the corner of the pub so decided to embrace the sunshine and sit outside. The food wasn't great, the beef was incredibly stringy which surely shouldn't be the case if it was their own Greendale beef and the rest was very bland. The customer service was poor, the bar staff could barely take an order let alone greet you on arrival or make you feel welcome. It took over 30 minutes for our plates to be cleared too, despite the waiting staff walking past our table with nothing in their hands several times. I waited at the bar numerous times whilst the bar staff ignored me to have a chat in the corner! The Manageress seemed good but why aren't the rest of the staff trained appropriately? Having worked in Customer Service for over 10 years, I struggle to believe they can't find staff who can be pleasant and welcoming. Overall, I wouldn't recommend a visit, which is sad as it used to be a great little pub!

author: yolly11
title: Enjoyable evening
text: We booked a table in advance as we were told it could get busy. We have 2 young children under 4 so the table they sat us on was perfect! Gave us lots of space & we didn't feel as though we were sitting on top of other diners & having 2 babies, that was great. The waitress was from Portugal & she was just amazing! Great with our children & just made our whole experience of eating out more pleasurable. We ordered the pan fried salmon & pan fried chicken & both were really tasty. The children enjoyed the soup & shared our mains. Would definitely like to visit again. I hope the waitress will get to hear about how much she made our dining out experience enjoyable.

author: LindaWestYorkshire
title: Lovely welcome, lovely stay.
text: My friend and I stayed at The Kings Arms for one night last week. Lovely, friendly welcome. The rooms were extremely clean, comfortable and spacious. Plenty of tea and coffee and delicious biscuits! We ate in the restaurant, both had salmon, and thoroughly enjoyed the meal and the surroundings. Breakfast comprised of a delicious cooked buffet, cereal, fruit juices and all the usual accompaniments. Otterton is one of my favourite villages. The riverbank walks are just beautiful. Ladram Bay is a short walk up the hill....gorgeous coastline. Extremely enjoyable.

author: BG5O
title: Nice quick overnighter on the LONG drive
text: When we arrived we were directed to our room to dump our stuff. The Kings Arms is located by a river (not the small one running through the town, a bigger and nicer one) on which you can walk your dog. The food we had for dinner was very tasty and filling. During the night, I only had a terrible sleep because THE DOG WAS SNORING SOOO LOUDLY!!! Otherwise, the beds were comfortable and spacious with an en-suite bathroom. In the morning, we were happy to find FREE breakfasts such as; A full english breakfast, A vegetarian english breakfast, A light breakfast, Eggs Benedict and more. Two improvements: 1. Make the playground better for kids aged 4+. 2. Give free coffee and tea in the breakfast room.

author: stevec607
title: Good pub & food
text: It must of been my 10th visit over 5 years whilst stopping at Ladram Bay. This year the place hadn't changed much since my last visit in 2015. A great array of beers, ales and of course cider!. We spent one evening at the kings for my partner's birthday party. The party was around 15 and we all dined in the restaurant at the side. The food was spot on and service was excellent..apart from a slightly rude arrogant waitress who served us. One suggestion for improvement. The outdoor playground hasn't changed and needs attention. It's always busy however, it needs to be brought up to modern day standards.

author: JohnDaniels51
title: Good little inn in very attractive surroundings
text: We stayed for two nights and liked both the accomodation and the food. We have stayed before but the ownership has changed. It is now owned by the family running the Greendale farm shops. As they have their own fishing fleet, fish is a good choice on the menu, my wife had flounder, something different from the usual. The food in fact was very good and locally sourced. We opted for the "light" breakfast the first day, just as well we didn't try the "normal" portion as we'd have had a job getting out of the chair. Our room was comfortable but, as this is an old building, was not oversized. The bed was comfortable and I thought the price we paid was fair. The staff were very helpful and the service at mealtimes excellent. Otterton is in the East Devon AONB with numerous walks and, as the only place offering accomodation in the village (as far as I know), the Kings arms makes a very good base.

author: benjamink76
title: Ciabatta was very dreary and the service poor
text: We arrived for a late lunch: although they had a busy lunch (judging from the amount of tables being cleared)-nonetheless, when my partner and I arrived the place was almost empty. the service was very slow. I ordered a goats cheese and Mediterranean ciabatta (approx £8.70) and my partner a Marie-Rose sandwich. When the ciabatta arrived: What a disappointment! The vegetables were under cooked and unseasoned (no salt, no pepper, no herbs, no balsamic vinegar.....nothing!)- it was bland. the best part was the goats cheese. My partner's sandwich was okay- the best part was the bread (which was good)- but there's not that one can do to a Rose-Marie prawn sandwich? The salad served with both our meals were dry- we had to call the waitress over and ask for some dressing. We are locals but we will not return. Overpriced and we left feeling cheated.

author: sarahd918
title: Dog walk followed by Sunday Lunch
text: We parked in Budleigh and walked along the river in the glorious winter sun. Incredibly busy walk. Arrived at the pub and was told it was heavily booked for lunch but could squeeze us in for an hour prior to the table be required which was nice but as we had the dog suggested we sat outside even though it's dog friendly. We even ordered a dog carvery for £2. I would normally have knocked you down a point for this but feel it could be easily rectified. We collected our food and sat down to eat in the space of a few minutes. However, the food was luke warm even though we must've been one of the first handful to eat. Otherwise lovely pub and good food. I would go again but if the food temperature was the same I wouldn't return.

author: nataliebH3634AS
title: Mrs Ball
text: Wow! are food looked absolutely fantastic as it was brought to our table but the saying all that glitters is not gold! Springs to mind! The food was cold! After complaining this was rectified very quickly by a very hot meal, unfortunately the steak turned from medium to well done! My husbands rare steak was very difficult to cut. Where do I start with the puddings? Meringues out of a box, soggy cheese cake base!! A very expensive meal costing over a £100, definitely not worth it and would not recommend.

author: defraybo
title: Home from home
text: Stayed here for one week after searching for a pet friendly hotel near Buderley Salterton. The welcome we had from Nickie was warm and friendly and our stay was a week of pleasure and comfort. Nothing is too much trouble for any of the staff and they are all happy and hard working. The food is top notch and for a hotel of this type the breakfast menu I have never seen any comparison, I'll try to add a picture of it. Our little shitzu dog was welcome with no restrictions within normal behavior and they even have two choices of dog breakfast if required. The pub lounge and restaurant area are very cleverly blended together on the ground floor but neither imposes on the other, the bar/lounge area is like having your best real ale pub under your own home, it is what it is, a real pub with real people you can chat to without the interference of soap TV or pool tables. The bedroom was adequate with own TV and I used it with my fire stick to watch Mobdro using the free WiFi, the bed was comfortable the shower exellent, and there is tea and coffee making facilities. The owner Elaine and manager Kevin are the key components to a team of very efficient hard working staff and the food and service is second to none, a true home from home. Thanks for a lovely week. We will be back Raymond /Kathleen /Dotty dog

author: CASIO5
title: disappointing Sunday carvery
text: We have been here many times for food and drink on our travels. The last time we were here was 2015 which we had food & drink. This year we stopped for evening drinks in the bar & outside garden which was lovely but we tried the Sunday Carvery which was very disappointing. The chef serving was pretty miserable and when asked if we could have an extra Yorkshire pudding pretty much pulled his face and said and your only allowed 2 meats !! Now i must say that this meal was for 2 x adults and 1 x child and the extra Yorkshire pudding, bearing in mind we had only had 1 Yorkshire each, was for my youngest child who wasn't having a lunch as thats all he had asked for. I think a bit mean as we went asking for a full dinner for free ? The food was very bland not much choice of veg and a strange mixture of salad peppers, celery & onion as a choice ? The gravy was probably worse very tasteless and cafe standard. Its a shame as the other meals we have had perilously have been good.

author: janderson2013
title: Rocky start
text: We stayed here for 2 nights whilst visiting family who have recently moved into a bungalow in sidmouth. We have 2 small dogs and booked a dog friendly double room. Upon arriving the hotel seemed well kept, the barman who booked us in hardly spoke English and we learnt too that one of the breakfast chefs was foreign and the morning waitresses spoke little English too. I personally felt that this detracted from the charm of a family run friendly B&B and it lacked the personal touch you expect from a devon B&B. We were shown to the garden room which was very small and very uninspiring, it had direct access at the side of the pub, we felt very far from the charm of the pub and we're woken up at 6.30am by banging which was either the bins being emptied or kegs being delivered or something, i say woken up but neither of us slept well as the bed was very poor quality and very uncomfortable, so the 1st nights stay was not pleasant and fell well below what we expected. At breakfast the first day it was disappointing to see no continental selection just cereals, juice and a hot buffet which was covered in parsley a pet hate of mine, it was even in the beans! So this is where the negativity ends, my husband complained to the manageress who was very helpful and we were offered another double room in the main house and someone to move our cases, it couldn't of been more different to the first, much bigger with a comfortable bed and biscuits on the tea tray (none in the 1st room )she also spoke with the chef and I was assured the parsley would be removed from the breakfast buffet for the next day, it was delicious with local produce and the buffet was kept hot too which quite often is a let down as buffet breakfasts can be luke warm. So for the £85 a night with breakfast and no charge for dogs the 2nd room would draw me back again it was just a shame the the 1st room was a let down and having to repack our cases to move rooms did dampen our stay.

author: elaineclineuk
title: LOVELY MEAL
text: On Friday we went to the Kings Arms. We had a lovely meal. We chose a curry from the buffet. We loved it. Very tasty. Would recommend it. We enjoyed the beer from the barrel - Proper Job. I had a strawberry pavlova. Delicious. Pleasant and attentive staff.

author: Manthatcan2
title: Don't upset your locals.
text: Having previously enjoyed and raved about the food and restaurant felt disappointed and let down when we visited on Monday. If a holiday menu is necessary then explain this or reduce the prices. My fish sharing platter was tasteless and straight from the freezer. Over breadcrumbed and over cooked. The lasagna for some reason is served from a buffet area and again was average not good. A tuna salad was also ordered, this was OK and served pink but rather overpriced. Only the faultless onion rings made the grade. Despite being early evening and only a few tables in no one checked our table or offered additional drinks. Don't let the standards slip please and think about your locals if you want our support and custom.

author: nyunyedli90
title: Great experience and professional staff
text: We spent 2 nights in this hotel and we were more then surprised. It's a beautiful and charming hotel in lovely village and we can just highly recommend it. We've met a very good service already with the booking and when we arrived friendly and professional staff help us with check-in and serve couple of nice drinks. They have more then 5 types of beer and great food, we chose to have salmon, one of the specials, which was just perfect, so we've got everything we needed, together with a very nice and clean vintage style room. It is a very busy place, so it is recommended to book a table what seemed to be a very good system because bar staff and waiters were very organised. Breakfast was very tasty and I had no problem to have a good breakfast even thou I am gluten free and vegetarian. One of the other positive facts was that they are really dog and children friendly pub and hotel, with a special doggie menu so we will for sure come back, when we will have children. We couldn't see any negatives and we are looking forward to coming back.

author: N6904CAalant
title: Over priced extremely average food
text: Went with friends for lunch. 3 chose the fish platter which could best be described as cheap buffet food, i.e. a few small fish some with an an identity crisis.All deep fried, why does the menu not mention this, fish cake burnt and dried out, the smallest prawns in history, served with a salad at £14.95. I had the ham platter which was 3 slices of ham with a variety of bits of salad and pickle, 2 pieces of dried out tough bread. £14.50. Why pay that for an average ham salad. Cheapest plonk was £16. An expensive rip off, not even good pub food, left hungry and very disappointed. Will not be back, we are local and they should realise in the out of season period local recommendations meant a lot

author: StephanieL495
title: One night B&B
text: On our way further into Devon we stayed for one night at The Kings Arms. On arrival we were greeted very warmly everything was explained regarding meal times etc and we were given the key to room 6. The room looked recently refurbished in lovely pale colours and was a good size, the bed was comfortable and we both slept well.The en suite was very snug so really only suitable for quite a small couple which we are, the fan runs for half an hour once you have switched the light odd so l recommend leaving the light on above the sink. We booked in for dinner both of us opted for the sausage and mash, the sausage was very tasty but the potato and gravy bland ( l mentioned this on the feedback form). The bar restaurant is very pleasant and there were some very comfy sofa's. The breakfast menu is amazing with lots of unusual choices, we both had The eggs Benedict which was delicious. I would stay again as we were treated very well and the room was lovely. But l would go elsewhere for supper.

author: 977janr
title: Wish it was our local
text: We stayed in room 14. Fresh, clean and lovely comfortable bed. The shower room is a little 'tired' and I would recommend checking the dimensions of the shower entrance if you are more than size 14! But still better than many I have experienced. The facilities are delightful - lovely airy dining areas and a relaxing lounge bar. The food is delicious & attractively served (be warned the portions are generous). Breakfasts are freshly cooked (except Sunday which was buffet style). The staff are delightful and highly professional. This is a really friendly establishment where you are instantly treated like a local....and if you have a dog it is heaven for all parties. The only problem we had was getting our large labrador into the car after his sausage, potato & gravy breakfast!!

author: JuliaW493
title: Overnight stay
text: Nice pub. Lovely room with four poster bed. Very comfortable. Bath so big you could get lost in it ! Ate in the restaurant. Bit of a wait for food but well worth it. Would recommend the steak and the vegetarian fish and chips. Good choice for breakfast in the morning. Will be back.

author: DianeV89
title: A good place to stay
text: The King's Arms is in a lovel,y small village just outside of Budleigh Salterton. It is newly renovated, with clean, well designed rooms and a good restaurant. Staff are friendly and helpful. We stayed for one night only, using this as good meeting place to visit a relative. It is a rural setting in a beautiful part of Devon. Well worth a visit. There is plenty of parking space, the settees and chairs around the bar area are comfy. The menu in the restaurant is good food served well, fish and chips, beef stifado, sausage and mash. All well presented. We had pate and garlic mushrooms for starters, all good.

author: E8309RYpeterg
title: Couldn't do enough for us
text: We stayed for 3 nights late April 16. Unfortunately we found the room we were initially put in too noisy (extractor fans and noisy pipes - we live in the middle of nowhere so any noise disturbs our sleep). However as soon as the owner was aware of this, he moved us to another room immediately and without any prompting from us. On our return later that day we found all our luggage, dog beds, etc had already been moved for us. They really couldn't do enough for us. Excellent choice at breakfast, cereals, yogurts, and a variety of cooked foods - I really don't understand the comment from an earlier reviewer that a cooked breakfast was cost extra as this is certainly not the case. If I had 1 criticism of breakfast it would be for them to give each table their own cafetiere of coffee - the waitress was a little slow in refilling. We also ate their each evening and have to say the evening fare was just as good, well presented and very tasty. Overall a lovely place to stay and excellent value for money.

author: Debbiec645
title: Lovely stay
text: Stayed at The Kings Arms twice during last month. On both occasions the rooms were immaculately clean and spacious. Comfy bed and hot shower. The staff were very welcoming and service was very good. There was a wide choice of food for breakfast and we also enjoyed lunch and dinner. It is located in a very pretty village and is reasonably priced. We will return. Thank you.

author: bebejam2015
title: Could be better
text: Lovely place , lovely people but food a bit mediocre. Three visits here in past 6 months , disappointed each time. Menu looks good enough to eat but food lacks a certain something. Liver was overcooked , staff said I should have sent it back ?. Fish batter crisp but very greasy , far too many chips. Owners and bar staff really friendly , dogs welcome , and they feed them. But so far I haven't had a meal to really enjoy which is sad as its about the only local pub. Super location , car park . Will continue to come here and put up with the low food standard because there aren't many other places close by.

author: N4004OCjaned
title: What a wonderful find - will definitely return
text: Very helpful and friendly owners, and extremely dog friendly. We stayed for just one night but will definitely return for a longer stay. Our bedroom was immaculately clean and the bed was very comfortable. We took our dog down to the bar area when we went down to dinner, and again for breakfast in the morning. They even offer a doggie dinner. A relaxing stay - just perfect. Lovely wood burner, comfortable leather sofas, and delicious food and wine. What more could you want? Thank you for a lovely stay.

author: 239Keith
title: Dog Friendly Pubs
text: Came here after walking my two dogs. Excellent service. Warm and friendly welcome. Coffee is excellent. Would recommend. Lots of people eating in the restaurant on a Monday. Food looked really good at very reasonable prices. You can even have a doggy dinner for your dog. Staff insisted on bringing my coffee over to me as I had my hands full with two dogs. Really good.

author: Little_Kingfisher
title: Excellent return visit
text: Returned to The Kings Arms to stay while visiting relatives in the village. Was not at all disappointed. Management had changed since previous visit and there were lots of lovely details added since last stay to make the pub and accommodation even more comfortable and a pleasure to stay. My room was tastefully decorated with a comfortable bed and ensuite facilities. The WIFI was free and reliable. All staff were friendly and the food served was truly delicious. I can definitely recommend this place as a wonderful place to stay and eat. It even has a menu for dogs which is a really appreciated both by dogs and their owners. I look forward to my next stay...

author: Bootle45
title: Exceeded expectations, excellent service.
text: We were doing a walk last Saturday along with 4 friends and we had booked a table as it was a very convenient midway point. I read a few of the more critical reviews and I was beginning to wonder if I had made the right decision. I am pleased to say everything was extremely good and I would not hesitate to recommend The Kings Arms. The food was extremely filling, two of our party had fish and chips, which were very big portions and very tasty. We had the prawns with Ciabatta bread which were huge,we could easily have shared one. I recognised the owners as they have had a few restaurants in the Exeter area over the years and they have always been extremely well run. A special mention about the staff who were excellent, very polite and very efficient. Well worth a visit, highly recommended. Bootle45

author: B1550FSkarenw
title: Lovely location - great food
text: I stayed there recently with a group of people celebrating a 60th birthday, mixed ages with children and dogs. The accommodation is great, modern very clean and they do allow pets but only in some of the rooms. I am not a pet owner myself so it was good to know they keep some rooms for guests with dogs and don't book those out to guests who don't. The location is great a 2 and half mile walk alon the river into Budleigh is lovely and it's all flat. Great for kids and pets. We had a great meal on both fri and Sat evenings but it's best to book. I had Sunday lunch there it was very good but very busy so you have to book. Can't fault the place. Wifi and telephone signal were poor.

author: bcsTampa
title: Enjoyable Dining
text: We went to the King’s Arms in Otterton, Devon County, UK, for dinner with friends that live in the area. Our friends recommended The Kings Arms and we were not disappointed. My wife and I had the battered cod fish and chips that were very good. The portions were large and we could have split an order if we had realized the amount being served. All of the fish and meat is fresh and is provided to the restaurant by Greendale Farms. The restaurant had a good selection of wines and their own brand of IPA beer. The beer was excellent and a second pint was enjoyed. Prices for dinner were moderately priced. Service was excellent. The next time we visit the area we will be sure to return.

author: T8035GUsusanw
title: Lovely dog friendly hotel
text: We stayed one night specifically so we could do the beautiful walk along the river Otter to Budleigh with our dog Amber. We know the Kings Arms from holidays at Ladram Bay over many many years and were pleasantly surprised to find out it was dog friendly. It has been done out since I last visited for food and it is gorgeous. We didn't expect a plush room having a dog but it had just been painted and refurbed and was absolutely beautiful. Lots of space, light, modern and frankly one of the nicest rooms we've stayed in. We did worry a bit about the beautiful white bedding, but it managed to escape the wet dog! We had a lovely meal in the evening, a wonderful atmosphere and great service. Can't fault anything. Very reasonably priced and I would recommend it highly to anyone. Will definitely return.

author: collins14
title: Very Nice
text: We took a drive into Otterton from where we were staying, this place is lovely, nice warm welcome from the staff, as we had not booked there was plenty of places to sit. There was a comprehensive menu to choose from along with a big choice of specials. We had the Prawn Cocktail, and soup to start with and they were delicious, the soup was homemade and nice and hot with a slice of crusty bread to accompany. We opted for the Rump Steak which was cooked exactly how we liked it, nice homemade onion rings, chips, peas and a nice mushroom. We also had peppercorn sauce to compliment. Service was excellent and we were looked after very well. Nice place to go for a special occasion. We did not stay we just ate in the restaurant.

author: emmap863
title: Very impressed!
text: We stayed here for 2 nights with our dog, the staff were very friendly and accommodating and I don't think we have a bad word to say about it. We chose this B&B as they were pet friendly, allowing dogs into the rooms and bar area. Our room was clean, nicely decorated and equipped with tea/coffee and TV. The pub itself is set in a quiet and pretty village only a short drive to exmouth and sidmouth. Breakfast couldn't be faulted, everything was fresh and cooked perfectly! We did have an evening meal here too, again couldn't fault the food. We both had steak which was very tasty and cooked well. Although we stayed midweek we were surprised by how busy The Kings Arms was during lunch and evenings which I think speaks volumes for the service that they give. We would definitely go back here again!

author: Lisajr66
title: Lovely!
text: I stayed at the Kings Arms for 2 nights, the room was spacious, clean and nicely decorated. The bed was really comfortable. The breakfast was delicious. I ate dinner one evening and the food was clearly all freshly cooked. The meal was delicious. The staff are all really friendly and can't do enough for you. I will definitely be back. Aaron

author: flowwer11
title: Beautiful village, modern pub
text: Stayed overnight in this pub.It did seem a shame that in a quaint, old village, the pub was ultra modern and had lost it's character but it was very busy so obviously popular. I cannot fault the accommodation. The room was large and airy, the bed was comfortable and the shower room modern with a great power shower. We arrived around 8.30 and were told we needed to be quick if we wanted to eat. The food was okay but not wonderful, perhaps because of our late order but staff were very helpful. The bar staff offered us samples of ales and ciders to try which was a nice touch as they had several to choose from. Breakfast in the morning was either full fry up on a help yourself service or toast and cereal. Scrambled egg as well as fried would have been a nice option. Overall a good stay and at a reasonable price

author: Jodie_Thomas_Ware
title: LOVELY HOME COOKED FOOD
text: I am very surprised by some of the previous negative reviews regarding the food. We stayed in the village this past week and ate at the King's Arms on three evenings. Each time the food was lovely and unquestionably home cooked. The chef is also extremely friendly and a real asset to the place. On the first evening he asked us if we were "ok for a lift" once we had finished our meal. It turned out that each evening he offered a taxi service to diners - particularly those that were staying at the Ladram Bay holiday village. Now that's a service you don't get very often. My husband was also very impressed with the ales on offer. If you're in the area try the King's Arms for good quality, reasonably priced food with friendly staff.

author: phonelessinphuket
title: Lovely one night stay
text: Our room was clean and spacious with free wifi. We had a couple of drinks in the afternoon and then went back down for dinner at 8pm. The menu was varied and we both thoroughly enjoyed our dinners. The waiting staff were delightful and we were lucky enough that the weather enabled us to sit out in the paved terrace with the statues and ornaments. The wine was well priced and my husband enjoyed a few local beers. Breakfast the next morning was buffet style and perfectly adequate. The lovely waiting lady informed us when the freshly cooked eggs were coming out and made sure we wanted for nothing. All in all a very nice stay, thank you.

author: charlottej31
title: Great Pub
text: Lovely room, clean, lovely decor and comfy bed. The food was first class, and it tasted as good as it looked. I still have memories of the gorgeous raspberry cheesecake! The food was so artistically presented as well. It is obvious that it is freshly prepared using local produce. The staff are friendly and eager to please. Nothing is too much trouble. Breakfast was good as well, and the 'full English,' will set you up for the day. Thank you Elaine and staff, for a memorable stay in this lovely little village.

author: RowanB919
title: A hotel that aims to please its clients.
text: Short week-end in the Kings Arms. Looking at local properties so needed a comfortable hotel to stay for 2 nights. Many local people drinking and eating (always a good sign) The menu is excellent, not too much choice, which always indicates heavy use of the freezer, but plenty of local fresh produce. Beer is well kept and not at stupid prices. Breakfast was superb and you could ask for additional portions (eggs, toast etc) without being charged extra. Bedroom quiet and comfortable with a great shower (V. important). Staff friendly and service excellent, landlord great fun, all in all, a great stay over, will definitely go back again.

author: 26AlanF
title: great location
text: Stayed here with a group of 10 other friends for two nights and used as a base for walking a section of the South West coast path. Excellent value for money with no hidden or expected frills. Good clean comfortable rooms albeit some of the en suites are rather small and awkward to use. Nice varied menu with something to suit all and within a reasonable budget. Staff were very polite and helpful. Location is great for anyone who enjoys walking in this lovely part of the country. The hotel is also the local pub but don't be put off, it's an added bonus as once you have parked the car, then everything is at hand. There is also a local Mill for cream teas which I would highly recommend.

author: ValandBrian3589
title: A really good experience - Val & Brian from Bournemouth
text: Stayed overnight after a Dorset and Devon roaming holiday. This was a last night and it was by far the best of the 5 places we stayed at. Really friendly staff. Very clean and relaxing room. Had a meal in the restaurant that night - superb value and quality. The breakfast was sensational - a real hearty and large full English. We will definitely stay here again - cant wait. Well Done!!!!

author: null
title: Excellent value
text: We stayed for 2 nights 11/12th August 2012. The room was very comfortable,new beds we were later informed. Shower was good.Pet friendly, but was also a no dog area in the conservatory .Staff very friendly. Food was excellent. We had 2 meals off the special menue-dover sole and the burger--they were very good and fish was very finely cooked.Breakfast was first class-full english. Good location near the river Otter.We found it quiet at night,but was the Olympics.Beer good. It was very busy early evenings but we dined 7.45/8.15 and it was much quieter.We read some comments about a rowdy bar and were concered,but we didn't see that as the early trade maybe more from the campers? It is a good value comfortable good food pub/hotel in a good location.

author: Davidwoodland
title: Another enjoyable break at The Kings Arms
text: My wife and I stayed at this lovely country pub for two nights on 9th and 10th August 2012. Our room was immaculately clean and overlooked the car park and a 'chocolate box thatched cottage at the side of the pub. All the staff were friendly and helpful and the check in took about 20 seconds! I like my food so will happily recommend the Full English breakfast. Delicious local sausage, bacon, eggs, toast, beans, fried bread, tomato along with coffee and orange juice. We also ate at the pub's restaurant on both nights. The belly pork was fantastic and the portion sizes were very generous. The village of Otterton is surrounded by beautiful countryside and there are some wonderful walks along the river Otter as well as through the town towards Ladram Bay.

author: TreacleToo
title: Does what it says on the tin. Apart from the bathwater.
text: The Kings Arms is a pub with rooms, and doesn't claim to be anything else. It was the perfect overnight stop on a two day walk - friendly, unpretentious, pubby. The service was a bit vague but very friendly and the food was generous, hot and filling. The beer was good, the cat was old and moulty, and the bed was comfy. Downsides: we had to pay the extra for the 'four poster room' as I was late booking and it was the only room left. The quality of the fixtures and fittings wasn't up to much (donkey's breakfast wallpaper, two blown bulbs in the wall lights, wobbly curtain tie-backs etc), and the (windowless) bathroom was painted a sinister red with no shower, just a vast double-ended bath. Which brings me on to the main gripe - no hot water! We arrived footsore and exhausted in the late afternoon after walking all day and could have done with a hot bath so were very put out to find the water was barely tepid. The bath was so big (and the water pressure so low) that the barely-warm water was cooling down faster than the bath was filling up. A pity, as in all other respects we had a great time.

author: CloudbaseAndBeyond
title: A quiet retreat in Dorset
text: We had a pleasant stay at the Kings Arms, very friendly staff and a nice location. We've found it hard to judge the rating, 4 stars as the price was okay, 3 stars as we found the bed uncomfortable and the room was next to the main road [not very busy though]. Breakfast was good and the venue itself very pleasant. My partner is allergic to dogs and cats. The pub obviously has dog walkers as part of its clientele, so this caused us a bit of concern. we were also greeted by a beautiful cat one evening. As vegetarians, the options for evening meal were, well, one option. We lucked out and it was curry night. Unfortunately the advertised vegetarian option was a no show. Overall, nice place to stay

author: esrews
title: Superb unbooked stay.
text: Turned up at this pub, having decided to extend my stay in Devon by a day. Nothing was too much trouble. Despite being nearly fully booked they found a room which fitted my requirements ie dbl ensuite + 2 dogs. Clean comfortable room, good evening food, if you like fish excellent fresh local fare. Beautiful riverside walk in close proximity. My wife & I are frequent Pub B&B users. The Kings Head is a real find to be noted, child friendly & dog friendly. Last but not least breakfast was top of the range. My overall opinion a bargain for the price.

author: misskitty35
title: Lumpy bed, basic room and not very clean!
text: I hardly slept during our stay. The bed had a large lump that had given me backache! The tv was placed right next to an inside wall and was difficult for my partner to watch from his side of the bed. There was dust everywhere and the inside of the kettle was minging! The bathroom was basic but mouldy and the shower had poor power and leaked. The shower cubicle would not open properly and was difficult to close. We were not shown to our room and were given basic info by the owner. Breakfast was average but staff were helpful. We moved to another hotel the next day but returned to eat/drink in the bar which provided tasty food!

author: 286dacek
title: Bed bugs
text: Everything seemed so good in this hotel (location close to city centre, helpful and kind staff, clean room) until I woke up in the middle of the night....and there were crawling bedbugs in my bed! Many - more than 10 and of all sizes. And as you can assume - I had numerous bedbug bites. Hotel apologized for this and offered a new room immediately. Luckily - no bedbugs noticed in that new room. Later they promised to refund 50% of the total stay. But unfortunately this did not help me much as bites resulted in strong alergic reaction, so I had to see doctor and take medicines. And even now, 10 days after it is not over. Such bad experience I had in this hotel.

author: RomanticBohemian
title: Simple, good, but very poor wifi
text: Good sized room with a small kitchen, fridge. It was simple and clean. Small but good shower. Pillows could be better, they were too thin and soft. The biggest issue with this hotel is the wifi. It took almost one minute to load any page on the net. We were told to call the provider, a third company that provides this service to the hotel, which we did. They rebooted the provider, it got just a bit better, but not much; this place definitely needs a better provider!

author: HendrikM
title: Good value and location, some problems starting with rude reception staff
text: The hotel is not in the centre but just 10 mins away walking so it is quite handy to visit the sites and also close to the train station. The room was quite comfortable and has also a small kitchen, though we didn't use it and instead had some great food in the city! But there were some problems: no toilet paper in the bathroom, the A/C wouldn't work when there was too much 'humidity' which guess what being the middle of august there was plenty! so we're meant to open the door to let it escape. We had a room on the ground floor which had a glass door to the car park which actually make us feel quite unsafe and of course no privacy allowed so we had to keep the curtains closed. The reception staff needs some training - and manners. Upon arrival an extremely rude lady asked for immediate payment - which in our experience tends to happen at check-out particularly when we booked with a card guarantee. We tried to pay in cash and she refused our 500Eur note because it could be 'fraudulent'. We explained it was legal tender and being tourists we had no smaller change. She was totally unhelpful and made us feel as if we were criminals for wanting to settle our bill.

author: Rappe2014
title: Very kind staff, otherwise very average
text: First up, it's nicely located; just a 10-minute walk from the railway styation, only a few minutes to the tram stop and about 10 minutes to the city centre. The staff at the reception was very kind and they even told us where to find a supermarket and a boulangerie. Our room was at the top (8th) floor and the view was nice. The fitted carpet wasn't to our taste and there was a bit of an odour coming from it. The temperature in the room was also quite high and the AC was noisy. The kitchen was great (but you had to do your own dishes before leaving, or pay a 20€ fine) and the beds were nice (incl. the sofa bed). The shower was difficult to use ('cause it was in a bathtub and just a poor shower curtain separated it from the rest of the bathroom) but worked well. At the end of our stay it was a nice surprise that the room cost us about 25 euros less than was promised during the reservation.

author: X4472ZLbrads
title: Not far from rail station and rental car pickups. Easy walk to main petite France attractions.
text: Staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was ok. Bed was firm but not unbearable. Kitchenette was good. Very small shower with a curtain that tries to stick to you while washing. Easy parking on site. Short walk to the river and the tourist areas. The free wifi was often painfully slow.

author: Jwmc96
title: Good experience.
text: I enjoyed a quiet twin room ensuite with a tiny but well designed kitchen area. Room was very clean and I was not disturbed by any noise. Staff were available 24hr and were friendly and helpful with excellent English when my French was inadequate. Close by there is a good small Carrefour and also an artisan bakery. The Gallery of Modern Art , the tram route and the main railway station are all within 10/15mins walk. Excellent small restaurant close by " La Grande Vitesse" family run, authentic , and good value. Pizza take away on the same street. The Adagio is walking distance to Petit France which is a very attractive area to explore. The city is readily explored on foot / tram.

author: Hedo-epicureans
title: Fantastic, highly recommended
text: First time in an aparthotel and wouldn't hesitate to recommend & return. Good location, easy walk into the centre and quite peaceful at night. Parking (for a fee) available underground. We had a 1 bedroom apartment, it was clean, modern and a good size. The kitchen, despite being very small, had everything we needed as equipment for making breakfast, lunch and uncomplicated suppers. Comfortably and tastefully furnished lounge and bedroom. Lovely big windows made it bright and airy. Helpful & friendly reception staff. Excellent value.

author: Avatar1289
title: Clean & Comfy!
text: We were here for 3 nights stay and we find this hotel very clean! This is a surprise to us as we find that not many hotels of this range are so clean! Beds were so comfy. There is a mini kitchenette with all cooking utensils, all you have to do is buy some basic food from nearby Carrefourre and prepare you own meals. The only setback -- the wasn't any basic toiletries provided ie. there was no Toothpaste, shower cap, cotton buds etc etc apart from the shower gel cum shampoo provided. Towels are clean as well Front desk staffs were friendly. Location -- not too far from train station but it took us some time to locate it the first time as it was situated slightly away from where hotels normally centered at. Nevertheless, moving around Strasbourg is convenient with tram and there is 1 station just 5 minutes walk from this hotel. Just be sure you have enough coins as the ticketing machines do not take notes!

author: hw3862002
title: nice location, good amenity
text: I stayed here 7.27~7.29. Hotel is located near the station(10min to walk) and near the Petti France(5min to walk). Thanks to fully equiped kitchen wares I could cook. Clean bathroom. Quiet room. comparatively spacious room. The only inconvient thing is Wifi. But in our room we could use wifi until about 11:00.after then we couldn't . Except that we are very satisfied with the hotel. If given chance I would like to stay here again.

author: RodriguezVidal
title: Excellent location, courteous service, quiet neighborhood
text: Our third floor studio apartment was clean, with a kitchen equiped with all we could need. The shower was small but the bathroom itself very spacious, soap/shampoo was provided in the shower and sink. Good air conditioning and sound attenuation. We only heard noise when France won a FIFA match and during the July 14 fireworks. The common areas are clean and comfortable with free bagels, pain au chocolat and croissants after the breakfast service is finished. They were expanding the wifi service to the whole building, so the service was interrupted sometimes. But, in my opinion, their best asset is their staff. They were helpful, courteous and pleasant. Special thanks to Mlle. Alida, a very professional and efficient lady who brightened our day with her beautiful smile.

author: RonandVince
title: WIFI needed
text: The room was really large with a beautiful bathroom. The small kitchen was a delight. Breakfast provided y the hotel was excellent. However, having to go to the lobby for WIFI access was really unacceptable. That is , if you could even get a connection. "They were working on the system" Today, travelers really need WIFI access. For a hotel not to have it in the rooms with a strong signal is pathetic. For this reason I would really think twice about staying in this hotel group in the future. Vince

author: EvidencebyFran
title: Close to the centre of Strasbourg
text: This hotel is in an excellent location, it is well maintained and meticulously clean. The staff were very helpful and the parking is very secure. Breakfast was good value and fresh, get in early to avoid the crowd. The wifi is available in reception only, but there are plenty of chairs. There is Ethernet Internet in the rooms (free). My only complaint was that because we stayed for 5 nights, we were not offered any cleaning service, we had to pay for it. However, guests that stay 1-3 nights get free cleaning every day? We bought our own toilet paper as they only left one roll for 5 nights stay. Otherwise an excellent hotel.

author: PalladioAndrea
title: Location, Location, Location
text: With a 5 minute walk to Petite France and a 15 minute walk to the Cathedral or train station, the location is perfect and much quieter and less expensive than staying in the centre ville. No car is needed to see the sites in Strasbourg from here. The rooms are pretty basic accommodations, even in the super studio, with only two chairs, a small eating table, a desk, bed and very small kitchenette. No gourmet meals need to be attempted, as Strasbourg has an abundance of incredible places for lunch and dinner. If you want a better selection of groceries than what is available at the nearby supermarkets, are looking for prepared foods from a traiteur, and are not in town on market days, it is worth going to Rue Des Orfevres, near the Cathedral, or Rue D'Austerlitz, where you can find some great traiteurs and patissieries. The lack of WiFi (only cable connections in the room) in the room makes for an interesting competition for the few seats in the lobby during the evening, for those who need to be online. As other reviewers have mentioned, the staff is very professional and it is best to request a room at one of the two top floors to reduce the amount of street noise. You also get a great view of the tiled rooftops of the city.

author: Joana70
title: Low price Aparthotel. Good location near the Strasbourg historic sites. Well conected with bus and tram.
text: Very good low-price aparthotel. Near the historic sites of Strasbourg - Petit France, with near conection to the subway - station Modern Art Museum. To go to the historic center I was going on foot because it´s close to this sites. I have stayed here four nights in a superior studio well equiped with a kitchenette to make the meals, it has micro-have, little stove, fridge only with a lack of a toaster. If you want to make the meals you have nearby a supermarket and a bakery. It has free wi-fi and if you want a hairdryer, just ask in the reception and you can use them for free until the checkout. I advise to stay in the superior floors, it´s where I stayed for the first three nights, because in the last night I stayed on another studio in the first floor but this one was very noisy from the other rooms and from the street. In the lower floors you have the noise from the street, especially in the early morning when they have a truck at the front of the aparthotel that suplies them. I have stayed many times in the Accor hotels and the Adagio Aparthotel it has reasonable price, it has a confortable studio and it has a well equiped kitchenette, very good for medium stays.

author: hectortravelling
title: average quality; very close to PetiteFrance
text: Average hotel. Rooms (studios) are spacious, with a minikitchen; clean enough. The shower has a curtain which makes it easy to make the whole bathroom wet and in my room the shower curtain was far too long (I did not like having it wet inside the shower). No hair dryer in the room. Free Wi-fi in the lobby. Wired free internet connection in the room with ethernet. Breakfast buffet and breakfast room are a bit basic. Walking distance to the old town; 5-10 minutes to Petite France.

author: Skopik
title: Clean budget hotel with good access
text: New hotel, everything new and functional. Very good location, walking distance to city center. 8 EUR parking is good choice to avoid meter parking on the street. Room was very clean and nice, kitchen corner well equipped, big fridge. It depends very much about what room you get. We had 2 rooms with our friends, one room was on the top floor with great balcony and beautiful views, other room was just basic with window (still OK) Drawbacks: - they provide only one set of towels per room (regardless the fact that there are two people). Pay extra money for more towels. They do not change towels every day.. - the bed is queen size only (some cca 150-160 cm in width) - may be an issue for some couples that use to sleep in nice large bed

author: Millsie99
title: The perfect hotel with easy access
text: We booked the Adagio via the Internet, and were delighted with an immaculate apartment. With basic cooking facilities in the room, including a coffee maker it made things very easy for us to start the day at our pace! The room was absolutely spotless and had a lovely bathroom with shower. Together with free Internet access and even a balcony, we highly recommend this hotel. We ate at local restaurants and boulangeries, and with the tram station just around the corner found it so easy to get into the centre of Strasbourg. I have some difficulty walking, but still managed to walk everywhere based from this hotel, and so consider it an ideal base for exploring Strasbourg on foot or by tram. Parking was possible right outside the front door (or on-site for a small fee). We will definitely use this hotel again on our next visit. It was perfect for us.

author: Elebereth
title: Clean and confortable
text: Close to the tram station of Laiterie and Musee Art Moderne, this nice and clean hotel is the good option if you plan to spend some days in Strasbourg. Our room was very very clean and comfortable. Everything was new and in good shapes. The only thing I didn´t like so much was that our window was directly facing the street and it is a little bit uncomfortable, not for the traffic, but because we had to keep the shutters always closed when we were in... With 8 euro per person you could also get the breakfast which is served till 11 am in the hotel´s restaurant. We were quite satisfied of it. If you have a car, the hotel has many parking spots in the private garage for something like 8 euro per day which is nothing if you think that many hotels located in the very heart of the city center aks even more than 20 euro per day! The reception is open 24h/24h so that is not a problem if you arrive late and they are very kind.

author: JimmyCornr
title: Good choice for a city break
text: Rooms are great, big enough and clean, the bathroom is quite big and clean, the kitchen area has the basic needed facilities like coffee machine, fridge, kitchenware. Although our room was right next to an elevator it was quiet, the hallway and the bathroom separate the room from the main hallway, the additional door between the room and the hallway/bathroom helps a lot. Breakfast wasn't the best, it was ok for a first morning before starting to explore the city, it consisted of all sorts of cheese, jam, bread and croissant, we were happy we only payed for one breakfast (if you want the breakfast you need to pay for it in advance when you get to the hotel). WiFi works only next to the reception, make sure you ask for the network key, it won't be provided by default. Also make sure you ask for the code from the main entrance in the hotel, if you go for a walk and arrive later in the evening you'll have press some buttons in order to get in, or phone the receptionist who might be engaged in a conversation and ignore you. The staff were ok, quite busy but helpful. The hotel is situated close to La Petit France and the old town, close to the train station (about 10-15 min walk), easy to find. We would go back to the Adagio Access Petite France in case we travel to Strasbourg again, I also recommend it to other travelers.

author: Lulucm23
title: Practical, clean and comfortable accommodation
text: Booked direct for a 40% discount on room rate which made the stay very good value. Room (superior studio) was comfortable, clean and quiet and it was a real bonus having the kitchenette (apart from the slight noise from the fridge which not used to). Boulangerie and supermarket round the corner. Not in the best part of town but convenient for the station and tram. Everything worked well and the shower room was spacious and plenty of hot water and towels adequate. Rooms a little starkly furnished, but goes with the territory for this type of aparthotel. Booked for 4 nights so housekeeping extra if required but did not need this and to be frank it was nice to have the privacy of no-one coming to the room, even if it did mean making the bed as usual! Widescreen HD TV OK showing French and German channels but nothing else. Cable internet worked fine. Would recommend as an excellent option if you want a bit of independence during your stay and don't want to be too central.

author: MBFN
title: Standard "no frill" hotel
text: The only good thing about this hotel : very close to the Petite France / train station, next to Museum of modern art. Still 15-20 mins to the center on foot. The rooms are charmeless, tiny bathroom with minimal confort, kitchen reduced to the minimum. We had the bedroom on the street side, and hopefully good noise isolation and a lot better than our kids's, on the parking side, face to face to another building. Don't forget to book the parking, because it's nearly impossible to park on the street (and paying). However, nowhere to stop to get the code of the garage door (before you check-in). Reception friendly but highly inefficient (waited 15 min to get our key). Wifi a disaster, just good to read emails. Breakfast is not worth the €7.70 per person (nothing cooked). Go to the local baker to buy your croissants and baguette and make coffee in your studio!

author: GustavoSette
title: Convenient, but not as good as the reviews suggest.
text: The hotel staff is very slow. We arrived by car and we could not park before checking in, which took a long time. Luckily, I was with my wife and she managed to get away with the car. The hotel's internet does not work. The room is poorly distributed and the bed, very tight. the breakfast was mediocre, which forced us to cross the street and have breakfast at the Ibis' restaurant (which is good). The good part is the location, but is only suitable for those who are used to walking. It's about 10 minutes walking to Little France and another 10 to the Cathedral. In short: a functional hotel due to location and parking, but with zero charm in a so charming region!

author: sauerbrauten
title: Cancellation policy unclear
text: My girlfriend and I booked this hotel on booking.com, and on that site it said that there was no charge for cancellation. We wanted this option because my girlfriend was working in the south of Germany at the time on unpredictable shifts. As it turned out, we had to cancel our reservation, which we did 2 days before the arrival date, by phone with a hotel staff member, and were told it would be OK. However, when we came home, we found that the hotel had charged us the full price of the reservation. We phoned the hotel and booking.com, and the end result was we received an email from booking.com to say that we would not get our money back because it had never been possible to cancel the room. We never saw this stated on the booking.com web site, and we certainly would not have booked it if cancellation was not possible. In addition, the hotel staff member who confirmed the cancellation never told us that we would be charged. If you book this hotel and need a cancellation option, you should phone in advance to check the reservation conditions and also get confirmation by email from a hotel staff member (not just from booking.com) before confirming the reservation.

author: jim_s69
title: Clean, comfortable. value for money
text: It was recently converted from a former office block with showrooms at ground floor. It was clean, comfortable, provided good value for money, basic kitchen area with, sink, 2 hotplates. microwave, fridge, kettle. Excellent bathroom with wc, basin & shower, comfortable and clean. Free internet access via their cable in rooms and wifi in reception area. Extremely helpful staff. 2 minutes from tram stop for Museum d'Art Moderne and No 10 bus route, 10 minutes walk from station (10 euros + by taxi). 10 minutes walk from centre of picturesque Petty France area. Our only complaint is that given 30+ television. channels none were in English, so we used France24 online to keep up to date with news.

author: TrailBlazer619425
title: short break
text: perfect for a short break.. good central position. and not necessary for a car. main bus station within 5 to 10 min. walk... depending on ones fitness lol !!! very friendly staff.. especially Sarah.. The breakfast was not bad either...great choices

author: 214evaf
title: A little gem
text: I stayed in Albany hotel during the '18 Raisin Weekend. What an experience! I was in the centre of all the happenings and also just across the street from the Younger Concert Hall where I attended my daughter's concert. The hotel is charming, welcoming, and has a lot of character. Remember, this is an old building so do not be surprised by its little quirks. The pipes will make noises, you will need to figure out the flushing system, the stairs will creak, and the windows will not seal well. But that's exactly what I loved about this place! My reward was a perfect location, a cozy living room, a spotlessly clean room with a comfy bed, a selection of books to read, a sparkly-clean dining room, a beautiful garden, and an excellent breakfast cooked to your order! Add the welcoming and helpful staff and you can't go wrong with this place! I will be back.

author: geoffd192
title: Lovely stay
text: Lovely hotel in great position for Town Centre. Was visiting my son at the University but was a relaxing break. Definitely recommend to others. Friendly staff. Breakfast particularly nice. Generous check out time- was 11 am when I stayed. Also night reception available that is helpful if you are planning to arrive very late as I did. Parking is limited in vicinity.

author: FightingLeprechaun
title: Comfortable Hotel with Great Service!
text: My wife and I stayed at The Albany Hotel for 4 nights in August, booked through Kevin Fogarty's Scottish Golf Experience. We stayed in a double room with two twin beds pushed together (Room 9, I believe), which was spacious and very comfortable; on our last night, we were moved to Room 3, which featured a very small double bed, and was significantly less roomy. Staff was very friendly and competent. Breakfast was generally good, especially the cooked selections, and the dining room was very comfortable. This hotel is located just a 10 minute walk from The Old Course, which was very convenient, as I had to join other die-hard golfers queuing up at 0200 for an open tee time! By the way, I enjoyed my round at The Old Course...it was nothing less than magical! The Albany Hotel offers luggage storage, which came in handy on our day of departure. The desk also called us a taxi for our trip to Leuchars train station. While this is not an inexpensive hotel, its location and amenities made it a good value.

author: Mukaji
title: Very comfortable hotel!!
text: Stayed at their single room which was big enough for me to stay over. The room was very clean and their free wifi was strong and stable. The breakfast next morning was full Scottish breakfast and very good. I will definitely come back to the Albany Hotel when I visit St. Andrew's again in the near future. All the staff members were so courteous! Highly recommended place to stay when you visit St. Andrew's.

author: mabercik
title: Scottish Golf Adventure
text: The Albany is quaint little hotel in the heart of St. Andrews within short walking distance to all of the downtown shops, restaurants, pubs, and points of interest as well as to the Old Course. The staff was exceedingly friendly and tremendously helpful during the six days that I spent with them. The daily complimentary full breakfast was greatly enjoyed and appreciated. Of great convenience was the free on street parking outside of the hotel which became more available toward the late afternoon. The single bed rooms were modest in size but clean and comfortable. For golfers, the ground floor golf storage facility was very handy. The Albany is an excellent, reasonably priced choice for anyone wishing to experience the magic of St. Andrews particularly golfers chasing the dream of playing the Old Course.

author: ricfrantz
title: the Albany & Golf at St. Andrews
text: Visited 8 Aug18 thru 13 Aug 18 with my son. Reason for the trip was to play golf at the Old and New Courses at St. Andrews. Location of the Albany was perfect. We were a short 10 minute walk from the golf courses, and a 5 minute walk to the Restaurants and Pubs in St. Andrews. The Albany is a small but very nice place. Nice lounge with bar, and full breakfast every morning. Staff is very friendly and accommodating.

author: HKBilly
title: Lovely hotel in great location
text: One minute walk to main shopping areas yet on a relatively quiet road, particularly at night. Single room was compact, but with a nice tv and welcome tray of goodies. Toilet was quite small, but the shower was excellent and shampoo, conditioner etc were of excellent quality. Everything was spotless. Staff were very friendly and breakfast was fabulous, with the full Scottish not in the slightest bit greasy. Wish I had stayed longer, but I definitely would go back. The only drawback was parking. It is on the street outside. I was very lucky to get a spot on arrival, but I can see it can be a problem on occasions.

author: minnie7182017
title: FANTASTIC HOTEL
text: We stayed in this lovely gem of a hotel for 2 nights at the weekend. The room was spotlessly clean and had beautiful French doors, leading out to a very nice balcony. The bed was extremely comfortable and a good night's sleep is assured. A welcoming tray with tea/coffee and biscuits awaited us on our arrival, which was much appreciated. The staff were all first class, with their welcoming smiles and pleasant manners. Breakfast was always delicious and there was a varied choice on the menu. There is free parking outside the hotel, although you may need to drive around a couple of times to get a space. Would most definitely return to this beautiful hotel and cannot recommend it highly enough.

author: mbkasparian
title: Review of our stay
text: Hi, Mike and I are home now from our trip. We loved the Albany Hotel, it was our favorite place we stayed in two and a half weeks traveling in Europe. We have some suggestions though to make it perfect. The toilet was very problematic to flush and the front door to lock and unlock. We had stayed in the Bunker room with two single beds. Guests should not have to struggle with two basic things, like using the key and flushing! Hand/body lotion would have been nice to have as well. The great things were the cute plaids on carpet and headboards, the breakfast and view of the garden every morning, and of all the places we stayed in Europe The Albany was the ONLY one with wash cloths!! Thank you for making our stay memorable.

author: NeilK143
title: Albany Hotel
text: Conveniently situated in central St. Andrews. Walking distance to most locations. Reasonably priced. Excellent breakfasts. Helpful receptionists. Small bar. Comfy beds. I overheard some complaints about the electric showers

author: AZ-LGE
title: Great Location
text: Excellent location close to everything in St. Andrews. We could walk to the castle and catherdral. We were also only one block off Market Street where all the restaurants and shopping were located. The first floor room was much nicer than our room on the 2nd floor as it French doors out to a deck with a table and chairs. Since the weather was gorgeous, we had happy hour drinks there as it was much larger than our room on the second floor. It was a great place to stay but definitely catered to guys who were golfing. B&B was £330 for 2 nights.

author: Philippa911
title: Good location except for lack of free parking
text: I would go back to the Albany Hotel, but I would pay extra for a bigger room. My husband is over six feet tall, and, with no cupboards and a fairly small bed, we could have done with more space. Friends had booked one of the suites downstairs and that was beautifully appointed. I set off the fire alarm while drying my hair one morning, and it was quite humorous to open my door to three burly fireman who suggested I dry my hair further away from the smoke detector, then cast their eyes about our room and said perhaps I could open a window... That said, there is a lounge and bar for guests if you do need to expand your elbows, and we had some lovely evenings chatting with fellow guests. Breakfasts were delicious, with authentic, local offerings of haddock, kippers, black pudding etc., and the staff were delightful - welcoming and helpful. The location is perfect for seeing the town on foot, however I received two parking fines of 60GBP each during my stay, which took the shine off, a little. I would have appreciated a heads-up about where we could park our vehicle, and where we couldn't!

author: BazSilver55
title: Very Comfortable Stay and Brilliant Breakfast
text: Had a lovely one night stay at The Albany. We had been upgraded to the Garden Suite which was really lovely and spacious with a large bedroom and lounge and an adjoining bedroom. The suite had two very comfy sofas and access to a little private garden which we couldn’t make use of due to the time of year but can imagine it would be llovely in warmer weather. The room was very clean and bathroom well stocked with towels and toiletries. All the staff were very friendly and professional and made us feel welcome. The breakfast included in the price was brilliant. I’ve stayed in lots of 4 and 5 star hotels world-wide but I don’t recall having nicer coffee and the Eggs Royal were just amazing. The hotel is also in a great location for access to the beach and shopping. Would definitely return to The Albany.

author: Mazrich
title: Great hotel
text: Four of us stayed in this hotel in the Garden Suite from 12th - 14th January. It was perfect for us. Very clean. From the minute we arrived we felt very welcomed from the friendly staff who took an interest in us and made us feel relaxed. Nothing was a bother to them. The Garden Suite itself has a lovely patio area which would be really nice to sit out on in summer. The breakfast was one of the best we have had from fresh fruit salad, full Scottish, kippers, omelettes, scones. All served by smiling, friendly staff who always took the time to ask if we were enjoying ourselves. The central location of the Albany is yet another feather in its cap. We will be back the Albany and thank you to all the hardworking staff.

author: 535NigelL
title: Friendly family-run hotel in excellent location
text: I spent two nights at the Albany Hotel in December 2017 while visiting my daughter in St. Andrews. The location was perfect for me (opposite her hall of residence) and two minutes walk from the town centre. My single room was fine, and better than I would expect for a small hotel like this. However don't expect luxury. The breakfast was very good, and the staff could not have been more helpful and friendly. I will certainly stay there again when I next visit St. Andrews.

author: 215trenam
title: Wonderful!
text: The staff at the Albany were superb and I enjoyed engaging with them. They made me feel like I was a guest in their home vs a visitor in their hotel. The breakfast room was excellent, I enjoyed a home-cooked traditional Scottish breakfast each morning. The main living room is warm and inviting and the staff had a fire going each day/evening while I was there. Every evening I would rest and read in that room.
