The location is perfect, an easy walk to all of the must-see spots in St. Andrews. My new go-to place whenever I am in St. Andrews.

author: 15heidif
title: Very good breakfast and good location but.......
text: The location of this hotel is excellent, the breakfast was very good indeed, and the staff I encountered were very pleasant and helpful. What let this place down, I feel, was that it felt very much like an oversized B&B that wasn't quite able to sustain the demands that a larger establishment require. The room, whilst clean, was cheaply renovated (e.g. clunky sliding door on the bathroom that didn't close properly, four different kinds of wallpaper all painted over with magnolia paint, an impractical sink that spills water over the edge when you try to wash your hands, and an electrical shower with low water pressure that intermittently turned scalding hot). There was no central heating in my room (the heat was provided by a wall mounted electric heater), and the room itself was painfully close to the 24hr reception desk. There was clearly an issue with the plumbing, as every time someone in the room above ran water, the sink would gurgle loudly in my room, which unfortunately kept me awake much of the night. The toiletries were not replenished on day 2 of my stay, which I found rather inconvenient. When taken together, I don't feel that the price charged by this hotel is justified by the standards offered.

author: 10nico123
title: Great hotel, fantastic location
text: This was a one night stay for three of us on a girly weekend. The hotel is in a great location very central to the town. The room was clean and well decorated. The bathroom was equally as clean and we also had a lovely terrace looking onto the garden. The breakfast was very tasty and staff were attentive and friendly. The only fault we had was that the residents in the next room decided to have a cigarette in their room and it made our room smell, stopping us sleeping. We did inform reception in the morning and they said they would look into it. However we wouldn't let the actions of these selfish people put us off staying again.

author: gioiacaterina
title: The Bunker!
text: We had a lovely overnight stay in the Albany Hotel in St Andrews. When we told on arrival that we were in The Bunker, we weren't sure what to expect! The room was lovely and the bathroom beautiful. I had the best night's sleep for ages in the comfortable bed. The staff are friendly and helpful and the selection at breakfast was great. We had eaten out the night before and I couldn't do it justice but I thoroughly enjoyed what I had. The only problem is parking but that is not the fault of the hotel. This was our second visit and it will certainly not be our last.

author: stevea887
title: One of the nicest hotels in St. Andrews
text: I stayed in 'The Den' just past the reception desk and I've been lucky enough to stay in this room three time before. I've also stayed in one of the other rooms upstairs as well - all for work trips. The hotel is cosy, and small in places but very comfortable. If you need lots of space then maybe a bigger chain hotel is ideal but....if you want a real local experience, with lovely comfortable individual rooms, in a great part of St. Andrews, complete with a small hotel bar, and a very good Scottish breakfast then I would highly recommend this place. Also helps that the hotel is open 24 hours too. Pauline on the desk and Kevin in the breakfast room were lovely hosts and made my colleagues and I feel very welcome. I look forward to coming back here again soon. Steve A, (Visiting St. Andrews for work)

author: tdh590
title: Nice hotel, great location in St. Andrews
text: Staff was excellent and attentive to our needs. Good breakfast, nice lounge and bar area. Room was clean and cozy. A short walk to pubs, restaurants, and shopping. Also close to the Old Course at St. Andrews. Had a pleasant stay and will stay there again when in St. Andrews. Only set back is limited car parking.

author: longhorn67
title: Two night stay in large suite...
text: Our family of four spent two nights this July at the Albany Hotel while visiting our daughter who was taking a summer course at St. Andrews. The room was large and comfortable, with plenty of room for four. Nothing elegant -- the furniture was a bit dated -- but a really good deal. The downstairs room had its own garden access, which was nice. The breakfast , which was included, was delicious, and the little dining room was very nice. Hotel and dining room staff were very friendly and professional. Location can't be beat -- the hotel is right in the middle of town, a short walk to the university, shops and restaurants. If our daughter attends St. Andrews as a full-time student next year, we will definitely make the Albany Hotel our regular lodging choice!

author: I43KQjeffh
title: Nice
text: This is a fine hotel with a nice breakfast, that is served very quickly. The room was quite large, well maintained and clean. The bed was comfortable. We got to the hotel by train to Leuchars, then the bus to St. Andrews and then a short walk. The hotel is an easy walk to the golf course and the castle and cathedral. Like a lot of old buildings the layout of rooms can lead to some noise - people talking and doors on door closers closing loudly. This is not a big issue, just a quirk.

author: 63vet
title: Would not stay again.
text: We were spoiled by a hotel in Troon. This one had NO help with baggage. Carry your own up and down two flights. Very impersonal. You're just a person in a room. Not rude, but no personal interaction. Serve only breakfast, which was okay, probably the best part. Rooms were extremely small. You barely had room to turn around in the shower. Ceiling was about 7 feet at the very most.

author: Gspexarth
title: Can't wait to go back
text: This was our first but definitely not last trip to St. Andrews, thanks in part to our wonderful stay recently at the Albany. The accommodations were comfortable and inviting, and the people there could not have been nicer. Breakfast in the morning was wonderful each day, and I really enjoyed looking out at the beautiful courtyard garden. The hotel is centrally located, so you're just a short walk from anywhere you'd like to be in town. After a day of golf or sightseeing we'd frequent the cozy lobby for a drink and relaxing. If you are looking for a charming home away from home with fantastic service, you don't want to miss this hotel. Thank you for a wonderful trip!

author: simonleyton
title: Another wonderful stay
text: Yet another great trip to St Andrews and we had to stay at the Albany. Always so friendly and such a comfortable place. The "Bunker" is our favourite room yet. Nice size for a twin and with 3 different area's. Breakfast was up to it usual high standard and warmly served each day by the warm welcoming staff. Great selection of cereals, mini pastries & fresh fruit along with cooked breakfast. The kippers became my favourite on this 6 day visit, served with a perfectly cooked poached egg. Can not wait to be back.

author: COntentedtravel1234
title: Excellent place to stay if you are attending a St Andrews graduation but book early
text: We stayed here because our youngest son was graduating from St Andrews. We had booked last August when we knew the approximate date and at that time, there was only one room left! The location can not be faulted. Because my husband has had knee problems in the past, the hotel kindly accommodated us on the ground floor. The room overlooked the main street which was lovely as we were able to watch people gathering for the ceremonies. Parking was relatively straight forward after 5 pm and we were able to leave the car for the duration. The staff are genuinely kind. The breakfast is good -- particularly the Albany Woodcock. Should we go to St Andrews again, we would definitely stay here.

author: patty398
title: Loved our stay at Albany
text: We loved the atmosphere at the Albany Hotel. We were welcomed by staff and shown to our room. Our college age son was with us, so we had a suite, very elegantly appointed. The suite also had a private balcony that overlooked the lovely garden. Breakfast was great, and in a lovely room or one could also eat at tables in the garden. The location could not have been better- right across from the university. The cathedral, castle, high street, and golf courses were no more than two blocks away in different directions! We highly recommend the Albany!!

author: mdrlondon87
title: Great location
text: We were visiting for a few days and had a lot of plans. Location is excellent. Hotel is well maintained, clean and staff friendly. Bedroom was small but that's what we booked and it was comfortable. Wi-Fi in our room was awful throughout. Made more difficult as it was a basement room so phone signal was weak. Often we picked up messages when we left the hotel. Breakfast was good, but was disappointed there's no Black Pudding on menu and that juices are long life packet juices and not fresh. Overall good and good value for st andrews.

author: 969tjw
title: A lovely B&B in a wonderful location
text: We arrived at the Albany Hotel after a very long drive to get to St. Andrews. The front desk staff was very helpful in telling us how to get to both the restaurant that we had reservations and to the Castle and Cathedral. Although the room we rented was all the way on the top floor we were able to make it up the with all our suitcases. The room was nicely situated. I think it would have been helpful if someone would have explained the shower "contraption" to us but we did finally figure it out after a few minutes. LOL. The breakfast in the morning was very yummy and the hostess was very nice! Love that the golf course is so close to the hotel - well within a 5-10 minute walk.

author: merylheha
title: University visit day
text: We booked online attracted by the picture showing it to be a period property. The location was ideal for us visiting the university across the road but would suit anyone wanting to be in walking distance of St Andrews' tourist attractions. Nowhere we went was more than about a 20 minute walk. The staff were welcoming and friendly. Our room was on the top floor consisting of a twin & light, airy ensuite bathroom. It was well equipped, clean & tastefully decorated. The breakfast was included in the room rate & the choice was varied and tasty. We stayed 2 nights and I would happily book again.

author: robsf2015
title: Cozy and Nice in St Andrews - a Gem
text: My daughter is studying in St Andrews and this was my first visit. I was looking for a cozy, centrally located and not too pricey. I booked Albany Hotel very quickly - just really looking at location and price. It turned out to be a real Gem. Loved the attentive service and heart-felt engagement of the staff. Enjoyed the conversations with my daughter in front of the fire-place. Ellen, the lovely lady checking us in, even encouraged us to have hot chocolate and wear p-jays to enjoy the fireplace better. Very sweet! The rooms were comfortable and parking on Main Street in front of the hotel was free. We loved the Albany.

author: 494marthad
title: Enjoyed the Alany
text: The hotel was close to centre of the town. Our room was spacious with very comfy bed and pillows. Plenty hot water for showers. Breakfast was great with plenty of choice. Staff were all pleasant and helpful. Could hear some noise from other residents coming in at night. It is an older building. It didn't spoil our stay.

author: 837jm
title: A small friendly hotel in an excellent location.
text: We booked this hotel at a weeks notice because of location and reviews.We were not disappointed.We have never been to St Andrew's before. The hotel was easy to get to on foot from the bus station.It was in a historic part of St Andrew's close to the university and the sea. On arrival we were met by a very friendly and helpful receptionist who could help us book somewhere for an evening meal if we wanted. We were put in a room called The Bunker on the ground floor. The room was nice and warm which helped as it was cold ,wet and snowing on our arrival . The room had a lot of character and was very cosy.The bathroom was a good size with a walk in shower.Toileteries were provided and everything worked well.The beds were very comfortable and we both had a very good sleep.After going out for a meal we came back into the small bar area with some friends and enjoyed a really nice evening with a good choice of alcoholic beverage.Again the staff were very obliging and helped make it a very enjoyable relaxed evening. AS we stayed for two nights we went out after our comprehensive breakfast and within 100 yards we had reached the ruins of St Andrews church and walked along the very attractive front and did a circle into the town.We then came back and had a cup of tea and biscuits provided. If we came back again we would definitely stay at The Albany again because it was so friendly ,cosy ,relaxed and in an ideal position for all the amenities.Also we would try to book The Bunker room. We loved it.

author: Hjlundbeck
title: Friendly but could be improved
text: The hotel was friendly and the staff were very welcoming but there a few things that the hotel could improve to make it a more pleasant stay. We arrived and went to our rom which was freezing cold. There is electric heating and it wasn't turned on. The room itself is maybe a bit dated but it was very clean. We were going to miss breakfast in the morning due to a late night the previous night but the fire alarm went off at 9am. The staff weren't very apologetic and the breakfast was okay. It was basic but did the job. Overall a tidy, clean hotel which is a bit dated and the staff could just make a few extra touches to make it more pleasant for the guests.

author: J407AIdavidf
title: Nice people, nice hotel, nice location
text: My wife and I have just returned from a 2 night stay at the Albany. We normally stay outside of St Andrews, but decided to give the hotel a try based on the price and it's location. We were not disappointed. The location was superb, and everything in the town was easily accessible. The staff were warm and friendly and very accommodating. I think that Duncan, the night porter, deserves a special mention. He is your man if you need a late night drink and does a sterling job. The rooms was on the small side but was perfectly acceptable. The breakfast was hot and tasty with a reasonable selection, and overall my wife and myself were very happy with our stay. In fact, we are planning our next visit.

author: bramwells2016
title: Wedding Party
text: We have just come back from an amazing stay in the Albany Hotel, St Andrew. It's a small friendly guest house, with a bar... The rooms were clean, warm and had everything you needed. The staff were so warm and friendly, nothing was too much trouble. They coped so well with a large, over excited wedding party for our daughters wedding. We had family and friends travelling from Europe and all over the uk. The breakfasts were delicious coping with vegitarians, meat only, and everything in between Ellen on the font desk helped organise everything, she was calm and welcoming at all times, Vicky coped with our noisy group over breakfasts.. Just made the most special day of our daughters wedding go with a relaxed party atmosphere.. Thank you the Albany.

author: Anon_Friend_5
title: Warm - Welcoming - Homey
text: Still thinking about our recent trip and telling friends and families about our experiences and memories. To do that properly, I must recount our experience at The Albany Hotel. The Albany is not the largest or most modern hotel one will ever stay, but the warmth and welcome home attitude provided by the “family” at The Albany could never be matched by any “big box hotel”. The 5* rating started with the greeting, attention and outgoing attitude provide by Ellen and the rest of the staff from the office through kitchen Staff. Everyone made us feel like they could not do enough for us. The hotel is conveniently located for a short (5-10) walk to anywhere - many different Restaurants, all shopping or points of interest and of course golfing. Some of the rooms may be small but the rest of the experience of our stay made up for that easily. If I ever get the chance to visit St. Andrews again the first thing I will do is check the availability of rooms at The Albany and that should tell you how we felt.

author: Y9088HGgaryh
title: An overnight stay for a theatre outing
text: This was a return trip for my wife and I. The reception was warm and friendly - and this set the standard for all of the staff. The night porter was very helpful and accommodating with [ very reasonably priced ] drinks and the dining room staff were very attentive. Our room [ 9 ] was spacious and very comfortable. It enjoyed the benefit of overlooking a very busy and dynamic street. Everything about the Albany is of high quality and the owners, clearly, have a well motivated, highly skilled and exceptionally friendly team. This is a great hotel which I would recommend to anyone staying in St. Andrews - well located, well priced and very comfortable. The breakfasts are a bit special - worth a visit just to get one.

author: msngriz
title: Loved the Albany - great location
text: Just stayed at the Albany about 10 days ago. We had 4 rooms, I had room 18, top floor with a few of St. Andrews University - beautiful. The room was great and the staff was exceptional. Liz serves the breakfast most mornings and she is great. My family/friends rooms were not quite as big as mine, but we spent most of our time golfing, sightseeing and having a blast in St. Andrews. It is only steps from great coffee shops, restaurants/bars etc.... great time. Well done Albany.

author: jww0715
title: Excellent location
text: This hotel is located in the heart of St Andrews. Price was reasonable and accommodation comfortable. We were in Room 11 which is downstairs by the Breakfast Room. The Room was nice and private. Only problem was that the floor above tended to creak from residents' in the above room walking about - a problem if they are people who go to bed late! Breakfast was excellent, did my poached eggs just as I like them. Parking can be a problem if you arrive during the day between Mon and Sat. However, spaces outside the hotel are available free with no time limit. Be careful not to park in the pay zone 100m up the road. The hotel has a sitting room with bar and there is a night porter.

author: KingdomOfFife
title: Short but enjoyable stay
text: We picked the Albany as it was close to where our night out would begin, without looking at reviews or pictures. The initial phonecall was answered by a friendly and helpful member of staff which kicked things off nicely. When we arrived, we were given a room on the top floor, reached by a charming spiral staircase.. the room itself was well-appointed, everything worked with comfortable beds and an excellent shower. Only complaint with bathroom was the noisy 'saniflow' waste disposal unit but was obviously installed for a reason..avoid flushing the toilet during the night! After freshening up we headed down to the cosy traditional bar, where we awaited our friends in front of the coal fire with a cold beer.. The morning after, a good breakfast was in order to soak up the remaining alcohol, and a good breakfast was found. Staff at all times were friendly and most helpful. We were thanked for our custom on departure and assured we would be back in St. Andrews.

author: Donegore43
title: Compact and Bijou, good value for money
text: Stayed at the Albany, whilst attending some lectures at the university. Check was fast and friendly. I had booked a single room. It was very compact but functional. No AC (Not much need in Scotland!), but had free view TV, tea and coffee facilities, and ensuite shower room. Breakfast was very good with a good menu for cooked breakfast, as well as cereals, yogurts and pastries. Breakfast staff were very friendly and some of my party ordered additional items such as kippers and haggis on the side, which wasn’t an issue. If you need to visit Saint Andrews for Uni or golf for a few days and don’t want to pay a fortune then The Albany is a good place to stay.

author: Hollie_Mariee
title: Good location
text: Great central location, I agree with some other reviews that this place is more like a b&b than a hotel. We had room 12 next to the reception with a terrace area outside. The wardrobe in the room wouldn't open and was locked shut! Strange.... Also there was no long mirror and no lamp by the dressing table so it was very dark trying to get ready. The shower was terrible, followed the guide and still had a trickle of either boiling or cold water. Also the shower door doesn't slide on the runner so could be unsafe. However my gripe is the noise, from 5am there were alarms, doors being banged and loud voices chattering away, not sure if it was a one off noisy morning?. However the breakfast was lovely and freshly cooked and the staff were friendly. I would of been disappointed and said something if we were staying for longer than one night but it was ok for a stopover

author: Wonkyknees
title: View Their Website Carefully
text: Although this hotel is centrally located in St. Andrews, at $300 Canadian per night, it's overpriced - even in a touristy town. We really didn't think it lived up to the description on its website. Our small room had a fairly tacky décor, although the bathroom had been updated and was quite satisfactory. Be prepared to lug your suitcases up as many as three flights of winding stairs - yes, they look charming in the photos but..... As for the free parking in front of the hotel: you'll be lucky to find any. These stalls are heavily occupied throughout the day and only become available in the evening. However, the website does warn about the parking enforcement so I can't say I wasn't forewarned when I received a 60 pound ticket. Parking is a nightmare in this town. On the bright side - the staff is personable and helpful and the breakfast was fine.

author: 102madamep
title: Great little hotel!
text: My husband and I stayed here for a week, as he golfed I pursued sight seeing. Super helpful staff. Lovely breakfast and service. Loved the shower. Beds comfortable. I would return and recommend this hotel. All of St. Andrew's attractions were within walking distance.

author: alisonl843
title: A Little Gem in the Heart of St. Andrews
text: We stayed at The Abany while visiting St. Andrews for our daughter's graduation ceremony. St. Andrews is a very small town so we had to book well in advance, but the Albany was one of the very few hotels who did not insist on a three night booking. On our arrival we were delighted to find a beautiful little traditional hotel in a perfect location - directly across the road from where the graduation ceremony was taking place. The hotel has clearly recently been refurbished and our room was beautifully decorated, spacious, spotlessly clean and very comfortable, - we even had a little terrace outside with a table and chairs. There is a quaint and comfortable bar in the hotel and a traditional Scottish breakfast was served in the pretty dining room. The staff were helpful and friendly to a fault and we wouldn't hesitate to come back here if we are back in St. Andrews.

author: tbc3
title: Golf vacation hotel
text: A great little hotel for a St. Andrews Golf vacation. Located conveniently, only 6 blocks to the old course, 4 blocks to the old cathedral ruins, and with many restaurants located within 4 blocks and walking distance. Located within the University of St. Andrews campus area. The rooms are clean and comfortable, but small and you may have to climb steps as there is no elevator. It is very clean and the breakfast area is quaint & charming with excellent breakfast, both serve yourself and cooked to order. Parking is on street and hard to find until about 5:00 p.m.

author: NunzioeSilvia
title: Amazing and lovely week-end in St Andrews
text: My girlfriend and I have spent 2 days in this lovely, cosy and welcoming hotel. The room we got that was also an upgrade to the room with garden was really comfortable , clean and classy. The bed was comfortable and of a good size. The reseptionist Elen was really helpful and professional. She gave us the right suggestions and she tried to accomodate all our needs.....I asked her to buy a rose for my girlfriend and leave it on the bed when we were out for dinner. She unbelivebly bouth the rose and put on the bed with some rose petal and she kept the soft light on as long as she tidied up the bed. My girlfirend was amused. The location is also pretty central just a few steps in front of St Andrew University and from the seaside.

author: JMFothers
title: Fab Hotel & Excellent Value
text: Had a perfect stay at this little gem of a hotel. Perfectly located for walking to restaurants, bars, and shops. Staff were welcoming & friendly. The room well appointed, clean & comfy and like the rest of the hotel was freshly decorated in a classic style and with what seemed like new carpets. The bathroom was clean and fixtures also looked as though they had been recently replaced. Contrary to previous reviews, I could not see signs of wear & tear or "strange smells" anywhere. Breakfast was wonderful! Both a large selection of both buffet style foods and delicious, hot, freshly cooked foods were offered with plentiful drinks hot and cold. Excellent value and most enjoyable stay. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend to friends and family and would visit again.

author: cdab
title: small boutique hotel
text: The Albany hotel is well sited on North Street close to Cathedral an Castle and within easy walking distance of most of University campus. The hotel is a large townhouse over several floors. Receception and a small residents lounge make up the ground floor. I had a single room on the first floor which in comparison to most "chain" hotels was very small with a single bed rather than a queen or double. Although small it was well furnished and ok for a short stay. Breakfast was served in a conservatory on a lower level. The breakfast had lots of options and was very tasty. Overall a good stay.

author: FlossyM87
title: Fine
text: I stayed here for one night. The location of the Albany hotel is good though parking can be a little difficult. The rooms/hotel are dated but clean. The bathrooms are small and there was a lot of furniture cramped into the room I was staying in. The lady at reception was very friendly and helpful. Breakfast was average and was served in a small room with lots of tables and chairs in. It felt a bit awkward. All-in-all it was fine for one night but I would probably stay somewhere different if I were in town for longer than an evening.

author: RENSHAWWELSH
title: Quaint and Friendly.
text: Always happy to stay here. This is a small hotel with plenty of character. Some of the rooms are a little small and pokey and the carpets need a complete revamping. There is a cozy common lounge with bar. Breakfast is cooked to order and is excellent. Free WiFi that works. Located across the road to the Uni. Would be happy to return ANY day.

author: sandrads27
title: A charming, well situated hotel with lovely service!
text: We first discovered The Albany hotel last year when we were moving my eldest daughter to St Andrew's University. We had the pleasure of experiencing the single rooms as well as the suite during that visit. This past stay was due to a miscommunication from the letting office and so we found ourselves homeless for the nite, but were thankfully rescued when Ellen at The Albany, found the suite available due to a late cancellation. The rooms are clean, well appointed and very comfortable. I must recommend the main floor suite as it has 2 rooms: the smaller twin room with a door to a balcony overlooking the small, quaint gardens. The breakfast room on the lower level is small, but for what it lacks in expanse, it well makes up as a delicious breakfast spot. After a nice morning run on the Sands....their English Breakfast hit the spot! Well situated, with friendly and efficient staff...your stay at The Albany Hotel will be delightful!

author: JoeyMumbles
title: "What the cover says"
text: 1st time to St Andrews. Visited for Christening over Bank Holiday weekend! Great location within walking distance of bars restaurants beach and links! Good value compared to other options in St Andrews! It isn't 5 luxury or quirky boutique but that's not how it markets itself! Small and compact room but perfectly functional! Nice hot shower! Breakfast was excellent! Service from reception to breakfast room was courteous and friendly! Planning on return to St Andrews and would definitely consider the Albany again!

author: Linenbaron
title: Not good value for money
text: For £100 per night this was not very good. More like a B & B than a hotel. Rooms and bathrooms are tiny - also electric showers that produce only a very poor flow of water. Surely it would be possible to plumb in some decent showers. Breakfast ordinary - served in a dungeon type room in the basement. Bar area also poor. This establishment just happens to be very well located and doesn't bother to make an effort to improve. Roll on the opening of Premier Inn in St Andrews - then they will have to up their game

author: PaulaF701
title: Clean and comfortable
text: We stayed in the family room (1 double, 1 single) on the top floor -- no lift so you will schlep your bags up multiple winding stairs. Neat old hotel with lots of character. Breakfast was very good. The street was a little noisy as partiers were on the street. I thought the price was a bit steep but that seems to be the going rate in St. Andrews. The location was great for walking anywhere in St. Andrews.

author: Aamir27
title: Exceptionally friendly
text: I stayed here for a night right before an interview for the St Andrews university the following morning and was very impressed by the service received. The room was very well furnished and felt like I was staying at a hotel with a much higher star rating. In booking this room I had to make last minute changes such as an extra guest and the staff had already noted my reasoning in the first phonecall and had already prepared just in case I had the additional guest. Everything was great to be honest nothing I can complain about. Good shower, good facilities and everything. The following morning despite having to check out by 11am the interview was much later and the staff offered to look after my bags and my impression was they were prepared to go the extra mile with all our requests. Staff were polite with all our interactions and the breakfast was great too. I can't personally fathom where the negative reviews came from, perhaps they stayed in the wrong hotel by mistake. I paid slightly more for when I had to travel to Leicester for an interview and got half as much service and felt very much like a number. Many thanks to all the staff who made us feel very welcome especially the gentleman who wished me good luck for my interview!

author: DavidNJ27
title: Excellent little hotel
text: My wife stayed here when she came over to help my daughter get settled at University of St. Andrews for the semester and I returned with her again for a visit. Stayed at the Albany both times and had excellent experiences. Clean rooms, excellent breakfast made to order. Right across the street from the main part of the campus. Rooms on the small side but as expected in Europe. Had an enjoyable scotch tasting session with the proprietor in the little sitting room in front of the fireplace. Very helpful about things to do or places to see and arranging transportation back to Edinborough Airport.

author: Silvinrio
title: Good surprise
text: I was looking a last minute hotel or B&B in St. Andrews. We founded an offer in The Albany, I stayed several times in St. Andrews but it was my first time in The Albany. The location could not be better! The staff very friendly and helpful, all of them! Breakfast was good, a lot of choice. Room could be bigger and less noisy, that was the only problem.

author: Mr_M_From_Notts
title: AVOID! Liars, noise and no sleep!
text: This is possibly the worst "hotel" on the face of the earth. Don't be fooled into believing this business is suitably named. It is most definitely NOT a hotel, a guest house or B&B would be more apt. We were lied to upon booking regarding the room, the noise is more akin to a Youth Hostel rather than a hotel. You can quite literally hear everything that is happening in the "hotel" from your room. Expect to be woken by late night revellers, early morning workmen and general noise. The facilities are awful and if you have a dust allergy I would suggest you bring your own dust buster as well as every room has a horrid musty smell. If you book here expect to pay 5 star prices for a Guest House that would struggle to be awarded 1 star. The only plus side is the location isn't too bad.

author: PellegrinaIsrael
title: Very nice place to stay
text: This is a charming, quaint B and B in the heart of St. Andrews, on "B & B Row". There are several things that set this one apart from the pack, though. First, the owners are unusually kind and gracious; the small but cozy sitting room has a homey gas fire going; the rooms are large and well-equipped- unusually so- with little thoughtful touches such as blow-dryers and toiletries; and the breakfasts are tasty and ample. The beds were comfortable, and the inn was quiet. In fact, my only caveat was that the spacious bathroom featured only a shower stall rather than a bathtub. In short, I enjoyed my stay, and I'd definitely recommend this B and B to anyone visiting St. Andrews. While it didn't have the views of the previous B and B I had stayed at, the graciousness of the owners more than makes up for that.

author: Ageingvat
title: Cosy place to stay
text: I stayed in this hotel for two nights and found it to be reasonably comfortable, the lounge is a very warm & welcoming place to enjoy a quiet drink ( no draft beer ) if you so desire. My room, a double for single occupancy was on the top floor, the restaurant for breakfast is in the basement, the room itself, although a double had not a lot of room to spare, however, it was adequate and comfortable, those who are not particularly fit would do well to keep in mind there is no lift to any of the floors, by the time you have had breakfast you will have burned off the extra calories by the time you get back to your room if it happens to be on the top floor. Perhaps it is worth noting the hotel has no provision for evening meals therefore you will need to eat elsewhere. Breakfast, first class, good selection, well prepared, eggs done to perfection. Location,excellent for easy access to the town and places of interest. Parking, free street parking when you can find a space, best to time it around close of business or first thing in the morning. Cost, is fair for the area, if you think not, have a look at what others are charging. Staff, unlike some other reviews, I found the staff to be most friendly and very helpful. Stay again, yes I would without any hesitation.

author: bubblesCoDurham
title: Superb Staff, Comfortable Suroundings - Brilliant!
text: Our daughter was married from the Albany on 29th September this year. Obviously we have stayed at the Albany previously but I have had to write another review as the staff were absolutely superb. Everything we asked for happened i.e. we asked for continental breakfast to be available, we asked for a buffet to be prepared, extra Prosecco to be available and it was. We had the Garden Suite and the Junior Suite booked which were very reasonably priced and very spacious - really superb to fit in the bride, bridesmaids and hairdresser on the morning of the wedding. We could not ask for a better location - it was more or less opposite the wedding venue, or better service from the staff. Many of the guests stayed overnight on the Friday and Saturday and I didn't hear of any complaints only compliments. We will certainly be re-visiting at our earliest opportunity. Once again a massive thank you to all.

author: 31yrfemale
title: Overpriced - basic room
text: Hotel staff were very friendly. Breakfast was serviceable - not gourmet cuisine but fine enough. What I could not understand is the price - it seemed very expensive at £115 per room per night. Our twin room was small, fairly basic, with outdated decor. Plus it was noisy as next to the dining room. The bathroom was small - good shower though! Maybe we just had a bad room - if booking, ask to NOT be in the twin room right next door to the dining room. It was very clean though, and my bed was comfy.

author: BDR85
title: Great location for visiting the university
text: I went to St. Andrews to visit my son who is a student there. The Albany is directly across from Younger Hall and a few paces from St. Salvator's Chapel and Quad. The room was not luxurious, but certainly comfortable. My room was at the front of the hotel at ground level, but to my surprise was quite quiet at night. Breakfast was a typical Scottish breakfast. The staff was pleasant but did not go out of their way to be helpful.

author: 662jenniferm
title: Wedding April 2012
text: We got married in St Andrews at the end of April and all the wedding party stayed at the Albany. We were looking for a small hotel that is reasonably priced and it fitted the bill exactly. We cannot praise the service they provided highly enough. From the first time we visited, as potential guests, the staff did all they could to be helpful and showed us round the rooms. The Garden Suite was perfect for 4 of us to get ready in before the wedding, and lovely as a bridal suite that night. The groom stayed in the triple room with his brothers, and the reception staff were more than helpful in finding them a place to get ready after they had to check out of it. They were also very accomodating when the partners of bridesmaids and groomsmen showed up on the morning of the wedding, letting anyone they could into their rooms a bit early. The breakfasts were of a high standard, with something for everyone. The location was perfect for us, right in the middle of St Andrews. If you are looking for a friendly, small, well priced hotel within walking distance of attractions then I would recommend this one!

author: WendyB497
title: Wendy B
text: The Albany is located in a central but quiet part of St Andrews. Restaurants, the Byre Theatre and shops are all within a few minutes walk. Being an old Georgian building there are the usual creaking floorboards. All the staff were friendly and helpful. An excellent breakfast was served in the garden restaurant (only open for breakfast) - plenty of choice and hot food cooked to order and served on warm plates. It's obviously very popular with golfers. Cleanliness and attention to detail in the individual rooms meant that everything was to hand. I will definitely visit again.

author: Wyvernian
title: Sound base for St Andrews
text: The Albany is more like a superior B & B than a hotel, but it is clean, pleasant and ideally located in a quiet but central area of town. We had the excellent garden suite, which gave us an adjoining bedroom to our two children, who slept in a large lounge/bedroom. There is indeed access to a small, pleasant garden, and we found this very useful in allowing the kids to let off steam outside rather than inside. There was a problem with the heating when we arrived - radiators were only slightly warm and one wasn't working at all. We had to mention this three times and despite being received with concern by the staff, it was not satisfactorily resolved on the first night, although we were finally given a freestanding fire by a helpful young American staff member. The problem was rectified on day 2 and the heating was fine after that, but it was just a little disappointing not to get it sorted for the first night. Breakfasts were very good, with less usual items such as smoked haddock, black pudding and haggis among the offerings. It was also possible to get malt whiskies (and other drinks) served in the lounge to a late hour, which was very welcome, though the selection of malts could have been a little more adventurous. On the whole a pleasant stay though perhaps a little over-priced for what it is.

author: Expats-in-Wien
title: Perfectly adequate 3* hotel
text: I stayed in a single room at the Albany in early November while visiting my daughter who is a student at the university. The reception assistant at my arrival was extremely helpful and kind helping with a luggage issue I had. On the plus side: the lobby lounge area is nicely decorated, comfortable and pleasant, the breakfast is very good, the location is excellent and the price very reasonable. On the minus: my room (a single) was very small and I thought oddly decorated (unlike the very nice lobby)--a bit like staying in someone's spare room that had been put together with leftover furnishings--bed not very comfortable, linens and bedding of cheap quality, pillows awful unless you like firm foam pillows (no choices available--I asked). It took me until the second night to figure out that there were shutters to keep the street light out and how to turn on the wall heater. Apart from the initial desk clerk I met, the other front desk assistants were able to answer questions, but otherwise were just present--did not say hello or recognize me as I passed through the lobby, etc. If you are looking for an inexpensive, well-located place to sleep while in St Andrews, I recommend this hotel--it is clean and a fine place to stay. I prefer something at bit more upscale so will be looking for something else next time.

author: celticlegendltd
title: Friendly, welcoming, small hotel in the very middle of town.
text: The welcome was very good and the service and staff help and assistance, was top class at all times, from our check in, to departure after breakfast (good breakfast). The hotel location was perfect for us, attending a wedding in St. Salvator's Chapel, almost opposite. Pricing was quite high for a small double room, but certanly not above average for St. Andrews, an expensive town. The room was clean (and comfortable), as was the en-suite bathroom - did I mention small? I have stayed in hotels in St. Andrews before and this was the most welcoming and certainly as good value as anywhere. Professional from the first email reply to the last farewell.

author: Lucky525
title: Great little hotel
text: Four of us came to St Andrews for 5 days golf at stayed at the Albany. The hotel is in a great location, in the heart of St Andrews. From the moment we arrived the service we received was first class. I was a little apprehensive when I heard the room I was allocated was known as "The Bunker" but it was a delightful, clean, light filled room overlooking a lovely garden. The breakfast room overlooked the same lovely garden. The breakfast itself had a comprehensive range of cooked and continental options. There is a little bar area where guests can sit for a quiet drink before or after dinner and we made good use of that. The staff were all very friendly, from arranging laundry (at only 7 pounds a bag!) to booking and recommending restaurants. Would defintitely stay again.

author: khershner
title: Lovely inn, friendly staff, great breakfast
text: We stayed here on a last minute whim....not planning to stay the night in St. ANdrews, but got there a bit late in the day and then scurried around trying to find just the right place to make the experience a memorable one. Drove by The Albany, which has great 'curb appeal' and decided to take a chance to see if they had a room left. They did, on the first floor, just past the reception, which was no problem because it was sooo quiet and the room was lovely - had a view from the bay windows behind the bed of the garden in the back. The breakfast room is in the lower level and is light and airy and you can eat outside if you want to. We preferred to eat in the serene dining room. They had a traditional English breakfast with eggs, sausage, fresh juices, etc....and the staff were almost too attentive, but that's better than being ignored. Truly enjoyed our stay and recommend it with 'no reservations' to anyone looking for a nice place in town.

author: bubblesCoDurham
title: Wonderful - Will Definitely Be Back!!!
text: We stayed at the Albany on 1st and 2nd July as we had booked it 'blind' but upon reccomendation for our daughter's Wedding at the end of Septmember next year. We have to say we were incredibly impressed! The room was nicely decorated and the bed extremely comfortable. The breakfast was great - with hot coffee for a change!! All of the staff and the owner were fantastic. The bar was very reasonably priced and the hotel had an intimate 'family' atmoshphere. We were certainly made welcome and are positive we have made the right decision in booking the hotel accommodation for the Wedding - we are sure we will have a fantastic few days! I cannot reccommend you all highly enough - thank you, we had a lovely weekend.

author: MDonMills
title: Great hotel, super location
text: Great little hotel, very friendly and convenient as it's within walking distance of everything in St. Andrews. Lots of golfers stay here. Breakfasts were fantastic and the manager was very friendly and helpful. Would definitely stay here again. Room was small but very well appointed and more than adequate. Nice views out the back across gardens. Good value for St. Andrews.

author: SouthWalesPixie
title: Did the job though a bit disappointing
text: I'm not sure how many Scottish Tourist Board stars the hotel has but the hygiene wasn't exactly top notch (i..e. kettle in room, water glass, spoon for coffee) weren't very clean. It was all a bit tatty and cheap. Walls thin - so lots of noise from corridor and neighbouring rooms. Coffee at breakfast awful, condiments in room not filled up (there was only decaf!), Breakfast OK, staff very friendly and helpful though. It was paid out of expenses, think my room was about £100 for single which was rather extortionate so def no value for money. If I had paid myself I really would have walked out straight away. At this price one would expect at least for mineral water to be in the room but there wasn't any.

author: perrjojo
title: Friendly staff
text: The hotel is in a nice location on a quiet street, close to shopping , resturaunts and of course golf. The staff is helpful and friendly. The breakfast was good. There are many different sizes to the rooms. Our was VERY small and barely room to turn around in the bath. Ask for one of the larger rooms and you will be fine. It was quite expensive at 113 pound for two but then this is St Andrews. I would stay here again but ask for a larger room.

author: Arnietw0
title: Perfect location for function at University building !
text: I picked the Albany due to price and location. I searched trip advisor and thought there were a couple of average reviews but I booked just the same. So on arrival and during our overnight stay it was actually a lot better than I had first expected. The receptionist was very helpful and when we asked about a quick snack made sandwiches without hesitation. Room was fresh and clean and nothing negative whatsoever. Breakfast was good also and again anything asked for was provided quickly and without difficulty. I would return here no probs ! Phoned the hotel direct and got better price than on alpharooms or booking.com etc !!

author: 150timm150
title: Nice place, but take note it is cash only.
text: It was a very nice place and perfect location for catching a cruise. The room, while sparsely decorated, was clean and comfortable. The staff was very warm and friendly. The pool area was fantastic! It was quiet and beautiful. You almost forgot you were in a city. My only complaint would be is they don’t take cards of any kind, cash only. This wasn’t made very clear. That is the only reason for a 4 star.

author: 97hannahp
title: Wonderful
text: It is our last day today and we are very sad to be leaving this wonderful little place. Toni, Christina and all the other staff/family members are an absolute delight. The room we stayed in was fresh, bright and very clean and the bathroom was very modern also. We also had air con in the room which worked wonders. Toni was very helpful when we arrived and recommended things for us to do after getting to know what we were here for Location is ideal, so close to Tommys supermarket and close to the bus station and the marina. It takes only 25 mins to walk into old town from here and about 20 mins to Lapad where there is a strip of bars and restaurants and sunset beach with the cave bar (which Toni had recommended to us) There was no safe in the room we stayed in, however we didn't even feel like we needed one. We left jewellery out and money and everything was more than safe. Thank you so much Toni and team. We would definitely recommend and we would most definitely come back. You've helped make our holiday one to remember 😀

author: elaineLeicester
title: Relaxed Location
text: When we arrived we couldn’t decide if we were staying in someone’s home or a guesthouse !!! But this place grows on you. It’s relaxing clean secure and run as a family operation. Tony the owner and Christina who’s staff both can’t do enough for you. They even got me gluten free cereals and bread. There is a wonderful terrace to have breakfast on. We purchased wine and sat with other guests later to talk over our day. It’s also well situated for everything but is so quiet you think your in the countryside. Our only negative was we were offered a twin room as only room available which was very compact.

author: 97pete
title: Peacefully oasis just minutes from a busy harbour.
text: I write this review on my last day at the Bokun guest house. It has been a fantastic base from which to explore what Dubrovnik has to offer. Or if you just want to sit by the pool and relax, this is just the place for it. However busy the outside world is, once you enter the gate just a few feet off the main road, you are transported to a different world. The communal area where breakfast is laid out in the morning is a ceiling of grape vines and kiwi plants. We have spent many an evening chilling over a local bottle of wine, reading or chatting with other guests. Tony and his staff are all welcoming and attentive. The Bokun is run very much with a family atmosphere. We are already talking of coming back. I can’t rate the place highly enough.

author: allen_dunbar
title: Great guesthouse better than hotel
text: My family stayed at this most perfect accommodation. The guest house is like a farmhouse retreat in the middle of a city. Toni the owner could not been more helpful. The guest house rooms are of an excellent standard, modern and clean. We had 8 rooms in total, doubles, twins and apartments. The pool area is is very relaxing and combined with the lovely external breakfast area, this is a most peaceful place to stay. Ask Toni to cook his special Croatian meal while you are visiting, it will be the best meal you have whilst in Croatia ( not to say we had a bad meal). Nothing is a problem to Toni and his house keeper Christina. They are helpful with local information, best places to eat and visit and can give you a song if you wish:). Watch out for Toni's homebrew though.

author: garethl654
title: A fantastic Week at the Bokun
text: A wonderful stay at this hidden gem an oasis from the hustle and bustle .Arrived met by Toni who gave us an overview of the area. Our room was fine for what we needed. Breakfast was great the bread was lovely and fresh. Out through the green door and your into the port of Gruz lots of restaurants we ate every night in Gruz. Its a 30 min walk to the old town and about the same to Lapad where a drink at the cave bar is a must. Back at the Bokun we had a lovely meal arranged by Toni with wine it was very tasty cooked in his own style on the BBQ. The charm of this place is its location and feeling part of a larger family whilst your there Toni is a brilliant host supported by Krystina they will all do anything they can to help you enjoy your stay haven't mentioned the boat trip arranged by Toni which was wonderful and will be a separate review on Luca's page. One again thank you the Bokun for a lovely stay we hope to be back next year.

author: kkar830
title: Nice garden but not worth the money
text: The guesthouse has a beautiful garden and is a wonderful place to relax. The pool area is great and you can spend a whole day there... away from the tourist nightmare that is Dubrovnik (we were very disappointed by the city). However, the rooms are small and not very stylish. Breakfast is a disappointment with little freshness (packaged jams etc) and instant coffee. Beware that the guesthouse does not accept cards of any kind for payment, which means you need to withdraw a large amount of cash... just when you‘ll likely no longer need the currency. Overall, not worth the price.

author: anthonyglover
title: A taste of heavan
text: As many people have said before this is a little taste of heaven away from the hustle and bustle of Dubrovnik. Tony and his lovely staff are fantastic hosts. The guesthouse set in its own Garden of Eden behind its own drawbridge is wonderful. Swimming pool with sun beds, though you have to be brave to swim in April. One night Tony cooked for six guest on his Peka, a hidden talent we were not expecting. The best meal we ate in Croatia. A good bus service (every 10 mins) connects you to the Old Town and there are plenty of restaurants and bars close by. The boats to the islands depart right outside the front gate.Book early as this is a popular hotel!

author: dianesY3202ZO
title: A little gem, we arrived tense and departed relaxed.
text: This was our first trip to Dubrovnik and we loved it. This Guesthouse is a little gem; its location by the port is ideal which, is bustling rather than hectic, yet is within easy reach of all the busy tourist attractions. Tony and his staff, Christina in particular, made our stay memorable, comfortable and stress free. We run our own hospitality business in France and in our opinion they have got it spot-on. Would we stay there again? Absolutely. Would we recommend it to family and friends? Again, absolutely. Thank you for a great week and for allowing us to share your wonderful property.

author: JohnashBolton
title: Home From Home.
text: Spent a week in an apartment at the Bokun early September and thoroughly enjoyed it. Toni is a great and helpful host and he puts himself out to ensure you are comfortable in his small establishment. Don't quite know how many rooms they have but can't be more than ten in total. The communal terrace is a great place to meet the other guests and sit and have a beer or two and, weather permitting, breakfast. Christina ably supports Toni, particularly at breakfast times. I have to say the fresh bread and croissants were excellent along with the usual continental breakfast fayre. I can confirm all the previous reviews about this accommodation being quality are bang on and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend. Easy striking distance by foot or on the bus to Lapad or Dubrovnik and Cavtat is accessible by the latter. Toni and Family and Christina, thanks very much for sharing your company and your welcoming efforts during our visit. John and Julie Bolton

author: 266pamelam
title: Quiet little Oasis in a Bustling Town
text: Our lovely Croatian Holiday at the Bokun Guest house is almost over, we will be sad to go home to cold wet rainy British Summertime! Toni, Family & Staff have been most hospitable, we really didn't want for anything. The Guest house & grounds are beautiful, a quiet little oasis amidst a bustling port. Lovely swimming pool that we've enjoyed most days. Facilities are all you need & breakfast was a great choice of items. Everyone should take Tonys Friend Luka up on his island boat trip, this really was a relaxing day, very good value for money & lunch provided too, very leisurely. We Hope to come back sometime & enjoy the Croatian sunshine once more. We had a double room on the first floor which was all that was needed, plenty electrical points, a bed, storage, shower room, table & chairs & a fridge, we weren't here to stay in our room for the week so it definitely was more than adequate. Very clean & tidy. Breakfast on the terrace was fruit, yoghurts, croissants, bread, meats & cheeses, eggs, honey, jam, juice & tea & coffee, Kristina was very helpful pointing us in the right direction of a chemist & busses etc I wouldn't hesitate to come back to the Bokun, it really has been great :-)

author: ericfreeman53
title: Great Holiday
text: Just come back from a weeks stay at the Bokun Guesthouse. I think all the previous reviews say it all, it's a great place to stay. Quite, you would not think you were a stone throw from the harbour. Loved the pool area, never a problem getting sun beds. Toni and family are great hosts, however I do have a couple of minuses. The bathroom was very small, if on the large size you would struggle in the shower (can only speak for the room we were in, never saw any other rooms to compare). Personally I found the breakfast a bit repetitive. But I would not let this stop me from returning. Dubrovnik old town is a stunning place , about 25 minutes enjoyable walk or 12Kuna on local bus, 100 Kuna in taxi (expensive for how far the town is away. About 15 minute walk to Lapad beach, with good selection of bars and restaurants.

author: mrbarrington
text: This is an out of the way guesthouse with so much going for it. Great owner and staff who can't do enough for you. Some rooms are bigger than others and all very clean. So relaxed in that there is no bar or rip off prices just bring in your own drink sit in the shade under the grape vine canopy and enjoy the conversation of other guests. Great safe swimming pool and all behind a wall 100 yards from the harbour front with its boats and luxury yachts. This not a five star hotel but it has everything you could need. Tony the owner speaks first class English and his staff are so helpful and friendly. Would l come back here again......YES.

author: wanderlustLucerne
title: Family affair
text: Dubrovnik is getting a bit out of hand, overrun with tourists, and good accommodation at a sensible price is becoming a scarcity. The Bokun guesthouse is in the Gruz port area of town, a good couple of kilometres walk from the wonderful old town, but there’s also a bus available. There’s a safe public car-park right next door, for a fee. Bokun’s rate reflect Dubrovnic’s prices. It calls itself a guesthouse because it serves breakfast, on the terrace, and is not the customary Croatian-style apartment set-up. Rooms tend to be small, but very clean (apart from a touch of mildew in the shower-room) and well appointed. It also has a garden and a swimming-pool for guests to use, a big bonus point. It’s a bit of a family affair, with three generations in evidence. To save the trek into town for dinner, walk the shorter distance to the restaurants and cafés on the Lapad headland.

author: 353mattl
title: Secret Garden
text: We have just spent 4 nights in the most beautiful guesthouse and will definitely be returning. Behind the green door is a stunning garden with a beautiful terrace where breakfast is eaten. We had a studio it was lovely spacious with all the things you would need and the aircon we definitely needed. The pool area is stunning and very relaxing. Toni the host has lots of knowledge of the local area and is the perfect host nothing is too much trouble. The continental breakfast is yummy fresh bread and croissants boiled eggs meat cheeses yoghurts and fresh fruit picked from his garden well worth the money. Dubrovnik is amazing whatever your age. All in all we met some lovely people stopped in a stunning guesthouse the weather was perfect and we will return - thanks Toni.

author: colleen5034
title: Loved our stay here!
text: My husband and I stayed here for three nights on our first trip to Croatia. What a great start to our trip! The setting is beautiful, lovely rooms in a charming very old stone house surrounded by beautiful gardens. We ordered breakfast each day for an extra 7 euro and ate on the terrace which was so lovely. Christina was so wonderful, she greeted us upon arrival, serving us cold drinks and spending a lot of time with us answering questions and getting us acclimated. She was so delightful throughout our stay making us feel at home and even giving me an adaptor so I could use my curling iron. The pool is fabulous and so nice to come home to after being in the heat walking the walls and exploring Dubrovnik. If you are driving a car just be aware you have to pay for parking and have to get a ticket from a nearby newsstand. We loved our stay here and would love to go back someday! Thank you Christina and Toni!

author: Grumm
title: Put the Bokun on your bucket list
text: The ratings say it all, 5*, It's not the Ritz but it's a memorable place to stay. Close to restauants and buses and boat trips. Toni is an excellent host and will advise you on things to do and see. Rooms are clean and tidy, big comfortable beds but our bathroom was somewhat on the small side (small matter, ha ha). Large BBQ in the garden and lots of advice/help from Toni if needed. Local butcher a few minutes away, great sausages and chicken, and the veg market a bit further along. Loved it so much we are retuning later this year to learn how to BBQ a Peka!!! See you later Toni

author: chriseS5325WL
title: 100% Recommend
text: Currently co.ing up to our last day at the guest house and had a fantastic time. We have a standard double room, on suite bathroom, television, fridge so we can bring things back to keep cool. Toni has been a great host with lots of local knowledge on bakery's, markets, places to eat, drink and so much more. He set us up for a tour of the 3 islands which was fantastic and great value for money. The garden when you walk in is stunning with lots of flowers, vegetables, fruit. Outside area to sit and enjoy. A pool and sun loungers to sit and relax in the sun. Just 20 minutes away from the old town, lapad on the peninsula, where there are lots of bars and places to eat. Right on Gruz port where you can have excursions to places like Montenegro or Bosnia and Herzegovina.

author: 876maryp
title: Lovely stay in in sunny Dubrovnik
text: have just returned from a week staying at Bokun Guest House, Toni and his family and staff made us feel like part of the extended family. The rooms were clean and comfortable, my husband and I had standard room but our friends had a small apartment. The Guest house is set in a lovely garden where the family grow vegetables and flowers. It is about 25 mins walk into Dubrovnik but buses are regular and reasonable. Plenty of places to eat around about if you don't want to go int town to eat, local supermarket is just up the road, we had a couple of simple meals in the garden with items purchased there. We had a Dubrovnik card for one day which gave us unlimited bus rides, entry to walls, a number of museums and some reductions at shops and restaurants. We spent a relaxing day in Cavtat easily reached by bus or boat and walked more walls at Stom. A lovely stay all around.

author: andykshepherd
title: A very good guest house
text: A very good guest house tucked away in a calm oasis just 1 min. from the port. Toni and staff/family very helpful and friendly. The room was very clean, cool (a/c), everything worked and great to have a mini fridge. Dubrovnik is stunning, 30 mins walk or 5 mins by frequent (if very busy) bus. Lovely restaurants within 5-10 minutes walk. Toni organised a private boat trip for us with another family which was an excellent day out, Luka's boat was lovely and we had a very memorable day. Overall we had a great week at Bokun.

author: karenfsmith
title: Fantastic holiday
text: We have just come back from2 weeks at Bokun, very sad to leave. The accomodation is great, very friendly staff, clean & in a fantastic spot. The breakfast was great set you up for the day, with bread, meat, cheese, eggs, yoghurt, pastry & freshly ripened fruit from the garden & amazing tomatoes. Tony the owner & all the staff were great, the rooms were serviced every day with clean towels & the pool was area was spot on & never a problem getting a bed. There were plenty of places in the surrounding area to eat & drink, the old town which is absolutely gorgeous is a 20 min walk, or 5 mins on the very frequent buses. We went into the old town several times to sightsee & eat. The cable car & museum are well worth a trip. Tony organised a boat trip for us & other guests with Luca which was a great day. All in all if you like small & friendly, clean accomodation with plenty to do on your doorstep this place is great. Would definitely recommend.

author: 379jaynem
title: A wonderful week at Bokun Guesthouse
text: We stayed here for a week in July 2016. What a superb guesthouse right beside the harbour. Toni and his family are really friendly and Toni is very helpful in advising about places to go and to eat out. The breakfasts were lovely - eggs, ham, cheese, yoghurt, fruit (even plums from the garden picked by Toni's father), juice, pastry etc. Our room was small but really lovely, good air con, the pool area is peaceful and relaxing and you are provided with pool towels. It's about a 25 minute walk to the old town but the bus stop is very close by. We went to a restaurant called Peppers which is no more than a 10 minute walk round the harbour which is really good and we had a wonderful winetasting evening at Lekri Winery which we'd also really recommend. We took a trip to wonderful Montenegro which Toni organised for us, and also a trip to Cavtat which was good to see. Toni makes you feel very welcome, we'd really recommend Bokun!

author: martinrr2016
title: A hidden gem. Highly reccomended
text: Toni is a very friendly guy, and he and his family made us feel very welcome. Once we had been shown to our room, he gave us a map of the town and explained to us how to get to the places that we wanted to see. (marked out bus route's etc) He also highlighted the locations of a few decent restaurants for us. Our room was lovely and cleaned daily. The shower was hot, the bed was really comfy, and the air-con worked great (and quietly!)- a God-send on particularly warm nights!. The room had a strong fast free WiFi signal, What more could you ask for? Breakfast was delicious.. If you stay here - you will not start the day hungry that is for sure! The garden's are really beautiful and although we didnt try it, the pool looked very inviting! If we come back to Dubrovnik, we would certainly look to stay at Bokun Guesthouse again!

author: 495DavidF495
title: Serene setting, good proprietor
text: This is an easy place to hang out when not in active tourist mode. Our room had been remodeled in the past year. There is a very nice patio and garden area and a swimming pool. There are well-maintained (by the proprietor's, Tony's, parents) grounds with flowers and shrubs and vegetables. This place is behind an old private chapel that, itself, fronts on the "new" (600-years-old) harbor, so the Guesthouse is quiet but close to piers and miscellaneous retail. There is small supermarket ("Tommy") nearby and an open-air produce market, too. There is a good pharmacy nearby and at least one good restaurant, Peppers. Tony was very friendly and helpful, as were his wife and parents and staff; Tony is the English-speaker. Breakfast was serviceable and seemed right for the overall cost.

author: annetteg496
title: Lovely, quiet guest house in beautiful grounds
text: My friend and I were delighted to stay outside of Dubrovnik and get away from the crowds back to this haven of peace very conveniently located....just an 8 min. bus ride into Dubrovnik, off the main street where the cruise ships docked. The house was 450 years old, situated in a beautiful garden with a newly constructed swimming pool. We had a room which was called an apartment where a sofa bed was made up as we had asked for a twin bedded room. The breakfast was 50 kuna more and coffee was only instant. As we had a small fridge and hot plates we were able to buy what we needed in the was of food at the local market nearby. We didn't realize that there was no room service or change of towels unless requested, and we were there for 5 nights..In spite of these inconveniences we enjoyed our stay and everything as everywhere we had been was extremely clean. Wifi was free, but frequently didn't work

author: reisecamilla
title: Beautiful garden,but that's it
text: We had our hopes up from the great reviews, but were disappointed. The rooms are small, but clean. Tiny bathroom. Fridge didn't work. It's just ok. Slept very well as it's quiet and tucked away. Closes to the bus station. About 20 minute walk to Old Town, and the same to some very nice beaches in the area. Wifi worked best in the garden.

author: 880jesseg
title: Authentic Croatian experience
text: We stayed 2 weeks at bokun. The owner Tony was always helpful,friendly and accommodating. We stayed in one of the larger apartment's with cooking facilities which was great as bokun is 1min walk from local produce market. We found the location excellent as it is walking distance from the old city, lapad beaches and views of the harbour as you exit bokun. Bokun has a warm feel as it is surrounded by picturesque gardens where u can sit under the grape vines enjoying a drink of Toni's homemade wine. Despite being central on a busy rd its a quiet and tranquil location. Our room was clean and functional, linen and towels included. Overalwl a fantastic guesthouse that is very reasonably priced. We would return to if we ever visit Croatia again.

author: RosieFlower123
title: I'd highly recommend and would definitely go back to Bokun Guesthouse!
text: We stayed for 1 week between May-June. The guesthouse sits outside the town by the Marina, it's very beautiful and there's a few restaurants nearby. They're buses every 5 minutes to the Old Town which are very cheap, the location is great because you get to see more of the city, and it's a ten minute walk to Lapad Beach which is gorgeous. The owner, Toni, is very friendly and gave us loads of helpful tips and advice about where to go in Dubrovnik. The room had an en suite and was clean and quiet. I'd highly recommend it to anyone. We also got picked up from the airport and driven back which was all part of the deal. Great for couples and families!

author: WanderLoves
title: lovely overall
text: beautiful outside area to relax/hang out/use wifi/meet others, especially if good weather. very accessible location to old town and other parts of Dubrovnik. walk is about 25 min to old town, but bus stop 1 minute away comes very frequently and is 5-10 minute ride. host is very accommodating. breakfast is a good deal. one reallllly good restaurant 2 minutes walk away. one bus stop away from the main bus terminal, which is also near a few bar/cafes (in the other direction from the old town). shower/bathroom was a bit small but standard for most places in croatia (in our experience). overall, lovely experience and would stay there again if on a budget.

author: AimeeH936
title: nice place
text: We stayed here, and it was a pleasant peaceful place to stay away from the noise of the city. The only negatives were that we couldn't get any hot water to run (probably just being silly and not spotting something that would heat the water up), and the parking was a bit odd. We had to park in what seems to be a bus depot. It was hard to gain access to the parking through the barrier, as the guard wouldn't let us in without a struggle. This may have been a one off, as no-one else seems to have a problem with it so we were probably just unlucky. There also was something that I spotted that concerned me a little (but I do work with health and safety so I spot danger everywhere), it was that there was a gas bottle that was used to run the gas hob. I didn't like the thought of having a gas bottle in a place where I slept, but it is probably ok. The owner was friendly, if a bit stressed. Room was clean and comfortable, ktichen well equipped.

author: HeatherD280
title: Oldhands
text: We have stayed with Toni for over ten years now. The guesthouse is in an ideal position - equidistant between the bus station/ ferry terminal and the old town of Dubrovnik. It is on level ground, as opposed to many places in the old town or on the hill behind it, which often don't have easy access. It is a quiet oasis, with pleasant gardens. Plenty of nearby supermarkets, restaurants and cafe-bars, where you will see real local people as opposed to the old town where you might not be able to move on account of the hordes of tourists who are deposited there in busloads, from the gruesome cruisers. Toni's sister Dubravka is a knowledgeable professional guide, which is useful. A genuine, friendly, unpretentious family atmosphere. Wouldn't stay anywhere else by choice.

author: Snellerelli
title: Great Experience at Bokun Guesthouse
text: From arranging pick up from the airport to cluing us in on the best things to take in during our time in Dubrovnik, Toni was the model of great host! The guesthouse sits at the Gruz Harbor. There are ample places to get a coffee (white coffee is delicious there!) or a bite, and a grocer is a short walk away (Tommy's). The convenience of Toni's Guesthouse is outweighed by the friendliness of Toni & his family. He was more than happy to talk about his city and give us pointers on places to check out. He even made special arrangements for us as we took the ferry to Bari at about 10pm. It is a 15 minute walk to Old Town or the Pedestrian Walk on Lapad...but buses also cruise to either of these spots continually AND the walk is lovely. We stayed in a suite with a kichenette and dining area. It was more than spacious and felt like a home away from home. thanks Toni!

author: BJL79
title: Wonderful place to stay
text: Rather late in posting my review, but we stayed in this guesthouse last summer and had a really lovely time. It was our favorite of all the places we stayed in Croatia. The owner is great and it's close to the marina, yet set back in a quiet setting. It's a bit of a hike from the Old Town but the buses were frequent (and it's a nice walk if you're up for it). The neighborhood felt very "lived in" as well, which we liked. We walked down to the outdoor market every morning to get fruit, as well as expresso and pastries at a nearby cafe and bakery. Much cheaper than trying to find breakfast in the old town for sure! We only stayed two nights and wished we had stayed a bit longer to do daytrips from Dubrovnik.

author: MiGagnon
title: welcoming oasis
text: Without my stay at Bokun Guesthouse, my 1st trip in Croatia would have been ordinary. Great familly feel, amazing quiet garden hidden in the middle of busy Dubrovnik streets. And the price is really good. I really appreciated to chat with Toni about his country. He gave me precious tips about places I wanted to visit in Dubrovnik. I will totally recommend it to my friends! Txs a bunch Bokun familly! Mireille

author: yuetchow
title: Would not recommend
text: I book it through booking.com. he did not seem to remember me when we emailed till few days before my arrival. Demanded to see my booking document. Not a single smile. Need to tow my luggage up stairs(for a girl ) 10 min from bus station, 30 min from old town by foot. without breakfast and shared bathroom, rather try rooms (zimmer) Never speak a word about his organic garden. Not a bit of hospitality but a lot of hostility. Have never experience this with my years as a solo traveller.absolutely over-priced·

author: katertonks
title: One of the best places I've stayed
text: My friend and I stayed here back in July . It was a bit tricky to find, but once we go there, we were amazed. This place is family owned and reeks of charm. Our room had air conditioning - a difficult thing to find in Croatia - and was very reasonably priced. We had to share our bathroom with another room, but this wasn't a problem for us. Possibly the best part is the tables in the beautiful garden where you can eat your meals. You can also pay and the family will cook extra dinner for you. Everyone was so kind and generous and the place was just too picturesque for words. It is also a short walk/bus ride to town.

author: Jayney79
title: Very good value accommodation
text: We stayed here for 1 night and couldn't fault it. We arrived in Dubrovnik by Bus, and the hotel was about a 5-10 minute walk from the bus station (although if you ring they will ome and pick you up from the station for free). The hotel is found up an alleyway behind a green iron door, where the gardens are fantastic, full of fruit, vegetables and flowers. We were shown to our room, which turned out to be an apartment. It had a seperate bedroom and bathroom, and a large room with table/chairs, sofa, tv, and kitchenette, it was a shame we weren't staying longer! It takes about half an hour to wak to the old town, although buses are avaiable not far from the hotel, but the walk is nice, a little hill, but views of the coastline for some of it. We had a whole day in Dubrovnik before we moved on, and we able to keep our bags at the hotel after checking out, whcih was a great help. If you don't mind being slightly out of the city centre, this is an ideal place to stay, great value, near to the bus station, and nice rooms.

author: justinmY9506GT
title: Close to Airport
text: Hampton Inn, Woodland, CA is a nice option for traveler's flying into and out of Sacramento International Airport. Very easy to find, with quick access to Interstate 5. Property itself is pretty basic for a Hampton, but nonetheless clean and comfortable. I stayed on the 3rd floor. Room was nice, but the floor as a whole, including the elevator, was very cold. Lobby was comfortable, so not sure of the cause. My in-room heating unit worked fine, so I was comfortable. There are several fast food and or sit-down eateries close by. Check-In and out processes were quick and without issue. Staff were courteous and professional.

author: clintock20
title: Dated Hotel
text: I want to preface this negative review by saying the staff was accommodating and professional. The simple fact is that this hotel seems old. Not sure if it is or not, but everything seems dated; from the elevator, the carpet, the rooms, the tv, etc. Even the remotes to the tvs seem like they are from the 90s. The other issue I had was the limited parking. There are only a few spots in front of the entrance. So you have to walk all the way around the building after parking to get in. (unless you have already checked in and have a key to get in the other entrances)

author: Ammo68
title: Quiet , decent place to stay / CLOSE TO AIRPORT
text: I am in woodland / ROSEVILLE a lot and this is a good location . Beds are good , rooms are clean , staff for the most part is friendly . It’s near the freeway but super quiet .
